TAIPEI, April 15 (Reuter) - Taiwan's money rates finished
mixed on Monday, dealers expecting overnight to rise further
amid current bullish stock market and income tax payments.
    Overnight ended at 6.134 percent against Saturday's 5.949,
while 30-day commercial paper fell to 7.00 from 7.10-7.15.
    Though Taiwan share prices hit a new 11-month high on
Monday, attracting liquidity into the stock market, bond traders
did not expect significantly tighter conditions as the central
bank monetary policy remains relaxed.	N2:LOA

ISTANBUL, April 12 (Reuter) - Turkey's leading private banks
cut their lira deposit rates in short term maturities after the
recent sharp falls in overnight money rates and t-bill yields.
    Three leading private banks Akbank <AKBNK.IS>, Is Bankas
<ISATR.IS> and Yapi ve Kredi Bankasi <YKBNK.IS>jointly lowered
their one and three-month deposit rates by five points to 75
percent and 80 percent respectively, effective from Monday.
    They kept their six-month deposit rates at 90 percent and
one-year deposit rates 95 percent.
    Private Sumerbank and Tarisbank also lowered their
short-term deposit rates by between 2-5 percentage points while
private Egebank slashed the deposit rates on all maturities by
four points, effective from Monday.
    More private banks are expected to follow suit next week,
bankers said.
    The treasury managed to lower its t-bill yields by more than
20 points in two auctions this month, after a month-long cash
squeeze eased in the money market.
    The central bank supported the downward trend in interest
rates by gradually lowering its overnight bid-offer rates. The
overnight money rates sank to a low 45 percent this week from 90
percent levels earlier this month.
    In the t-bill market, yields plunged to below 120 percent
levels, from 135-140 percent on April 1.
    Money and t-bill rates firmed today due to fresh cash demand
ahead of the weekend and public sector salary payments due on
Monday. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75	N2:LOA

TAIPEI, April 11 (Reuter) - Taiwan's central bank said on
Thursday it will relax restrictions on the use of funds raised
by local firms' overseas through depositary receipts (DRs) and
convertible bonds (CBs), effective immediately.
    From now on, local firms can apply to have the funds raised
overseas sent to Taiwan and exchanged for Taiwan dollars, which
can be used to repay outstanding bank loans, the bank said in a
statement.
    Use of the funds will be limited to paying back bank loans
that are used for local expansion, investments in the island's
major economic development plans, and investments in major
high-technology industries, it said.	N2:LOA

ABIDJAN, April 12 (Reuter) - The first of three regional bonds
to be quoted on the Abidjan Stock Exchange (BVA) were officially
launched on Friday, bankers said.
    The five billion CFA offer by Ivory Coast State bank Caisse
Autonome d'Amortissement was issued through the local unit of
U.S. bank, Citibank. Denominated in 10,000 CFA units, it matures
in three years and has a yield of nine percent net of tax, a
Citibank official said.
    It was the first bond by the Caisse Autonome d'Amortissement
to be handled by a bank other than the French-linked ones that
dominate the Ivorian financial sector.
    The second is a five-billion CFA bond that has been fully
subscribed since its issue by Benin brewer SOBEBRA in January. It
is for seven years, with a face value of 100,000 CFA and yields
9.5 percent, BVA's chief economist Romain Yao said.
    The third, for three billion CFA also has a face value of
100,000 CFA and yields 6.91 percent over five years. It will be
issued by SAGA-Cote d'Ivoire, a unit of French transport group
SAGA.	N2:LOA

LONDON, April 11 (LPC) - Railtrack Group Plc signed on
Tuesday a 2.35 billion stg bank loan, according to market
sources.
   Led by BZW Syndications, the credit will form the core
financing for Railtrack, which is slated to have a public
offering of shares in May.  The facility will also provide cash
to help fund the Thameslink 2000 project.
    Joining the deal as underwriters were Barclays Bank, Credit
Suisse, Deutsche Bank, Fuji Bank, Kredietbank, Midland Bank,
Royal Bank of Scotland and West LB. These eight each pledged
about 300 million stg to the credit, but will sell a portion of
their exposure down through a general syndication.
    Launch of general syndication is scheduled for Tuesday April
16. For top level commitments of 100 million stg or more, banks
will receive 10 bps fees, sources said.
    The credit is split into two tranches, one of 1.65 billion
stg and one of 700 million stg, both with a final maturity of
five years. Barclays Bank is serving as facility agent.
   Railtrack owns the track and stations formerly controlled by
British Rail and will gain revenue by charging train companies
that use its facilities.

BREMEN, Germany, April 16 (Reuter) - Cash-strapped German shipbuilder Bremer
Vulkan Verbund AG will probably file for bankruptcy on May 2, union officials
said on Tuesday.
    Separately, a German magazine reported that Udo Wagner, management board
chairman of Germany's largest shipbuilder, planned to step down only three
months after taking the helm.
    Wolfgang Dettmer, deputy head of the Bremer Vulkan yard in Bremen, said
court-appointed administrator Jobst Wellensiek had not ruled out that the group
would be forced to file for bankruptcy in early May.
    Bremer Vulkan filed for protection from creditors in late February and has
until May 10 to work out a debt rescheduling agreement with its creditors to
stave off bankruptcy.
    The works council said it would start talks this week aimed at preventing
thousands of job losses in the immediate aftermath of a bankruptcy.
    Bremer Vulkan at one point employed 23,000 people but the bankruptcy would
not affect around 9,000 workers as several units have been hived off.
    Meanwhile, Manager Magazin reported in a summary of an article to be
published its next edition that tensions had flared between Wagner and
Wellensiek and supervisory board chairman Hero Brahms.
    Neither Wagner nor Bremer Vulkan was available for comment.
    Wagner, formerly finance chief at Asea Brown Boveri (ABB), assumed his
position on February 1, replacing Friedrich Hennemann who left Bremer Vulkan as
huge losses and misuse of public subsidies became public.
    Only three weeks after taking up his new job, Wagner announced that Bremer
Vulkan was seeking protection from creditors and that the courts would appoint
an administrator.
    The magazine said in light of growing speculation Bremer Vulkan would be
forced to file for bankruptcy there is little else for Wagner to do at the
company.

LONDON, April 11 (Reuter) - Newsquest Capital Plc, the UK
newspaper publisher acquired by Kohlberg, Kravis Roberts & Co in
a leveraged buyout from Reed Elsevier <ELSN.AS><REED.L>, has
issued $120 million in high yield bonds, CS First Boston said on
Thursday.
    CS First Boston lead-managed the $120 million issue of 11
percent senior subordinated notes due 2006.
    Christian Purslow, a director for CS First Boston, said the
issue represents the first UK leveraged buyout to access the
U.S. high yield market, which was done at a rate substantially
lower than traditional European mezzanine debt.
    CS First Boston had advised KKR on its buyout of Newsquest
Capital, formerly Reed Regional Newspapers, for 206 million stg.
    Credit Suisse and CS First Boston had arranged a 115 million
stg credit facility, comprising a 95 million stg eight-year term
loan and a six-year 20 million working capital facility, to fund
the acquisition.
Proceeds of the high-yield offering were used to refinance
seller notes issued by Reed Elsevier and to repay a portion of
the bank debt, Purslow said.

SINGAPORE, April 16 (Reuter) - Videocon Petroleum Ltd has
signed a US$46 million loan facility for the Ravva oil and gas
development project in Madras, India, the company and lending
banks Bank of America and Banque Paribas said on Tuesday.
    Videocon Petroleum is part of the Videocon Group <VDCI.BO>,
which is one of the leading manufacturers of consumer
electronics products in India.
    The agreement was signed on March 29, the joint statement
said.
    The Ravva project, estimated to cost US$243.7 million,
represents Videocon's first move into the petroleum sector.
    The project, located 400 km northwest of Madras, consists of
seven unmanned offshore platforms, onshore processing and
storage facilities and gas lift and water injection facilities,
the statement said.
    Command Petroleum <CPH.AX> unit Command Petroleum (India)
Pty Ltd is operator of the Ravva field.
    Earlier this month Command said it was preparing to complete
the RC-1 development well in the Ravva Contract Area as an oil
producer. Command said drill stem tests flowed 35.8 degree API
oil at a maximum stabilised rate of 5,998 barrels per day, but
added the flow rate was limited by the testing equipment.
    India's Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd <ONGC.BO> has a
40 percent stake in the find, Videocon 25 percent, Command 22.5
percent and Marubeni Corp <8002.T> 12.5 percent through an
affiliate.
    The project is expected to be commissioned in late 1996 and
is projected to produce 139 million barrels of oil equivalent
over 14 years, the statement said.	N2:LOA

TOKYO, April 11 (Reuter) - A bill to revise Japan's Deposit
Insurance Corp (DIC) law includes provisions for the government
to guarantee debt incurred by the corporation, according to a
draft released by the Ministry of Finance (MOF) on Thursday.
    The DIC, which was set up by Japanese banks and the Bank of
Japan (BOJ), is a semi-public entity which insures deposits at
deposit-taking institutions. It is funded by a premium paid by
banks and is overseen by MOF.
    The bill, which is expected to be approved by the cabinet
and submitted to parliament on Friday, is one of three
financial bills whose submission to parliament was held up by a
month of political wrangling over the 1996/97 state budget.
    After the ruling coalition and the opposition agreed late
on Wednesday that the government may delay the use of public
money for a controversial scheme to help wind up the nations's
ailing mortgage firms, the budget was passed in the Lower House
of parliament on Thursday.
    The other bills relate to improving management of Japan's
financial institutions and dealing with bankrupt institutions.	N2:LOA

TOKYO, March 11 (Reuter) - Japanese banks plan to revamp
the current settlement system for foreign exchange transactions
to avoid chances of secondary failure should a bank fail with
unsettled foreign exchange debt exposure to other banks, an
official of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan
said on Monday.
    The association plans to introduce the new settlement
scheme, involving a collateral system against unsettled claims,
in the first half of fiscal 1997/98 starting April 1997, the
official said.
    The association represents all types of commercial banks.
    The new system requires banks to set aside collateral in
cash or government bonds to hedge against risks of not being
able to recover claims in the event of a bank failure, the
official said.
    It also proposes the establishment of daily credit lines
for clients with foreign exchange debt exposure to banks.
    Under the planned changes, the current forex settlement
time of 3 p.m. (0600 GMT) would be expanded to any time between
9 a.m. (2400 GMT) and 5 p.m. (0800 GMT).

SHANGHAI, Aug 23 (Reuter) - China has started discussing with the
governments of Japan and France loans to finance Shanghai's new international
airport, the head of the airport construction department said on Friday.
    The first phase of the airport will cost 12 billion yuan and construction is
due to begin in September, Wu Xiangmin told reporters.
    About a third of this cost will be foreign government loans, mostly to buy
foreign equipment and materials which China cannot produce, he said.
    The main provider will probably be the Japanese government whose loans are
not tied to purchases of Japanese goods, unlike those of other governments that
are tied to purchases of goods from their own countries, he said.
    The rest of the funding will come as loans from China's State Development
Bank and the department's own three billion yuan in capital, he said.
    The first phase, with one runway, is due to start operation at the end of
1999 and be completed in 2005, with an annual capacity of 20 million passengers
and 750,000 tonnes of cargo, he said.
    The final planned airport envisages four runways and an annual handling
capacity of 70 million passengers and five million tonnes of cargo, he said.
    But his department has no timetable or cost estimates for this final plan,
which will depend on the growth of Shanghai's aviation sector.
    In the 1986-90 period, Shanghai's passenger growth at its existing Hongqiao
airport grew an annual 23 percent, reaching 11 million in 1995 and an estimated
13 million in 1996, he said.
   Initial estimates show Shanghai's passenger volume in 2000 at 20 million,
while Hongqiao's capacity is only 9.6 million, so there is an urgent need for a
new airport, he said.
    Currently, Shanghai ranks top among Chinese airports for cargo and third,
after Beijing and Guangzhou, for freight, he added.	N2:LOA

WARSAW, Aug 22 (Reuter) - Poland's Banking Guarantee Fund
(BFG) agreed to lend Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) 8.6
million zlotys to help it take over a branch of the failed
Bydgoski Bank Budownictwa (BBB), WBK said in a statement.
    WBK said that under an agreement with BFG, the fund would
lend it the sum for 10 years at a preferential rate equal to
one-third of the central bank's discount rate, now at 22
percent.
    Newspapers have earlier reported that WBK wanted to
integrate the Bydgoszcz branch of construction bank BBB, which
lost financial liquidity in 1995, into its own network.

obligations to its clients while making sure its shareholders
would not be hurt by such an operation.
    The guarantee fund was launched last year with government
and central bank start-up capital and is supported by banks'
contributions.
    It is designed to guarantee individuals' deposits and
offer soft loans and other help to institutions willing to
bail-out troubled banks.
    WBK is 36 percent owned by Allied Irish Bank Plc <ALBK.I>.

ROME, March 15 (Reuter) - Bad loans in the Italian banking
system jumped 20.88 percent year-on-year in December to a new
record 110.13 trillion lire, up from November's rise of 19.18
percent, the Italian Banking Association (ABO) said.
    The ratio of bad loans to deposits hit 10.26 percent in the
month, up from 10.11 percent in November, ABI said in its latest
monthly report. The ratio was 8.76 percent in December 1994.
    According to the latest data available, bad loans at banks
holding short-term deposits rose 17.51 percent in November,
below the 19.46 percent seen in October. The bad loans/deposits
ratio was 10.70 percent against 10.74 percent in October.
    At banks with medium-to-long term deposits, the growth in
bad loans slowed to 28.80 percent year-on-year in November from
32.76 percent in October.
    But the bad loans/deposits ratio rose to 7.85 percent from
7.79 percent, ABI said.

said, compared with a 2.05 percent rise in November.

HONG KONG, March 11 (Reuter) - Asian debt markets were busy
on Monday, with several new issues launching.
    Banque Indosuez Hong Kong branch swooped in late with a HK$1
billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
    The 39-month issue pays a coupon of 45 basis points over the
Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate. Fees are 16.25 basis points
for top-tier managers for an all-in return of roughly 50 basis
points.
    Application has been made to the Hong Kong Monetary
Authority to accept the issue as eligible for its Liquidity
Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
    Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks
because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase
agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
    Arrangers are HSBC Markets, which will handle books, and
Chemical Securities Asia, Sakura Finance, Societe Generale Asia,
UBS Hong Kong and Westpac Hong Kong.
    Also from Hong Kong, Chevalier units began general
syndication of a HK$5.45 billion loan to finance commercial and
residential developments in the territory.
    Arrangers of the Chevalier deal are Banque Nationale de
Paris, Credit Lyonnais Hong Kong branch, HSBC Capital, Hang Seng
Finance, Industrial Bank of Japan Hong Kong branch, Sanwa Bank
Hong Kong branch and Sumitomo Bank Hong Kong branch.
    Details of the Chevalier deal have been floating around the
market for some time.
    Another big Hong Kong dollar loan, a HK$5.75 billion deal
for consortium Harvest Sun, closed today. Proceeds of that one
will be used to fund development of a Mass Transit Railway site
associated with Hong Kong's new airport.
    The latest South Korean bank deal was out, with Cho Hung
Bank launching its US$120 million floating rate note.
    The three-year deal pays a coupon of 30 basis points.
    Although the deal was launched loan-style and participation
levels are spelled out, fees are an identical 15 basis points
regardless of commitment.

tighter than the 36 basis points given on similarly A3-rated
Hanil Bank's US$200 million three-year note issue launched last
Wednesday.

Exchange Bank's US$200 million three-year note issue, which paid
36.7 basis points all-in to the syndicate.

the market this year.

rocketed in 1994 and 1995, it said.

113.6 billion yuan, up 10.6 percent, and government expenditure
would be 110 billion yuan, it said.	N2:LOA

TOKYO, March 15 (Reuter) - Total debt of bankrupt Japanese
companies in February surged 62.6 percent from a year earlier
to 901.64 billion yen, a private research company said on
Friday.
    The debt was driven up in February mainly by failures of
two non-bank financial institutions which had debts of more
than 100 billion yen, Tokyo Commerce and Industry Research Co
(TSR) said.
    Despite the huge rise in debt, the number of bankruptcies
in February edged down 0.5 percent from a year earlier to
1,164, the first decline in seven months.
    But the TSR said the level was still comparatively high and
that more problems could emerge. More and more small and
medium-sized firms are facing sales difficulties and large
debts with the delay in Japan's economic rebound, it said.
    Bankruptcies are defined as insolvent companies in the
process of liquidation or reorganisation under court protection
from creditors.
    Among the big business failures in February were non-bank
financial institutions Equion Co Ltd, which had debts of 310.6
billion yen, and Aichi Corp, which had debts of 182.0 billion
yen.	N2:LOA

WASHINGTON, March 20 (Reuter) - U.S. legislators writing the
final version of the 1996 farm bill voted on Wednesday to make
peanut growers ineligible for federal supports if they
repeatedly refuse to sell their crops.
    House and Senate negotiators decided on a voice vote to make
growers ineligible for supports if they reject, for two
consecutive years, offers from processors to buy the peanuts at
prices at least as high as the loan rate.
    The provision would replace a House proposal for a five
percent penalty on loans if a grower decided to take the
price-support loan instead of the same sales price.
    House Democrats said the five percent penalty was punitive
and would drive down peanut prices. Supporters said it would
prevent growers from driving up the cost of a programme that was
being designed to operate at no net cost to taxpayers.
    Wording to set the support for peanuts grown under quotas at
$610 per short ton, a 10 percent cut from the $678 now
available, was left unchanged.
    The House-Senate compromise also reduced the chance to sell,
lease or transfer quota rights across county lines but staying
within the home state. Originally, the farm bill would have
allowed unlimited movement of quotas.
    Under the compromise, 40 percent of quotas can be
transferred under a formula allowing 15 percent in 1996, 10
percent in 1997 and five percent in each of the next three
years.
    Last month, the House refused by a three-vote margin to
phase out the peanut support programme.
    House Agriculture chairman Pat Roberts cited this narrow
vote in warning negotiators that they would be courting disaster
if they tried to eliminate the modest reforms in the farm bill.	N2:LOA

HONG KONG, Sept 3 (Reuter) - Asian debt markets were busy on
Tuesday, as a number of new launches and debt-related news
enlivened the market.
    A U.S. missile attack on Iraq in retaliation for that
country's attacks on Kurds in northern Irag had no effect on
secondary market trading in debt issues, traders said.
    Among new issues, Guoco Group unit Fresco Resources launched
a US$180 million floating rate note issue.
    The five-year deal pays a coupon 80 basis over the six-month
London Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return is
95 basis points to top-tier managers.
    Arrangers are Fuji International Finance, Banque Nationale
de Paris, Bayerische Landesbank, BZW Asia, JP Morgan Securities
and Sumitomo Finance Asia.
    Another Hong Kong company, Guangdong Investment, launched a
US$80 million floating rate note issue via Schroders Asia.
    The deal has a five-year maturity but can be put or called
on the third and fourth anniversaries. It pays a margin of 140
basis points over LIBOR and an all-in of 170 basis points.
    Schroders has been mandated along with Tokai Asia to arrange
a HK$500 million floating rate certificate of deposit for Asia
Commercial Bank.
    Beijing-based China International Trust and Investment Corp
(CITIC) today launched three tranches of Samurai bonds worth a
total of 40 billion yen via lead managers Nikko Securities and
Nomura Securities.
    Another ITIC, Guangdong ITIC, closed a US$70 million FRN.
    South Korean banks Kwangju and Kyongnam each have mandated
four banks to arrange US$50 million FRN issues. Both will pay
around 50 basis points over LIBOR for three-year paper.
    South Korea's Newmax International (HK) is in the market
with a US$50 million FRN, bankers said.
    Bankers also said that Cho Hung Bank is taking bids on
three-year paper. Cho Hung is hoping to pay LIBOR plus 30 basis
points, which would a few basis points tigher than its last
deal, the bankers said.
    Hyundai International Merchant Bank reportedly still is
taking bids on its US$100 million FRCD. Bankers said the deal,
which is for five years with a three-year put, is being
discusssed at about 65 basis points over LIBOR.
    South Korea today announced more financial liberalization
measures, including a proposal to allow more overseas borrowings
by Korean companies in order to ease domestic interest rates.
    Korean firms now face few restrictions if money borrowed
offshore is used for offshore projects, but offshore funding
raised for domestic use is tightly controlled, bankers noted.
    In other debt news, Moody's Investors Service downgraded
Thailand's short term debt ratings.
    The ratings cut was another blow to Thailand's financial
markets, which have suffered as the country grapples with
political and economic problems.
    Secondary debt market traders in Hong Kong said Thai
paper--particularly that of second-tier banks--has traded poorly
recently, partly because of the country's woes but also because
the deals were priced too tightly at the start.
    Philippine bank paper also is turning slightly soggy, not
because bankers are bearish on the Philippines, but because
supply has increased sharply this year.
    Bankers said Security Bank is considering a new issue,
adding its name to Rizal Commercial Bank and Allied Bank, which
are taking bids now. PCIBank already is fixed for a five-year
fixed-rate bond, which it will launch via Merrill Lynch.

HANOI, Sept 7 (Reuter) - A World Bank plan to upgrade
Hanoi's road network and restore order to its treacherous
streets has been submitted to the government, the official
Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said on Saturday.
    VNA said most of the $24.8 million earmarked for the
four-year project would be spent on improving four arterial
roads, the shabby but bustling old quarter and the elegant
northwestern district built by Vietnam's former French colonial
masters.
    Under the plan, traffic control at 212 of the capital's road
intersections would be improved and 43.4 km (27.1 miles) of road
would be repaired.
    Some $2.8 million of the funding would help provide traffic
police with modern equipment and improve the efficiency of the
Urban Transport Control department.
    More than 2,500 people were killed in road accidents in
Vietnam in the first six months of this year -- this in a
country where the majority still ride bicycles.
    Swarms of motorbikes and, increasingly, cars have arrived on
the nation's chaotic and often potholed streets since economic
and social reforms were launched in the late 1980s.
    Small motorbikes are the most popular form of transport in
the cities, but traffic rules are lax and crash helmets are
considered expensive and unfashionable.
    VNA did not say whether the government would approve the
project. However, aid projects are rarely turned down.	N2:LOA

LONDON, September 5 (LPC) - The State of Israel has asked
banks to prepare bids for a new syndicated loan of at least $200
million, according to bank sources.
   A number of bidding groups are coalescing, bankers say,
including British, American, German, Swiss and Israeli banks.
   Banks are structuring loans of between $200 million and $250
million with final maturities of between five and seven years.
Pricing on the credit should be about 30 bps over LIBOR, bankers
say, with some more agressive bids with a margin closer to 25
bps.
   In September 1995 Israel took a $100 million credit arranged
by Bank Leumi, BZW and Chemical Bank. That deal had a four-year
element priced 45 bps over LIBOR and a five-year element with a
margin of 50 bps.
   Though the likely sharp drop in pricing may partly be
explained by an oversupply of funds in the loan market, Isreal's
credit profile has also improved.
   In December 1995 Standard & Poor's raised the State of
Israel's long-term foreign currency debt rating to A minus, from
BBB plus, citing the government's commitment to reducing its
debt burden.
   Israel also plans a $750 million note programme and a $200
million Eurobond in the fourth quarter, both to be led by
Merrill Lynch.

sources said.

the special accounts.

NEW YORK, September 5 (LPC) - Dominicks Supermarkets
mandated Bankers Trust New York Corp <BT.N> and Chase
Manhattan Corp <CMB.N> for a $325 million bank loan, banking
sources said.
    The loan will replace higher-priced bank debt the company
undertook during its leveraged buyout in March 1995, they
said.
    The 6.5-year credit is will be split between a $100
million amortizing term loan and a $225 million revolving
credit, each priced at 150 basis points over the London
Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR), according to a Securities and
Exchange Commission filing.
    The March 1995 deal was split between a $100 million
revolver and about $280 million of loans targeted at
institutional investors. The existing loans bear interest at
275 to 400 basis points over LIBOR, bankers said.
    The institutional loans are sold to non-bank investors,
such as prime rate funds and insurance companies.
    The move by Dominicks to replace institutional bank loans
with lower-priced credits is part of an overall trend in a
market that has seen pricing drop consistently across the
credit spectrum, according to several lenders.
    Also, the deal, which comes in conjunction with an initial
public offering, is another example of a leveraged buyout
entity returning to the public market in a short time period,
lenders said. Many companies now complete that process in
fewer than 18 months, much sooner than had been seen in the
past, according to lenders.
    Dominicks, based in Northlake, Illinois, was acquired by
Yucaipa Cos in the 1995 LBO.

accounting standards, it had net earnings of 74.08 million yuan

SHANGHAI, March 28 (Reuter) - A Shanghai newspaper on
Thursday called for reforms to make it easier for the city's
residents to obtain mortgages to buy thousands of empty
apartments.
    Since 1991, the Shanghai branch of the China Construction
Bank has given loans totalling 18.837 billion yuan for
construction of apartments for sale, but only 790 million yuan
to people for mortgages to buy them, the Business News said.
    The result is that thousands of apartments lie empty for
want of buyers, it said. Shanghai residents want to buy them but
cannot afford to.
    As of the end of 1995, Shanghai residents had more than 200
billion yuan of personal assets, of which 139 billion was in
bank deposits, it said.
    There are several reasons why banks have little interest in
giving mortgages -- the procedures are complicated and, in the
absence of a national law, banks have no legal guarantee they
can reclaim the property in the event of a default, it said.
    Another is that the interest banks can charge on home
mortgages is lower than what they pay out on deposits. Repayment
periods are too short and rates too expensive for most citizens,
it added.	N2:LOA

TOKYO, March 29 (Reuter) - Japan's stopgap budget worth
11.62 trillion yen for the first 50 days of the forthcoming
fiscal year became law on Friday after being approved by the
full Upper House.

period from April 1, 1996, until May 20. The measure was needed

party Shinshinto had blocked passage of the full budget.
    The party was protesting against a government plan to
earmark public money in the budget to help wind up ailing
mortgage firms.

public works projects to support the nation's fragile economy.
    That was equivalent to 31.1 percent of the planned public
works spending in the budget for the full year.
    The stopgap budget projects revenues of 3.76 trillion yen
from taxes, public bonds and other income. The remaining 7.86
trillion yen will be supplied by cash management bills which
will be issued as needed, Finance Ministry officials said.	N2:LOA

SYDNEY, March 31 (Reuter) - Home loan affordability
continued to rise in Australia in the December quarter,
according to a quarterly survey released on Sunday.
    An indicator compiled by the Real Estate Institute of
Australia and MGICA Ltd showed home loan affordability rose 3.3
percent nationally. The indicator measures median family income
against average new loan repayments.
    During the quarter the size of the averge new loan decreased
0.8 percent, average monthly loan replayments were down 1.6
percent and median weekly family income increased 1.6 percent.
    Interest rates offered by both banks and building societies
were lower than in the September quarter, helped by strong
competition in the mortgage market.
    Nationally, average monthly loan repayments fell to A$973 in
the December quarter from A$989 in the September quarter.
    However, average monthly payments in New South Wales rose to
A$1,173 from A$1,112, Western Australia rose to A$918 from
A$904, the Australian Capital Territory rose to A$970 from A$950
and Tasmania rose to A$739 from A$708.
    In Victoria, average payments fell to A$866 from A$890,
Queensland fell to A$939 from A$982 and South Australia fell to
A$792 from A$816. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800	N2:LOA

MOSCOW, March 29 (Reuter) - Norsi, one of Russia's biggest
oil refineries, has agreed with Moscow Narodny bank to borrow
$250 million from foreign investors to build a new refining
complex, Interfax news agency said on Friday.
    It quoted company officials as saying Narodny was in
negotiations with the World Bank, the European Bank for
Reconstruction and Development and several other international
financial institutions about a loan for Norsi.
    The project involves building a new high-yield refining
complex to process four million tonnes of oil a year (equivalent
to around 80,000 barrels per day) with both Russian and foreign
equipment. Norsi's current throughput is 1.3 million tonnes of
crude a month (about 312,000 bpd).
    It refined 12.5 million tonnes (around 250,000 bpd) last
year, 21.2 percent below 1994's levels. Crude purchases will
rise by 300,000 tonnes a month (some 72,000 bpd) from April,
Interfax said.
    The complex would allow Norsi to boost light product yield
from crude gradually to 86 percent from 54-58 percent at the
moment, cutting costs by 25-30 percent.
    Gasoline and diesel fuel output will rise 20 percent from
two million tonnes and four million tonnes a year respectively
at the moment, production director Vladimir Fokin said.
    Norsi also plans to close an ethylene petrochemical comlex
this month for upgrading, to cost $60 million, in order to boost
production to 350,000 tonnes a year from 130,000 tonnes at the
moment.
    Another petrochemical complex, to make 80,000 tonnes of
polyethylene a year, will be built by BSI of the United States.

BEIJING, March 30 (Reuter) - China will from April 1 require
enterprises that want to borrow money from financial
institutions to apply for a loan certificate from the central
bank, the official Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.
    The system was aimed at tightening control of bank loans to
stop enterprises being able to borrow large amounts for long
periods without revealing their financial situation, it said.
    The national certification system, to be launched on April 1
in 200 cities, would help the central People's Bank of China to
keep abreast of debt among enterprises, it said.
    Some badly-managed enterprises had opened accounts at a
number of banks and had been able to borrow separately from each
because of loose controls, it said.
    All enterprises that wanted to borrow money or that had ever
borrowed from financial institutions were required to apply for
the certificate from the central bank.
    The certificate would include details of the enterprises
credit situation, it said.
    The China Securities newspaper said in January each
enterprise would be issued one loan certificate. Only the
central bank and its branches could issue the certificates,
which would be used when applying for loans, it said.	N2:LOA

By George Nishiyama
    TOKYO, March 29 (Reuter) - The government on Friday gave
companies a long-awaited green light to issue asset-backed
securities inside Japan, but they are unlikely to rush to issue
such securities, company officials and brokers said.
    With no strong demand for funds now and not much scope for
a secondary market for investors, growth of a market in such
securities would be inhibited, they said.
    In an asset-backed securities scheme, a firm transfers
assets to a company set up specifically for that purpose. The
subsidiary then issues securities, usually as bonds or
commercial paper, with the assets as backing.
    Currently, the Ministry of Finance allows Japanese firms to
issue such securities only in overseas markets.
    But as part of a package of deregulatory steps announced on
Friday, Tokyo said it would allow leasing and credit firms to
issue asset-backed securities domestically from April 1.
    Such securities are given credit ratings based on the
quality of the asset, not the issuer's creditworthiness.	N2:LOA

MOSCOW, Sept 26 (Reuter) - Inkombank plans to issue level-one American
Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in New York by the end of this year, an Inkombank
official said on Thursday.

SHANGHAI, Sept 26 (Reuter) - China on Thursday issued new
rules widening the range of items that can be used by both local
and foreign-related firms as collateral to guarantee loans.
    The new rules, published in the Finance Times, allow
companies to use bank guarantees, fixed assets and real estate
mortgages as collateral. The previous rules did not cover
foreign-invested firms and only allowed the use of bank
guarantees.
    The new rules, issued by the People's Bank of China, said
both local currency and foreign exchange could now be used for
collateral.
    The Finance Times quoted a spokesman for the central bank as
saying that new rules were promulgated because the old ones were
now out-of-date given the pace of financial reform.
    The amount used as collateral by a non-financial body must
not exceed 50 percent of its net assets and the firm's annual
foreign exchange income, the rules said.
    The former rules said the amount must not exceed the foreign
exchange held by a firm.	N2:LOA

slow week slowly on Friday.
    Indonesia's Bank Niaga set a US$40 million floating rate
certificate of deposit issue. The issue has a final maturity of

    The deal pays a margin of 80 basis points over the Singapore
Interbank Offered Rate. Participating banks receive a fee of six
basis points for underwriting and a management fee of 30 basis
points on their final allotment.

Hanil Bank, WestLB and Bayerische Vereinsbank.
    The issue is expected to have a coupon of LIBOR plus 55
basis points and an all-in return of 68-70 basis points.
    Asian Banking Corp is the latest in a long line of Korean
banks to take their tale to Europe. The top tier banks have had
little trouble selling their story outside Asia, but merchant
banks such as Asian Banking Corp are finding it more difficult,
bankers said.
    Allied Banking Corp of the Philippines has mandated Standard
Chartered Investment Banking to arrange a US$50 million FRCD.
    The three-year deal pays a coupon of 85 basis points over
LIBOR and an all-in return of 92 basis points.

TAIPEI, Sept 30 (Reuter) - Loans extended by Taiwan banks to
construction firms fell 18.54 percent to T$391.62 billion in
August from August 1995, marking the 16th consecutive month of
negative growth, the central bank said on Monday.
    August's decline followed a 17.42 percent fall in July.
    In the wider picture, loans extended by Taiwan banks to all
private businesses fell 4.95 percent to T$2.894 trillion in
August from a year earlier, the central bank announced.
    August's overall decline was the fifth monthly decline in 10
years, and all of those were in 1996, the statement said.
    Lending fell 0.35 percent in January, 0.80 percent in May,
1.1 percent in June and 2.21 percent in July, it said.
    The central bank official attributed the flat-to-negative
recent growth to an overall slowing in the economy.
    Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to
companies in the construction sector, which has seen deep
recession since the local real estate market peaked in 1989.
    In late August, the central bank scrapped all of the
selective credit controls on land to boost the real estate
market and the economy, and analysts had expected the move to
gradually show effect.

By Trevor Datson
    STOCKHOLM, Sept 30 (Reuter) - Sweden's largest dedicated
property company made its debut on the Stockholm bourse on
Monday, marking an end to the big four banks' unwilling tenure
as the country's largest real estate owners.
    With property holdings valued at around 25 billion crowns
($3.8 billion), Diligentia becomes easily the largest real
estate company in Sweden, outgunning building and property
combines Skanska<SKAb.ST> and NCC<NCCb.ST>.
    Diligentia is the latest property group to be spun off by
Sweden's major banks in a move which they hope will draw a line
under a financial crash in the early 1990s.
    Shareholders in Wallenberg group banking arm S-E-Banken
<SEBa.ST> received an extra payout of one share in Diligentia
for every 10 shares held in the bank.
    As one property company after the other failed in the wake
of a collapse in real estate values, banks were saddled with
huge stocks of buildings -- taken over as collateral on bad
loans -- which they were neither ready nor willing to manage.
    Only state-controlled Nordbanken <NORB.ST> was spared the
worst of the crisis as its bad loans and unwanted property were
hived off into companies with solid-sounding names like Securum,
Retrieva and Castellum.
    But S-E-Banken, Handelsbanken <SHBa.ST> and Swedbank
<SPARa.ST> were all left with major real estate holdings, which,
under bank legislation, they were not allowed to own.
    Recognising the anomalous situation, legislators changed tax
rules last autumn to allow banks -- and only banks -- to pay out
shares in their property companies to shareholders without
attracting a swingeing tax bill.
    Swedbank's Tornet <TORN.ST> and Handelsbanken's Nackebro
<NBRO.ST> were disposed of in this way in May and June,
respectively, and both have outstripped market expectations.
    Diligentia was given a hesitant welcome by Swedish investors
on Monday. Its shares opened at 82 crowns but a combination of a
weak bourse and a recoil in property shares after a protracted
rally sent it back to 79 crowns as investors cashed in on their
windfall.
    Even so, Diligentia is undervalued, analysts say. With an
estimated value of 25 billion crowns, the portfolio should be
worth something like 475 crowns per share.
    A depressed market and the the sector's dubious history rule
out a share price anywhere near these levels but an investment
in Diligentia still has plenty of potential if the company's
listed counterparts are anything to go by, analysts say.
    The Tornet share has appreciated by 28 percent since its May
7 launch date and Nackebro has gained 20 percent since June 28,
both easily outstripping the rest of the market.
    Sweden's fifth-largest bank, Foreningsbanken<FORBa.ST>, has
yet to announce a timetable for the disposal of its real estate
unit Mandamus but has said it plans to sell properties at home
and abroad to a value of 3.5 billion crowns by the end of 1998.	N2:LOA

until March 14, 1997 unless an agreement is reached or creditors
representing 66 percent of the debt decide to call the debt in.
@

TOKYO, Feb 1 (Reuter) - The finance and health ministries
have agreed in principle to ease regulations on fund management
by Japan's Public Welfare Fund, which currently manages about
38 trillion yen, government officials said.
    Under current regulations, the fund must entrust two-thirds
or more of the money to life insurance firms and trust banks,
and the rest to investment advisory firms.
    The new rules will allow the fund to entrust up to 50
percent of the money to investment advisers from April, they
said. The limit will be completely lifted in March 1999, they
said.
     Current rules also require fund managers to put at least
50 percent of the fund's money in safe assets of which the
principal is guaranteed, 30 percent or less in domestic stocks
and foreign currency assets, and 20 percent or less in real
estate.

said.	N2:LOA

HONG KONG, April 2 (Reuter) - Asian debt markets were marked
by news of lots of new loans on Tuesday.
    The largest was a US$150 million term loan for Taiwan chip
manufacturer Macronix International.
    The seven-year amortizing loan has an average life of 4.5
years. It pays a margin of 65 basis points over the London
Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of about
72 basis points to top tier managers.
    ABN AMRO Syndications Asia is the arranger.
    Proceeds of the loan will be used to fund an eight-inch
wafer fabrication plant.
    ABN AMRO also is arranging a number of loans for Indian
companies.
    It launched a US$45 million seven-year bullet loan for Steel
Authority of India last Friday. The deal pays a margin of 75
basis points over LIBOR, and includes a covenant obliging the
government of India to continue to hold at least 51 percent of
the borrower, which now is largely state owned.
    Other arrangers are Chase Asia, Sakura Finance Asia, Societe
General Asia and State Bank of India.
    ABN AMRO also recently completed a US$13 million club loan
for Indian Hotels with Union Bank of Switerzland and Credit
Lyonnais joining.
    Next week, ABN AMRO, Citibank International and Societe
Generale Asia plan to launch a US$75 million loan for Indian
Petrochemical Corp.
    Indonesian corporates also were locking in loans. Putra
Surya Perkasa unit Putra Surya Multifinance set a US$25 million
loan to be used to fund lease operations.
    The three-year bullet loan pays a margin of 200 basis points
over the Singapore Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an
all-in of 240 basis points to the top tier.
    A two-tranche US$33 million loan for fluorescent tube and
bulb maker PT Sinar Angkasa Rungkut is in syndication, said
arranger HSBC Investment Bank Singapore.
    The US$29 million term loan facility has a maturity of five
years and pays 200 basis points over SIBOR. The US$4 million
revolving credit facility has a maturity of 2.5 years and pays a
margin of 175 basis points over SIBOR.
    There is a commitment fee of 25 basis points. Other fees
were not disclosed.
    The sole capital markets issue revealed on Tuesday was a
US$50 million floating rate note issue for Guangdong
International Trust and Investment Corp (Hong Kong).
    The three-year notes, which will be privately placed, pay a
margin of 100 basis points over LIBOR, bankers said.
    Arrangers are Korea Long Term Credit Bank, Peregrine Fixed
Income and SEOULBANK, they said.
    GITIC usually raises funds via syndicated loans, but it has
issued floating rate notes in the past.
    As a private placement, the deal was structured to meet the
demand of investors, which are expected to be banks, non-bank
financial institutions and leasing companies.

TAIPEI, April 1 (Reuter) - Loans extended by Taiwanese banks
to construction firms fell 14.91 percent to T$436.4 billion in
February from a year earlier, marking the 10th straight month of
declines, the central bank said on Monday.

January, it said in a statement.

since December 1985's 1.25 percent fall, it said.

subsequent small growth to a slowing economy.

to construction firms due to the flagging local real estate
market after its peak in 1989.

Corp (DIC) was unable to protect them sufficiently in the event
of future credit union collapses.

mortgages it will buy from them, the paper said.

applicant, the price of the home and amount of down payment,

SEOUL, April 26 (Reuter) - South Korea plans to limit its
restrictions on credit to the nation's top 10 business
conglomerates instead of the current 30 biggest conglomerates, a
Finance and Economy Ministry spokesman said on Friday.
    The move, part of the government's efforts to streamline
bureaucracy, was reported to President Kim Young-sam by Finance
and Economy Minister Rha Woong-bae on Thursday, he said.
    He said regulations on credit control would be revised by
the Monetary Board led by central bank governor.
    Credit control has been a powerful policy tool in South
Korea where money is both tight and expensive. The government
has imposed a basket credit ceiling on 30 conglomerates, known
as chaebol, in order to prevent their excessive economic and
financial concentration.
    Under the current system, the basket credit ceiling for the
top five chaebol is 4.88 percent of total bank lending and for
the 30 chaebol 9.63 percent. Bank loans provided to the
conglomerates for designated core business lines are excluded in
calculating the ceiling. New ceilings are expected to be worked
out by the Monetary Board, the spokesman said.	N2:LOA

BOGOTA, Colombia, April 22 (Reuter) - Colombia's central bank
has decided to allow the country's banks to use foreign credit to
finance their loans in pesos, a central bank official said.
    The official told Reuters that banks and financial
corporations will be able to make loans in pesos equivalent to
a maximum of 10 percent of the equity they hold in foreign
currency like U.S. dollars.
    Before the central bank's decision, banks were only
allowed to use foreign credit to finance loans in foreign
currency. The central bank also reduced the maximum amount
banks must hold in their foreign currency positions to 20
percent from 30 percent of their equity, the official said.

outlining its latest measures, a bulletin released by the
National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF)
explained them in detail.

explanation of the measures adopted by the central bank's
board of directors last Friday.
    The bulletin said the central bank had expanded its
definition of equity to incorporate foreign currency accounts
held by banks that had been excluded when they calculated the
value of their equity.

trillion yen as of the end of September.

institutions which take deposits and lend mainly to members.
Most borrowers are small and medium-sized businesses.	N2:LOA

Industrial Bank of Japan to support the purchase of generating
plants from National Power plc <NPR.L> and PowerGen plc <PWG.L>,

guaranteed by Eastern owner Hanson Plc <HNSN.L>.

with Industrial Bank of Japan but would not elaborate.

credit, Eastern and Industrial Bank of Japan are working towards
a successor deal that would have limited recourse to Eastern,
sources said.  A limited recourse deal would likely be larger.

electricity generation. Hanson announced on Monday that Eastern

Barking plants.

million stg over the next 10 years.
    Additional payments linked to output could bring the
purchase price to 1.7 billion stg, according to National Power.

    IBJ is understood to have two additional banks lined up to
join the deal, though no official comment has been made. The
credit should have a final maturity of seven to 10 years,

except agricultural financial institutions, industry sources

limelight in the Asian debt market on Tuesday by launching a
three-year HK$1.5 billion issue for Hongkong and Shanghai
Banking Corp.
    The floating rate certificate of deposit issue, the bank's
first public CD issue this year, was launched at par to float at
30 basis points over the one-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered
Rate.
    With fees, the all-in return to top-tier managers is 35
basis points. The next two levels receive 34 and 32 points
respectively.
    The response deadline is May 15 and tentative deposit date
is May 24.
    The issue is part of the bank's existing CD programme, which
was recently raised to HK$15 billion from the HK$8.0 billion
first announced in late 1994, said HSBC Markets' head of new
issues Mark Bucknall.
    Excluding today's issue, roughly HK$6.0 billion of the
programme had been issued to the public or to private investors
in 32 issues, with maturities ranging from one to six years.
    Bucknall said the programe was in response to investor
demand.
    Application has been made to the Hong Kong Monetary
Authority to accept the certificates as eligible for the HKMA's
liquidity adjustment facility (LAF), or discount window, HSBC
Markets said.
    Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks
because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase
agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
    Also on Tuesday, Bank of America announced it had arranged
two commercial paper programmes, one of US$50 million for China
International Marine Continers (CIMC) and one of US$75 million
for National Bank of Pakistan.

U.S. commercial paper market.
    The National Bank of Pakistan programme, supported by a
letter of credit issued by Credit Suisse, was fully completed,
with nine international banks joining the syndication.

leaving US$20 million to be finished some time in July. Societe
Generale issued a letter of credit to support the CIMC issue.

Imperial Bank of Commerce, Credit Lyonnais and Sanwa Bank had
been named lead arrangers of a project finance facility designed
to raise US$615 million to fund telephone network expansion in
Indonesia.
    Bank of America is PT ARIA West's sole financial adviser on
the telecommunications project.
    In China, television picture tube maker Hua Fei Colour
Display Systems mandated CCIC Finance and ABN AMRO Syndication
Asia to arrange a US$265 million financing package.
    It comprises a US$65 million on-shore financing tranche A
and a US$200 million five-year term loan tranche B.
    Tranche A will be shared among the arranging banks with
tranche B to enter syndication in late June or early July, CCIC

PARIS, April 30 (Reuter) - French welfare fund CADES plans
to raise some 30 billion francs in domestic and Eurobond issues,
banking sources said on Tuesday.
    They said bankers held a meeting with French Treasury and
CADES (Caisse d'amortissement de la dette sociale) officials on
Monday who detailed CADES's plans for raising some 140 billion
francs by the end of June to pay back debts run up by the
welfare system.
    CADES planned to raise around 60 billion francs through bank
loans, mainly from French commercial banks.
    It would raise roughly 35 billion francs through issues of
commercial paper on the French domestic market and 35 billion
francs through issues of euro and U.S. commercial paper.
    Banking sources said the figures were meant to give only a
rough guideline, and should not be added together to show the
total amount CADES would raise between now and the end of June.
It has to raise 140 billion francs by end-June.
    They said CADES was likely to start issues of commercial
paper almost immediately while bond issues were not expected
before next week at the earliest.
    The French Treasury will hold its own sale of government
bonds this week with an auction on Thursday at which it has said
it plans to raise 16 to 18 billion francs.
    CADES plans to begin bond issues in French francs and ecus,
and while it does not rule out borrowing in foreign currencies,
most of its fixed-rate borrowing is likely to be in francs and
ecus, the sources said.
    CADES plans to be extremely cautious about taking on any
foreign exchange risk, the sources said.
    The government published a decree in the official journal
last Friday setting up CADES and named a board of directors
which includes two Treasury officials.
    Banking sources said the government was also looking at
changing rules which limit the amount securities funds (OPCVMs)
can invest in non-state-guaranteed bonds to enable them to buy a
large amount of CADES issues.
    CADES also emphasised the need for transparency in its
operations to encourage investors, the sources said.
    Treasury and French government officials were not available
for comment.

TOKYO, April 30 (Reuter) - Japanese banking sources said on
Tuesday they had not been approached by the ruling coalition
government to provide more money to help liquidate seven failed
mortgage firms.
    The daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported at the weekend that
the ruling coalition was considering pressing the banks to
double their planned contribution to a special fund for the
mortgage liquidation scheme to two trillion yen.
    Under the coalition plan, banks in turn would be allowed to
enjoy additional tax breaks on their bad loan write-offs, the
newspaper reported, without giving any sources.
    By boosting the banks' burden, the coalition wants to avert
criticism of its plan to spend 685 billion yen worth of
taxpayers' money on the scheme. The unpopular government plan
to use tax money has provoked fierce public criticism.
    The banking sources, however, said they had not discussed
such a plan with the Finance Ministry nor did they plan to in
the near future.
    The feasibility of such a plan was also in doubt, because
banks already losing money would enjoy less benefit from any
additional tax breaks on loan write-offs and were unlikely to
agree to any increase in their contribution, the sources said.	N2:LOA

TOKYO, April 30 (Reuter) - Japan's economic problems have
not stopped it boosting yen loans to Asia and the rest of the
world, official statistics released on Tuesday showed.
    Japan's yen loan commitments for the last fiscal year to
March 31 rose 23.9 percent on the previous year to 1.09
trillion yen ($10.4 billion), while actual payments totalled
654.5 billion yen ($6.29 billion), up 4.9 percent.
    The figures were contained in the annual report of The
Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund of Japan and showed Asia
remained the biggest beneficiary of yen loans at 881.8 billion
yen ($8.47 billion) on a commitment basis, up 11 percent on the
previous year.
    But Asia's overall share dropped to 80.7 percent from last
year's 90.0 percent as Japan raised its commitments to regions
such as Central and South America, the Middle East and Africa.
    Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan joined the list of recipients and
Tokyo resumed yen loans to Bulgaria for the first time in 20
years, the report said.
    Most of the loans were for the improvement of economic
infrastructure in developing countries, especially in the area
of transportation, the report said.
    Yen loans for environmental projects also rose to a record
218.6 billion yen, or 20.8 percent of the total committed.
    Japan reduced the average interest rate on yen loans
committed in fiscal 1995 by 0.21 percentage points to 2.53
percent for commitments made last year, in line with a cut in
Japanese interest rates, the report said.
    Yen loan recipients had repeatedly called upon Japan to
ease its repayment conditions in the light of the yen's surge
against the dollar last year, it said.
    The report said all yen loans committed in 1995/96 were
untied -- that is they do not require the recipient to give
contracts to Japanese companies for the projects financed.
    Yen loans have often been criticised as steps by Japan to
create new business for Japanese firms.
    The report said 27 percent of the total value of all
contracts on yen-loan financed projects went to Japanese firms
last year and 60 percent to firms from developing countries.
    Industrialised countries, excluding Japan, took 13 percent
of the total, it said.

MOSCOW, Sept 23 (Reuter) - Russia has no plans to amend the results of last
year's controversial auctions under the shares-for-loans scheme, a spokeswoman
for First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin said on Monday.
    Key players in the auctions, in which stakes in privatised companies were
tendered in exchange for loans to the government, agreed last Friday the results
would not be reviewed, spokeswoman Larisa Zelkova said.
    The round table talks included representatives of Russia's Security Council,
the Finance Ministry, the State Duma lower house of parliament, the
parliamentary audit chamber, three banks -- Menatep, Rossiisky Kredit and
Alfa-Bank and oil firms Sidanko and Yukos.
    The auctions, which were designed to plug holes in the 1995 budget late in
the year, were highly contentious. Winners were often closely associated with
the auction organisers and the winning bids were frequently close to the
starting price.
    Under the original terms of the auctions, winners had to hang on to their
shares until September 1 and could then sell them, keeping 30 percent of the
proceeds and paying 70 percent into the budget.
    However, Security Council Secretary Alexander Lebed wrote to President Boris
Yeltsin asking for the period in which winners had to hold the shares to be
extended until March 1, 1997.
    In response, Yeltsin told Lebed and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to
resolve the issue and come up with proposals by October 1, a government source
said.
    Lebed had said the shares had been sold at far below their real value.
    Privatisation Minister Alfred Kokh, speaking before his appointment, said on
September 4 he had no plans to extend the period in which auction winners had to
hold the shares.
    The scheme brought in some 4.7 trillion roubles last year.
    Officials have said the era of mass privatisation is over and that the
government will concentrate on fewer projects to raise 12 some trillion roubles
this year.
    Russia plans to hold an investment tender, open to foreign investors, for 15
percent of oil company Sibneft on October 25. The minimum price for the shares
is 65.04 billion roubles and the minimum investment is $33.56 million, according
to the Federal Property Fund's Reforma bulletin.
    ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK) and Stolichny Bank Sberezhenii
won the right to manage a 51 percent stake in Sibneft in a shares-for-loans
auction late last year.	N2:LOA

HONG KONG, Sept 20 (Reuter) - Eurofima launched and closed a
Hong Kong dollar bond, while Nichimen HK brought a leveraged yen
floating rate note to Asian debt markets Friday.
    Eurofima, the European Company for Financing of Railroad
Stock, launched a six-year HK$400 million bond. The bond, which
pays a 7.72 percent coupon semi-annually, was priced at 100.25
to yield 108 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries or 35
basis points over Hong Kong's Exchange Fund Notes.
    A syndicate manager at arranger Societe Generale said the
high coupon appealed to investors. He said the timing of the
issue was based on a view that a tightening by the U.S. Federal
Reserve at next week's policymaking meeting could spur some
profit-taking in longer-dated U.S. paper, depressing yields.
    Lower yields on U.S. paper generally translate into lower
yields on Hong Kong paper and that means less investor demand
for Hong Kong denominated paper.
    Japanese trading company Nichimen launched through its Hong
Kong branch a 1.0 billion yen leveraged FRN.
    The way the deal is designed, the coupon increases along
with the yen LIBOR rate up to a certain point and then goes to
zero. It is meant to appeal to investors that expect yen
interest rates to rise but not substantially.
    Japanese institutional investors are the target.
    Arranger Union Bank of Switzerland said today that APP
Global Finance's five-year US$500 million floating rate note
issue has been oversubscribed by 20-25 percent in syndication.
    The borrower has not yet decided whether it will increase
the FRN or scale back allotments, UBS said. Allocations are
expected to be made on Monday.
    Most of the paper was taken by Asian accounts.
    The issue size, at US$500 million, is very large for an
Asian-targetted deal. Most transactions of that size for Asian
borrowers are sold into the U.S. Yankee market, partially on the
view that Asian accounts cannot absorb large amounts of paper.
    Proceeds of the FRN ultimately will be used by Asia Pulp and
Paper.
    In other debt news, Philippines Finance Secretary Roberto de
Ocampo said the Philippines will work to exempt from a 20
percent withholding tax the soon-to-be-issued uncollateralised
bonds offered in exchange for Brady bonds.
    Today marks the deadline to submit offers for the exchange.
    On Tuesday, arranger J.P. Morgan announced an amendment to
the offering that will allow investors making offers for one of
the new bonds to switch into the other if their first choice
does not attract enough demand to push it over the US$200
million chosen as the minimum amount that will be accepted.
    For example, an investor wishing to subscribe to the fixed
rate bond has the choice of taking the floating rate note issue
if the bond is undersubscribed.
    The minimum amounts have been set to assure liquidity in the
issues. Acceptance offers will be announced next week.

MEXICO CITY, Sept 21 (Reuter) - Mexico's Finance Ministry
said Saturday that the North American Development Bank has
approved the first finance packages for two water projects on
the U.S.-Mexico border.
    The border region was earmarked for special attention and
funding under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA)
between Mexico, the United States and Canada, especially for
environmental infrastructure projects.
    No figures were given for the amounts of the packages, which
are both on the Mexican side of the border.
    The first is a credit to partially finance a system of water
storage and treatment of waste water in the town of Naco in the
state of Sonora.
    The second is for partial credit guarantees for a waste
water treatment plant for an industrial corridor in Matamoros,
in the state of Tamaulipas.
    Other Mexican border towns that are earmarked for project
finance are Nogales, Piedras Negras, Puerto Penasco, Ciudad
Juarez, Mexicali, Tijuana, Nuevo Laredo and Ensenada.
    U.S. towns that are listed to receive funding are Brawley in
California, Mercedes in Texas and Somerton in Arizona, the
ministry added.	N2:LOA

BANGKOK, Sept 24 (Reuter) - The Bank of Thailand said on
Tuesday outstanding foreign loans tapped by Thai-based borrowers
through offshore banking units fell for the first time in July
after it introduced in measures to curb short-term borrowing
inflows.
    The central bank said outstanding out-in foreign loans
imported by offshore banking units fell to 767.8 billion baht
($30.7 billion) at the end of July from 774.9 billion a month
earlier. This compared with 595.4 billion a year ago.
    It said total out-out offshore loans channelled through
licensed banks also declined slightly to 486.9 billion baht at
the end of July from 491.5 billion the previous month and
against 262.4 billion a year ago.
    Out-in loans are foreign borrowings brought in by offshore
banking units for re-lending to Thai-based clients. Out-out
loans refer to offshore funds lent to borrowers in third
countries but processed by Thai-based offshore banks.
    Thailand in late June started requiring offshore banking
units to set aside a seven percent cash reserve on short-term
foreign funds of less than one year maturity used for re-lending
to local clients.	N2:LOA

HONG KONG, Sept 24 (Reuter) - Commercial Bank of Korea's
floating rate note was the sole launch in a slow Asian debt day
Tuesday, but bankers say there are deals on the way.
    The three-year FRN was priced at par to float at 30 basis
points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. Fees
are 15 basis points split as five basis points for management
and underwriting and 10 basis points for selling.
    Salomon Brothers International is the lead.
    Bankers in Hong Kong said the pricing is a squeeze.
    At 35 basis points all-in, Baa2 rated CBK is paying about
the same return as A3-rated Hanil Bank's US$90 million
three-year FRN launched last month.
    Commercial Bank of Korea's outstanding FRN due May 1999
currently is indicated at about 50 basis points over LIBOR in
the secondary market, traders said.
    That deal, a US$140 million FRN launched by Merrill Lynch in
May, paid an all-in return of 39 basis points for three years.
But bankers said the issue was structured in such a way that a
few investors ended up owning the paper at a much wider spread.
    There are other Korean deals on the way.
    Hyundai International Merchant Bank's US$70 million FRCD is
set for launch Wednesday. Asian Banking Corp has mandated six
banks to arrange US$60 million floating rate certificate of
deposit issue that is expected to launch on Friday.
    An FRN for Dong Bang Peregrine Securities is scheduled to
launch in October.
    Among corporate issues, bankers said the US$50 million FRN
for Newmax International Hong Kong will start general
syndication tomorrow.
    Taking a look at Philippines bank issues, Rizal Banking
Corp's three-year FRCD reportedly has been mandated to LTCB Asia
at an all-in return of about 90 basis points. Bankers are still
awaiting mandates for Allied Bank and Union Bank of the
Philippines deals.
    For Indonesia, Bank Niaga has mandated two banks to arrange
a US$40 million FRN. And pricing for Dharmala Inti Utama's
US$100 million FRN is set for Wednesday.
    Peregrine Fixed Income launched the three-year deal for
Dharmala with an indicated coupon of 265-300 basis points over
LIBOR earlier this month.
    APP Global Finance has increased its FRN to US$600 million
from US$500 million after after receiving a strong response.
Bankers said most of the paper stayed in Asia, but there was
some European demand.
    On the loan side, Kerry Properties has increased its loan to
HK$4.0 billion equivalent from HK$3.6 billion following an
oversubscription in syndication, the arrangers said.
    From the local currency markets, the Philippines today
announced that its debut 10-year government bond would pay a
coupon of 16 percent.
    The Philippines also said that its exchange of Brady bonds
for a sovereign fixed-rate issue cut its debt by US$84 million.

BUDAPEST, Sept 20 (Reuter) - A Hungarian-led consortium will construct a 43
km long part of Hungary's M3 motorway, a project to be financed partly by
Germany's Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau and the European Investment Bank (EIB).
    <M Harom Konzorcium>, the winner of an international tender with Italian,
German, Austrian and Portuguese participants, is led by Hungary's Betonutepito
Nemzetkozi Rt, the Transport, Telecommunications and Water Ministry (KHVM) said
on Friday.
    Members of the consortium are Hungary's Magyar Aszfalt Kft, Hidepito Rt and
Austria's Ilbau GmbH, KHVM said in a statement.
    Works will start next month and are to be completed by September 1, 1998,
secretary of state Kalman Kovacs told a news conference.
    Construction costs of the motorway between Gyongyos and Fuzesabony,
north-east Hungary will amount to 23.9 billion forints plus VAT, a KHVM
statement said.
    The VAT is currently 12 percent.
    In addition to budget sources EIB will grant 95 million ECUs and
Kreditanstalt will provide 127 million marks. The loans have to be repaid in 20
and 18 years, respectively, after a five-year grace period.
    The construction is part of a project to upgrade and build a 100 km long
motorway between Budapest and Fuzesabony.
    Reconstruction works on the Budapest-Gyongyos part of the M3 motorway began
in August by Portugal's Mota & Companhia <MOTP.IN>.

BAKU, Sept 20 (Reuter) - Azerbaijan issued its first
Treasury bills on Friday, in a bold step by the oil-rich but
economically-strapped country to tap the government paper market
for much-needed cash.
    The National (central) Bank said five billion manats' worth
of one-month T-Bills were auctioned at an average discount of
7.58 percent, producing an average annualised yield of 31.18
percent.
    Investors, mainly newly-authorised dealers, snapped up the
entire issue of short-term paper, giving the state coffers 4.87
billion manat in revenue.
    The former Soviet republic of Azerbaijan sits on huge oil
reserves in its sector of the Caspian Sea and has attracted
billions of dollars in foreign investment from Western and
Japanese oil consortiums.
    But its economy is in shambles after seven years of a
debilitating war with Armenia over the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh
enclave and economic reforms have lagged behind those in most
former Soviet republics.
    Gross domestic product shrank 17.2 percent last year after a
21.9 percent slip in 1994, and industrial output showed
similarly steep declines.
    There is a rudimentary two-tier banking system, with nearly
250 small banks. Parliament has passed a law on securities, but
there are no stock exchanges or investment funds.
    The country has not undertaken privatisation but plans to
turn some monopolies into joint-stock companies and possibly
later invite in foreign investors.
    The International Monetary Fund granted Baku an $85 million,
2-1/2 year standby loan in 1995, but has said the country's
reforms have been too slow, especially in privatisation.

RIGA, March 21 (Reuter) - Latvia and the International
Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday they signed a new standby
agreement for the Baltic state worth 30 million SDRs or about
$45 million.
    IMF representative Emmanuel Van Der Mensbrughe announced the
agreement and the figures at a news conference after talks with
Latvian Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss.
    Agreement on the standby came as Latvia pulls itself out a
government revenue and banking crisis, sparked last year by the
closure of Banka Baltiya.
    The agreement came shortly before the old standby
arrangement expired and a new accord looked unlikely as the
planned budget deficit for 1996 stayed outside IMF
recommendations of 40 million lats (around $80 million).
    But Van der Mensbrughe said steps taken by the new
government of Prime Minister Andris Shkele to cut the deficit
and speed up privatisation convinced the IMF a deficit this year
of 40 million lats (around $80 million) was possible.	N2:LOA

TOKYO, March 25 (Reuter) - Senior negotiators from Japan's
ruling coalition and the main opposition party Shinshinto
started the second round of talks on Monday night to break a
parliamentary deadlock over the national budget, an official
from the ruling coalition said.
    At the meeting, the two sides were to discuss whether
leaders from the three ruling coalition parties, including
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, and Shinshinto head Ichiro
Ozawa should meet to break the impasse later on Monday,
together with Lower House Speaker Takako Doi, the official
said.
    At an earlier meeting held this morning, the two sides only
reaffirmed the remaining gap over how to deal with the budget.
    Shinshinto lawmakers have been staging a sit-in in
parliament for three weeks in an attempt to block passage of
the budget for the year starting on April 1.
    The party has demanded that the government drop an
unpopular plan from the 1996/97 budget to use 685 billion yen
of tax money to help wind up seven ailing mortgage firms. The
delay in passing the budget has made it necessary for the
government to draft a stopgap budget to cover government
running costs for a 50-day period starting from April 1.

TOKYO, March 26 (Reuter) - Japan eased trust banks' special
reserve requirements on Tuesday, after a proposal to relax the
requirements was approved in a morning cabinet meeting, a
Finance Ministry spokesman said.
    The measure became effective right after the cabinet's
approval, he added.
    Trust banks are now able to set aside a smaller amount of
their reserves as a result of the easing, and this will free up
extra funds which the trust banks can use to write off problem
loans to ailing mortgage firms, banking industry sources said.
    Trust banks are commercial banks which manage and invest
the assets of their clients as well as taking deposits.
    Under the new requirements, trust banks are required to set
aside reserves equivalent to 0.5 percent of the total amount of
trust accounts they have, the spokesman said.
    Previously, trust banks were asked to set aside up to three
percent of their total trust accounts.	N2:LOA

KUALA LUMPUR, March 27 (Reuter) - Bank Negara Malaysia said
on Wednesday the rate of inflation as measured by the Consumer
Price Index moderated in 1995 to 3.4 percent versus 3.7 percent
in 1994.
    For 1996, the Malaysian central bank said in its annual
report that it expects to keep inflation under four percent.
    Price increases throughout 1995 were moderate except for
May-August when prices rose between 3.5 and 3.9 percent due to
higher prices of food, beverages and tobacco.
    At the producer level, the Producer Price Index for the
domestic economy rose 5.5 percent in 1995, compared with 4.9
percent in 1994. This reflected increases in the prices of
rubber and crude palm oil.
    The central bank said it was increasingly concerned about
surging prices in certain areas of the property market during
1995 and enacted measures including tightening loan conditions.
    For 1996, inflationary pressures are expected to remain as
the economy races to a ninth consecutive year of strong growth
in an environment of full employment, Bank Negara said.
    It said efforts would be strengthened to promote savings. A
further potential source of inflationary pressure, if left
unchecked, is rising wages, the central bank said.	N2:LOA

scheme to wind up mortgage firms to go ahead.

COTONOU, Aug 30 (Reuter) - The International Monetary Fund
(IMF) has approved a $40 million three-year loan to Benin under
the West African country's Enhanced Structural Adjustment
Facility, Finance Minister Moise Mensah said.
    The credit aims to support the government's economic reform
programme and the first annual loan of $13 million will be
disbursed in two equal instalments, the first of which is
available immediately.
    Benin's last ESAF expired in March 1996. The IMF said the
economic programme for 1996-99 aimed at annual real gross
domestic product growth of over five percent, annual inflation
of about three percent, and a reduction in the external current
account deficit, excluding grants, to about 5.5 percent of GDP
by 1999.
    Benin is targeting GDP growth of 5.5 percent for 1996 and
5.8 percent for 1997. The external current account deficit is
put at 7.3 percent of GDP for 1996 and 6.4 percent in 1997, from
8.6 percent in 1995.
    The government aims to reduce the overall budget deficit,
excluding grants, to 6.6 percent of GDP in 1996 and 6.2 percent
in 1997, from seven percent in 1995. Measures to increase
revenue will include a reduction of customs exemptions, and tax
increases on certain products.
    Mensah said the privatisation programme would continue,
concentrating on state-run hotels and vegetable oil processor
Societe Nationale pour l'Industrie des Corps Gras (SONICOG).
    An action plan for developing production of cotton, Benin's
main export, is due to be adopted by the end of 1996.
    Talks with the Paris Club of official creditors on a
reduction of Benin's $1.4 billion debt are scheduled for
September 23.	N2:LOA
