HONG KONG, Aug 29 (Reuter) - Asian bankers had plenty to
talk about Thursday despite a dearth of new debt deals.
    Starting with Indonesia, bankers say APP Global Finance, a
subsidiary of Asia Pulp and Paper, now plans to raise funds
solely through a floating rate note issue.
    The company had been expected to raise US$500 million
through a combination of an FRN and a 144a fixed-rate bond.
    Union Bank of Switzerland <SBGZ.S> is the arranger.
    Asian bankers say the FRN might be a hard sell because it is
secured by Asia Pulp and Paper shares. Equity backing is
considered less desirable than a claim on property, for example,
because stock prices are more volatile.
    Asia Pulp and Paper is a member of the Sinar Mas group,
which currently has another deal in the market via Sinar Mas
Finance, which on Wednesday launched a US$50 million floating
rate note issue.
    Another Sinar Mas member, Tjiwi Kima, is seen bringing a
loan issue.
    From South Korea, Kwangju Bank has mandated KDB Asia to
arrange its first floating rate note issue.
    Bankers said the US$50 million FRN has a final maturity of
three years and will pay a margin of 45 basis points over the
six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
    Fees are not decided yet.
    Kwangju Bank is one of South Korea's specialized banks.
Another specialized bank, Kyungki, has a three-year FRN in the
market that is paying a coupon of 40 basis points and an all-in
return of 49 basis points to the top tier.
    Bankers report that about US$10 million of the Kyungki deal
has been sold so far.
    Among the other specialised banks, Kyongnam Bank also has a
deal in the works, while Chung Chong Bank is considering a
transaction as well.
    Korea Exchange Bank Hong Kong's HK$500 million floating rate
certificate of deposit is expected to launch next week via Chase
Manhattan Asia and Jardine Fleming Bank.
    The deal has a final maturity of 364 days.
    There have been a few one-year transactions for Korean
credits in the last couple of months and bankers said that tenor
has advantages for both parties to the deal.
    With Korea expected to join the Organization for Economic
Cooperation and Development this year, Korean banks may want to
issue short-dated paper on the view that they can refinance in
1997 much more cheaply.
    For lenders, the short-dated FRCDs offer a better return
than commercial paper. Moreover, paper maturing in less than a
year qualifies for a 20-percent risk weighting.
    Bankers said Kookmin Bank is considering a three-year Hong
Kong dollar deal. The all-in is expected to be in the mid-50s
over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
    PCI Bank's rumoured new issue is expected to carry a
five-year maturity and, even more unusual for Philippines bank
credit, a fixed coupon.
    In Thailand, Siam City Bank is expected to come to market
with an FRN.
    There's also a Thai Yankee in the offing, with petroleum
concern PTTE&P expected to bring a bond.
    Singapore's Total Access, which recently had its senior debt
rated BBB-minus by Standard and Poor's Corp, also is seen
launching a Yankee issue.
    Late on Wednesday Union Bank of Switzerland said that
Countrywide Corp's floating rate note issue had been raised
US$100 million to US$250 million due to robust demand.
    UBS, which took a large share of the original amount to take
advantage of the strong secondary market interest, reportedly
took the full US$100 million.
    Taiwan's First Commercial Bank is expected to launch its
FRCD on Friday.
    -- Andrea Ricci (852) 2843-6371 fax (852) 2845-0636	N2:LOA

SEOUL, Aug 30 (Reuter) - The Korea Securities Research
Institute proposed on Friday the launch of a fund to protect
investors in case of bankruptcy or failure of securities firms,
a finance ministry official said.
   
    The research body, which is under the control of the Korea
Securities Dealers Association, suggested establishing the
Securities Investors Protection Corporation, which would set
reserve requirements for all securities houses.
    Under the requirement, all securities companies would have
to put aside one percent of their equity capital as reserves
with the Securities Finance Corporation. They would also have to
keep 0.1 percent of the annualised average of customers
desposits as reserves.
    The official said this would guarantee that all stock
investors would get back up to 20 million won of their deposits
in case of a bankcruptcy or failure.	N2:LOA

TOKYO, Aug 29 (Reuter) - Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF)
said in its budget plan that it hopes to issue a total of 22.88
trillion yen in new government bonds in fiscal 1997/98 starting
next April, up from a planned 21.03 trillion yen this fiscal
year, a ministry official said on Thursday.
    MOF has planned an overall budget of 21.34 trillion yen for
itself for the next fiscal year, up from a planned 19.01
trillion yen for the current fiscal year. 
    It has also requested an additional 12.8 trillion yen under
a special framework in the 1997/98 state budget to finance
public works projects and economic structural reforms.
   
    A large part of the ministry's budget will be used to cover
debt-servicing costs which are likely to total 18.27 trillion
yen in 1997/98.
    Yields on the new bond issues are expected to be around 4.4
percent, the MOF official said.
    MOF has also allotted a budget of 31.45 trillion yen for
refunding bonds next fiscal year, compared with a planned 26.56
trillion yen for this fiscal year.
    Final approval is expected to be given in December after
negotiations between MOF and other ministries.	N2:LOA

HONG KONG, Sept 13 (Reuter) - Korea Exchange Bank slipped in
with a US$100 million floating rate note issue launched in
London, the only launch in a slow Asian debt day Friday.
    The one-year FRN was launched at par and re-offered at
99.975 to float at 20 basis points over the three-month London
Interbank Offered Rate. Fees are five basis points.
    Fuji International Finance was the lead.
    One-year issues have become popular among Korean borrowers
on the view that they will be able to finance at better terms
next year if South Korea joins the OECD by end-1996, as is
expected.
    In Hong Kong, Yang Zi Lin, chief executive of the Hong Kong
and Macau regional offices of the Bank of China, said he expects
the bank's debut Hong Kong dollar debt issue to be extremely
successful.
    Yang said that at least half of the 40 banks contacted by
Bank of China already have expressed interest in joining the
facility and that he believed all of the banks approached
eventually would commit to the deal.
    Bank of China group member China Development Finance Co will
arrange the HK$2 billion five-year FRCD for Bank of China.
    Yang confirmed speculation that the certificates would pay
an all-in return of about 40 basis points over the Hong Kong
Interbank Offered Rate, comparable to that paid by similar bank
issues in the territory.
    Earlier today, sources at CDFC confirmed that Bank of China
issue had received approval from China's State Administration of
Exchange Control (SAEC).

Investment Bank Asia and J.P. Morgan Securities Asia announced
that they have been mandated to arrange a HK$3.5 billion
equivalent term loan facility for Hong Kong's CITIC Pacific.
    As for deals already done, arrangers of Wheelock's revolving

to HK$5 billion from HK$4.5 billion after being oversubscribed
in general syndication.
    The facility already had been increased from HK$3 billion in
the sub-underwriting phase.
    In other loan news, Banco Santander, J.P. Morgan Securities

of Switzerland said they would arrange a US$115 million
project-related loan to fund a bridges and tunnel project in
China's Guangdong province.
    In the capital markets, lead manager Deutsche Morgan
Grenfell said it was pleased with the market response to the
US$200 million floating rate note issue of General Housing Bank
of Thailand, a DMG source said.
    The housing bank FRN, launched Thursday in London, replaced
Thailand's sovereign FRN issue.
    DMG sold US$11 million more than its US$114 million
allotment and bought some of the co-managers' share. The issue
was placed with institutional investors in Europe and Asia.

BELGRADE, Sept 17 (Reuter) - Yugoslavia is prepared to
consider all possibilities in negotiations with its foreign bank
creditors to reschedule some $2 billion of commercial debt, a
member of the negotiating team said on Tuesday.
    Dragana Gnjatovic told Tanjug news agency that Belgrade
would consider all options -- reprogramming or refinancing the
debt, writing it off, converting it into commercial paper,
buying it for shares or exchanging it for bonds.
    Last month Belgrade said it would resume talks with the
London Club of commercial bank creditors in Belgrade in the
first half of September, but there has been no word since.
    The two sides are trying to settle rump Yugoslavia's $2
billion share of the commercial debt left over by the former
Yugoslav federation.
    The talks are complicated by sanctions imposed on Belgrade
for its role in the Bosnia war and arguments among the former
Yugoslav republics over how to divide up assets totalling up to
$100 billion.
    Gnjatovic said the debt would have to be restructured so
that the repayment burden would allow the country to service its
foreign debt and at the same time secure foreign currency for
imports.
    According to the latest internationally accepted standards
creditor countries should not allocate more than 18-20 percent
of export earnings for repaying foreign debt if they are to keep
developing while meeting their financial obligations, she added.
    Any higher repayment burden would bring Belgrade into the 
debt trap in which the former Yugoslavia was stuck from 1983-89,
she said.
    Asked about the structure of the Yugoslav foreign debt,
Gnjatovic said the largest part was to creditor governments
grouped in the Paris Club.	N2:LOA

    HONG KONG, Sept 12 (Reuter) - Bank of China has mandated
China Development Finance Co to arrange a HK$2 billion floating
rate certificate of deposit issue, bankers said Thursday.
    They said the facility has a final maturity of five years
with no put or call options.
    This is the first Hong Kong dollar issue for Bank of China.
    The bank last year yanked a HK$5.0 billion deal after
Moody's Investors Service downgraded its rating to Baa1, which
made the issue ineligible for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's
Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
    Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks
because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase
agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
    At that time, eligibility for LAF required that issues must
be HK$1.0 billion or more in size and carry ratings of A2 and
Single-A by Moody's Investors Service and Standard and Poor's
Corp, respectively.
    But in May 1996, the HKMA said that it would accept ratings
of the Japan Bond Research Institute (JBRI) and IBCA.
    The change meant that many issuers, notably Bank of China,
now are eligible for LAF status.
    Last year's suspended Bank of China issue was hugely
oversubscribed--it launched at HK$1.0 billion--and bankers said
a new issue is likely to be similarly well received.

TOKYO, Sept 11 (Reuter) - A key Japanese government panel 
will start discussion on deregulation of foreign exchange
operations so that it can submit a bill for revision of the
foreign exchange law to the next ordinary parliament session,
financial sources said on Wednesday.
    The Committee on Foreign Exchange and Other Transactions,
an advisory panel to the Ministry of Finance (MOF), will start
discussing on Thursday ways to allow corporations to engage in
foreign exchange business currently limited to banks.
    The Committee will discuss in detail the qualifications of
new participants, a range of foreign exchange business they can
cover, and the role of supervisors.
    In June, the committee called for revisions and a
comprehensive overhaul of the Tokyo forex market but details
and the timing of deregulation were not decided.
    Financial sources said the areas of business that new
participants are allowed to do would include currency exchanges
and loans to overseas companies and derivatives. Regular
banking business such as foreign currency deposits and overseas
remittance would be excluded, the sources said.
    A MOF source said details have not been decided but added
that too much supervision would undermine efforts to stimulate
the Tokyo foreign exchange market.	N2:LOA

HONG KONG, Sept 11 (Reuter) - A couple of South Korean
merchant banks made their move on Wednesday with new issues,
while Tingyi Holdings formally launched its big FRN.
    Bankers also took a closer look at APP Global Finance's
US$500 million deal, which was presented in Hong Kong today.
    Kyongnam Bank brought its US$50 million floating rate
certificate of deposit issue. The certificates have a final
maturity of five years but can be put or called after three.
    The deal pays a margin of 45 basis points over the London
Interbank Offered Rate and with fees an all-in return of 50
basis points to the top tier.
    Arrangers are KDB Asia, LTCB Asia, Merrill Lynch Far East
and Standard Chartered Investment Banking.
    Hansol Merchant also launched an FRCD. The US$30 million
deal has a final maturity of three years and annual puts.
    It pays a margin of 49.5 basis points over LIBOR and an
all-in return of 52.5 basis points to the first put.
    The arrangers pointed out that by putting the issue in the
first year lenders benefit from the reduced BIS capital reserve
requirement. The paper will be redeemed at 99.7 if put in year
one and at 99.775 if put in year two.
    The transaction carries an ownership covenant stipulating
that Hansol Paper Co must retain at least 30 percent direct
ownership of the borrower.
    Bankers said the issues may be a difficult sell. These banks
are not as popular as the large commercial banks, despite the
more attractive spread. Moreover, supply of South Korean paper
is on the rise again, bankers said.
    Kyangju Bank is expected to launch its US$50 million FRCD on
Friday. Other merchant banks in the market are Kumho, Saehan,
Hyundai International Merchant Bank and Asian Banking Corp.
    Add to those Boram Bank and Cho Hung Bank and the list
starts to get very long.
    Hanil Hong Kong is doing something a little different with a
Hong Kong dollar deal in the works.
    Recent Korean corporate issues haven't fared very well, a
result that some bankers attribute to unfavorable events.
    Daewoo's last syndication wasn't helped by the conviction of
Daewoo Group chairman Kim Woo-choong on charges of bribing
former South Korean president Roh Tae-woo.
    Similarly, U.S. missile attacks on Iraq scared banks away
from Hyundai Engineering's recent transaction because the
company has significant interests in Iraq, one banker explained.
    Elsewhere, Tingyi Holdings formally launched its US$150
million floating rate note via arranger ING Barings. The company
is Hong Kong-listed, Taiwan-owned and China-based.
    While some bankers said they do not want to take on China
risk, others said Tingyi, a giant in the instant noodle market,
is an attractive credit at the deal's price.
    The three-year notes pay a margin of 110 basis points over
LIBOR and an all-in return of 125 basis points.
    APP Global Finance held a roadshow for its US$500 million
secured FRN in Hong Kong today.
    The funds ultimately will be used by Asia Pulp and Paper,
which has no direct or indirect ownership interest in the
borrower. The transaction has been structured to maximize tax
benefits in Singapore, where Asia Pulp and Paper is
headquartered, and to help lower the company's gearing ratio.
    Some bankers have expressed reservations about the deal,
which is secured by Asia Pulp and Paper shares rather than fixed
assets. But others said they like Asia Pulp and Paper's story
and are planning to take a closer look at the issue.
    The roadshows, so far held in Taipei, Seoul and Hong Kong,
have been well attended and some of the paper has been placed.

TOKYO, Sept 12 (Reuter) - An association of Tokyo-based
shinkin banks said on Thursday that it would announce a plan to
bail out financially troubled Musashino Shinkin Bank.
    A news conference will be held at 4 p.m. (0700 GMT), an 
association official said.
    Shinkin banks are small credit associations which take
deposits and lend mainly to members and are supervised by the
Ministry of Finance (MOF).
    Zenshinren Bank, a national association of credit
associations, and Tokyo-based shinkin banks have been working
out a programme to bail out Musashino Shinkin, which is reeling
under problem loans now estimated at about 39 billion yen,
industry sources said on Wednesday.
    Under the programme now being worked out, Musashino's
problem loans will be separated from healthy loans and those
problem loans will be taken care of through financial aid
provided by Zenshinren and other shinkin banks, they said.
Musashino's business, including healthy loans and deposits,
will be taken over by a shinkin bank, they added.	N2:LOA

TASHKENT, Sept 10 (Reuter) - A group of 14 foreign banks
plan to set up a syndicate to provide financing for a gold joint
venture in the Central Asian state of Uzbekistan, an Uzbek
official source said.
    Representatives of the banks, including France's Ste
Generale <SOGN.PA> and Germany's Dresdner Bank <DRSD.F>, were
due to arrive in Tashkent on Wednesday to discuss the plan, the
source in the State Geology and Mineral Resources Committee told
Reuters.
    The Amantaitau Goldfields venture requires about $350
million in project financing, but it was not clear how much of
this would be provided by the banks.
    The venture to develop the Amantaitau field is 57 percent
owned by Uzbekistan, with a further 35 percent belonging to
British conglomerate Lonrho Plc <LRHO.L> and eight percent to
the International Finance Corp, a unit of the World Bank.
    Lonrho won a tender earlier this year to take part in the
project in the Central Asian state's Navoi province.
    The Uzbek newspaper Business Partner said it involved the
development of four open quarries, one underground mine and
construction of an ore enrichment facility, which should come on
stream in the first quarter of 1998.
    Uzbek official sources and representatives of Lonrho in
Tashkent declined to estimate reserves.
    Business Partner said the project's life could be 12-17
years.
    Trade journals say Uzbekistan is the world's ninth largest
gold producer, with output last year of 63.6 tonnes.
    President Islam Karimov has said the desert nation has gold
reserves of around 5,000 tonnes.

LONDON, Sept 12 (LPC) - A host of international banks are
competing to finance up to 1.6 billion sterling ($2.49 billion)
in debt for British power plant projects, according to banking
sources. The massive Teeside Power and Humber Power companies
are currently negotiating with potential lenders to refinance
existing debt and for fresh funds for expansion.
    Humber Power Ltd is seeking about 275 million stg for
construction of the 510-megawatt second phase of its power
station in Humberside, bankers say. Humber Power may also
refinance the 520 million stg credit that financed its 750-
megawatt first phase.

Imperial Bank of Commerce, Deutsche Bank, HSBC, NatWest Markets
and Union Bank of Switzerland - are making proposals to Humber
Power, which is sponsored by Imatran Voima Oy, Midlands
Electricity and ABB-Asea Brown Boveri.
    Humber's first phase, not due to come on stream until 1997,
is financed via a 17.5-year loan struck in 1994.  The bulk of
that credit is priced 110 bps over LIBOR.
    At the same time, Teeside Power Ltd is in talks with banks
for a refinancing of the 795 million stg project financing of
its plant in Cleveland, according to bank sources.
    Teeside, which is controlled by Enron Corp <ENE.N> unit
Enron Power, is currently taking bids from at least three banks.
Teeside is already in operation and will seek a loan of at least
12 years. Pricing on its current deal, put into place in 1991,

HONG KONG, April 18 (Reuter) - Asian debt markets offered a
mixed bag of deals on Thursday.
    Sakura Finance Asia released details of a US$60 million
floating rate note issue for Korea International Merchant Bank
<87710.KS>.
    The five-year issue has a put in year three and pays a
margin of 45 basis points over the London Interbank Offered
Rate. With fees, the all-in return to top-tier managers is 60
basis points.
    That's more than the 50 basis points KIMB paid for a
three-year floating rate certificate of deposit issue last
November. But bankers pointed out that the market has been awash
in South Korean bank paper this year and that the pricing on the
FRN is in line with market conditions.
    Other arrangers for the KIMB deal are KEB International,
Hong Kong and Shanghai Bank, Development Bank of Singapore and
Standard Chartered Investment Bank.
    In other news, Hong Kong's Dao Heng Bank closed its HK$1.5
billion FRCD issue, said arranger Bayerische Landesbank.
    The three-year certificates pay a coupon of 40 basis points
and, with fees, 48 basis points to top tier managers.
    The issue is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and
application has been made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to
accept the issue as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment
Facility (LAF), or discount window.
    Hong Kong's Chevalier Group today signed its HK$5.45 million
two-tranche term loan facility, which will be used to finance
two private sector participation scheme projects in the
territory.
    Speaking at the signing ceremony, Chevalier chairman and
managing director Chow Yei Ching noted that Chevalier is a major
participant in these types of PSPS projects, which involve both
residential and commercial building.
    The company has secured nine PSPS projects in Hong Kong,
representing 23 percent of the total PSPS projects developed in
the territory so far, he said.
    Chow acknowledged that the company's profit margins were
slim in 1995, but he said he expects performance to improve.
    That's partly because many new projects associated with Hong
Kong's new airport are expected to come on stream in the next
few years, he said.
    Looking ahead, Indonesian clove cigarette manufacturer
Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna is expected to launch a US$150 million
revolving credit/term loan facility soon, perhaps as early as
Friday.

BEIJING, April 21 (Reuter) - China will move to boost
agricultural production by encouraging businesses to invest in
the sector and by using them to administer farming loans, the
China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
    The ratio of agricultural output growth compared to
industrial output had fallen to 1:5 from 1:1.3 in 1984, the
newspaper said.
    Enterprises in several areas would be chosen to serve as the
bearers of syndicated bank loans earmarked for agriculture in a
bid to boost productivity, it said.
    At least 90 percent of investment in agriculture was
currently in the form of government loans or was administered
through government departments, it said.
    Firms that took on agricultural loans would be responsible
for repayment and so would be more likely to introduce the
latest technology and management techniques, it quoted Yu
Xiaosong, vice minister of the State Economic and Trade
Commission, as saying.
    Outstanding agricultural loans by the Agricultural Bank of
China totalled by 157.8 billion yuan ($19 billion) by the end of
March, while loans from the Agricultural Development Bank of
China totalled 478.3 billion yuan ($58 billion), it said.
    To encourage participation in the scheme, businesses who
took part would be given preference in obtaining land-use rights
and export licences, Yu said.
    China had used more than $10 billion in foreign investment
in its agricultural sector since 1978, it said.
    China's grain output in 1995 was a record 465 million
tonnes.
    Up to 180 billion yuan ($22 billion) in investment would be
needed to raise grain yields by 50 million tonnes by 2000, the
newspaper said.	N2:LOA

BUCHAREST, April 18 (Reuter) - Romania's Senate, on Thursday started debate
on a long-awaited draft bank privatisation bill, a benchmark under loan accords
with international lenders.
    State radio quoted Reform Minister Mircea Cosea telling the upper house of
parliament he hoped the law would bring financial flows needed to restructure
and revive some economic sectors which were less attractive during transition.
    The law is expected to take some weeks to pass.
    Under the draft law, sent to parliament last year, bank privatisation has
two stages: increasing banks' capital through share issues and selling stakes
held by their majority stockholder, the State Ownership Fund (FPS).
    The banks' shares can only be sold for cash to Romanian individuals and
private companies and to foreign investors. Equity will be raised by auctions
and public or private offers.
    The government project said the five regional private ownership funds
(FPPs), which hold 30 percent of the state-run banks due to go private, should
transfer their shares to FPS.
    This proposal had been criticised by FPPs which said that swapping the bank
stakes held by for shares in state firms of doubtful value was a form of
nationalisation.
    The Senate's privatisation commission amended the project saying the
transfer should be made with the FPPs accord.
    Romania should have privatised two of the six state banks last year to match
demands under loan arrangements with the International Monetary Fund and World
Bank. In the absence of a law the country failed to meet those targets.
    Development bank <Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA> (BRD) and farm lender
<Banca Agricola SA> are seen as the most likely to turn private when parliament
passes legislation.
    The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has had convertible
technology loans to both but has focused on the BRD, , saying it could be
interested in up to 20 percent.
    Other banks supposed to go private are the powerful <Banca Romana de Comert
Exterior SA> (Bancorex) which handles almost half of Romania's foreign trade,
<Banca Comerciala Romana SA> which finances most of industrial sector and <Banc
Post SA>.
    <Banca de Export Import Eximbank SA> may remain in state hands as it is seen
as strategic for export guarantees.
    Romania has around 30 commercial banks. Private banks account for some one
third of banking activities in Romania.

    SAO PAULO, May 24 (Reuters) - Brazil's 2016 coffee crop,
which began harvesting a few weeks ago, is forecast at 49.67
million 60-kg bags, the Agriculture Ministry's crop supply
agency Conab said on Tuesday, revising its expectations near the
low end of its January outlook of 49.13 million to 51.94 million
bags.
    Conab's second of four annual estimates is up 15 percent
from last season's drought-damaged harvest of 43.24 million
bags. 
    The forecast also falls on the lower end of market
estimates, which tend toward 54 million to 62 million bags.
Government- and producer-linked forecasters in Brazil
consistently see the crop about 10 percent below market and
trade estimates. [nL2N16V13R]
    If the harvest meets Conab's forecast, it would be the
nation's second-largest, behind 50.83 million bags in 2012.
    Conab said it expected arabica to account for 40.27 million
bags of this year's output, while conillon, the local variety of
robusta, would make up the remaining 9.40 million bags of the
crop.
    While the distribution of rains helped the arabica output to
gain nearly 26 percent from last year, dry weather in conillon
areas, especially in northern Espirito Santo, caused production
of that crop to fall 16 percent and limited the overall coffee
harvest's gains this season, Conab said.
    The jump in national output comes after two years of drought
and high temperatures that crimped the potential of the world's
largest coffee producer and exporter.
    The improved moisture with the early and steady return of
spring showers over the coffee belt followed by consistent,
widespread rains through the key developmental stages of the
crop can be seen in the 14 percent gain in yields, which jumped
to 25.6 bags per hectare from 22.5 bags last year, Conab said.
    A 1 percent increase in planted area to 1.94 million
hectares (4.8 million acres) also helped expand the crop's
productive potential.

LONDON, April 19 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe rose on Tuesday amid strong exports and after
reports of an outage in a U.S. Gulf Coast refinery.
    
    * Several tankers were booked to deliver gasoline from
Europe to the U.S. East Coast, with nearly 1 million tonnes of
product booked on the route for loading in April already.
    * Exports of reformate and gasoline blending components to
China have sharply dropped this month from earlier this year as
stocks in the country remain elevated, traders said.
    * The Atlantic basin is nevertheless facing rising supply
excess that some traders said could pressure refining margins
throughout the peak summer demand season.
    * Nigeria continued to pull gasoline cargoes from Europe but
payment issues are creating delays in deliveries, according to
traders.
    * Nigeria's state oil company is in a standoff with energy
giants ExxonMobil XOM.N and Royal Dutch Shell RDSa.L over
ownership of physical crude cargoes as the West African nation
seeks to shore up its creaking budget.[nL5N17L51U]

catalytic cracking unit at Royal Dutch Shell Plc's RDSa.L
316,600 bpd joint-venture refinery in Deer Park, Texas, could be
shut for up to six weeks of repairs, sources familiar with plant
operations said on Tuesday.[nL2N17M13R]

barrel per day (bpd) Pernis refinery in the Netherlands has shut
down, traders said on Tuesday.[REF/E]

MOSCOW, April 26 (Reuters) - Urals differentials remained
unchanged on Tuesday after Surgutneftegaz awarded its second
Urals tender this week, mathing Monday's price levels.
    The company's tender to sell 400,000 tonnes of Urals went to
Trafigura, Talmay and Shell at discounts of $2.60-$2.70 a barrel
to BFOE on Tuesday, traders said. The cargoes will load from the
Baltic port of Primorsk on May 17-18, 18-19 and 20-21 and from
the Baltic port of Ust-Luga on May 17-18. [nL5N17T5R5]
    In the Platts window, Spain's Cepsa bid for 100,000 tonnes
of Urals loading from the Baltic ports on May 13-17 down to a
discount of $2.75 a barrel to BFOE but couldn't find a seller.
    Traders said that Spainish and Mediterranean refiners were
keen to buy Baltic Urals and the arbitrage window from the
northwest Europe was wide open. At least 500,000 tonnes of Urals
were set to go to the south of Europe from the Baltic ports,
traders said.
    There were no bids or offers for Urals loading from
Novorossiisk in the Platts window, traders said, though price
levels remained firm due to a lack of 80,000 tonne Urals cargoes
in the May loading plan.
    Greece's Hellenic Petroleum issued a tender on Tuesday to
buy 80,000 tonnes of Urals for delivery to Greece June 1-3.
[nL5N17T2PI]
    Premiums for CPC Blend rose amid healthy buying interest and
a limited number of cargoes remained for loading in the second
half of May, with all cargoes loading in the first half of the
month cleared, traders said. 
    Traders said that a cargo loading in the last ten days of
May changed hands at a premium of $0.70-$0.80 a barrel to BFOE,
but this was not confirmed and no details were avilable.
    Hellenic Petroleum issued a tender for two CPC Blend cargoes
of 85,000 or 135,000 tonnes for delivery to Greece May 20-24 and
May 25-30, traders said. The tender closes April 27.
    The were no bids or offers on CPC Blend and Azeri light in
the Platts window, traders said.

LONDON, April 25 (Reuters) -    * Forties differentials
were offered at their lowest levels since early April on Monday,
under pressure from an apparent excess of unwanted barrels in
the region. 
    * Shipping data last week showed Shell fixed the VLCC Samco
Sundarbans to sail to South Korea carrying Forties on May 2,
potentially absorbing more than three Forties cargoes.
    * But at least two VLCCs have loaded Forties in the last
couple of weeks, along with four Aframaxes, and, as yet, have no
destination, meaning some 7 million barrels of Forties are
currently without a home.
    * The contango in the swaps curve has reached its steepest
in two weeks, after intense pressure on swap rates for
prompt-loading cargoes.
    * Some 4 million barrels of Forties sailed to Asia in the
same month last year, yet no VLCCs have made this trip so far
this month, according to Reuters trade flows data.
    * The Brent/Dubai swap spread <DUB-EFS-1M> is off last
week's highs, but still close to its strongest since the start
of the year, meaning North Sea barrels compete less effectively
for Asian buyers.
    * Overall, some 43 million barrels of the 12 North Sea
crudes tracked by Reuters have loaded in the month to date,
compared with 49 million at this point last year.
        
    WINDOW SUMMARY
    * Glencore bid for a cargo of Forties for loading May 20-24
at a discount of 55 cents to dated Brent. 
    * ENI offered a cargo of Forties for loading May 20-22 at a
discount of 30 cents to dated Brent.
    * Total withdrew an offer for a cargo of Forties for loading
via STS at Scapa Flow from the Aframax Liteyny Prospect at a
discount of 35 cents to the dated price on May 6-12.
    * Shell withdrew an offer for a cargo of Forties for loading
May 12-14 at 90 cents below dated Brent.
    * No deals were concluded in the window, nor were any
trades, bids or offers reported for any other grade.

* Total books VLCC Alice from Asia to Europe
    * Diesel cargo will be largest Europe has ever received
    * Storage levels in region hold near record highs

    By Ron Bousso
    LONDON, April 18 (Reuters) - Europe is expected to receive
its largest-ever diesel cargo after French refiner Total
<TOTF.PA> booked a super tanker to sail to the region even as it
faces brimming storage tanks and wilting demand.
    Total has chartered the newly-built very large crude carrier
(VLCC) tanker Alice to ship 270,000 tonnes of diesel, three
times the typical cargo size on the route, from Asia to the port
of Antwerp in Belgium, according to shipping data and Reuters
ship tracking.
    A cargo of this size is bound to put more pressure on
Europe's diesel prices in a  market already facing an influx of
imports in the coming weeks from all corners of the world.
    Euronav-owned Alice left the port of Gunsan in South Korea
on its maiden voyage on January 13 and loaded its cargo at the
Vopak Dialog Pengerang Terminal in Malaysia before being
directed to Europe in early February, according to Reuters data.
    A typical VLCC voyage from Malaysia to northwest Europe
lasts around 32 days. Alice is one of dozens of VLCC set to be
built this year for crude oil trading, but often maiden voyages
are used to transport clean products, according to traders.
    The delivery of the cargo comes at a time where Europe's
diesel storage is near maximum capacity. Rising global
production of diesel and slowing demand have led to a sharp
increases in global storage levels over the past two years with
few signs of the glut easing soon.[nL5N17A588]
    New, ultra-modern refineries that have started production in
recent years in Asia and the Middle East have radically changed
the global diesel trading markets. 
    At the same time, ever-bigger ships are being used to
transport the product around the world, but the VLCC Alice would
be the first tanker of its size to reach European shores with a
cargo of refined product, according to several traders. 
    Europe's diesel prices are considered the global benchmark
for the road fuel due to its large fleet of diesel cars.     
    
    REVERSE ARBITRAGE
    While Total imports diesel into Europe, other tankers
carrying the fuel are being diverted to the U.S. East Coast in a
rare arbitrage that highlights the growing problem of finding an
outlet for diesel in an increasingly oversupplied market.
    The 90,000 tonne Minerva Pisces was redirected in recent
days to the New York Harbour from Gibraltar, some two weeks
after loading diesel at Reliance Industries' <RELI.NS> 580,000
barrels per day Jamnagar refinery in the west coast of India,
according to Reuters shipping data.
    The tanker reached Europe via the Cape of Good Hope, a
detour from the faster route via the Suez Canal that has become
a normal move as traders seek to keep cargoes on water for as
long as possible due to record-high global stocks and tepid
demand.
    At the same, the world's top oil trader Vitol chartered the
60,000 tonne Kamome Victoria from the Baltic port of Ventspils
to Florida with a cargo of diesel, according to traders.
    Several other diesel cargoes have been diverted in recent
months even though the arbitrage from Europe to other market
remains rare. [nL8N15V2IP]

    SINGAPORE, July 12 (Reuters) - Asia's 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums fell
to a one-month low on Wednesday as deal values slipped and suppliers lowered
their offers further to accommodate weaker buying interest. 
    Fuel oil inventories across Europe were up in June compared with May, and
weekly inventories in the Fujairah oil storage hub were largely unchanged. 
    
    CASH PREMIUMS 
    - 380-cst cash premiums <FO380-SIN-DIF> to Singapore quotes fell by $1.03
on Wednesday to 15 cents a tonne, their lowest since June 12. 
    - Three cash deals were reported on Tuesday, totalling 60,000 tonnes of
380-cst fuel oil.
    - All three deals were concluded at $289 a tonne, equivalent to a discount
of about minus 10 cents a tonne at the front of the window up to a premium of
about 20 cents a tonne at the back of the window.
    - By comparison, Monday's two trades exchanged hands at a 90 cent and $1.75
a tonne premium to Singapore quotes. [nL4N1K23OO]
    - In a reflection of the growing aggressiveness in suppliers' offers,
Wednesday saw sellers offer 380-cst cargoes at premiums of $1 a tonne to
Singapore quotes across the trading window, down from Tuesday's offer of $1-$3
a tonne.
    
    FUJAIRAH INVENTORIES
    - In the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ)
fuel oil inventories were down 25,000 barrels, or 0.2 percent, in the week to
July 10 at 12.102 million barrels, data via S&P Global Platts showed.
[nL4N1K32OL]
    - Despite rising summer demand, fuel oil inventories in the Fujairah hub
have failed to draw over the past weeks partly as a result of weaker bunker
fuel sales after the recent ban on Qatari-owned and operated vessels from
calling at UAE ports, industry sources said. 
    
    EU INVENTORIES 
    - European fuel oil stocks rose to 69.10 million barrels in June, up 1.2
percent from May, but were down 11.5 percent from the same time last year,
Euroilstock data showed on Tuesday. [nL8N1K22X8]
    - Seasonal maintenance at some units had concluded by the end of May, while
solid margins encouraged refineries not in turnarounds to run at capacity. That
lifted European crude runs in June to 10.471 million barrels per day (bpd), up
2.6 percent from May and 5.4 percent year on year. [REF/OUT]
        
    TENDERS
    - Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC) unexpectedly issued a spot tender to
export fuel oil in July, three industry sources said on Wednesday. [nL4N1K33NJ]
    - KPC has not issued spot fuel oil export tenders since April, sources
said, after the scheduled decommissioning of the 200,000 bpd Shuaibah refinery
on April 1, which reduced Kuwaiti fuel oil supplies by about 250,000 tonnes a
month.

    OTHER NEWS 
    - The Dutch competition watchdog said on Wednesday that it was
investigating a possible price-fixing cartel among fuel companies in ports in
the Netherlands and Belgium. The ACM watchdog said it had visited some of the
dozens of companies active in fuel production, transportation, storage and
trading in Rotterdam, Antwerp and Amsterdam after receiving information from
the police.[nL8N1K31HB]

in Singapore have helped raise the East-West arbitrage spread to a three session high.

Mercuria bought 80,000 tonnes of the fuel from Trafigura, Shell and BP.

to Total and another 20,000 parcel to Vitol.

    - Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories fell 3.5 percent, or 114,000 tonnes, to a

    - This came as net imports fell 14 percent to a 2-week low of 1.05 million tonnes.

of 119,000 tonnes.

production rose last week just as OPEC exports hit a 2017 high,
casting doubt on efforts by producers to curb oversupply.

August on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) had narrowed to

$5.30 a barrel in the previous session.

barrel by Tuesday on mounting selling pressure. [nL3N1JV3O1]

quarter amid peak summer demand and supply constraints on the

SINGAPORE, July 6 (Reuters) - The Asian jet fuel margin rose to the highest since late
December on Thursday supported by large cargo purchases in Singapore and a spot requirement in
the Middle East, trade sources said.

since Dec. 30, 2016 when it was at $12.90 a barrel, Reuters data showed. 
    - HIN LEONG SNAPS UP JET FUEL: Oil trader Hin Leong snapped up 500,000 barrels out of the
700,000 barrels of jet fuel that traded in Singapore on Thursday. This follows earlier purchases
by Chinese traders such as Unipec and China Aviation Oil, which helped lift sentiments for the
aviation fuel. 
    - EMARAT SEEKS JET FUEL:  Emirates General Petroleum Corp is seeking 60,000 tonnes of jet
fuel for delivery in mid-August in a tender that closes on July 10, traders said. 
    - INDIA OFFERS JET FUEL: India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd has offered
40,000 tonnes of jet fuel for delivery in mid-August in a tender that closes on July 12, traders
said. 
      MRPL last sold a similar-sized cargo for mid-July loading to Litasco at a discount of
$1.25 a barrel to Singapore quotes and a late-July loading cargo to Vitol at a discount of $1 a
barrel, traders said. <MDIS/TENDA> 
    -  SINGAPORE OIL STOCKS: Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks climbed 16 percent to
a two-week high of 11.606 million barrels in the week to July 5, latest data from International
Enterprise showed.
       India shipped about 63,000 tonnes of diesel to Singapore and Malaysia sent about 55,115
tonnes of the fuel to Singapore, the data showed. But there were no other diesel imports that
arrived in the city-state last week, according to the data. 
       India and South Korea shipped about 70,000 tonnes of jet fuel to Singapore, the data
showed.
    -  BANGLADESH LNG DRIVE TO HIT DIESEL DEMAND: Bangladesh's plan to start importing liquefied
natural gas (LNG) next year will likely dampen its demand for oil used in power generation,
government and industry sources said. [nL3N1JW2Q0]
       The South Asian nation typically ships in around 2.5 million tonnes of fuel oil and 3.2
million tonnes of diesel annually, making it one of the top 10 such importers in the region.
       But its push towards cleaner gas is likely to displace some of that appetite for oil,
with the country's first floating LNG import terminal due to begin accepting cargoes in May next
year.

SINGAPORE, July 11 (Reuters) - Cash and ex-wharf premiums came under renewed pressure
on Tuesday as suppliers turned more aggressive in their offers for the fuel oil in order to
stimulate demand, industry sources said. 
    Selling pressure also dragged the front month fuel oil cracks to a near three-session
low on Tuesday despite weaker crude oil prices.

    PHYSICAL MARKETS
    - Cash premiums for 380-cst fuel slipped to $1.18 a tonne to Singapore, down from $1.22
a tonne on Monday. 
    - Suppliers on Tuesday offered 380-cst cargoes at premiums of $1-$3 a tonne to
Singapore quotes, down compared to Monday's offer of $1.75-$3 a tonne. 
    - Two cash deals were reported on Tuesday totalling 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil. 
    - One deal was concluded at $280 a tonne, equivalent to a premium of about $1.75 a
tonne to Singapore quotes, while the second deal traded at a premium of 90 cents a tonne. 
    - By comparison, Monday saw one cargo change hands at a premium of $1.25 a tonne. 
    - Click on [O/AS] for more details.
    
    EX-WHARF 
    - Ex-wharf premiums, a key indicator of prompt supply fundamentals, have eased over the
past two weeks amid weaker demand for Singapore bunker fuels.
    - Premiums of the break-bulk cargoes averaged $3.91 a tonne over the last two weeks,
well below the $5.69 average in the previous two weeks, Reuters data showed. 
    - Falling crude prices have prompted shippers and charterers to lift fewer quantities
of bunker fuels in anticipation of further price declines, industry sources said. 
    - Sources also said aggressive bunker pricing in other key ports including Fujairah and
Hong Kong have somewhat dampened demand for Singapore bunkers. 
    
    CRACKS
    - The Rotterdam barge fuel oil crack to Brent crude for August on the Intercontinental
Exchange (ICE) was down about 30 cents a barrel to a discount of around $5.25 a barrel by
4:30 p.m. Singapore time (0830 GMT).
    - This came despite sharp declines in crude oil prices over the past week as concerns
of a persistent crude oil oversupply weighed. [nL4N1K21TT]
    - Expectations of tighter supplies and the beginning of peak seasonal demand since the
start of June catapulted fuel oil cracks to some of their highest levels in years towards
the end of the month. [nL3N1JH360] [nL3N1JI3ZV]
    
    TENDERS
    - India's Essar Oil has withdrawn its offer for 27,000 tonnes of low-sulphur fuel oil
for delivery on Aug 1-5 at Vadinar. [nL4N1K2233]
        
    PAKISTAN TURNS TO LNG 
    - Pakistan says it could become one of the world's top-five buyers of liquefied natural
gas (LNG), with Petroleum Minister Shahid Abbasi predicting imports could jump more than
fivefold as private companies build new LNG terminals. [nL8N1K13W5]
    - Cheaper than fuel oil and cleaner burning than coal, LNG suits emerging economies
seeking to bridge electricity shortfalls and support growth on tight budgets.

SINGAPORE, July 13 (Reuters) - Cash differentials of Asia's benchmark 180-cst fuel oil
flipped to a premium for the first time in fourth months on Wednesday and ex-wharf
premiums remained steady above $1 a tonne to Singapore quotes amid robust demand for
bunkering fuels. 
    One 40,000 tonne 180-cst fuel oil cash deal was reported in the Platts window on
Wednesday, trading at a premium of about $1 a tonne to Singapore quotes for the first time
in months, industry sources said.
    Cash differentials of the benchmark 180-cst fuel oil <FO180-SIN-DIF> were assessed at
a premium of 26 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes, the highest since March 22. 
    Another 80,000 tonnes of the more actively traded 380-cst fuel oil changed hands in
the window on Wednesday, albeit at slightly weaker price levels, weighing on cash
differentials, sources said. 
    Cash discounts of the 380-cst fuel <FO380-SIN-DIF> slipped 12 cents to $1.11 a tonne
below Singapore quotes. 
    Meanwhile, despite slipping from yesterday's two-month highs, ex-wharf premiums of
380-cst fuel oil remained above $1 a tonne to Singapore quotes as Singapore marine fuel
sales continue to demonstrate strength.
    While sales of Singapore bunker fuels slipped 6 percent in June compared with the
previous month, sales are still above 4 million tonnes a month and well above the 2016 and
2015 monthly average, official data showed. [nL4N19Z352]
    Although volumes of 380-cst continued to represent the bulk of total sales at 73
percent, the proportion of 500-cst fuel sales grew to 22 percent of the total, its highest
since records going back to 2012. That gain was at the expense of 380-cst fuel, the June
sales of which fell to their lowest on record. 

    RELATED NEWS:
    - The global glut in oil is refusing to ease and acts as a major dampener on crude
prices despite robust demand growth and steep declines in non-OPEC production, the
International Energy Agency said on Wednesday. [nL8N19Z136]
    - OPEC on Tuesday gave an upbeat outlook for the oil market in 2017, saying global
demand for its crude would be higher than its current production and pointing to a supply
deficit rather than a sizeable, price-sapping surplus. [nL8N19Y31J]

SINGAPORE, July 12 (Reuters) - Singapore ex-wharf premiums for 380-cst fuel oil rose
to a two-month high on Tuesday on firm demand for bunker fuels and slightly tighter
availabilities of the marine fuel, said a bunker fuel trader.

ex-wharf prices <BK380-B-SIN> settled at about $243 a tonne.

while the daily average traded volume for July stands at 55,000 tonnes.

SINGAPORE, Oct 3 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differentials remained steady on Tuesday
as spot demand from South Africa and the United Arab Emirates helped boost sentiment, especially
with maintenance in the region curbing supply, traders said. 
    
      - SOUTH AFRICA SEEKS: South Africa's PetroSA is seeking 13,500 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur
diesel for Nov. 9-11 delivery into Mossel Bay in a tender that closes on Oct. 4 and is valid
until Oct. 6.
      - EMIRATES SEEKS: Emirates General Petroleum Corp (Emarat) is seeking 18,000 tonnes of
10ppm sulphur diesel for delivery over Oct. 27-28. The tender closes on Oct. 9 and is valid
until Oct. 11. 
      - TAIWAN OFFERS GASOIL: Taiwan's CPC Corp has offered either 50ppm or 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for loading from Kaohsiung in November in a tender that closes on Oct. 5. 
      - RUSSIA DIESEL EXPORTS: Exports of ultra-low-sulphur diesel from the Russian Baltic Sea
port of Primorsk could rise by 11 percent to 880,000 tonnes in October, up from the 770,000
tonnes initially planned in September, three industry sources said. [nL8N1MD4V5]
        Information provided by the sources showed that seven tankers are scheduled to be loaded
in Primorsk between Oct. 1 and Oct. 10. The full-month schedule has not yet been made available.
      - JAPAN REFINING: Japan's No.2 oil refiner by sales, Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd, on Tuesday
said it plans to refine 420,459 barrels per day (6.15 million kilolitres) of crude oil in
October-December, down 11 percent from a year earlier, due to scheduled refinery maintenance. 
        The Tokyo-based firm said it shut the sole 160,000 barrels-per-day No. 1 crude
distillation unit (CDU) at its Aichi refinery on Tuesday for scheduled maintenance, with the
scheduled restart seen around mid-November. 
        During the Aichi maintenance in October-November, Showa Shell Sekiyu would supply
gasoline and gas oil to Idemitsu as part of the arrangements that the alliance that the two
firms signed in May ahead of their stalled merger plans. [nL4N1MD51R]

SINGAPORE, June 29 (Reuters) - A drawdown in inventory of diesel in Singapore further
boosted the profit margin for refining the fuel to a more than two-month high on Thursday,
industry sources said. 
    
    - SINGAPORE STOCKS: Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks dived 20 percent to a 5-1/2
month low of 9.993 million barrels in the week to June 28, latest data from International
Enterprise showed. 
    There were no diesel shipments from China to Singapore, while diesel exports from Singapore
to Australia fell to about 19,000 tonnes compared with 107,000 tonnes the previous week.
    There were also lower volumes of the fuel shipped to Malaysia and Vietnam, the data showed,
likely contributing to the drawdown in inventory. 
    - JET FUEL DEALS EASED: There were no jet fuel cargoes exchanging hands in the Platts'
trading period known as market-on-close (MOC) in Singapore, for the first time this month,
traders said. 
    - VIETNAM BUYS: Vietnam's Saigon Petro bought 10,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for
July 1 to 3 loading from Singapore, Malaysia or Thailand at a premium of about $1 a barrel to
Singapore quotes, an industry source said. 
    - TAIWAN'S DIESEL EXPORTS CURBED: Taiwan's Formosa Petrochemical Corp may not export any
diesel in the spot market until the fourth quarter of this year, potentially boosting margins
for the fuel, industry sources said. [nL3N1JP3ML]
      The refiner has not exported any diesel in the spot market since January, while overall
diesel exports from Taiwan have fallen by about 10 percent, according to the sources and trade
data.

LONDON/SINGAPORE, Oct 2 (Reuters) - Royal Dutch Shell
<RDSa.L> has hired a former manager in Sinochem's London office
to help bolster its crude oil trading into the Chinese market,
sources told Reuters. 
    Zheng Qingpu, who worked as the deputy general manager for
Sinochem in London, has joined the Shell crude oil trading desk
in Singapore, the sources said. 
    Major trading houses and independent oil firms are chasing
qualified and well-connected staff for their Asia trading desks,
spurred on by the opening up of China's oil imports to include
independent refineries. 
    Shell declined to comment on staff moves. Qingpu, who
managed West African trading for Sinochem, did not immediately
respond to a request for comment.
    The sources told Reuters that Qingpu was initially expected
to take a job with Statoil, but then opted for Shell. Statoil
declined to comment. 
    Companies last year began plucking staff from state giants
including Sinochem and CNPC to grab a larger share of the $50
million a day in new crude flowing into China, which many expect
to grow even further. [http://reut.rs/2xaab9L
]
    Sources in London said Qingpu's connections and experience
in China drove Shell to poach him. Sources in Singapore said his
knowledge of West African oil was also a key qualification. 
    China's imports from Angola surged about 28 percent in
August from a year ago to about 983,500 barrels per day (bpd),
according to official customs data, while its Angolan imports
for the first eight months of 2017 hit 1.05 million bpd, a gain
of 16.6 percent from the same period last year. [nEAP222437]

    - CHINA DIESEL DEMAND: Sales of large LNG trucks are expected to hit record levels in China
this year as the government steps up an anti-pollution campaign that includes curbs on
heavy-duty diesel vehicles.
      LNG trucks account for about four percent of the more-than-six-million heavy vehicles able
to haul 40 tonnes-49 tonnes of goods that are on China's roads. The vast majority of the 43
billion tonnes of freight transported across China last year was by highway.
     However, demand for LNG trucks has soared as companies and manufacturers shift to vehicles
that run on gas, which Beijing sees as a key part to its war against smog.
     Sales of LNG heavy trucks surged 540 percent to nearly 39,000 in the first seven months of
the year, according to Cassie Liu, a truck analyst with IHS Markit Consultancy.
     That was partly fuelled by a ban this year on the use of diesel trucks to transport coal at
northern ports in provinces such as Hebei and Shandong, and in the city of Tianjin.
    - INDIAN OIL DIESEL TERM: Indian Oil Corp awarded an October 2017 to March 2018 diesel term
contract to sell the cargoes to Chinese trader Unipec, trade sources said. 
    The term tender was for IOC to sell eight cargoes of 13,300 tonnes to 14,700 tonnes each of
0.2 percent sulphur gasoil and 1,100 tonnes each of 50ppm sulphur diesel to be loaded from
Haldia.
    Price details of the award could not immediately be confirmed but could be around minus 85
cents a barrel to IOC's price formula, one of the traders said. 
    - MRPL OFFERS DIESEL: India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) has offered
its second diesel cargo for October loading, trade sources said.
    Diesel demand in India was anticipated to rise at the end of monsoon season but has yet to
materialise enough to curb exports, traders said. 
    -INDIAN JET FUEL CARGOES: India's MRPL likely sold a November loading jet fuel cargo to
Vitol at a discount of $1.10 a barrel to Singapore quotes, while Essar Oil likely sold a
November-loading cargo to BP at a premium of 90 cents a barrel to Middle East quotes, traders
said. 
    - NEW LOAD POINT IN PLATTS PRICING: Oil price agency S&P Global Platts will include
ExxonMobil Singapore Chemical Plant's Banyan facility as a loading point in its Singapore
pricing process for gasoil and jet fuel from Nov. 1, it said in subscriber note on Monday.
    The facility was previously known as the Jurong Aromatics plant.
    This follows ExxonMobil Asia's acquisition of the facility from Jurong Aromatics Corp in
August. 
    From Nov. 1, sellers will be able to nominate the Banyan facility as a load point for
cargoes traded on a free-on-board (FOB) Straits basis, Platts said in the note.

SINGAPORE, Oct 6 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil and jet fuel cash differentials held steady on
Friday, though several refinery maintenance and outages in Asia and Europe are expected to boost
the margin for the fuel, trade sources said. 

    - SINGAPORE AIRLINES TO CUT FUEL CONSUMPTION: Singapore Airlines intends to cut fuel
consumption, review its supplier relationships and invest in digital technology under a
three-year transformation plan to boost its competitiveness, according to an internal
newsletter. [nL4N1MH16J]
    Singapore Airlines and Hong Kong-based rival Cathay Pacific Airways are struggling against
mounting international competition from Chinese and Middle Eastern rivals, without domestic
flights to underpin their earnings.
    In a September staff newsletter obtained by Reuters, CEO Goh Choon Phong said the airline
was working on 56 initiatives, which also included more self-service options for customers and
slashing in-flight food and beverage waste.
    It was also reviewing its organisational structure and reviewing its route network, he said.
    - TAX CUTS MAY PROVIDE BUFFER FOR INDIAN REFINERS: Credit Suisse said an excise duty
reduction on petrol and diesel and a likely cut in value-added tax will give buffer to oil
marketing companies (OMCs) until oil prices hit $65 per barrel. 
    Earlier this week, the oil ministry asked for a 5 pct decrease in additional state levy, a
day after the federal government trimmed factory gate tax on petrol and diesel by 2 rupees per
litre. 
    The brokerage said near-term margins could stay weak as OMCs pass on full tax-cut benefit,
but will normalise in the coming months. [nL4N1MH16N]
    - RUSSIAN OIL PRODUCT OUTPUT: Lukoil said on Friday that the output of oil products from its
largest refinery, Norsi in the Nizhny Novgorod region, was almost unaffected by a fire on
Thursday.
    But Russian pipeline monopoly Transneft said on Friday the fire could impact its monthly
supply schedule. Four people died as a result of the incident. [nL8N1MH237]
    - VITOL'S VIEW ON OIL INDUSTRY: The world's largest oil trader, Vitol, expects the oil
industry to shrink given the quickening pace of the global shift to electric cars and away from
fossil fuels, its chief executive said on Thursday. [nL8N1MG5TD]
    Vitol CEO Ian Taylor told an event at Chatham House in London that he saw oil demand peaking
around 2028-2030.
    Of more immediate concern for the industry is the low oil price <LCOc1>. The market has
shown signs of rebalancing, but Taylor said rising U.S. oil exports will put oil prices under
renewed pressure in 2018 although he said prices could recover towards $60-$65 a barrel in the
next two to three years.

high of 10.684 million barrels in the week to Oct. 4, the latest data from International
Enterprise showed. <O/SING1>
    India increased its gasoil shipments to Singapore to a total of about 267,000 tonnes from
about 148,000 tonnes the week before, the data showed.

units at its 404,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) Pernis oil refinery in the Netherlands, the company
said on the refinery website.

units involved. [nL8N1MF57A]

week to Thursday on high import levels, according to data from
Dutch consultancy PJK International.[ARA/]

due refinery outages in the region which have crimped regional
production, traders said.

night, the company said in a statement. Some units were shut
down, and there is increased flaring at the refinery, it
said.[nL8N1JQ2PG]

week, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said.

million tonnes in July from 1.417 million tonnes planned in

8.1 million tonnes, according to Thomson Reuters research.

after the draw in U.S. stocks.

to help bolster its crude oil trading into the Chinese market,
sources told Reuters.

Sinochem in London, has joined the Shell crude oil trading desk
in Singapore, the sources said.

qualified and well-connected staff for their Asia trading desks,
spurred on by the opening up of China's oil imports to include
independent refineries.

West African trading for Sinochem, did not immediately respond
to a request for comment.

to take a job with Statoil, but then opted for Shell. Statoil
declined to comment. 
    Companies last year began plucking staff from state giants
including Sinochem and CNPC to grab a larger share of the $50
million a day in new crude flowing into China, which many expect
to grow even further. [http://reut.rs/2xaab9L
]
    Sources in London said Zheng's connections and experience in
China drove Shell to poach him. Sources in Singapore said his
knowledge of West African oil was also a key qualification.

August from a year ago to about 983,500 barrels per day (bpd),
according to official customs data, while its Angolan imports
for the first eight months of 2017 hit 1.05 million bpd, a gain

SINGAPORE, Oct 4 (Reuters) - The low-sulphur diesel cash differential rose on Wednesday on
the back of tight supply of the fuel in the region, trade sources said.
    
    - DIESEL SHIPPED TO ARGENTINA: Oil trader Trafigura has provisionally the Grand Ace 5 to
ship ultra-low sulphur diesel from Bahrain to Argentina, shipping fixtures showed.

refinery shutdowns due to a hurricane could have made arbitrage economics for that route
profitable, traders said, though this could not be confirmed.
    - JAPAN'S EXPORTS OF DIESEL, JET FUEL: Japan's exports of jet fuel in the week to Sept. 30
more than doubled from the previous week, while its gasoil exports more than tripled, data from
Petroleum Association of Japan showed on Wednesday. <O/JAPAN1>
    The refinery run rate, however, fell to 87.6 percent in the week to Sept. 30 from 91 percent
in the previous week, the data showed. This could curb exports in the coming weeks.
    - INDIA CUTS TAX ON DIESEL: India on Tuesday cut the excise duty on petrol and diesel by 2
rupees a litre to protect retail consumers from higher global crude oil prices, a move analysts
said could widen the country's fiscal deficit.
    The cut in the petrol and diesel duties will cost 130 billion rupees ($1.99 billion) over
the next six months, the finance ministry said in a message on Twitter.

    By Nidhi Verma and Florence Tan
    NEW DELHI/SINGAPORE, Oct 3 (Reuters) - India's Reliance
Industries Ltd <RELI.NS> has purchased crude oil cargoes from
the United States for the first time, drawn by the lower price
for U.S. oil versus global benchmarks, three trade sources said
on Tuesday. 
    Reliance, the owner of the world's biggest refining complex
at Jamnagar, is joining state-run refiners Indian Oil Corp
<IOC.NS>, Bharat Petroleum Corp <BPCL.NS> and Hindustan
Petroleum Corp <HPCL.NS> in importing U.S. crude. The purchase
illustrates the vast reach of U.S. oil exports since the
government rescinded a decades-long ban at the end of
2015.[nL4N1M6434] [nL4N1KP3BL]
    For this purchase, Reliance bought 1 million barrels of West
Texas Intermediate (WTI) Midland and a similar-sized cargo of
Eagle Ford crude, both of which are expected to arrive in
November, the sources said.
    U.S. producer Occidental Petroleum Corp <OXY.N> sold the WTI
Midland cargo, they said.
    Reliance did not respond to Reuters' email seeking comments.
    There was also no reply to an emailed request for comment
from Occidental sent outside of U.S. business hours. 
    Opportunities for Indian refiners to import more U.S. crude
increased after the discount for West Texas Intermediate, the
benchmark for U.S. crude, to global benchmark Brent stretched to
its widest since 2015 during September. <CL-LCO1=R> [nL4N1LN2CI]
    State-run Indian refiners have bought a total 7.85 million
barrels of oil from the United States so far. [CRU/TENDA]
    India's imports of U.S. oil follows Indian Prime Minister
Narendra Modi's visit to Washington in June when President
Donald Trump said his country looked forward to exporting more
energy products to India.
    On Monday, Indian Oil, the country's top refiner, received
its parcel of the U.S. crude at the eastern port of Paradip, the
company said in a statement.
    Including the U.S. as a source for crude imports for
refiners will go a long way in mitigating the risk arising from
geo-political disruptions, Sanjay Sudhir, the joint secretary
for international cooperation at the oil ministry, said in the
Indian Oil statement.
    U.S. crude oil shipments to India have the potential to
boost bilateral trade by up to $2 billion, the U.S. embassy in
India said in a statement on Monday.

LONDON, Oct 2 (Reuters) - Benchmark European diesel refining
margins weakened along with the rest of the oil complex on
Monday, despite still tight supply throughout the Atlantic
basin.
    * Distillate supplies were slipping across Europe as imports
from the United States remained limited and shipments from Asia
and the Middle East were expected to stay flat on the month. 
    * U.S. Gulf Coast exports, a key source of Europe's diesel,
have ramped up as refineries return to normal operations
following Hurricane Harvey, but there is fierce competition for
the barrels from Latin American buyers, traders said.  
    * While more than 600,000 tonnes is now expected to arrive
on the route in October, this is roughly half of what had been
regularly arriving before the storm. 
    * Demand to export distillate cargoes from northwest Europe
to Latin American destinations such as Brazil and Argentina has
also continued, pulling some supply from the region. 
    * Exports of ultra-low-sulphur diesel from the Russian
Baltic Sea port of Primorsk could rise by 11 percent to 880,000
tonnes in October, up from the 770,000 tonnes initially planned
in September, three industry sources told Reuters on Monday.
[nL8N1MD4V5]
    * Sources had expected Russian exports, which fell in
September, to remain subdued due to seasonal maintenance. 
    * Europe's own production is limited by seasonal maintenance
despite strong margins that have encouraged those who can to
delay works.     
    * Hedge funds have accumulated a record bullish position in
middle distillates such as diesel, heating oil and gasoil,
anticipating stocks will be relatively tight this winter.

Thursday amid a surge in buying appetite from BP and Hin Leong for a second straight session.

in anticipation of a tightening in near-term supplies, or opportunistic buying amid lower outright
price levels from a week ago.

$1.85 a tonne, broker sources said.

about $2.75 a tonne, Reuters data showed.

seven cargoes, followed by Vitol with 60,000 tonnes in three cargoes and Total with two 20,000-tonne

Mercuria. [nL4N1MF2AF]

25-27 delivery, but sources said the second cargo was possibly not awarded.

Oct. 4, down 3 percent, or 107,000 tonnes, from the previous week, official data shows. [O/SING1]

eight-week low of 457,000 tonnes.

SINGAPORE, Oct 2 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differential slipped on Monday, but tight
supply of the fuel limited losses, especially ahead of several refinery maintenance that is
expected to curb supply further, industry sources said.

production at its Kochi refinery, two sources close to the matter said. [L4N1MD2J7]

(FCCU) at an older crude distillation unit (CDU) and the newly commissioned petrochemical fluid
catalytic cracker (PFCC) at the new CDU are curtailed, one of the sources said. 
      BPCL cancelled a gasoil sell tender as a result of the production shortage, a second
source said. [nL4N1MD2CK]   
    - GTL DIESEL: Qatar's Oryx GTL has offered up to two cargoes of gas-to-liquid (GTL) diesel
for loading in November and December, according to a tender document. 
      The company offered two cargoes of 40,000 tonnes each. The tender closes on Oct. 9 with
offers to remain valid for up to 72 hours. [nL4N1MD2EJ]
    - JAPAN REFINERIES: Japanese oil refiner Cosmo Oil Co said it shut the 75,000-bpd No. 1 CDU
at its 177,000-bpd Chiba refinery, east of Tokyo, on Sept. 30 for scheduled maintenance.
[nL4N1MD1RX] 
      The CDU is set to be shut for around 1-1/2 months, a company spokeswoman said.
      Japanese oil refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co said it plans to shut the sole 160,000-bpd No. 1
CDU at its Aichi refinery on Tuesday for scheduled maintenance. [nL4N1MD1SZ]
      The CDU is expected to restart around mid-November as earlier planned, a company spokesman
said.

SINGAPORE, Oct 10 (Reuters) - Cash premiums of Asia's 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil fell to a
near one-month low on Tuesday amid weaker deal values in the Platts pricing window, industry sources
said. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    In the paper markets, the Nov/Dec 380-cst time spread <FO380SGSDMc2> halted two sessions of
declines, edging up to $1.75 a tonne from a near-one-month low of $1.50 a tonne in the previous
session. The 380-cst Nov/Dec time spread was trading at a premium of $2.75 a tonne at the start of
the month. 
    Lower expectations of tight Singapore fuel oil supplies in the coming months has scaled back
some gains in 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums and time spreads which rose to multi-month highs in
late-September. [nL4N1M62GH] [nL4N1M33MG]

oil.

against 2.26 million tonnes in September.
    - Hin Leong has been the top buyer of fuel oil cargoes in the window this month with 320,000
tonnes, followed by BP with 300,000 tonnes. 
    - Mercuria topped the list of suppliers in October, having so far sold 480,000 tonnes, followed
by Vitol with 80,000 tonnes.

offer that closes on Oct. 11 and is valid to Oct. 13, industry sources said. [nL8N1ML2YQ]
    
    BUNKER MARKET
    - Shipping fuel suppliers are filing millions of dollars in claims over unpaid marine fuel bills
against now-defunct Singapore-based peer Universal Energy, formerly one of the city state's largest
bunker suppliers but which has now entered liquidation. [nL4N1ML2HZ]
    - Overall creditor claims against Universal Energy - which went into voluntary liquidation on
Oct. 3 - total to about $100 million, according to estimates from several industry sources and a
news report from oil pricing agency S&P Global Platts.
    - The case has sent shockwaves across Singapore's bunker fuel market, the world's biggest,
tightening credit as financiers become more wary of the sector, trading sources said.

SINGAPORE, Nov 23 (Reuters) - A lack of buying interest despite lower supplier offers relative
to the previous session for physical cargoes of 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil in the Singapore
trading window weighed on cash premiums of the mainstay fuel on Thursday. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    By contrast, relatively stronger bids for 180-cst fuel oil cargoes pushed cash differentials of
the fuel higher on Thursday but failed to result in any deals. <FO180-SIN-DIF>
    Higher deal values on Wednesday pushed 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums to a two-week high while
aggressive supplier offers for 180-cst cargoes dragged cash differentials of the 180-cst fuel to a
near two-week low. [nL3N1NS3AN]
    Meanwhile, Singapore onshore fuel oil stocks slipped to a seven week low over the past week
despite a near doubling of net imports into the city-state. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories slipped 0.5 percent, or 18,000 tonnes, to 3.51
million tonnes in the week to Nov. 22, official data shows. [O/SING1]
    - This came despite a 93 percent rise in net imports into Singapore to 830,000 tonnes; a
three-week high. 
    - In the previous week, net imports were at a three-month low of 430,000 tonnes. [nL3N1NM2XO]
    - Onshore fuel oil inventories are currently 1.6 percent lower from their year-ago levels. 
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to China topped the weekly list (368,000 tonnes); followed
by Hong Kong (149,000 tonnes) and Bangladesh (95,000 tonnes).
    - The largest Singapore net imports originated from Russia (255,000 tonnes); followed by the
U.S. (227,000 tonnes), Iran (167,000 tonnes), and the Netherlands (106,000 tonnes). 
    - Singapore imports from Iran resumed after a four-week absence while imports from Brazil
(101,000 tonnes) were at a six-month high. 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - No cargo trades were reported in the Platts window on Thursday for the first time since Oct.
20.
    - A total of 1.14 million tonnes of fuel oil have traded in the window in November so far,
against 1.56 million tonnes in October and 1.04 million tonnes in November last year.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - The UAE's Adnoc has awarded at least three of four cargoes of 70-80-cst straight-run fuel oil
(SRFO) with a maximum 1.2 sulphur content, each 90,000 tonnes in volume, loading from its Ruwais
refinery at premiums of about $25-$29 a tonne to Singapore 180-cst fuel oil quotes, industry sources
said. 
    - GS Caltex was awarded two cargoes and Mercuria won one similar cargo, sources said, but the
result of the fourth cargo remained unknown.
    - The loading dates of the cargoes are Dec. 10-12, 15-17, 20-22 and 25-27. 
    - Korean refiner SK Energy did not bid for Adnoc's latest SRFO offering since it had lifted a
similar cargo in November, a source with knowledge of the matter said. 
    - Taiwan's Formosa sold up to 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4 percent sulphur
content loading from Mailiao on Dec. 4-6 to Trafigura at an unknown price level, sources said.

SINGAPORE, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Supply of diesel and jet fuel remained in balance with spot
demand, keeping cash differentials for both fuels in check, though expectations of higher
exports from China next year could weigh, traders said on Monday. 
    
    - INDIA OFFERS JET FUEL: India's Essar Oil has offered 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel for loading
from Vadinar over Dec. 25 to 29 in a tender that closes on Nov. 29. 
      The company last offered an early December loading cargo, though results of that tender
were not immediately available. 
    - JORDAN BUYS GASOIL: Jordan Petroleum Refinery Company buys over 4 million barrels of
gasoil and gasoline for delivery over January to June, 2018 from Vitol, traders said.
[L3N1NX32A]
      The company bought 3.35 million barrels of 10ppm sulphur gasoil at a premium of $3.92 a
barrel over Middle East 500ppm sulphur gasoil quotes, they said. 
      BB Energy and Total also participated in the tender, one of them said.     
    - PAKISTAN SEEKS GASOIL, JET FUEL: Pakistan State Oil is seeking unspecified volumes of jet
fuel and gasoil for delivery in February, traders said.
    - INDIA'S BPCL CANCELS TENDER: India's Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPC) has cancelled a
tender offering 35,000 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur diesel for Dec. 5 to 7 loading from Mumbai due to
low bids and a change in loading program, an industry source said.
      The refiner will likely re-issue the tender, the source added.
      India's diesel demand has recovered slightly post-monsoon but is still no where near its
peak, and is prompting continued exports of the fuel, the source said. 
    - THAILAND SELLS GASOIL: Thailand's PTT likely sold 35,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil
for Dec. 7 to 11 loading at a premium of about 40 cents a barrel, traders said. 
      The Thai refiner last sold a smaller sized cargo of 15,000 tonnes of the fuel for
mid-November loading at a discount of 5 to 10 cents a barrel, they added. Both results could not
be confirmed. 
    - CHINA ISSUES MORE CRUDE IMPORT QUOTA: China has issued crude oil import quotas for 2017 of
1.5 million tonnes to three independent refiners, three sources familiar with the situation said
on Saturday, a sign Beijing is easing its policy towards these companies sometimes known as
teapots. [nL3N1NV078] 
      The quotas are the latest sign that the government is relaxing its policies towards the
independent refiners after cutting import quotas and banning them from exporting fuel earlier
this year.

sessions of losses after expectations of ample near-term supplies of the industrial fuel dampened
sentiment, industry sources said.

minus $5.12 a barrel. On Friday, the front-month crack sank to a seven-month low of minus $5.26 a
barrel. <FO180BRTCKMc1>
    Meanwhile, improved buying interest for spot physical cargoes of 380-cst fuel oil helped lift
cash premiums of the fuel away from a near two-week low it reached on Friday. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
