SINGAPORE, Nov 8 (Reuters) - The East-West (EW) arbitrage spread of 380-cst fuel oil narrowed on
Wednesday amid no shortage of fuel oil inflows into Singapore as well as weaker fuel oil prices in the
city-state relative to Rotterdam prices, industry sources said.
    
    ARBITRAGE 
    - The December 380-cst EW arbitrage spread narrowed to about $19.75 a barrel on Wednesday, down
from about $20.25 a barrel in the previous session, broker sources said.
    - Despite the narrower spread, sources said arbitrage opportunities between northwest Europe and
Singapore remain 'workable', but is unlikely to attract many large fixtures amid ample near-term
inventories and as the year draws to an end. 
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for November are expected to close at around month-average
levels for the first time in two months, notionally assessed at 6.3-6.4 million tonnes for the month,
assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed. [nPGEG3SRFa]
    - The arbitrage flows are boosted by recovering Western arrivals, near record-high inflows from
the Middle East and 11-month high intra-Asia volumes, the assessment said. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil inventories fell 743,000 barrels (or about 111,000
tonnes) to 8.641 million barrels (1.29 million tonnes) in the week to Nov. 6, data via S&P Global
Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - Snapping three straight weeks of inventory builds, Fujairah fuel oil inventories are now at a
four-week low. 
    - Weekly Fujairah fuel oil inventories averaged 10.4 million barrels (or 1.55 million tonnes)
since records began at the start of the year.
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Four cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel
oil and 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Pakistan's PSO is seeking to import up to 565,000 tonnes of fuel oil for delivery in January,
sources said. [nL3N1NE34W]
    The tender seeks up to import up to seven 65,000 tonne cargoes of high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO)
into port Qasim on an FOB basis in January and up to two 55,000-tonne cargoes of low-sulphur fuel oil
(LSFO) into Karachi on a CFR basis between Dec. 25 and Jan. 31.
    PSO's import tender closes, and is valid until, Dec. 6.
    - PSO recently concluded its import requirements for December, lifting only three of the nine
cargoes it initially sought. [nL3N1NC3HQ]
    
    LNG BUNKER FUELS
    - Container shipping giant CMA CGM said on Tuesday it would use liquefied natural gas to power
nine extra-large vessels it has ordered, in a first for an industry grappling with how to comply with
tougher rules on emissions. [nL5N1ND6R1]
    - Shell Trading (US) Company announced late on Tuesday it has finalised a long-term charter
agreement with Q-LNG Transport LLC for an LNG bunker barge with a capacity to carry 4,000 cubic meters
of LNG fuel. [nL3N1NE23M]
    - The ocean-going LNG bunker barge, the first of its kind to be based in the U.S., will supply LNG
to marine customers along the southern East Coast of the U.S. and support growing cruise line demand
for LNG marine fuel, it said in a statement.

SINGAPORE, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Cash premiums for Asia's 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil cargoes slipped
to a near one-month low on Thursday amid lower deal values and weaker offers when compared with the
previous session. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    This came as Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories snapped four weeks of builds, falling 8.1
percent, or 309,000 tonnes, from previous week to a total of 3.53 million tonnes in the week to Nov. 8,
official data shows. [O/SING1]
        
    INVENTORIES
    - The decline in inventories over the past week was the largest volume change in weekly stocks
since the week to Sept. 13 when inventories fell 449,000 tonnes. [nL4N1LV3C6]
    - Weekly net imports into Singapore were down 18.6 percent from a week earlier to 0.72 million
tonnes, a four-week low.
    - Despite the inventory decline, current fuel oil stocks are 12.7 percent higher year-on-year.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Hong Kong topped the weekly list (162,000 tonnes);
followed by China (110,000 tonnes) and Vietnam (23,000 tonnes).
    - The largest Singapore net imports originated from Russia (230,000 tonnes); followed by Malaysia
(138,000 tonnes), Iraq (125,000 tonnes), and India (89,000 tonnes).
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Two cargo trades were reported in the Platts window totalling 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Glencore bought the two 20,000-tonne cargoes from Vitol at a premium of 75 cents a tonne to
Singapore 380-cst quotes, sources said. 
    - By comparison, two 380-cst fuel oil cargoes trades on Wednesday were reported in the window at
premiums of $1 a tonne and $1.25 a tonne to Singapore 380-cst quotes. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - In a rare move, Thailand's PTT bought 80,000 tonnes-90,000 tonnes of 650-cst to 700-cst
high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) from Saudi's Samref refinery Yanbu loading over Nov. 17-21, industry
sources said. [nL3N1NF273]
    - The pricing of the cargo, its discharge destination and PTT's reason for the purchase could not
be confirmed.
    - Saudi's Sasref refinery, a joint-venture between Saudi Aramco and Shell, sold up to 80,000 tonnes
of 380-cst HSFO loading in Jubail over Nov. 15-18 to Shell at an unknown price, sources said. 
    - Shell placed on subjects the Eagle Baltimore aframax tanker to load 80,000 tonnes of fuel oil
from Jubail on Nov. 18 for discharge into Fujairah on the following day, Reuters Eikon ship tracking
data shows.
    
    SAUDI FLOWS
    - While not unusual for this time of year, fuel oil exports from Saudi refineries, including those
in Rabigh, Jubail and Samref have been on the rise in recent weeks as domestic demand for power
generation falls with the passing of summer, industry sources said. 
    - Eikon ship tracking data shows the Aramco Trading Company (ATC) chartered aframax, the M.T. Jag
Lavanya, carrying up to 80,000 tonnes of HSFO from the Rabigh refinery in Saudi, due for arrival in
Singapore by Nov. 11.

    SINGAPORE, Dec 1 (Reuters) - A ship carrying diesel has left
Saudi Arabia heading towards New York for the first time in more
than two years, according to Thomson Reuters Eikon ship tracking
data and traders.

of diesel, left Yanbu in Saudi Arabia on Nov. 27 with New York
as its destination, the Eikon data shows.
    If the ship unloads in New York, this will be the first time
since February 2015 the United States has imported diesel from
Saudi Arabia, U.S. Energy Information Administration data shows.
    The tanker is one of several carrying diesel from other
origins heading to the New York Harbour trading hub after a
sharp drop in East Coast stocks and winter's approach led to a
rally in prices for the fuel. [nL8N1NZ5MX] 
    Benchmark U.S. diesel prices <HOc1> hit a more than two-year
high on Nov. 24, opening a number of rare arbitrage options,
according to traders.

distillate inventories <DST-NDS-T-EIA>, a three-year low,
according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.
    U.S. East Coast inventories <DST-OUT-1-EIA> sank below
five-year lows in late October, following damage from the
devastating Atlantic hurricane season and strong U.S. and
foreign demand. The fuel stocks later rebounded, but still fell
below 2016 levels last week. 
    Profits from shipping diesel cargo from Saudi Arabia to New
York were higher than to Europe, which could have prompted the
rare shipment, a middle distillates trader said.
    The cargo loaded from Saudi Arabia's Yanbu Aramco Sinopec
Refining Co (Yasref), which is majority owned by oil giant Saudi
Aramco <IPO-ARMO.SE>. China's Sinopec <600028.SS> holds the
remaining stake. 
    Refinery officials were not available for comment outside
normal Middle East office hours. 
    The bulk of diesel imports into the United States over April
to September this year have come from Canada, the latest EIA
data showed. There are no diesel shipments from the Middle East

SINGAPORE, Dec 5 (Reuters) - Cash differentials of Asia's 180-cst and 380-cst high-sulphur fuel
oil fell to multi-session lows on Tuesday amid a build-up in supplier selling pressure which saw
physical trade volumes climb to a two-month high, industry sources said. 
    Some suppliers were keen to clear their fuel oil inventories as the calendar year draws to a
close, traders said. 
    Cash premiums of the mainstay 380-cst slipped to 42 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes, their
lowest since Sept. 12. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    Cash differentials of 180-cst fuel oil fell to a two-week low of minus 27 cents a tonne to
Singapore quotes on Tuesday, down from a premium of 38 cents a tonne on Monday. <FO180-SIN-DIF>
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Ten cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 80,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel
oil along with 120,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Of the ten deals, eight were suppliers hitting buyers bids, suggesting suppliers were keen to
sell their cargoes, industry participants said. 
    - In another sign of strong interest to sell physical fuel oil cargoes, the premiums paid for
physical cargoes at the end of the trading window were generally lower than the premiums paid for
cargoes at the start of the trading window.
    - Mercuria bought nine of the ten cargoes. Vitol bought one. 
    - Total and Gunvor each sold three cargoes, followed by Shell which supplied two cargoes.
Glencore and Reliance each sold one cargo. 
    - Tuesday's trade volumes are the highest since Oct. 5 when a total of 280,000 tonnes of fuel
oil exchanged hands in the Singapore trading window. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details.

    - Taiwan's CPC is seeking 40,000 tonnes or 80,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 3.5%
sulphur content for delivery into Kaohsiung in January in a tender closing on Dec. 5 and valid until
Dec . 7-8, sources said. 
    - Taiwan's Formosa is offering up to 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4 percent
sulphur content loading from Mailiao on Dec. 19-21 in a tender closing on Dec. 5 with same day

    - India's Reliance is offering up to 40,000 tonnes of carbon-black feedstock (CBFS) with a
maximum 1.2 percent sulphur content for Dec. 26-27 loading from Sikka, sources said.
    - Reliance previously offered a similar CBFS cargo loading from Sikka on Dec. 7-8 which may have
been awarded to Saudi's ATC at an unknown price level, sources said.

SINGAPORE, Dec 7 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil and jet fuel cash differentials remained
steady on Thursday as spot demand from Vietnam offset increased inventory in Singapore, traders
said.
    
   -  VIETNAM SEEKS GASOIL: Vietnam's Petrolimex is seeking 35,000 tonnes of 10ppm sulphur
diesel for loading in late December, trade sources said. 
      The spot requirement is on top of the 105,000 tonnes of gasoil the company already bought
for December, they added.
    
    - SOUTH KOREAN TERM: South Korean refiners may have concluded their term negotiations to
sell gasoil for next year, traders said.
      Hyundai Oilbank likely sold its 10ppm sulphur diesel at a discount of 10 cents a barrel to
the 10ppm sulphur gasoil Singapore quotes while GS Caltex may have concluded its 2018 term to
sell 500ppm sulphur gasoil at a discount of 60 cents a barrel to 10ppm sulphur gasoil quotes,
they added.
      This, however, could not immediately be confirmed. 
    
    - SINGAPORE STOCKS: Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks edged higher by 1 percent
to a two-week high of 11.251 million barrels in the week to Dec. 6, latest data from
International Enterprise showed. <O/SING1>
      India, China and South Korea increased their diesel exports to Singapore from a week ago
while Iran shipped about 57,000 tonnes of diesel to the city-state from none the previous week,
the data showed. 
      About 41,000 tonnes of diesel was shipped from Singapore to Brazil last week in an unusual
move, the data showed.   
    
    - CAO SHIPS JET FUEL TO U.S.: China Aviation Oil has placed the Citrus Express on subs to
ship 40,000 tonnes of jet fuel from Dalian to the U.S. west coast on Dec. 21, shipping fixtures
showed.    
    
    - PAKISTAN SEEKS GASOIL: Pakistan State Oil is seeking a 500ppm sulphur gasoil cargo for
delivery into Karachi over Dec. 21 to 23 and a similar cargo for delivery over Jan. 12 to 31,
traders said.
      This is in addition to two cargoes it had requested earlier for delivery in February, they
added.
      Pakistan's high fuel oil inventory due to a shift towards liquefied natural gas (LNG) in
the power sector may have caused the refineries to lower run rates in the country prompting the
imports, traders said, though this could not immediately be confirmed.

SINGAPORE, May 31 (Reuters) - Spot demand from Thailand boosted cash differentials for low
sulphur diesel on Wednesday, trade sources said, while spot demand from Indonesia also supported
higher sulphur gasoil and jet fuel.  
    
    - THAILAND SPOT DEMAND: Thailand's PTT and Star Petroleum Refining (SPRC) are seeking spot
gasoil cargoes for delivery in June, which in turn is helping to support cash differentials for
the 10ppm sulphur diesel, traders said.
    PTT is seeking 30,000 tonnes of 45ppm sulphur diesel for delivery over June 7 to 15 and SPRC
is seeking 30,000 tonnes of the fuel for delivery in June, traders said. [nL3N1IX2DC]
    PTT is seeking gasoil due to a refinery maintenance planned in June, a source close to the
matter said. The refinery will shut unspecific units for 10 to 15 days, the source added.
    The company has been importing gasoil since February due to an earlier maintenance in April
or May, the source said. 
    Thailand's Bangchak Corp has shut a hydrogen unit and a hydrocracking unit for 22 days for
planned maintenance from May 19 to June 9, the company said. [nL3N1IX2LY]
    
    - INDIAN GASOIL TENDER: India's Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd (HPCL) is likely to have bought
65,000 tonnes of 40ppm sulphur diesel for delivery into Mundra over June 15 to 20 from Vitol at
a premium of between $2.70 and $3.20 a barrel to Middle East quotes, traders said, though this
could not be confirmed with the relevant companies.
    
    - AFRICAN SPOT PURCHASES: Tanzania's Petroleum Bulk Procurement Agency will import 64,285
tonnes of 50ppm sulphur diesel for delivery over July 1 to 3 and 64,284 tonnes of the fuel for
delivery over July 18 to 20 from Addax Energy at premiums of $17.94 a tonne over Middle East
quotes, traders said. 
     It will also import 22,464 tonnes of jet fuel and kerosene for delivery over July 10 to 12
from Sahara Energy at $59.45 a tonne above Middle East quotes, they said. 
     Kenyan oil importers will import 78,664 tonnes of jet fuel and 225,883 tonnes of 50ppm
sulphur diesel for delivery over June to August from Aspam Energy, KenolKobil, Kencor and Galana
Oil, traders said. 
     They are likely to pay a premium of $2.99 a tonne above Middle East quotes for the jet fuel
cargo and premiums ranging from $7.54 to $25.80 a tonne for the gasoil cargoes, the traders
added. <MDIS/TENDA>

cargoes for delivery in June likely to meet domestic shortages during planned refinery
maintenance, traders said. <MDIS/TENDA> <REF/A>

month though it was up 3 percent from the same period last year, data from Japan's Ministry of
Economy, Trade and Industry showed on Wednesday. [nL3N1IX1PP]

    SINGAPORE, May 31 (Reuters) - The front-month East-West arbitrage spread remained
firmly shut on Wednesday as fuel oil prices in the Rotterdam hub were relatively stronger
than those in Singapore, making shipments into the city-state uneconomical. 
    While the tight arbitrage spread could potentially lead to fewer Western arbitrage
arrivals over the near term, industry sources said the spread could be forced wider if fuel
oil supplies in Singapore turned out to be lower than expected. 
    
    SWAPS MARKET
    - Broker sources pegged the June East-West spread at about $10 a tonne, and the July
spread at about $13 a tonne on Wednesday.
    - In Europe, the 380-cst June/July Rotterdam barge spread was pegged at a premium of
about $1 a tonne, well above the corresponding contract in Singapore which was trading at a
discount of about minus $1 a tonne. 
    - Despite falling onshore fuel oil inventories in Singapore, the weakness in
Singapore's 380-cst prompt month time spreads over the past two weeks has been largely
attributed to ample inventories of the fuel stored aboard ships. 
    - Industry sources estimated about 2 million tonnes of fuel oil are stored in VLCCs
around Singapore as a result of active physical trade in the Platts window since March. 

    ARBITRAGE ARRIVALS    
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for May closed lower than expected, at 6 to 6.1
million tonnes, down from earlier expectations of around 6.5 million tonnes, assessments by
Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed. [nPGE0sPnga]
    - But after 5 months of above-average supplies coming into Singapore, sentiment here
has turned more bearish, prompting traders to delay May arrivals into June, or redirect
them elsewhere.
    - Despite being lower-than-expected, the May arrivals are still higher than last year's
average of 5.9 to 6 million tonnes.

data showed.

    * A flurry of offers in the Platts window showed sellers

SINGAPORE, Feb 21 (Reuters) - Asia's jet fuel crack held above $15 a barrel on Wednesday versus
about $12 from a year ago, making it the most profitable refined oil product for refiners as
supplies remain tight. 
    - A prolonged cold spell in Japan and strong demand for air travel have sustained the jet fuel
bull-run which started this year. 
    - In Japan for instance, firm demand for kerosene used for heating persisted. 
    - Official data showed Japan's kerosene stocks fell 130,000 barrels to 7.9 million barrels in
the week to Feb. 17, the lowest stock level since March 2017. [nL4N1QB0T2]
    - The fall in kerosene inventories took place despite higher refinery run rates, the data
showed. 
    - Although kerosene is not used as a fuel for airplanes like jet fuel, refiners typically have
to reduce jet fuel supply yield in order to obtain a higher amount of kerosene. 
    - Traders expect jet fuel supplies to remained squeezed even after the cold spell as refineries
are about the begin their maintenance season, starting in South Korea this month. [REF/A]
    - Japan's JXTG has begun maintenance at a crude distillate unit (CDU) in Marifu since late last
month. 
    - In total, Japan is expected to shut 14 out of 29 CDUs for maintenance this year. [nL4N1QA0U9]
        
    * INDIA EXPORTS: India exported about 2.7 million tonnes of diesel in January, down 200,000
tonnes versus December but slightly higher than in November, official data showed. [nL4N1QA29Z]
    
    * INVENTORIES: Middle distillates stocks held in the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone were at a
three-week high of 2.51 million barrels in the week ended Feb. 19, data from S&P Global Platts
showed. [nL4N1QB2FF]
    - U.S. distillate inventories <USOILD=ECI>, which include heating oil and diesel fuel, were
seen down 1.6 million barrels last week, a preliminary Reuters poll showed on Tuesday. [nL4N1QA3SO]

SINGAPORE, Sept 19 (Reuters) - Asia's cash premiums for gasoil with 10 ppm sulphur content
rose to their highest levels of this year on Wednesday buoyed by stronger demand, while the
front-month spread widened its backwardated structure.
    Cash premiums for 10ppm gasoil <GO10-SIN-DIF> climbed to 77 cents a barrel to Singapore
quotes, the highest since S&P Global Platts switched the benchmarks in Asian gasoil grades last
January to maximum sulphur content of 10 ppm sulphur, from 500 ppm sulphur previously.  The
premiums were at 60 cents a barrel on Tuesday. 
    The refining margins, or cracks for 10 ppm gasoil <GO10SGCKMc1>, which has fallen about 9
percent since hitting a near three-year high a couple of weeks ago, rose to $15.85 a barrel over
Dubai crude during Asian trading hours, compared with $15.62 a barrel on Tuesday.
    The Oct/Nov time spread widened to 80 cents a barrel, from 72 cents a barrel on Tuesday.
    Backwardation, when the front-month contract is more expensive than subsequent months, is
usually seen as a sign that the market is rebalancing and prices are likely to head higher in
future months.
    There is firm buying interest for gasoil, especially in the physical market, and the
upcoming fourth quarter typically being the strongest for middle distillates, the fundamentals
should remain supported in the short-term, trade sources said.  
    Meanwhile, cash discounts for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> narrowed to 8 cents a barrel to
Singapore quotes on Wednesday, after a stronger physical deal in the Singapore window. On
Tuesday, the cash discounts were at 16 cents per barrel.
    Jet fuel refining margins <JETSGCKMc1> climbed to $15.23 a barrel over Dubai crude on
Wednesday, up from $15.04 a barrel on Tuesday.
 
        
    FUJAIRAH STOCKS
    - Middle distillates inventories in the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) rose about 0.1
percent, or 6,000 barrels from a week ago in the week to Sept. 17, data via S&P Global Platts
showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - Fujairah middle distillate stocks were at 4.18 million barrels in the week ended Monday,
the highest weekly levels since July last year.
    - Since the start of the year, middle distillate inventories in the Fujairah oil hub have
averaged 2.7 million barrels a week, compared with a weekly average of about 3.3 million barrels
in 2017, Reuters calculations showed.
    - Compared with year-ago levels, weekly Fujairah middle distillate inventories were about 72
percent higher.
    
    
    API INVENTORY DATA
    - U.S. crude stocks rose last week, while gasoline inventories decreased and distillate
stocks built, industry group the American Petroleum Institute said on Tuesday. [nZXN04EA00]
    - Distillate fuels stockpiles, which include diesel and heating oil, rose by 1.5 million
barrels, compared with expectations for a 651,000-barrel gain, the API data showed. [API/S]

LONDON, Sept 19 (Reuters) - Spot trade was limited on
Wednesday despite BP bids in the window, while November Nigerian
loading programmes emerged. 
    
    * BP returned to the window bidding for cargoes of Forcados
up to dated Brent plus $1.65 a barrel and Qua Iboe to dated
Brent plus $1.55 a barrel, within the range of the last few
days.
    * November loading programmes for Nigerian grades began to
emerge with Qua Iboe showing a rise to eight cargoes, or 253,000
barrels per day, up from 183,000 bpd in October.
    * Other programmes to emerge were Erha, Agbami, Yoho, Okono
and Escravos. [nL9N1UC00C]
    * Traders were still waiting for Angolan allocations in
November but state firm Sonangol was said to have four spot
cargoes available for the month.

    * Oil pricing agency S&P Global Platts has moved closer to
revamping its dated Brent benchmark, launching new price
assessments for two grades of U.S. crude in Europe in response
to the swell of imports into the region. [nL8N1W52CK]
    * Trade finance could be revolutionised with the launch of
blockchain platform komgo SA, which is due to go live before the
end of the year. It is backed by Royal Dutch Shell and trading
firms Mercuria Group and Gunvor Group, among many others.
[nL8N1W541L]
    
    TENDERS
    * IOC was believed to have awarded a tender to purchase a
West African grade to Equinor and Chevron, traders said.
    * Thailand's PTT is looking for 300,000 to 1 million barrels
of light sweet crude for delivery between Nov. 25 and Dec. 20.
The results are due on Thursday.
    * Taiwan's CPC issued a tender to purchase an unspecified
amount of light sweet crude for delivery in November. The tender
closes on Tuesday, with results due on Thursday.
    * Indonesia's Pertamina issued a tender to buy two 600,000
barrel cargoes of light sweet crude for delivery over Nov. 1-7
or Nov. 14-21. The size of the tender made a WAF grade an
unlikely choice, traders said.

northwest Europe weakened on Tuesday as supplies in the region
were seen rising.

recent days, traders said.

LONDON, June 8 (Reuters) - Global oil oversupply could take
up to 18 months to clear even if supply swings into a deficit of
1 million barrels per day, BP Chief Economist Spencer Dale said
on Wednesday.
    He said the market was expected to achieve a balance between
production and consumption in the second half of 2016. 
    But there has been a massive stock build of about 350
million barrels in developed economies and a similar number in
emerging economies, Dale said.

some 12 to 18 months to clear, he told reporters ahead of the
release of BP's Statistical Review of World Energy.
    Oil prices have fallen by more than half over the past two
years due to an oversupply estimated at nearly 2 million barrels
per day.

LONDON, June 7 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe fell to their lowest in nearly a month on
Tuesday as arbitrage to the United States narrowed and Nigerian
imports appeared under threat.     
        
    * Strikes at French refineries will continue until Friday,
CGT union officials said, scuppering Total's plans to restart
operations at the Grandpuits, Gonfreville and Feyzin refineries,
all of which have been offline since late May. [nP6N0X501W]
[nL8N18Y2Q8]
    * The delay should have been supportive to gasoline cracks,
as it postponed France's return as a net gasoline exporter, but
traders said narrowing arbitrage to the United States put
Europe's gasoline under downward pressure. 
    * U.S. gasoline margins <RB-CL1=R> saw their largest daily
decline in nearly four months on Monday on fears that resurgent
fuel imports will flood a saturated market. The crack is at its
lowest seasonal level in five years. [nL3N18M4U7]    
    * While around 800,000 tonnes of gasoline are set to arrive
in the U.S. in June from Europe, new bookings are becoming
difficult due to falling prices in the States. 
    * Exports heading to Nigeria, the largest West African
consumer of transportation fuels, had also gone quiet due to
currency problems that prevented independent importers from
buying cargoes.  
    * The return of units worldwide from refinery maintenance is
also expected to pressure margins, with Morgan Stanley
estimating that around 2.7 million barrels per day of refining
capacity is set to return from May to June, and an additional 2
million bpd will return in July.

SINGAPORE, Jan 24 (Reuters) - Planned refinery maintenance in Indonesia and an unplanned
outage in Japan are keeping cash differentials supported for gasoil and jet fuel in Asia, trade
sources said. 
    Pertamina shut down its Balongan refinery on Monday, with the restart scheduled for Feb. 23,
Toharso, its refinery director said. [nJ9N1EZ00Q]
    It is seeking 1.2 million barrels of gasoil for delivery in February, traders said. 
    Oil refiner TonenGeneral Sekiyu KK said on Tuesday a fire at its Wakayama refinery in
western Japan was extinguished after 40 hours and output remains constrained at the facility.
[nL4N1FE1ML]
    Output remained at a lower-than-normal level as of Tuesday, a company spokeswoman said,
without giving a concrete operating rate.
    Asian gasoil margins are expected to firm from March when several refineries undergo
maintenance, traders said.
    Pertamina's Balikpapan refinery is scheduled to close in April, while the plants in Cilacap
and Dumai will be shut down in the second half of 2017, he added.
    Osaka International Refining Co Ltd will conduct scheduled maintenance on the 115,000
barrels per day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) at its Osaka refinery from March 11 to April
1, an industry source familiar with the matter said on Tuesday. [nL4N1FE2FL]    
     ADNOC's refining operations have likely stabilised with the restart of a crude distillation
unit following a fire earlier this month, traders said.
    At least two ships have been provisionally booked by ST Shipping and Mena Energy to load
diesel from Ruwais in late January, shipping fixtures showed.

LONDON, Jan 19 (Reuters) - Diesel refining margins in
northwest Europe edged higher on Thursday as arbitrage from the
U.S. Gulf appeared set to fall.
        
    * U.S. distillate stockpiles, which include diesel and
heating oil, fell by 1.0 million barrels, versus expectations
for a 162,000 barrels increase, Energy Information
Administration data showed. [nL1N1F916W]
    * Arbitrage from the U.S. Gulf into Europe had already been
limited to around 700,000 barrels in January, and the stock draw
could further limit shipments to Europe. 
    * Low water levels along the Rhine river, a key passageway
from Europe's import hubs to consumers in Germany and
Switzerland, have prevented barges from sailing to buyers fully
laden. <WL-KAUB>
    * The issue has kept buyers in mainland Europe from taking
new deliveries, and led to building stocks in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp import hub. Stocks this week rose by
nearly 10 percent to 3.224 million tonnes, according to Dutch
consultancy PJK International. [nL5N1F95T4]
    * The ARA builds have weighed on distillate margins in the
hub, but profits at inland refineries in Switzerland and Germany
are booming due to the Rhine problems, sources said. 
    * German consumer heating oil stocks fell to 57 percent of
tank capacity at start of January, down from 60 percent at the
beginning of December, data from a trade source showed on
Thursday. [nL5N1F92WV][O/GEXP]
    * The January figure is the second month of declines, and is
two percentage points below the five-year average of 59 percent
of tank capacity.
    * A cold snap drove consumption in inland Europe and also
the Mediterranean, where several large tankers, including the
110,000 tonne Navig8 Goal are preparing to discharge.     
    * Traders said if the Rhine issues persist, more cargoes
could leave ARA for the Mediterranean or elsewhere.

MOSCOW, Jan 26 (Reuters) - Export offer prices for Turkish
steel rebar fell sharply after a slump in the price of imported
steel scrap in Turkey.
    Turkish rebar is offered for export at $410-$420 per tonne
FOB Turkey on an actual weight basis, Reuters monitoring showed.
    Turkish suppliers tried to negotiate much higher prices with
buyers in the United Arab Emirates a week ago, but had no
success. [nL5N1F82HM].
    Prices of billet and rebar went down after the collapse of
prices for scrap bought by Turkish steel mills. [nL5N1FG29T]
[nL5N1FF55J]
    Middle Eastern buyers of Turkish rebar expect a further fall
in prices and are reluctant to buy now, industry sources said.
   Emirates Steel Industries, a rebar producer in the UAE,
reportedly postponed a decision on February prices due to market
volatility. The company does not want to cut prices, but
understands that traders will go for Turkish products if they do
not cut, a source in the Middle East told Reuters.

    SINGAPORE, Jan 27 (Reuters) - The prompt-month time spreads of 380-cst fuel oil edged up on
Friday but ended the week sharply lower after reaching several multi-month lows over the week,
dragged down by selling pressure amid expectations of rising prompt supplies. 
    Some traders however said the recent downward pressure on the fuel oil complex was to some
extent exaggerated given the small changes in Singapore onshore inventories of the fuel over the
past two weeks, as well as expectations of lower arbitrage supplies in February that would have
to meet steady demand for the industrial fuel used in marine fuels and power generation.
[O/SING1]
    The Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) traded Feb/March time spread for the 380-cst fuel
narrowed their discount to 25 cents a tonne from Thursday's settlement of minus 50 cents a tonne
by 1330 Singapore time (0630 GMT), industry sources said.
    Asia's fuel oil market concluded trading four hours earlier than usual at 1230 Singapore
time (0430 GMT) on Friday ahead of the lunar new year holidays that begin Saturday. 
    According to Reuters data, the 380-cst Feb/March contract <FO380SGSDMc1> swayed from a $1.25
a tonne premium at the start of the week, to a 50 cent a tonne discount on Friday while setting
three multi-month lows along way.
    On Friday, the discount on the Feb/March contract was at its widest since Oct. 6. 
    In physical markets, aggressive supplier offers saw cash premiums of 380-cst fuel
<FO380-SIN-DIF> sink to 7 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes, down 90 cents a tonne from the
previous session, their lowest since Oct. 18.
    Four cash deals were reported in the Platts window totalling 80,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel
oil, industry source said.
    Sources said cargo trades of the 380-cst fuel were concluded at lower premiums on Friday,
compared with Thursday, ranging between minus 25 cents a tonne to plus $1.70 a tonne to
Singapore quotes. 
    
    ARA INVENTORIES 
    Fuel oil stocks in independently held storage in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub
fell to a twelve-week low of 619,000 tonnes in the week to Thursday, data from Dutch consultancy
PJK International showed. [ARA/]
    ARA residual fuel inventories <STK-FO-ARA> were 12.3 percent lower from the previous week's
total of 706,000 tonnes, marking three consecutive weeks of declines.

MOSCOW, Jan 26 (Reuters) - Steel billet from CIS is being
offered to Turkish buyers at lower prices as imported steel
scrap prices drop in Turkey, industry sources said.
    A Ukrainian supplier, which offered billet to buyers in
Turkey at just above $380 per tonne FOB ��Azov Sea last week,
lowered its offer to $370 FOB on Wednesday, a Turkish trader
told Reuters.
    Another international trader said he had seen offers from
Russia at $380 per tonne FOB Black Sea. A week earlier, the
upper limit of offers was $410 per tonne FOB.
    Earlier this week, the market was hit by a sharp decline in
prices for imported steel scrap in Turkey amid the depreciation
of the Turkish lira [nL5N1FE1K7]. The decline in scrap prices
continued on Wednesday. [nL5N1FF55J].
    Lower prices of scrap, which is used in steel production,
and which partly competes with billet, has put pressure on
prices for semi-finished steel.
    Market participants were expecting a decline in prices for
billet from CIS a week ago as the fall in the price of the lira
makes imported products more expensive for Turkish buyers
[nL5N1F859E].
    
    CHINA ON HOLIDAY
    New opportunities for exporters from the CIS have emerged in
Asia, as Chinese suppliers' activity has dropped due to Lunar
New Year celebrations, which begin on Friday.
    Russian and Ukrainian companies are actively offering square
billet in Southeast Asia at $410-$415 per tonne CFR Asia. Deals
were concluded at $405-$410 CFR.
    Market participants said billet prices in the Asian region
are on a downward trend.

SINGAPORE, Jan 19 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil and jet fuel cash
differentials slipped on Thursday as inventory of the fuels
built up in Singapore, trade sources said.    
    Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks jumped 22.4
percent to a five-week high of 11.954 million barrels in the
week to Jan. 18, latest data from International Enterprise
showed.
    Bangladesh, Cambodia and Malaysia imported lower volumes of
diesel from the week before, while Iran and South Korea resumed
diesel shipments to Singapore, contributing to the increase in
stocks, the data showed.
    Indonesia shipped nearly 150,000 tonnes of diesel to
Singapore in the week ended Jan 18, data from International
Enterprise showed. 
    This is an unusual move, traders said, though no further
details were immediately available.
    United Arab Emirates imported nearly 40,000 tonnes of jet
fuel and about 24,000 tonnes of diesel from Singapore in the
week ended Jan 18, according to the data.
    The UAE is usually a net exporter of both fuels and seldom
imports them, traders said.
    It was not immediately clear who shipped the cargoes.
    Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) may take two to three
months to restart a gasoline-making residual fluid catalytic
cracker (RFCC) unit after a fire at its Ruwais refinery, three
industry sources said. [L4N1F939Z] 
    Emarat likely bought 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel for Feb. 3 to
4 delivery into Jebel Ali from Noble at 85 cents a barrel above
Middle East quotes, an industry source said though this could
not immediately be confirmed.

SINGAPORE, Jan 23 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil and jet fuel
differentials fell on Monday on ample supply of the fuels as
China ramped up exports, overshadowing the impact of a string of
refinery outages, traders said. 
    China's December diesel exports surged 81.4 percent from the
same month a year earlier to 1.78 million tonnes, customs data
showed on Friday, the highest monthly level on record.
[nB9N1DC00T]
    This was in line with record production of diesel, which
rose 0.6 percent in December to 15.27 million tonnes, data from
the National Bureau of Statistics showed. [nB9N1FA00G]    
    China shipped nearly 570,000 tonnes of diesel to Bangladesh,
about 360,000 tonnes to Hong Kong and nearly 220,000 tonnes to
Singapore, according to China's General Administration of
Customs in official customs data. <O/CHINA4>
    It also shipped 92,500 tonnes of diesel to the United
States, according to the data.
    The majority of stocks in Singapore are of the lower sulphur
10ppm diesel grade, a North-Asian trader said.
    Supply of 500ppm and 0.1 percent sulphur gasoil is tight,
with demand robust from Indonesia, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and
Egypt, the trader added. 
    India's Essar Oil likely sold 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel for
Feb. 9 to 14 loading to Vitol at a premium of 50 cents a barrel
to Middle East quotes, traders said, though this could not
immediately be confirmed.     
    Oil refiner TonenGeneral Sekiyu KK on Monday said it had cut
operations to a minimum at its 132,000-barrels per day (bpd)
Wakayama refinery in western Japan following a fire on Sunday in
its lubricant-making facilities. [nL4N1FD0ML]
    This follows a string of refinery outages over the past two
weeks which prevented the gasoil margin from falling further,
traders said.

The tender closes on Jan. 24 and is valid until Jan. 26. 
    - Bahrain Petroleum Co (Bapco) has offered 40,000 tonnes of

    - China Aviation Oil is seeking 25,000 tonnes of jet fuel

SINGAPORE, Feb 20 (Reuters) - Asia's jet fuel cash premium persisted at more than $1 a
barrel to Singapore benchmark prices, the highest since November 2012, due to a supply crunch. 
    - Jet fuel offers in the Singapore cash market remained few and far between against a
constant stream of bids recently. 
    - This has resulted in no deals being sealed in the last week, with jet fuel the most
thinly traded among other refined oil products in the Singapore cash market. [O/AS]
    - The unusual colder-than-expected weather in Japan, healthy demand from airlines,
especially during the current Lunar New Year festive season, and ongoing and coming maintenance
in the Middle East and Asia have turned the sector into a seller's market. [REF/A]
    - Japan's weather bureau had said on Friday that a La Niña weather pattern is continuing,
with a 70 percent chance of it ending during spring, which runs from March to May. [nT9N1CH00X]
    - Kerosene inventories in Japan have been falling, with official data showing that the
stock level was at a six-month low in the week to Jan. 27 at 10.65 million barrels.
[nL4N1PQ1YW]
    - By Feb. 10, Japan's kerosene stocks were even lower at about 8 million barrels.
[nL4N1Q51LM]
    - Kerosene is used for heating in Japan and jet fuel yield typically has to be minimised in
order for a refiner to obtain a higher volume of kerosene. 
    - It was not just Asia that was experiencing a jet fuel supply crunch. 
    - Europe's jet fuel differentials were similarly strong, having risen last week to their
highest since late 2014.

buying activity in the ARA hub while exports held steady.

Nigerian
offshore stocks dwindle, traders said.
    * Traders are looking into locking in storage tanks starting
in
the fourth quarter for winter spec gasoline in the ARA hub,
brokers said. 
    * Buying activity in the ARA hub and inland markets in
Germany and
Switzerland was very weak due to extremely low water levels
along the Rhine river, traders said.
    * The low water levels mean barges are able to load up to
700
tonnes, roughly a third of the average capacity, brokers said.
    * Total naphtha flows into Asia for August are expected to
close
lower versus the monthly average year-to-date of 5.5-5.6 mln
tonnes and July's 5.3-5.4 mln tonnes, largely on lower eastbound
arbitrage arrivals, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research
showed.

LONDON, Aug 7 (Reuters) - Benchmark northwest European diesel refining margins were little
changed on Tuesday as imports from the U.S Gulf Coast were expected to rise. 
    * Buying activity in the ARA hub and inland markets in Germany and Switzerland was very weak
due
to extremely low water levels along the Rhine river, traders said.
    * The low water levels meant barges are able to load up to 700 tonnes, roughly a third of
the
average capacity, brokers said.
    * Weakening demand for diesel in Latin America is leading to a higher numbers of cargoes
from the
U.S. Gulf Coast being offered into the European and Mediterranean markets, traders said.
    * At least two very large crude carriers -- Xin Hui Yang and Tonegawa -- are expected to
come to
Europe on their maiden voyage from Asian shipyards with diesel cargoes, according to ship
brokers and traders. 
    * Two long-range (LR2) newbuild tankers, Argironissos and Gagarin Prospect, are also
expected to
arrive on the same route. 
    * Russian exports of ultra-low sulphur diesel (ULSD) from the Baltic port of Primorsk will
fall by
6 percent on a daily basis in August to 1.314 million tonnes from 1.398 million tonnes scheduled
for July, trading sources familiar with the loading schedule said. [nL5N1UM2OP]

SINGAPORE, Aug 7 (Reuters) - Asia's fuel oil market slipped on Tuesday, with cash premiums
<FO380-SIN-DIF>, cracks <HFOFARAACMc2> and time spreads <FO380SGSDMc1> extending losses, as
fresh spot supply from the Middle East helped relieve concerns of a persistent tightness in
Singapore fuel oil supplies over the near term, trade sources said. 
    Fresh spot tenders from Bahrain and Kuwait emerged this week, raising prospects of increased
fuel oil shipments from the Middle East into Singapore after months of below average flows, the
sources said. 
    With peak seasonal demand for fuel oil in the Middle East due to ease around end of August,
some trade sources now estimate Middle East fuel oil exports to Singapore to total about 1.6-1.8
million tonnes in August. 
    The higher Middle East exports in August are also supported by high inventories of the fuel
in the Fujairah oil hub, currently at a 2018 high, and a steeply backwardated market structure
which encourages reducing volumes held in storage, the sources said. [FUJAIRAH/]
        
    TENDERS
    - Kuwait's KPC has issued a tender offering up to 103,000 tonnes of three types of residual
fuels, trade sources said.
    - KPC offered 40,000 tonnes of bunker-grade 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 3.5 percent
sulphur content and another 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst heavy fuel oil. Both cargoes are due for
delivery on Aug 16-17 and the tender closes on Aug 7.
    - KPC also offered 23,00o tonnes of mixed coker gasoil and trim gasoil for Aug 25-26 deliver
in a tender closing on Aug 8.
    - Bahrain's Bapco is offering 60,000-80,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4
percent sulphur content for Sept 25-28 loading from Sitra in a tender closing on Aug 8. 
    - India's Reliance is offering two 40,000 tonnes of 280-cst carbon black feedstock (CBFS)
with a maximum 2.8 percent sulphur content loading from Sikka on Aug 27-28 and Sept 5-6 in a
tender closing on Aug 7 with next day validity. 
    - Pakistan's PSO has received offers for two 65,000-tonne cargoes of 180-cst fuel oil with a
maximum 3.5 percent sulphur content for Aug 21-31 delivery into Port Qasim.
    - PSO had sought three cargoes for Aug 21-31 delivery, but only two supplier offers were
made. 
    - BE Energy made the lowest offer at a $16.98 per tonne premium to Middle East quotes on an
FOB basis. The second offer was made by Vitol at $23.88 per tonne.
    - PSO's tender for its Aug 21-31 import requirements remains valid to Aug 15.
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
    
    WESTERN ARBS 
    - Separately, trade sources expect Singapore to receive about 3 million tonnes of Western
arbitrage fuel oil volumes in August, about 2 million tonnes less than what it typically
receives.
    - At least three suezmax tankers were provisionally chartered to load fuel oil this week
from Europe for discharge into Singapore, according to shipbroker reports and ship tracking data
in Thomson Reuters Eikon. 
    - Trafigura provisionally chartered the White Moon tanker to load 130,000 tonnes of fuel oil
from Malta on Aug 10-11 for a $2 million fee, the data showed. 
    - BP provisionally chartered the Zouzou N tanker to load up to 135,000 tonnes of fuel oil
from Ust-Luga in the Baltic Sea on Aug 11 for a $2.8 million fee.
    - UML, Socar's shipping arm, tentatively booked the San Jacinto tanker to load 130,000
tonnes of fuel oil from Rotterdam on Aug 10 for an undisclosed fee. 
    - All three tankers would be due for arrival into Singapore in the first-half of September,
the data showed.

SINGAPORE, Feb 10 (Reuters) - Spot demand from Vietnam lent
support to gasoil differentials despite ample supply of the
fuel, trade sources said.     
    Vietnam's top fuel importer Petrolimex bought three cargoes
of 35,000 tonnes each of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for loading from
Singapore, Malaysia or Thailand at a premium of about 55 to 60
cents a barrel to Singapore quotes, traders said.
    Vietnam's PV Oil followed with a tender requirement for
March and April seeking a total of 80,000 cubic metres of
gasoil, they added. 
    Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp is seeking 200,000 barrels
of jet fuel for delivery in February, traders said. 
    Refinery maintenance in Asia, which is expected to be
heavier than in previous years, will likely further boost gasoil
and jet fuel differentials, traders said.
    Japanese oil refiner Cosmo Oil Co said on Friday it planned
to shut two crude distillation units (CDU) this year for
scheduled maintenance. [nL4N1FV0PS]
    The two CDUs at Chiba and Sakai refineries are likely to be
shut for about 1-1/2-months each, a company spokesman said.
    Arbitrage economics to ship diesel to Europe also remain
unviable with oil product inventory in Europe remaining high,
traders said. 
    The region's stocks of crude oil and all oil products apart
from fuel oil edged higher despite the lower run rates, reaching
a total of 1.150 billion barrels in January, data from industry
monitor Euroilstock showed. [nL5N1FU529] 
    
    TENDERS: 
    - Pertamina is seeking 200,000 barrels of jet fuel for
delivery into Jakarta over March 23 to 25. The tender closes on
Feb. 14 and is valid until Feb. 17.
    - Ceylon Petroleum Corp is seeking 200,000 barrels of jet
fuel for delivery into Colombo over Feb. 21 to 22. The tender
closes on Feb. 14 and is valid for up to 72 hours.
    - PV Oil is seeking 80,000 cubic metres of 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for delivery into Nha Be and Mien Dong over March to
April. The tender closes on Feb. 10.

LONDON, Feb 9 (Reuters) - Diesel refining margins in
northwest Europe were largely stable on Thursday on stock draws
in ARA, refinery maintenance and firm demand in the
Mediterranean. 
    
    * Gasoil stocks in independent storage in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp hub fell by more than 3.5 percent in
the week to Thursday to 3.17 million tonnes, according to Dutch
consultancy PJK International. [nL5N1FU6NX]
    * The decline came as barge shipments on the Rhine picked up
amid rising water levels. However, barge brokers said the upper
Rhine water levels remain too low to fully load barges, and
water levels in that region are forecast to fall further.
    * Crude oil intake at Europe's refineries fell for a second
month in January, but stocks of crude and oil products also
edged higher for a second month, data from industry monitor
Euroilstock showed on Thursday. [nL5N1FU529]
    * Still, Euroilstock data showed that stock levels were
nearly 18 percent lower than January last year, illustrating a
gradual drawdown in recent months following more than two years
of build amid a global glut of crude oil.
    * Valero Energy Corp was repairing the hydrocracking unit
(HCU) at the 125,000 barrel per day (bpd) Meraux, Louisiana,
refinery on Wednesday afternoon ahead of a possible restart
overnight, said sources familiar with plant operations.
[nL1N1FT0RJ]
    * Some 700,000 tonnes of diesel are expected to sail this
month from ARA to the Mediterranean. This week alone, vessels
with 300,000 tonnes were booked to sail on the route. 
    * Cold weather and high refinery maintenance in the
Mediterranean have pushed diesel and jet fuel prices higher in
recent weeks.
    * Amid strong gasoil prices in Asia, spot arbitrage into
Europe from that region was largely closed. Some U.S.
distillates were en route to Europe from the Atlantic Coast, but
these volumes were limited and arbitrage from the U.S. Gulf was
also limited. 
    * Traders said between the mostly closed arbitrage and
refinery maintenance, supplies could stay tight in the coming
weeks. [REF/E]

importing and local production swamped the region. At least two

Africa, Asia Pacific, North America and Brazil, Dutch

SINGAPORE, Feb 9 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil and jet fuel differentials rose on Thursday ahead
of refinery maintenances from March, industry sources said.
    But an unprofitable arbitrage to ship cargoes to Europe is keeping inventories ample,
capping any further gains in prices, they added.
    Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks rose nearly 12 percent to a more than two-month
high of 14.408 million barrels in the week to Feb. 8, latest data from International Enterprise
showed. <O/SING1>
    China and South Korea more than doubled their diesel shipments to Singapore from the
previous week, while Australia imported less of the fuel which contributed to the build in
stocks, the data showed.
    Russia and Iran shipped diesel to Singapore while Malaysia's exports of the fuel also rose.
    Diesel cargoes, which were recently stored in tankers, are being shifted to landed tanks or
shipped regionally, as the backwardated market makes storing the fuel unprofitable, traders
said. 
    Arbitrage to ship diesel to Europe is not profitable as supply remained ample in Europe, one
of them said. 
    Spot demand from Vietnam's Saigon Petro also supported, though the volume was not big enough
to boost differentials by much, traders said.

SINGAPORE, July 3 (Reuters) - Asia's fuel oil markets shed recent gains to ease for a second
straight session on Tuesday as cash premiums and time spreads narrowed their premiums to
multi-session lows.
    Despite the weaker prices on Tuesday, trade sources said the fundamentals underpinning the
near-term fuel oil market remained bullish with firm seasonal demand and limited supplies continuing
to characterise the market.
    Weaker deal values and lean supply offers in the Singapore trading window weighed on cash
premiums of 180-cst and 380-cst fuel oil grades on Tuesday. 
    Cash premiums of 180-cst fuel oil <FO180-SIN-DIF> slipped to a one-week low of $4.26 a tonne to
Singapore quotes, while premiums of the mainstay 380-cst fuel oil <FO380-SIN-DIF> was at their
narrowest since June 21 at $3.93 a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    A persistent crunch in supply of fuel oil to Asia driven by reduced shipments from exporters
such as Iran and Venezuela, and a surge in Middle East seasonal demand has pushed a key fuel's cash
premium to Singapore prices to a three-year peak on Friday. [nL4N1TV5D2]
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Three cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of
180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) and 20,000 tonnes of 380-cst HSFO.
    - Hin Leong bought all three cargoes, lifting one 20,000 tonne 180-cst fuel oil cargo from Shell
and Trafigura each, while buying the 380-cst fuel oil cargo from Socar. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - In a rare move, Sri Lanka's Ceypetco sold tender up to 25,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil with
a maximum 2 percent sulphur content loading from Colombo on July 12-13 to Vitol at a discount of
$22.15 per tonne to Singapore 180-cst quotes on an FOB basis, sources said. 
    - Ceypetco typically imports fuel oil to meet its power generation demands and the reason behind
its unusual export tender could not be confirmed. 
    - In another unusual move, Kuwait's KPC bought two 380-cst fuel oil cargoes with a maximum 3.5
percent sulphur content for delivery over July 1-2 and July 14-15 from Shell at an unknown price
level, sources said.
    - KPC typically exports HSFO cargoes and its latest import tender could be due to higher

BENGALURU, July 3 (Reuters) - Asia's refining margins for 10ppm gasoil dipped on Tuesday,
lingering close to seven-month lows, while cash differentials marginally narrowed their
discounts but stayed near the lowest levels for this year due to abundant supplies. 
    Refining margins or cracks for 10ppm gasoil <GO10SGCKMc1> fell to as low as $13.11 a barrel
over Dubai crude in Asian trading hours, from $13.48 on Monday. The margins had fallen last week
to $12.97 per barrel - the lowest since early November.
    Diesel exports from China have risen recently and will likely increase further in the near
term as regional refineries return from seasonal maintenance, trade sources said. [nL4N1TP04H]
    Meanwhile, India's diesel exports are also on the rise due to weaker domestic consumption
during monsoons. [nL4N1TM3ZV]
    Diesel demand in India should start picking up in a month or so as the peak rainy season
dissipates, a Mumbai-based trader said. 
    India's demand for the transportation fuel typically takes a hit as travelling in some parts
of the country gets curtailed due to heavy monsoon rains, which also reduce the need for diesel
used in irrigation pumps.
    Cash differentials for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10-SIN-DIF> narrowed their
discounts by a cent on Tuesday and were at a discount of 24 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes. 
    Cash differentials for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> also narrowed their discounts and stood at 25
cents a barrel to Singapore quotes on Tuesday, compared with a discount of 28 cents on Monday.

    LONDON, Aug 30 (Reuters) - Gasoline exports from Europe
across the Atlantic are set to surge in coming days as traders
plug supply gaps after Tropical Storm Harvey crippled refineries
in the U.S. Gulf Coast.
    Nearly one quarter of U.S. fuel output was knocked out since
Harvey made landfall on Friday in Texas, where several large
refiners are located. [nL2N1LG0X1]
    Outages that could last for weeks led to a sharp rise in
gasoline and diesel futures prices in the United States and
Europe, opening several arbitrage opportunities.
    Traders have tentatively booked this week nearly 40 tankers
-- the equivalent of about 1.5 million tonnes of gasoline -- out
of Europe to carry gasoline on the transatlantic route,
including destinations such as New York, Mexico and Brazil,
according to shipping data and traders.
    That compares with an average of about 500,000 tonnes of
gasoline exported e week from Europe to the United States and
Latin America.
    Freight rates between Europe and the United States for a
37,000 tonne refined product tanker doubled over the past week
to about $16,000 a day, according to shipping brokers.
    High shipping costs and uncertainty over the impact of
Harvey on trade flows meant traders were still reluctant to lock
in the cargoes, several traders said.
    Traders in Asia have also scrambled to buy oil products to
ship to the United States and Latin America. [nL4N1LG30C]
    The U.S. Gulf Coast refining hub has in recent years become
a major supplier of fuels such as gasoline and diesel to
overseas markets such as Brazil, Mexico and Europe.

weekend due to a pipeline blockade and the National Oil Corp
(NOC) has declared force majeure on Mellitah grade exports from
the Mellitah oil terminal. 
    The shutdown of Sharara has also led NOC subsidiary Agoco to
shut down the 10,000 bpd Hamada oilfield, which shares export
infrastructure with Sharara, a Libyan oil source told Reuters.

SINGAPORE, Feb 27 (Reuters) - Asia's high-sulphur fuel oil crack for March widened its discount to
Brent crude on Tuesday, slipping to a four-week low amid limited trade activity and weak market
sentiment, trade sources said.
    The front-month 180-cst fuel oil crack to Brent settled at minus $8.24 a barrel, its widest
discount since Jan. 29 when it was at minus $8.76 a barrel. <FO180BRTCKMc1>
    The weaker fuel oil crack came despite lower crude prices on Tuesday amid concerns about rising
U.S. oil output offsetting signs of stronger demand and faith in the ability of OPEC production curbs
to curtail supply. [O/R]
    Market sentiment has been weighed down in recent weeks by sluggish demand and a slight overhang in
supplies, trade sources said.
        
    WINDOW TRADES
    - Four cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, including 20,000 tonnes of
180-cst fuel oil and 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - The increase in buying interest for physical cargoes helped boost the 380-cst cash premium to a
four-session high
    - Hin Leong bought all three 380-cst fuel oil cargoes, two from Gunvor and one from Glencore. Total
bought the 180-cst fuel oil cargo from Reliance. 
    - The volumes of physical fuel oil traded on Tuesday were the highest since Feb. 19 when 80,000
tonnes also changed hands.

sulphur content loading from New Mangalore March 12-14 at a premium below $20 a tonne to Singapore
380-cst quotes, trade sources said.
    - MRPL previously sold a similar cargo to BP for Feb. 23-25 loading at a premium of $13-$18 a tonne
to Singapore 380-cst quotes, sources said.
    - ExxonMobil's refinery in Thailand is offering 42,000 tonnes of blendstock components for export
from Sriracha on March 17-19 in a tender closing on Feb. 26, trade sources said.

SINGAPORE, July 19 (Reuters) - Asia's front month 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil time spread
climbed to fresh highs on Thursday, lifted by few signs of easing supply constraints and limited
arbitrage arrivals in August, trade sources said.
    The 380-cst time spread for August/September climbed to a premium of about $8 per tonne on
Thursday, broker sources said, its highest since June 2015. <FO380SGSDMc1>
    Western arbitrage flows into Singapore were expected to total around 3 million tonnes in
August, trade sources said. 
    Despite the wide front month arbitrage spread, trade sources said arbitrage opportunities
were limited by the steeply backwardated market structure. 
    The August 380-cst arbitrage spread was at $22 per tonne on Thursday, up from $21 a tonne on
Wednesday, according to broker sources.

374,000 tonnes) to 19.624 million barrels (2.929 million tonnes) in the week ended July 18, data
from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed on Thursday. [nL4N1UF375]
    - The 15 percent rise in weekly fuel oil inventories pulled residual fuel stocks away from
nearly four-year low hit in the previous week, the data showed. [nL4N1U838S]
    - This came as weekly fuel oil net imports into Singapore surged 111 percent from a week
earlier to a four-week high of 1.048 million tonnes in the week ended July 18.
    - Net fuel oil imports into Singapore averaged 762,000 tonnes per week since the start of
the year.
    - Compared with a year ago, the latest onshore fuel oil inventories were 14 percent lower.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Hong Kong topped the week ended July 18 at 78,000
tonnes, followed by Bangladesh at 66,000 tonnes and Sri Lanka at 11,000 tonnes.
    - In the week ended July 18, Singapore weekly exports to China were absent for the first
time in almost three months. Before that, Singapore exported fuel oil to China every week since
at least the start of 2016.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Malaysia at 316,000 tonnes,
followed by Russia at 213,000 tonnes, the United States at 180,000 tonnes and the Netherlands at

tonnes in the week to July 18.

SINGAPORE, Feb 3 (Reuters) - The 500ppm sulphur gasoil cash differential
remained firm on Friday as supply of the fuel remained in short supply, traders
said.
    With North Asian refiners maximising jet fuel production over diesel due to
firm heating demand during winter, the supply of 500ppm especially is tight, they
added.
    Demand for the fuel, on the other hand, is firm with Indonesia, Sri Lanka and
Myanmar buying additional cargoes, traders said.
    Supply of 10ppm sulphur diesel is still ample with the arbitrage to ship the
cargoes west not profitable at the moment, they said.
    This in turn has narrowed the price difference between the two grades, which
could prompt refiners to maximise production of the 500ppm sulphur gasoil, one of
them said. 
    Refining margins will stay firm in 2017, backed by limited additions to
refined product supplies and solid demand growth, SK Innovation, which owns South
Korea's top refiner, said on Friday. [nL4N1FO1L3]
    Strong regional demand is expected to help keep refining margins for diesel
and gasoline strong, despite rising Chinese exports of diesel and high stocks of
gasoline the United States, SK Innovation said.
    Gasoil cracks - a measure of refining margins - are expected to hold steady in
the first quarter, supported by winter demand from the United States and Europe,
Lee Yunhi, head of SK Energy's planning office, told analysts in a call.

SINGAPORE, Feb 2 (Reuters) - The Singapore middle distillates inventory slipped
on Thursday but the drop failed to stoke trade in the market, traders said.    
    Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks slipped 1.9 percent to a two-week
low of 12.89 million barrels, latest data from International Enterprise showed. 
    Diesel imports from India fell to 35,000 tonnes in the week to Feb. 1 from
132,000 tonnes the week before, the data showed. Shipments from Malaysia also fell,
while diesel exports from Singapore to New Zealand, China and Malaysia increased.
    Jet fuel exports from Singapore to Hong Kong also increased, according to the
data. 
    Trade activity was quiet with not much cargo movements for ultra low sulphur
diesel due to a closed arbitrage, industry sources said.
    Still, with clean freight rates having fallen, this could encourage more flow,
one of the sources said.
    India's Reliance is preparing to ship an ultra low sulphur diesel cargo from
India to east Mediterranean, the source added, though this could not be confirmed
with Reliance.
    Traders are starting to unwind their floating storage of diesel due to a
narrowing contango, where prices of cargoes loading in current month is lower than
in forward months, the sources said. 
    Sri Lanka has rejected a consignment of 40,000 tonnes of diesel supplied by oil
trading giant Vitol, after it failed standard tests, Petroleum Resource Minister
Chandima Weerakkody said on Wednesday. [nL4N1FH2HP]
    The cargo was rejected due to quality issues and the company has asked Vitol to
replace the cargo, a source close to Ceylon Petroleum Corp said.
    Vitol declined to comment on the matter. 
    South Korea's S-Oil Corp expects healthy refining profits this year, buoyed by
growing demand for oil products in places such as China and Southeast Asia.

    SINGAPORE, Feb 3 (Reuters) - Asia's fuel oil complex edged higher on Friday
but traders remained cautious as steady February arbitrage supplies could
present further downside risks.
    Traders said the market complex was starting to settle after concerns of
rising supplies sparked a sharp sell-off around the start of January when time
spreads, refining margins and East-West arbitrage spreads were at multi-month
highs. 
    Discounts of the 380-cst Feb/March time spread contract <FO380SGSDMc1> were
25 cents a tonne narrower on Friday to minus 75 cents a tonne but still wider
than Monday's settlement at minus 50 cents a tonne. 
    Since the start of the month, the front-month contract fell from an 18-month
high of plus $4.50 a tonne on Jan. 6, to a seven-month low of minus $1.25 on
Tuesday. 
    Singapore's March 180-cst fuel oil <FO180SGCKMc1> also snapped three
sessions of declines, narrowing its discount to Dubai crude after gaining 31
cents a barrel from the previous session to minus $4.82 a barrel, but still
remained well below the $3.47 a barrel discount seen at the start of the week.
    Refining margins of the February 180-cst fuel against Brent crude
<FO180BRTCKMc1> also recovered from Thursday's three-month low of minus $7.15 a
barrel to minus $6.75 a barrel on Friday.
    South Korean refiner SK Innovation <096770.KS> on Friday said it expects to
see fuel oil cracks remaining strong in the first quarter of the year amid
strong power generation and bunkering demand. [nS6N1BB00K]
    In physical markets, higher deal values helped narrow cash discounts of the
380-cst fuel <FO380-SIN-DIF> to 32 cents a tonne below Singapore quotes, up from
minus 58 cents a tonne in the previous session.
    Once cash deal was reported in the Platts window after Mercuria bought
20,000 tonnes of the 380-cst fuel oil from Shell at a discount of 25 cents a
tonne to Singapore quotes, industry sources said.
    On Wednesday, cash discounts of the 380-cst fuel were at a near six-month
low after sinking to minus 88 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes.

    Fuel oil stocks in independently held storage in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub rose to a three-week high of 710,000
tonnes in the week to Thursday, data from Dutch consultancy PJK International
showed. [ARA/]
    ARA residual fuel inventories <STK-FO-ARA> were 14.7 percent higher from the
previous week's total of 619,000 tonnes, snapping two weeks of declines.
    Compared to the same time last year, however, fuel oil inventories in the
ARA hub were 34 percent lower from the 1.08 million tonnes seen in the week to
Feb. 4. [nL5N1FN6G2]

showed no outgoing cargoes scheduled for the week.

SINGAPORE, Feb 1 (Reuters) - The Asian diesel margin slipped on Wednesday as trades of the
fuel slowed on the first day of the month after a flurry of activity in the last quarter of
2016, trade sources said.
    Traders were expecting the increased refinery maintenance season which starts in March to
lift margins. 
    Demand for diesel is also expected to be better this year than in previous years as a boost
in the mining sector lifts demand from Australia and Indonesia, they added. 
    Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp continued to seek gasoil cargoes in the spot market, which
also supported differentials for the 500ppm sulphur gasoil grade.
    With refiners increasingly switching to produce lower sulphur fuels, availability of the
500ppm sulphur gasoil is more limited, traders said.
    Japan's kerosene sales rose 24.2 percent in the week to Jan. 28 from the previous week,
latest data from Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ) showed. <O/JAPAN1>
    Stocks of the heating fuel fell to 1.3 million barrels, which is the lowest since June,
2016, the data showed. 
    A cold winter is likely boosting demand for the fuel, traders said.     
    Global air freight demand ended 2016 with strong December growth of 9.8 percent, the
International Air Transport Association (IATA) said on Wednesday but warned that protectionist
measures could hamper world trade. [nL5N1FL5ZR]
    Stagnant world trade could hamper jet fuel demand, traders said.

    - Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp is seeking 300,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for

    SINGAPORE, Feb 1 (Reuters) - Time spreads of 380-cst fuel oil on Wednesday recovered some of
the previous session's losses that had pushed some spreads contracts to fresh lows, but most
traders still see more downside risk than upside potential in February amid steady inflows of
the fuel into Singapore during the month.
    By contrast, other traders maintained that despite firm February inflows, the recent
collapse in the fuel oil market complex from multi-month highs is exaggerated given balanced
current inventory levels and steady demand for the industrial fuel.
    On the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the 380-cst fuel oil Feb/March spreads contract was
trading at minus 75 cents a tonne by 1800 Singapore time (1000 GMT), up from Tuesday's
settlement of minus $1.50 a tonne, industry sources said.    
    Discounts of the March/April time spreads were also narrower after gaining 50 cents a tonne
from the previous session to minus 50 cents a tonne.
    In physical markets, cash differentials of the 380-cst fuel <FO380-SIN-DIF> sank to a near
six-month low, dragged down by aggressive supplier offers and limited buying interest, sources
said.
    Cash discounts of the 380-cst fuel were assessed at minus 88 cents a tonne to Singapore
quotes, down 22 cents a tonne from Tuesday's discount of 66 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes,
its lowest since Aug. 16.
    Three cash deals was reported in the Platts window totalling 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel
oil in addition to 20,000 tonnes of the lower viscosity 180-cst fuel.
        
    FUJAIRAH INVENTORIES
    In the United Arab Emirates, the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone on Wednesday published its third
weekly oil products inventory data via S&P Global Platts. [nL5N1FM1AR]
    Inventories of heavy distillates and residues in the storage hub fell 901,000 barrels (about
134,000 tonnes), or 9.8 percent, from the previous week to 8.25 million barrels (or 1.23 million
tonnes).
    The reported figures include fuel oil and other heavy fuels used for marine bunkers and
power generation, but exclude non-energy residual products such as tar and bitumen, according to
the S&P Global Platts website.
    
    RELATED NEWS:
    - Glencore has become the largest buyer of Russian Urals oil from Rosneft, overtaking rival
Trafigura after taking a stake in Russia's biggest oil major last month, a Reuters analysis of
trade data showed. [nL5N1FK3CI]
    - OPEC's oil output is set to fall by more than 1 million barrels per day (bpd) this month,
a Reuters survey found on Tuesday, pointing to a strong start by the exporter group in
implementing its first supply cut deal in eight years. [nL5N1FL2X3]

northwest Europe weakened on Thursday, tracking U.S. benchmark
prices after a continued build in stocks in the New York
Harbour.

Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub fell by 10.7 percent in
the week to Thursday, data from Dutch consultancy PJK
International showed.[ARA/]

particularly to West Africa and Asia, where gasoline prices have
strengthened significantly due to refinery outages.

further support. [REF/E]

SINGAPORE, June 5 (Reuters) - Singapore 380-cst ex-wharf premiums improved on Tuesday, as buyers
seek to lock in supplies amid weaker crude oil prices, trade sources said.
    This comes amid ongoing shortages of finished grade bunker fuels that are expected to last well
into the next month, the sources said. 
    Ex-wharf premiums were at about $2-$3 per tonne to Singapore quotes so far this week, up from
about $0-$1 a tonne in the previous week, sources said.
    Sluggish demand for bunker fuels due to sharply higher crude oil prices in May has weighed on
ex-wharf and delivered bunker fuel premiums. [nL3N1SP3OM]
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Five cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, totalling 80,000 tonnes of
180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) and 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst HSFO.
    - Glencore and Gunvor each supplied 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst HSFO to Mercuria. 
    - Trafigura sold two 20,000 tonne 380-cst HSFO cargoes, one to Shell and another to Hin Leong. 
    - Tuesday's 180-cst and 380-cst fuel oil deals were concluded at lower premiums compared to
Monday, pulling cash premiums of both fuel oil grades away from their more than one-year highs seen
over the past week. <FO180-SIN-DIF> <FO380-SIN-DIF>

said in a statement on Tuesday. [nASA00OP4]

SINGAPORE, Oct 12 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differentials remained steady on
Thursday as fuel inventory dipped slightly, traders said.
    
    - SINGAPORE OIL STOCKS: Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks slipped by more than 1
percent to a two-week low of 10.529 million barrels in the week to Oct. 11, latest data from
International Enterprise showed. <O/SING1>
    - CHINESE REFINERS SEEK MORE QUOTAS: China's top two state refiners - Sinopec Corp and
PetroChina - have applied for additional quotas for exporting surplus gasoline, diesel and jet
fuel before year-end, according to two trading sources on Thursday. [nL4N1MN1UZ]
    The two firms applied for a combined 5 million tonnes of quotas for the rest of 2017. The
quotas include both tolling scheme and general trade, the sources said. 
    - JAPAN EXPORTS: Japan's exports of jet fuel and gasoil fell in the week to Oct. 7 from the
previous week as refinery utilisation rates fell, latest data from the Petroleum Association of
Japan (PAJ) showed. <O/JAPAN1>
    Still, kerosene inventory rose by 1.24 million bbls to the highest since Oct. 29, 2016,
according to the data, suggesting peak winter demand is yet to set in. 
    - GLOBAL OIL DEMAND: Global supply and demand for crude oil will be largely balanced next
year, as growth in consumption helps erode a three-year-old overhang of unused fuel and should
mostly offset a steep rise in output, the International Energy Agency said on Thursday.
    In its monthly oil market report, the Paris-based IEA said it continues to see global demand
for crude growing by 1.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2017, before moderating to 1.4 million
bpd in 2018.
    - CHINA TO BOOST ENERGY STORAGE CAPACITY: China aims to boost its large-scale energy storage
capacity over the next decade, the government's central planner said, in a major push to solve
the problem of stranded power in the west of the country as Beijing promotes the use of more
renewable power. [nL4N1MN1NA] 
    While China has led the globe in pushing for greater reliance on wind and solar power in
recent years, getting clean energy from western regions to urban users in the world's top energy
consumer has been a major headache.

SINGAPORE, Oct 12 (Reuters) - Asia's 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil cash premium <FO380-SIN-DIF>
slipped to a one-month low on Thursday, weighed down by rising Singapore fuel oil inventories and
weaker offers for physical cargoes from physical suppliers in the Platts window, sources said. 
            
    SINGAPORE INVENTORIES
    - Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories rose to a total of 3.54 million tonnes in the week to
Oct. 11, up 5.3 percent or 179,000 tonnes from the previous week, official data shows. [O/SING1]
    - This came as weekly net imports into Singapore rose 21 percent from a week earlier to a 2-week
high of 551,000 tonnes. 
    - Fuel oil stocks are now 0.2 percent higher year-on-year. 
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to China topped the weekly list (284,000 tonnes); followed
by Malaysia (244,000 tonnes) and Bangladesh (39,000 tonnes).
    - Largest Singapore net imports originated from Venezuela (329,000 tonnes); followed by Saudi
Arabia (151,000), Netherlands (132,000 tonnes), and Latvia (120,000 tonnes). 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Three cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling one 20,000-tonne cargo of
180-cst fuel oil and two 40,000-tonne cargoes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    IMO 2020 
    - More than 75 percent of ships will switch away from heavy high-sulphur fuels to lower-sulphur
middle distillates by 2020 when the International Maritime Organisation's (IMO) sulphur cap from 3.5
percent to 0.5 percent comes into effect, BMI Research said in a note on Thursday. [nL4N1MN1Z8]
    - Many shippers also likely to avoid large investments in retrofitting engines or scrubbers due
to uncertainties around possible regulations on carbon dioxide emissions from 2023, said BMI. 
    - High-sulphur fuel demand will see price fall; only around 15 percent of shipping fleet
anticipated to use scrubbers, BMI adds. 
    - Separately, the International Bunker Industry Association (IBIA) estimates the current
shipping fleet would only be able to consume around 10 million tonnes (around 170,000 bpd) of
high-sulphur fuel oil by 2020, said JBC Research said in a note to its clients. 
    - For 2020 we see global bunker demand at around 3.9 million bpd, implying that if the IBIA's
forecast is accurate, less than 5 pct of the global fleet would run on high-sulphur fuel oil, said
JBC. 
    
    TENDERS
    - KPC sold up to 88,000 tonnes of high-sulphur fuel oil to Litasco foe loading on Oct. 13-14 at
an unknown price level, an industry said. [nL4N1MN40F]
    - The cargo consists of 45,000 to 50,000 tonnes of heavy 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4.2
sulphur content, along with 25,000 to 38,000 tonnes of heavy 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 3.5
sulphur content.
