LONDON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe fell after U.S. stocks rose last week while
firm demand from the Middle East capped losses.
    
    
    * U.S. gasoline stocks <USOILG=ECI> rose by 2.5 million
barrels, with the largest build taking place in PADD 1, EIA data
showed. [EIA/S]
    * East of Suez demand for European gasoline cargoes remains
strong, with the Middle East continuing to pull cargoes.
    * Vitol booked the Iver Exact to load 37,000 tonnes of
gasoline in ARA early next week to go to Sudan, according to
shipping reports.
    * Vitol also provisionally booked a tanker to load gasoline
at the Turkish port of Aliaga with options for delivery to the
Middle East or transatlantic.
    * Demand from West Africa was limited by the need for gasoil
and kerosene in Nigeria, and traders said the country was asking
for those imports in crude for product swap cargoes delivered in
November.
    * China's top two state refiners Sinopec Corp and PetroChina
have applied for additional quotas for exporting surplus
gasoline, diesel and jet fuel before the end of the year,
according to two trading sources. [nL4N1MN1UZ]


      
    GASOLINE

    * Gunvor sold a barge each Vitol and Shell at $550 and $551
a tonne fob ARA, respectively, compared with a trade at $540 a
tonne on Thursday.  
    * Earlier in the day, some 8,000 tonnes of traded at
$550.50-$554 a tonne fob Amsterdam-Rotterdam, compared with
$546-$557 a tonne the previous day. Total and Gunvor sold to
Varo and Shell.
    * Gunvor sold to Total one barge of premium unleaded
gasoline at $568 a tonne, up from $561 a tonne.

SINGAPORE, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Despite rising crude oil prices, Asia's November fuel oil crack to
Dubai crude climbed to a near three-week high of $2.18 a barrel on Monday. <FO180SGCKMc1> [O/R]
    Potentially lower supplies of the fuel from key exporters including Russia, Iran and Venezuela in
the coming months may have contributed to the strength in the fuel oil, one Singapore-based fuel oil
trader said. 
    The latest official data showed Russian fuel oil exports <FO-RU-EXP> sank to just above 3 million
tonnes in August, their lowest since February last year, as refiners there process more of the fuel to
produce higher-value fuels such as gasoline and gasoil. [nL5N1M338M]
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - No cargo trades were reported in the Platts window on Monday. The last time there were no cargo
trades reported was on Oct. 2, the first trading day of the month. 
    - A total of 860,000 tonnes of fuel oil has traded in the window since the start of October,
against 2.262 million tonnes in September.

    - India's MRPL sold up to 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4.5 percent sulphur
content to Total for Nov 4-6 loading from New Mangalore at a discount of $7-$8 a tonne to Singapore
380-cst quotes on an FOB basis, sources said. [nL4N1MR3PM]

    - The world's top trading houses, among the most nimble entities in oil, say even they aren't sure
how to stay a step ahead of a coming cut in shipping fuel sulphur. [nL8N1MO40U]
    - Nearly a year after the International Maritime Organization finalised rules that will cap ships'
sulphur emissions at 0.5 percent of fuel content in 2020, from 3.5 percent now, the heads of trading
firms Vitol, Gunvor, Glencore and Mercuria said there were still too many unanswered questions.
    - The lack of clarity could create immense volatility in fuel prices if the bulk of vessels turn
to low-sulphur gasoil.

SINGAPORE, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Buyers emerged in the spot market as prices of gasoil and jet
fuel cargoes climbed on Wednesday tracking a rise in underlying crude oil prices, trade sources
said. 
    
    - PV OIL SEEKS GASOIL TERM: Vietnam's PV Oil is seeking 124,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for delivery over October to December through a term tender that closes on Oct. 12, a
tender document showed. [nL4N1MM3IR] 
    - PAKISTAN, EMARAT SEEK JET FUEL: Pakistan State Oil is seeking a jet fuel for December
delivery in a tender that closes on Oct. 25 and is valid until Nov. 1.    
      Emirates General Petroleum Corp (Emarat) is also seeking 50,000 tonnes of jet fuel for
November delivery, traders said. 
    - EGYPT JET FUEL OFFER: Egypt's Middle East Oil Refinery offers jet fuel cargoes for term
contract for loading over January to June, 2018, a tender document showed. 
      The company offered one cargo a month of 30,000 tonnes each of jet fuel for the period on
a free-on-board (FOB) Alexandria basis. The tender will close on Oct. 17 and is valid until Oct.
24. 
    - JET FUEL PRICES TO CLIMB: Global jet fuel prices will climb over the next five years,
supported by strong and rising demand for air freight and passenger travel, BMI Research said. 
    Consumption growth will remain supported over the fourth quarter of this year and the first
quarter of next year as economic conditions continue to improve, which will in turn boost air
freight demand, BMI said. 
    Growth will increasingly shift from developed markets to emerging economies due to
accelerating GDP growth, rising populations and growing per capita income, the firm said. 
    China will be largest driver of growth, while growth in Turkey, India, the United Arab
Emirates, Qatar and Indonesia will also be strong, it added.  
    Supply of jet fuel could tighten moving into the 2020s as the International Maritime
Organisation will reduce the sulphur cap for marine fuels, which will push shipowners to switch
from bunker fuel to marine gasoil, increasing the latter's yield over jet fuel, the company
said.
    - FORMOSA CUTS RUN RATES: Taiwan's Formosa Petrochemical Corp is operating its 540,000
barrels per day (bpd) refinery at Mailiao at about 70 percent capacity this month, its spokesman
said on Wednesday. [nL4N1L01RX]
    This is down by about 26 percentage points from September as the refiner shut its No. 1
residue desulphuriser unit earlier this month for planned maintenance which is expected to last
about 40 days. <REF/A>

LONDON, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Diesel refining margins in
northwest Europe edged higher on Monday as declining imports
from the U.S. Gulf Coast were set to tighten supplies in the
region.
    
    * Demand in the region remained subdued, with little buying
of heating oil in Germany in recent weeks, traders said.
    * Barge freight rates have risen in recent days due to lower
water levels along the Rhine river, according to brokers
Riverlake Barging. 
    * Imports from the U.S. Gulf Coast were set to once again
drop sharply in the coming weeks as the majority of diesel
exports go to Latin America.
    * Imports from Asia and the Middle East are expected to
exceed 1 million tonnes in October, traders said. Several new
tanker bookings appeared over the past day.
    * Money managers slightly reduced their bullish bets on
diesel on both sides of the Atlantic last week but they remained
close to a record high after Hurricane Harvey wreaked havoc on
U.S. refineries.
    * Rosneft <ROSN.MM> has announced the launch of its
programmes to sell oil products from its refineries in 2018,
including ex-Bashneft Ufa refineries, for delivery in
January-December 2018.[nL8N1MR2YV]
    * Indian oil refiner Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd <BPCL.NS>
sold a low sulphur diesel cargo through an export tender for the
first time as its refineries upgrade units and due to higher
inventory of the fuel, three industry sources said on
Monday.[nL4N1MR3MO]

shipping fuel sulphur. The new rules come into force in just

    * REUTERS SUMMIT-Where's the money?  For major trading

SINGAPORE, Oct 16 (Reuters) - More spot cargoes out of India
weighed on the Asian gasoil cash differentials on Monday as it
was unusual for exports from India to go up after the monsoon,
trade sources said. 
    
    - INDIA SELLS GASOIL: India's Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd sold
a 50ppm sulphur diesel cargo through an export tender for the
first time, traders said. [L4N1MR3JY]
      The Indian refiner sold a combination cargo comprising
15,000 tonnes of 350ppm sulphur diesel and 20,000 tonnes of
50ppm sulphur diesel for loading from Mumbai over Oct. 21 to 25,
traders said.
      The cargo was sold to Unipec at a discount of about $1 a
barrel to Singapore quotes, they added.
      While BPCL has exported higher sulphur gasoil grades in
the past, this is the first time the refiner is exporting the
50ppm sulphur diesel grade through a tender, an industry source
familiar with the matter said.      
      BPCL may have one more spot cargo to export in November,
the source added. 
      Separately, India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals
Ltd sold 50ppm sulphur diesel for Oct. 27 to 29 loading to Vitol
at a premium of 50 to 60 cents a barrel to Middle East quotes,
traders said.
      MRPL typically sells 500ppm sulphur gasoil but likely has
lower sulphur diesel after recent upgrades to its refinery, a
trader said. 
     It has also offered 80,000 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur diesel
for Nov. 6 to 8 loading in a tender that closes on Oct. 23. 
    - TAIWAN SELLS GASOIL: Taiwan's CPC Corp sold a cargo of
50ppm sulphur diesel for loading from Kaohsiung in November to
Winson Oil at a premium of $1.30 a barrel to Singapore quotes,
traders said.
      The refiner also sold a 500ppm sulphur gasoil cargo for
November loading to Winson Oil at a premium of about $1 a barrel
to Singapore quotes, they added. 
      CPC last sold an October loading 10ppm sulphur diesel
cargo at a premium of $1.50 a barrel to Singapore quotes,
traders said. 
    - EGYPT OFFERS JET FUEL: Egypt's Middle East Oil Refinery
(MIDOR) has offered two jet fuel cargoes of 25,000 tonnes each
for loading over Nov. 17 to Nov. 19 and Nov. 28 to Nov. 30 from
Alexandria port. The tender closes on Oct. 18 and is valid until
Oct. 20.

    SINGAPORE BUNKER SALES 
    - Sales of marine fuels in Singapore during July rebounded 3 percent from a one-year low in
the previous month to 4.036 million tonnes as more ships called for refuelling at the world's
largest bunkering hub, official data showed on Monday.
    - However, the July volume was 8.1 percent lower compared to the year-earlier levels when
4.394 million tonnes were sold, the third-highest monthly volume on record.
    - The number of ships that called at Singapore for refuelling climbed to 3,297 in July, up 5
percent from June but 3 percent lower from the same time last year, the data showed. The
increase last month snapped four straight months of declines.
    - But the volume of bunker fuel each ship took on in July declined to an average of 1,224
tonnes each, a four-month low, Reuters calculations showed.
    - Looking ahead, however, three Singapore-based bunker fuel traders cautioned that sales
volumes in August could decline amid concerns of bunker fuel quality issues in Singapore and
growing global trade tensions.

engines emerged in Singapore, prompting some ship-owners and charterers to seek bunker fuel
supplies from other ports. [nL4N1UR4Q4] [nL4N1UN36X]

a tonne or below.

the Singapore window remained muted with no offers or trades. Jet fuel cash differentials
<JET-SIN-DIF> were at a discount of 1 cent a barrel to Singapore quotes, compared with a
discount of 2 cents on Monday.

* Iran exports could fall to 700,000 bpd-FGE
    * Would pile pressure on oil markets
    * China expected to remain main buyer even with sanctions

    By Ahmad Ghaddar and Henning Gloystein
    LONDON, July 17 (Reuters) - Iran's oil exports could fall by
as much as two-thirds by the end of the year because of new U.S.
sanctions, putting oil markets under huge strain amid supply
outages elsewhere in the world.
    Washington initially planned to totally shut Iran out of
global oil markets after President Donald Trump abandoned a deal
that limited Iran's nuclear ambitions, demanding all other
countries to stop buying its crude by November.
[nL1N1TS0Y1][nL1N1TU0YV]
    The United States has since somewhat eased its stance,
saying that it may grant sanction waivers to some allies that
are particularly reliant on Iranian supplies. [nL1N1UB08Q]  
    But most analysts still think the sanctions will
significantly reduce Iran's crude oil exports with some of the
worst case scenarios forecasting a two-thirds drop to only
700,000 barrels per day (bpd).
    Energy consultancy Facts Global Energy (FGE) thinks Iran's
crude exports could fall to only 700,000 bpd because of
sanctions. Those exports would mainly go to China, with smaller
shares going to India, Turkey and to other buyers with waivers. 
    Another 100,000 bpd of condensates could find their way to
China, buyers with waivers and possibly to the United Arab
Emirates and Korea, FGE says.   
    China, the biggest single importer of Iranian oil at 650,000
bpd according to trade flow data in Thomson Reuters Eikon, may
ignore U.S. sanctions and keep importing. 
    India, which imported an average of 550,000 bpd of Iranian
oil in the first half, has yet to make an official announcement.
However, its state-owned refineries have been told to prepare to
find alternative supplies should Washington grant it no waivers
to sanctions. [nL4N1TV03U]
    
    South Korea and Japan, which together imported around
370,000 bpd of Iranian crude during the first half of 2018, have
said they would stop imports unless they get a U.S. waiver.
[nL4N1U21EI][nL4N1TT1UK]
    South Korea's imports of Iranian crude were down 40 percent
in June from the same month a year ago, customs data shows.
[nL4N1U82DX]
    Japan's biggest bank, MUFG Bank Ltd, will halt all
Iran-related transactions to comply with the imposition of U.S.
sanctions, according to a document seen by Reuters on Thursday.
[nT9N1ML000]

    Europe accounted for the biggest chunk of Iran's oil exports
in the first half of the year, with Italy and Turkey the top
importers. 
    Several refiners already stopped their purchases of Iranian
crude after Swiss lender Banque de Commerce et de Placements
(BCP) said it would stop financing Iranian cargoes by June 30.
[nL8N1TU6AV]
    Refiners in Greece and Spain have already started slashing
their imports of Iranian crude. 
    But key buyer Turkey said it would not cut off trade ties
with Iran. [nA4N1SG00B]

LONDON, June 23 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe slightly declined on Thursday amid limited
trade as stocks in the region dropped by 2.3 percent.
    
    * ARA gasoline stocks fell 2.3 percent in the week to
Thursday to 1.019 million tonnes from 1.043 million tonnes a
week earlier, according to data from PJK International.[ARA/]
    * The market continued to find support from exports to the
United States, where gasoline demand surged last week. East
Coast stocks, however, rose last week, limiting gains, traders
said. [EIA/S]
    * Around 1.2 million tonnes of gasoline have been booked to
load in June on the transatlantic route from Europe to the
United States, Canada and Mexico, according to Reuters shipping
data.
    * Strong demand in North Africa, particularly in Algeria and
Egypt, also supported. Middle East buying has been weak in
recent weeks compared to a year ago, traders said.
    * At least three cargoes of reformate have been fixed in
recent days to go from northwest Europe to China, according to
shipping data.
    * Stocks in Europe however remain high with little buying
inside the region, traders said.
    * Egypt's EGPC is running a tender to buy one cargo per
month of gasoline delivered to Alexandria in July, August and
September, as well as at least one cargo basis Suez.

LONDON, June 22 (Reuters) -    * North Sea crude oil
differentials fell on Wednesday, leaving Forties at its lowest
since early May, as owners of physical barrels were unable to
find any takers. 
    * Total did not offer any cargoes for loading via
ship-to-ship transfer, which it has done most days so far this
month. Traders tend to view STS loadings as a sign of an
oversupplied market and Total's apparent inability to sell its
barrels has added to that perception, trading sources said.
    * Reuters shipping data showed Shell has tentatively booked
another VLCC, the Orthis, to load Forties in July, but two
traders said they believed this cargo would likely be for fuel
oil, rather than crude.

below the dated price for loading July 5-7.
    * Statoil offered a cargo of Ekofisk at 10 cents below dated
Brent for loading July 8-10. 
    * Total offered a cargo of Ekofisk for loading July 13-15 at
20 cents above dated Brent.

LONDON, June 21 (Reuters) -    * Forties differentials held
unchanged on Tuesday at their lowest since early May, pressured
by barrels in floating storage which struggled to find a buyer,
although a new supertanker fixture could provide some support,
trade sources said.
    * Total offered Forties from the Maran Thetis via
ship-to-ship transfer (STS), without finding a buyer.
    * Demand has yet to pick up even though French port and oil
refinery strikes are mostly over. The strikes had backed up at
least 15 million barrels of crude at ports, analysts at Energy
Aspects said on Monday. 
    * Reuters trade flows data showed there has been a one-month
hiatus in shipments of North Sea crude to the French port of Le
Havre. In the last 12 months, a monthly average of 2.6 million
barrels of North Sea crude have discharged in Le Havre,
according to the data. 
    * Reuters shipping lists show Shell has chartered the VLCC
Neptun to carry Forties to South Korea later this week. There
are, thus far, no fixtures for any July-loading Forties cargoes
bound for Asia.
    
    WINDOW SUMMARY:
    * Total offered a cargo of Forties for loading June 26-30
via STS at Scapa Flow from the VLCC Maran Thetis at a discount
of $1.55 to the August cash BFOE price.
    * Total offered a second cargo for loading July 1-5 via STS
at Scapa Flow from the Maran Thetis at a discount of $1.40 to
the August cash BFOE price.
    * Statoil withdrew an offer for Forties for loading July 3-5
at 45 cents below dated Brent.
    * Total offered a cargo of Ekofisk for loading July 13-15 at
a premium of 25 cents to dated Brent. This compares with last
Wednesday's trade at a discount of 20 cents to dated Brent.
    * When adjusting for the Ekofisk quality premium of 60
cents, Ekofisk is still the lowest-priced crude and sets the
price of dated Brent.

LONDON, June 20 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe rose by around $1 a barrel on Monday as higher
U.S. prices improved arbitrage economics from Europe, but
persistent oversupply capped gains.

rbob crack versus July WTI was at a one-week high of over $16.50
a barrel.

higher exports of the motor fuel from northwest Europe, traders
said. High inventories on both sides of the Atlantic however
continue to weigh on overall margins, they added. [EIA/S] [ARA]
    * Arbitrage to Nigeria, a key outlet for Europe's gasoline,
had gone quiet on the back of importers' issues accessing U.S.
dollars and NNPC's limited access to crude oil. But some were
optimistic that reforms designed to relaunch interbank currency
trading and attract foreign investors would free up dollars for
importing. [nL8N1992QS]
    * A unit used in reducing sulphur content in gasoline has
been shut down at Total's Antwerp refinery, according to

June 8-10, Genscape said. [nIGB3760C2]

SINGAPORE, June 22 (Reuters) - The Singapore fuel oil market strengthened on
Wednesday, with front-month time spreads and cash differentials narrowing discounts to
multi-week lows as expectation of tightening near-term supplies continues to boost
sentiment, traders said. 
    The contango structure of 380-cst fuel oil's July-August time spreads was at its
narrowest since May 12 at $1.50 a tonne below Singapore quotes on Wednesday, up 25 cents
from its previous close. <FO380SGSDMc1>
    Five deals were reported in the Platts window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst
fuel oil and a further 60,000 tonnes of the 380-cst grade, industry sources said. 
    Coastal was both a buyer and seller of 380-cst cargoes on Wednesday. The Hong Kong
and Singapore-based physical bunker supplier bought 20,000 tonnes of the fuel from
Phillips66 at $248 a tonne while also selling two 20,000 tonne cargoes of the same fuel
to Vitol at a discount of $2.50 and $3 a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    Cash discounts of the 380-cst fuel oil contracted by 36 cents on Wednesday to $2.18
below Singapore quotes, their narrowest since May 16. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    
    ARBITRAGE WINDOW WIDENS 
    The front month East-West (EW) spread, the price difference between FOB Singapore
180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil and FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil with maximum 3.5 percent
sulphur, was unchanged from the six-week high of $20.50 a tonne reached on Tuesday.
<FOSGEWMc1>
    EW spreads were recently dragged down to their lowest since August 2013, with the
price differential settling at $13.75 a tonne on June 2 because of burgeoning Singapore
fuel oil inventories <STKRS-SIN> at or near record highs over the past month.
[nL4N18U2XD]
    By comparison, EW spreads averaged $33.46 a tonne throughout 2015. 
    However, the uneconomic arbitrage opportunities over the past month limited arbitrage
flows and caused near-term Singapore supplies to be seen as tightening, particularly in
late July and early August, prompting a recovery in EW spreads, industry sources said. 
    The modest recovery in arbitrage economics has prompted the first July fixture of a
very large crude carrier (VLCC) from Rotterdam to Singapore by BP at a cost of $3.5
million, sources said. 
    The vessel, New Voyage, is off the coast of Spain and heading to Rotterdam, where it
is due to load its cargo on July 4 before heading to Singapore, Reuters ship-tracking
data showed. 
    
    TENDERS & AWARDS
    - State-owned Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) awarded a 35,000 tonne cargo of 380-cst
HSFO to UAE-based Gulf Petrochem for a discount between $9.50 and $10.50 a tonne to
Singapore 380-cst quotes and due for loading from Chennai between June 20 and 22.
[nL4N19E1XJ]

LONDON, April 25 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe declined on Tuesday, dragged down by a closed
arbitrage to the U.S. East Coast while exports to West Africa
picked up.
    
    * A large number of tankers which were booked in recent
weeks have loaded in recent days to ship gasoline to the U.S.
East Coast, offering support to regional prices.
    * The transatlantic arbitrage is however currently closed

    * Low imports, refinery maintenance boost European prices

    By Ron Bousso and Jarrett Renshaw
    LONDON/NEW YORK, April 26 (Reuters) - U.S. East Coast
refineries are stepping up exports of diesel despite a regional
deficit of the fuel as strong overseas demand, particularly in
Europe, is proving more profitable.
    Two tankers carrying 60,000-tonne cargoes of diesel have
been booked in recent days out of New York Harbor to go to
Northwest Europe, traders said.
    The two vessels, River Shiner and Two Million Ways, were
chartered by Swiss-based trading house Trafigura [TRAFG.UL] and
will load fuel sold by Delta Air Lines Inc's <DAL.N> refiner
subsidiary Monroe Energy, near Philadelphia.
    They are expected to top up their cargo in New York before
sailing to Europe, an East Coast trader said.
    The BP-chartered <BP.L>, 37,000-tonne Arctic Breeze is
nearing its destination - Sete port in southern France - after
loading a diesel cargo this month at the Kinder Morgan <KMI.N>
terminal in New York, according to traders and Reuters shipping
data.
    At least one other 37,000-tonne tanker has been booked on
the transatlantic route, traders said.
    U.S. Gulf Coast refineries have become a powerhouse of
distillate exports amid a rise in demand from Latin America and
West Africa due to refinery outages there. [nL8N1HX578]
    While Europe historically relies on a steady stream of
diesel from the U.S. Gulf Coast, the rise in competition has led
to a marked drop in that region's diesel exports to Europe.
    The U.S. East Coast typically imports middle distillates,
including diesel and heating oil, to meet regional demand. Over
the past year, the region imported an average of around 180,000
barrels per day of distillates, according to the U.S.
government's Energy Information Administration. 
    Although it is not unusual to see exports of heating oil
from the East Coast during the warmer summer months, diesel
exports are more rare.
    European diesel refining margins <LGO-LCO1=R> have risen in
recent weeks as imports from the U.S. Gulf Coast, Asia and the
Middle East slowed due to seasonal refinery maintenance.
    At the same time, high refinery maintenance in Europe,
particularly inland markets such as Germany, has led to lower
regional production. [ARA/]

supply of the fuel remained tight, traders said.

in turn boosting differentials, a Singapore-based trader said.

after the government agreed to consult them before signing an oil tank deal with
India. [nL4N1HW4TU]
    Thousands of Sri Lankan motorists queued for fuel earlier in the day after
workers went on strike to demand the government scrap the deal which trade
unions say would give India too much influence over fuel prices.
    Sri Lanka has agreed with India to jointly develop and operate all the tanks
in the oil storage facility in the port town of Trincomalee, near the world's
second deepest natural harbour.
    Lanka IOC already operates 15 of the oil tanks and the rest have not been
used for decades.
    For its part, IOC has agreed to build a second refinery with a capacity of
at least 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) in Sri Lanka, while Modi pledged in 2015

LONDON, April 24 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe held relatively stable on Monday after the
previous week's sell-off in oil futures and weaker than expected
demand in the United States.
    * After reaching 10-month highs in mid-April on the approach
of the U.S. driving season, the European gasoline barge crack
swap fell by about 70 cents last week on an unexpected jump in
U.S. gasoline stocks. The crack swap is holding at about $12 a
barrel.
    * South Africa's antitrust body said on Monday that
liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) producers should cap supply
agreements at 10 years because longer deals favour big
wholesalers and deter new competitors from entering the market.
[nL8N1HW2KL]
    * European refineries processed 3 percent more crude oil in
March than a year earlier, Euroilstock data showed on Monday.
Gasoline output rose 2 percent. <O/EUROIL2>
    * India is aiming to cut its oil products imports to zero as
it turns to alternative fuels, such as methanol, in its
transport sector, a government official said at an investor
briefing on Monday. [nL4N1HW38M]

    GASOLINE 
    * Gunvor sold two barges of benchmark Eurobob gasoline. It
sold one to Phillips 66 at $535 a tonne fob ARA and the other to
Varo at $534 a tonne fob ARA. The levels are down from Friday's
$539-$540 a tonne fob ARA.

tonne fob Amsterdam-Rotterdam, down from $548 and $539 a tonne
in the previous session. Gunvor and Total sold to Shell and
Varo.
    * There was no activity on barges of premium unleaded.
    * No cargo trades were reported.
    * The May swap traded at $540 a tonne at the close, down
from $545.50.
    * Brent crude futures <LCOc1> were 30 cents lower at $51.66
a barrel by 1548 GMT.
    * Gasoline barge refining margins fell to $14.04 a barrel
from $14.14.
    * U.S. front-month RBOB gasoline futures <RBc1> were 1.03
percent lower at $1.6276 a gallon.
    * The RBOB crack versus U.S. crude <RBc1-CLc1> stood at
$19.21 a barrel, down from $19.48 at the previous day's close.

    SINGAPORE, April 25 (Reuters) - Fuel oil refining margins edged higher to a six-week high on
Tuesday, buoyed by weak crude oil prices, while 380-cst cash premiums edged higher as buying
interest from PetroChina resurfaced.  

    REFINING MARGINS 
    - May refining margins of 180-cst fuel oil <FO180SGCKMc1> edged higher towards a new 6-week
high as crude prices remained weak. 
    - The 180-cst fuel oil crack to Dubai crude <FO180SGCKMc1> rose 15 cents from the previous
session to minus $3.42 a barrel, while 180-cst margins to Brent crude <FO180BRTCKMc1> slipped to
minus $4.84 a barrel, up 21 cents from Monday.
    - South Korea's top refiner SK Energy, said it expects strong demand for gasoline to support
Asian refining margins <DUB-SIN-REF> in the current quarter. [nS6N1BB010]
    - Asian refined product margins could also be supported by operational limitations on
China's independent refiners, as well as lower Chinese export quotas on refined products, the
company said.
   
    CARGO TRADES
    - Eleven cargo trades were reported in the Platts window totalling 220,000 tonnes of 380-cst
fuel oil with most trades being concentrated at the middle and back-end of the window.     
    - Lifting nine of Tuesday's traded cargoes, PetroChina was the main buyer followed by CAO
and Coastal with one each. 
    - Sellers of the cargoes were mixed with Koch, Lukoil and Total supplying three each while
BP and Shell each sold one.  
    - 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums <FO380-SIN-DIF> were 11 cents a tonne higher than the
previous session at a premium of 92 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes.  
    - A total of 3.32 million tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil have traded in the window since the
start of April.   
    - Please click on <O/AS> for more details. 

    EX-WHARF MARKET
    - Ex-wharf premiums, a key indicator of prompt market fundamentals, remained firm around
$2-$3 per tonne in April so far compared to about $1-$2.50 per tonne in March.
    - Premiums of the break-bulk parcels of fuel oil were supported by firm cargo premiums and
steady demand for bunker fuels, which have largely exceeded expectations this year so far.  
     
    CHINA MARCH FLOWS 
    - China imported 1.31 million tonnes of fuel oil in March, up 46 percent from a year
earlier, while exports of the fuel during the month fell 20 percent to 0.63 million tonnes.

LONDON, Sept 6 (Reuters) - BP bid for many cargoes of four
Nigerian grades in the window on Thursday at the same level for
a third consecutive session. 
    Separately, a few spot cargoes changed hands while India's
IOC and Indonesia's Pertamina both took multiple cargoes of west
African crude in their latest tenders. 
    
    NIGERIA
    * BP returned again to the window to bid for 9 cargoes of
Forcados, Bonny Light, Qua Iboe and Bonga all loading at various
times throughout October up to dated Brent plus $1.70 a barrel. 
    * The level was unchanged from the previous two sessions
when BP bid for the same cargoes.
    * The four grades are used to underpin the
contracts-for-difference swaps market and trading in the
physical market can frequently be linked to a position on the
paper side.
    * Glencore sold its Oct. 22-23 cargo of Amenam to BP,
traders said.
    * Total was offering Amenam at dated Brent plus 75 cents a
barrel and was said to have three cargoes still. 
    * Just under 30 cargoes of Nigerian crude were available
from the Nigerian programme. 
                   
    ANGOLA
    * BP was said to have sold its cargo of Pazflor to an
independent refiner in China.
    * Eni and Unipec were still offering Olombendo, Chevron
still has its Oct. 19-20 Cabinda and Total was showing Gindungo,
traders said.
    * On a delivered basis to Asia, Statoil was offering CLOV,
Dalia and Girassol.    
    
    TENDERS
    * India's IOC tender for around 2 million barrels of crude
for Nov 1-10 was awarded to Shell and Chevron but grade details
did not immediately emerge.
    * Indonesian refiner Pertamina awarded its late October
delivery tender to Shell and Total for a cargo each of Nigerian
Bonny Light and to Glencore for a cargo of Congolese Coco.
    * Thailand's PTT is seeking between 300,000 and 1 million
barrels of sweet crude for delivery between Nov 5-20. The tender
closes on Wednesday and the results are due the following day.
    * Uruguayan refiner ANCAP is seeking a 360,000-barrel cargo
of light crude for delivery between Nov 12-16. The tender closes
on Thursday.

SINGAPORE, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Asia's front-month viscosity spread, the price differential
between the prompt-month swaps for 180-cst and 380-cst fuel oil grades, fell to a near
three-year low on Wednesday amid a growing supply imbalance between the two grades of the fuel.
    Supplies of 180-cst fuel oil have been on the rise in recent months, weighing on prices of
the lower viscosity fuel, while relatively tight availabilities of finished grade 380-cst fuel
oil has pushed prices of the mainstay bunker fuel higher, trade sources said.
    Higher 180-cst fuel oil exports from India's Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd since August
following an extended shutdown of a 6,000-tonnes per day hydrocracker at its Mumbai refinery
that could last until December have contributed the rise in 180-cst fuel oil supplies.
[nL3N1WV3N0]
    The December viscosity spread was at $3 a tonne on Wednesday, down from $4.50 per tonne in
the previous session and its lowest since January 2016, Refinitiv data in Eikon showed.
<FOVISSGDFMc1>
        
    TENDERS
    - India's BPCL has offered a second 40,000 tonne cargo of 180-cst HSFO with a maximum 3.5
percent sulphur content loading from Mumbai over Dec. 11-13 in a tender closing on Nov. 30. 
    - BPCL sold a similar 180-cst HSFO cargo to Gunvor loading from Mumbai on Dec. 6-8 at an
unknown price level. 
    - BPCL also offered up to 33,000 tonnes of light diesel oil (LDO) with 2.8 percent sulphur
content for Dec. 10-12 loading from Mumbai.
    - Since August, BPCL has typically exported about three 40,000 tonne cargoes of 180-cst HSFO
as well as one or two 25,000-33,000 tonne LDO cargoes each month. 
    - India's Nayara Energy in a rare move has offered 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst HSFO with a
maximum 3.5 percent sulphur content loading from Vadinar over Dec. 20-24 in a tender closing on
Nov. 28. 
    - Trade sources said the offer from Nayara, the specifications of which are that of finished
grade 380-cst HSFO bunker fuel, is unusual as it typically exports vacuum gasoil and low-sulphur
waxy residue cargoes. 
    - Kuwait's KPC sold up to 80,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4.2 percent
sulphur content for Dec. 4-5 loading to Vitol at a premium of about $5 per tonne to Middle East
quotes on an FOB basis.
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
        
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - No cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fuel oil inventories at the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fell 21 percent, or 1.611
million barrels (about 240,000 tonnes), to a nine-month low of 6.164 million barrels (0.92
million tonnes) in the week ended Nov. 26, data from S&P Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]

supplies, follows the imposition of some U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil exports from
early-November which has deterred some traders from importing Iranian fuel oil into Fujairah.

compared with 9.974 million barrels (1.489 million tonnes) in the year before, Reuters
calculations showed.

SINGAPORE, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Asian refining margins for 10ppm gasoil plunged to a
four-month low on Wednesday as additional Chinese exports are set to hit the market, adding to
already abundant supplies currently available in the region.
    Refining margins, known as cracks, for gasoil with 10 ppm sulphur content <GO10SGCKMc1> fell
to as low as $14.52 a barrel over Dubai crude during Asian trading hours on Wednesday, their
weakest since Aug. 2. The margins were at $15.24 a barrel on Tuesday.
    The drop comes as the Chinese government gets set to release 2 million tonnes of additional
fuel export quotas this year, taking total 2018 quotas to about 48 million tonnes.
[nL4N1Y31UC][nL4N1Y23EL]
    This fuel, mostly gasoline and diesel, follows the release of 2.93 million tonnes of
additional fuel a month ago. The new quotas reflect slower than expected domestic demand for
transportation fuels in China, according to sources. [nL3N1X62FJ]
    Benchmark gasoil margins have shed more than 20 percent in the last two weeks since hitting
a four-year peak of $18.92 a barrel on Nov. 15. 
    The margins, however, are still at their strongest levels for this time of the year since
2015 and traders said the slump may not last as arbitrage opportunities from the East to the
West will likely offer support to Singapore's gasoil cracks.
    The exchange of futures for swaps (EFS), which determines the gasoil price spread between
Singapore and Northwest Europe <LGOAEFSMc1>, was around minus $32 per tonne on Wednesday,
Refinitiv Eikon data showed. 
    At current clean tanker rates, the spread should be over $20 per tonne to make the arbitrage
flows profitable for traders, Reuters calculations based on Refinitiv data showed.
    Cash discounts for 10ppm gasoil <GO10-SIN-DIF> widened to 45 cents a barrel to Singapore
quotes on Wednesday, hurt by weaker buying interests in the physical market. On Tuesday, they
were at a discount of 37 cents a barrel.
    Meanwhile, cash differentials for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> were at a discount of 69 cents a
barrel to Singapore quotes, compared with a discount of 68 cents a barrel on Tuesday.
    The likelihood of a warmer winter is keeping a lid on kerosene heating demand, traders said,
adding the jet cash differentials would likely stay muted at least for the next two weeks.
    Kerosene and jet fuel are closely related and belong to the same grade of oil products with
jet fuel refining margins determining the profitability of both.
    Refining margins for jet fuel <JETSGCKMc1> slipped to $17.17 a barrel over Dubai crude on
Wednesday, from $17.41 per barrel a day earlier.
    
    
    FUJAIRAH STOCKS
    - Middle distillate inventories in the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fell about 28
percent from a week ago to 2.2 million barrels in the week to Nov. 26, data via S&P Global
Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - Since the start of the year, middle distillate inventories in the Fujairah oil hub have
averaged 2.9 million barrels a week, compared with a weekly average of about 3.3 million barrels
in 2017, Reuters calculations showed.
    - Compared with year-ago levels, weekly Fujairah middle distillate inventories were 51
percent higher. 
    
    
    API INVENTORY DATA
    - U.S. crude stocks rose last week, while gasoline inventories decreased and distillate
stocks built, industry group the American Petroleum Institute said on Tuesday. [nZXN04G800]

barrels, compared with expectations for a 857,000-barrel drop, the API data showed. [API/S]

LONDON, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Sellers cut offer prices for a
variety of Nigerian grades on Wednesday, though buyers remained
reluctant because of a surplus of unsold crude and slowing
demand from China's independent refineries, traders said.
    Asian gasoline refining margins have fallen into negative
territory for the first time in seven years and China's
so-called teapot refineries have more than enough crude in
storage to cover immediate needs, traders said.
    Demand for Angolan grades, which tend to go almost solely to
Chinese refiners, has also slowed. About 20 cargoes out of the
original 43 in the January programme were still available for
sale despite sellers cutting offers by between 20 and 40 cents. 
    State-run Sonangol, BP and China's Unipec have all offered
cargoes of Angolan crude this week but failed to place any,
traders said.
    Offers for Nigerian Qua Iboe eased to about $1.65 a barrel
above dated Brent, from $1.70 earlier this week. Chevron and
Total were said to be offering, but no buyers stepped in.
    In the Nigerian market, traders estimate that nearly a
quarter of the December programme remains available.

SINGAPORE, June 7 (Reuters) - Cash premiums of Asia's 180-cst and 380-cst fuel oil grades
continued to narrow amid lower deal values and lower supplier offers for cargoes of the fuel in the
Singapore trading window on Thursday. 
    Cash premiums for both fuel oil grades have trended lower this week despite expectations of
tight supplies of finished grade bunker fuels in Singapore in June and July amid a lack of arbitrage
supplies and a shortages of cutter and blend stocks, trade sources said.
    Cash premiums of 380-cst fuel oil fell for a fifth straight session to $1.87 a tonne to
Singapore quotes. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    The 180-cst premium fell for a fourth consecutive session to a two-week low of $1.72 a tonne to
Singapore quotes. <FO180-SIN-DIF>
    In the previous week, strong buying interest for spot cargoes boosted cash premiums of both fuel
oil grades to more than eight-month highs. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories dropped 7 percent, or 1.517 million barrels
(about 226,000 tonnes), to a two-week low of 19.535 million barrels (2.916 million tonnes) in the
week ended June 6, data from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed on Thursday. [O/SING1]
    - The weekly inventory build was contrary to a 60 percent increase in fuel oil net imports into
Singapore from a week earlier to a 55-week high of 1.492 million tonnes in the week ended June 6.
    - Shrinking Singapore fuel oil exports, which fell to a seven-week low of 215,000 tonnes in the
week ended June 6, contributed to the higher net import volumes.
    - Compared with year-ago levels, the latest onshore fuel oil inventories were 12 percent higher,
the widest year-on-year surplus since the week ended Jan. 3.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Hong Kong topped the week ended June 6 at 66,000

BEIJING, Sept 12 (Reuters) - China on Wednesday slashed its
forecast for 2018/19 soybean imports, due to the Sino-U.S. trade
conflict, expectations of low soy content in animal feed and a
fall in pig farm profits, increasing the government's supply
deficit estimate.
    Imports of soybeans in the crop year that starts on Oct. 1
will be 83.65 million tonnes, down 10.2 million tonnes from last
month's estimate of 93.85 million tonnes, the Ministry of
Agriculture and Rural Affairs said in its monthly crop report.
    Imports of the oilseed were also pushed down as Beijing
promotes lower-protein animal feed and forecasts larger domestic
output, the ministry said. 
    The changes pushed the 2018/19 soybean deficit forecast to
3.57 million tonnes from 250,000 tonnes in August, according to
the report. 
    The ministry also raised its 2018/19 domestic soybean output
forecast to 15.83 million tonnes from 15.37 million tonnes in
August.

By Amanda Cooper
    LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The oil price has recovered from
last week's battering, ostensibly soothed by the possibility
that OPEC and its partners could cut production to prevent
another global surplus from forming. 
    But the futures market shows investors remain unconvinced
that such a plan will work. 
    The January Brent futures contract <LCOc1> is trading at a
discount to the February contract <LCOc2>, a pricing structure
known as contango that reflects a perception among traders and
investors that oil supply will be greater than demand.  
    The oil price <LCOc1> fell nearly 5 percent to below $65 a
barrel last week.   
    Seeking to prop up prices, producer club OPEC and rivals
such as Russia and Oman partnered in January 2017, agreeing to
cut crude output by a combined 1.8 million barrels per day to
drain an overhang of unused crude and refined products.
    The output restrictions forced stocks to fall and pushed the
futures market into backwardation, a structure in which
near-term futures trade above those for delivery further ahead
and which reflects a belief that supply will fall short of
demand.
    Backwardation persisted for most of 2017 and half of 2018,
until the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and
its partners agreed to raise output to counter any shortfalls
from U.S. sanctions aimed at choking off Iranian production. 
    Since then OPEC, led by Saudi Arabia, has struggled to
persuade the market that it can indeed maintain the balance
between supply and demand. The futures structure is now trading
at its largest contango since July, which in turn was the
largest for a year.
    Fast-growing output from producers over which OPEC has no
influence, such as the United States, threatens to tilt the
market into surplus for the whole of 2019, according to
estimates from the International Energy Agency. [IEA/M]
    The physical markets, where actual barrels of oil change
hands, are groaning under the weight of oversupply and prices
for some types of crude are at multi-year lows, as is the case
for North Sea Forties, which is instrumental in determining the
benchmark dated Brent price <BFO->. 
    As a result, fund managers have cut their record-high bets
on a sustained rally in Brent and West Texas Intermediate crude
futures <CLc1> by 50 percent in just eight weeks to the lowest
since mid-2017.
    Any stray bulls out there are, for now, laying low.

    BEIJING, Sept 12 (Reuters) - China on Wednesday slashed its
forecast for 2018/19 soybean imports as farmer reduce their use
of the bean in animal feed because of the Sino-U.S. trade
conflict, leading the government to raise its supply deficit
estimate.
    Imports of soybeans in the crop year that starts on Oct. 1
will be 83.65 million tonnes, down 10.2 million tonnes from last
month's estimate of 93.85 million tonnes, the Ministry of
Agriculture and Rural Affairs said in its monthly crop report.
    The forecast is lower than the 93.9 million tonnes imported
during the 2017/18 crop year.    
    The ministry said the lower forecast for soybean imports was
due to the promotion of lower-protein feed for livestock and
poultry. Additionally, falling profits at pig farms should
reduce demand for soymeal feed for the herds. 
    The government also raised its estimate for corn demand due
to rising feed consumption and increasing ethanol production and
as soybean imports fall.
    While the size of the soybean import cuts are largely inline
with broader industry forecasts, the report marks the first
official assessment by the government on the impact of the trade
war. 
    The outlook illustrates how China's vast pig farming sector
is rapidly adjusting to a possible prolonged trade dispute with
Washington. In July, Beijing levied an additional 25 percent
tariff on U.S. soybeans, threatening supplies from the
second-largest exporter of the oilseed to China.
    The import outlook changes pushed the 2018/19 soybean
deficit forecast to 3.57 million tonnes from 250,000 tonnes in
August, according to the report. 
    The ministry also raised its 2018/19 domestic soybean output
forecast to 15.83 million tonnes from 15.37 million tonnes in
August.

SINGAPORE, Feb 17 (Reuters) - The Asian diesel cash differentials could firm
as Australia's largest refinery is expected to be shut for up to two months, in
turn boosting imports of the fuel into the country, traders said on Friday.     
    Oil major BP will shut its 146,000-barrel-per-day Kwinana refinery in western
Australia for turnaround in February for up to 8 weeks, the company said.
<REF/OUT>
    The main focus of the work will be maintenance to the residue cracking unit
which converts heavy oil from the crude distillation unit and vacuum distillation
units into lighter fuels such as diesel and gasoline. 
    This could tighten supply of the ultra low sulphur diesel which is usually
shipped to Australia from Singapore as refineries are set to enter peak
maintenance period soon, traders said. 
    Brazilian fuel sales fell to 135 billion litres in 2016, down 4.5 percent
compared with the previous year, led by a sharp drop in sales of hydrate ethanol,
national oil agency ANP said. [nE5N19901M]
    Sales of diesel fell 5.1 percent.
    Diesel shipments from Asia to Brazil have dropped as a result, traders said. 
    Spot demand from Pakistan State Oil supported gasoil and jet fuel, traders
added. 
    India's Essar Oil likely sold up to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for
March 17 to March 22 loading from Vadinar at a premium of about 70 cents above
Middle East quotes, traders said.
    It also likely sold up to 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel for March 11 to March 15
loading at a premium of about 60 cents a barrel to Middle East quotes, they added.
    Both deals could not immediately be confirmed.
    Indonesia's Pertamina could have bought two cargoes of 600,000 barrels each of
0.25 percent sulphur gasoil for delivery in early March from Hin Leong at a
premium of about 30 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes, a Singapore-based trader
said.
    But the deal could not be confirmed with the relevant companies.

By Roslan Khasawneh
    DUBAI, Feb 20 (Reuters) - Asia's physical and paper fuel oil markets diverged on Monday
as aggressive supplier offers widened cash discounts of the 380-cst fuel, while premiums of
the prompt-month time spreads inched higher on limited activity. 
    Aggressive supplier offers weighed on cash discounts after three cash deals were
reported in the Platts window at lower deal values compared with previous sessions,
industry sources said. 
    Cargill and Vitol lifted two offers from Mercuria for 20,000 tonnes of the 380-cst fuel
at a discount of 50 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes each. 
    Meanwhile, Mercuria also hit Sinopec's bid for a similar 20,000 tonne cargo at a wider
discount of $1.25 a tonne below Singapore quotes in a move that industry sources said
suggests that the Geneva-based trader was eager to offload some of its cargoes. 
    Mercuria was also offering 20,000 tonnes of the 380-cst fuel at a discount of $2.50 a
tonne to Singapore quotes for delivery between March 7-11, but failed to find a buyer. The
offer was about $1 a tonne less than the next most competitive offer for a similar cargo
for delivery in the same laycan.  
    By comparison, on Wednesday, when the 380-cst fuel last traded in the window, deals for
similar cargoes were concluded at a premiums around 30-40 cents a tonne to Singapore
quotes, data compiled by Reuters showed.
    In the paper markets, the March/April time spread premium for the 380-cst fuel was
largely unchanged until after the window when it inched 35 cents a tonne higher from Friday
to $2.35 a tonne by 1800 Singapore time (1000 GMT), sources said.
    Sources said they expect trading activity to remain subdued this week as many
participants come to London for the International Petroleum Week starting on Tuesday. 
    Liquidity will also remain limited on Monday as the Presidents Day holiday in the
United States keeps markets there closed for a long weekend.

    DUBAI, Feb 16 (Reuters) - Spurred by a surprise drop in fuel oil inventories, bullish
sentiment on Thursday lifted Asia's prompt month time spreads for 380-cst fuel oil to
multi-week highs. 
    Premiums for the March/April time spread of 380-cst fuel oil on the Intercontinental
Exchange (ICE) were trading at $2.70 a tonne by 1800 Singapore time (1000 GMT) on Thursday,
up by about 70 cents a tonne from around the same time in the previous session, industry
sources said. [nL4N1FZ46Q]
    Reuters data showed the 380-cst prompt month spread contract <FO380SGSDMc1> was at its
widest premium in six weeks.
    Industry sources said the strength in the prompt market structure was largely sentiment
driven.     
    On Wednesday, 380-cst fuel March/April time spreads widened their backwardated
structure amid active trade which stirred expectations of a bullish trading strategy in the
near term. [nL4N1G02DI] 
    Traders also said sellers covering their short positions after the spike in prices
likely contributed to the sharp rise in prompt month time spreads over the past two
sessions. 
    In the physical markets, no cash deals were reported in the Platts window on Thursday.
    Meanwhile, aggressive offers in the ex-wharf market weighed on premiums of the
break-bulk fuel as suppliers sought to clear some inventories and counter a slowdown in
demand that is typical at this time of year, industry sources said.
    
    SINGAPORE INVENTORIES:
    Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories fell 219,000 tonnes, to a total of 3.1 million
tonnes in the week to Feb. 15, official data shows. [O/SING1]
    This came despite a 10 percent increase in net imports from the previous week to
959,000 tonnes, a four-week high. [nL4N1G137N]
    Most traders were surprised by the drop in inventories since most had expected the
inventory build to continue for a third week on the back of high volumes of February
arbitrage arrivals. 
    According to some traders, the drop in inventories could be a result of suppliers
clearing some landed inventories to allow for new arrivals.

cuts from July if global crude inventories fail to drop to a targeted level, OPEC sources
said. [nL8N1G02XW]
    - Belarus's Bel Oil has bought 80,000 tonnes of Iranian Light and Heavy crude oil from
National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) for loading in February, four sources told Reuters.

a near seven-month low in the previous session amid falling stocks of the fuel across key storage
hubs and weaker crude oil prices.

compared with minus $9.62 a barrel on Tuesday, its lowest since Aug. 12. <FO180BRTCKMc1>

Intermediate dipping below $65, pulled down by a report of increasing U.S. crude inventories that
surprised many traders. [O/R]

(377,000 tonnes) to a five-week low of 21.691 million barrels (about 3.24 million tonnes) in the
week ended March 27, data from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed on Wednesday.
[O/SING1]
    - This came as weekly net imports of fuel oil into Singapore slipped 8 percent from the week
before to a two-week low of 803,000 tonnes, the data showed. [nL3N1RA3A5]
    - In the week ended March 21, Singapore fuel oil stocks climbed to a 2018 high of 24.22 million
barrels (about 3.61 million tonnes). [nL3N1R438M]
    - A fire broke out on Tuesday last week at an oil storage tank at Tankstore's Pulau Busing
terminal in Singapore that was said to contain an unknown quantity of fuel oil. [nL3N1R24YB]
    - Compared with year-ago levels, the latest onshore fuel oil inventories were 15 percent lower.
    - Fuel oil inventories in Singapore have averaged 22.277 million barrels (3.32 million tonnes) a
week since the start of 2018.
    - In the United Arab Emirates, Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil inventories slipped 3
percent to a three-week low of 7.149 million barrels (about 1.07 million tonnes) in the week to
March 26, data via S&P Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]

diesel

expectations for a 1.6 million-barrel drawdown, EIA data showed.

barge
freight rates, as a result of strong activity in the gasoline

expected

drop in

maintenance, according to traders.

SINGAPORE, July 21 (Reuters) - A Russian ESPO crude cargo
arrived at the U.S. West Coast earlier this week, marking the
first import of this grade by the United States in eight months
as demand in Asia slowed, Thomson Reuters Eikon data showed on
Thursday.
    Aframax tanker Sea Bay loaded the crude at Russia's Pacific
port of Kozmino in late June and it arrived at the Long Beach
port on U.S. West Coast on July 19, according to trade flow and
live shipping data on Eikon.

premiums to a six-month low and opened the arbitrage window for
the Russian oil to head to the U.S. West Coast. [nL3N17M2SU]
    The United States last imported ESPO crude in November 2015,
the data showed.

Thailand and a rise in inventory in Singapore weighed on cash
differentals of the Asian gasoil grades, trade sources said on
Thursday.

to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for Dec. 1 to 5
loading in a tender that closes on Nov. 6, traders said.

sulphur gasoil or 50ppm sulphur diesel for Nov. 19 to 21 loading
in a tender that closes on Nov. 3.

fuel stocks climbed to a more than one-month high of 12.003
million barrels in the week to Nov. 1, latest data from
International Enterprise showed. <O/SING1>

increased from the week before while exports of the fuel to
Vietnam, Myanmar and Hong Kong reduced, likely causing the
stocks to increase, according to the data.

Singapore to Malaysia nearly doubled from the week before, while
exports to Australia also increased. 
    -  BPCL CANCELS GASOIL TENDER: India's Bharat Petroleum Corp
Ltd (BPCL) cancelled a tender that offered 35,000 tonnes of
50ppm sulphur diesel for Nov. 11 to 14 loading from Mumbai,
industry sources said.
      The refiner cancelled the tender due to a recovery in
diesel demand and lower production, one of the sources said,
though details were not immediately available. 
    -     BPCL COMPLETES EXPANSION: BPCL has ramped up the
operating rate of its Kochi oil refinery after completing an
expansion at the plant in southern India, two sources with
direct knowledge of the matter said on Thursday.
      The refinery is currently running at about 13 million
tonnes per year (tpy), or about 260,000 barrels per day (bpd),
up from its original capacity of 9.5 million tpy, one of the
sources said.
      BPCL plans to gradually ramp up Kochi to its new capacity
of 15.5 million tpy, he added, without giving a timeline.

SINGAPORE, Nov 3 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil margin slipped on Friday as stocks of the fuel
remained ample in the region, with economics to ship the cargoes west less profitable than a
month ago, traders said. 
    
    - WINSON OIL BUYS: Winson Oil bought three cargoes of gasoil on Friday, returning to snap up
cargoes after a big buying spree in September, traders said.
      The company has sold most of the cargoes it bought previously to the Philippines,
Indonesia and South China's bunkering market, traders said, though this could not be confirmed. 
   
    - JURONG PORT: Singapore port operator Jurong Port is entering the oil storage business to
diversify its revenue as volumes passing through its cement and steel terminals fall amid a
slowdown in the construction and shipbuilding sectors, its chief executive said. [nL4N1N91NN]
      Jurong Port is building a 480,000 cubic metres oil storage terminal on 16 hectares (39.5
acres) of land on its site to store clean petroleum products to be ready in the last quarter of
2019.
      The tanks will be mainly for middle distillates, the company said.
      Despite a backwardated market - where front-month oil prices higher than in forward months
make the storing of oil products uneconomical and yield a glut in storage capacity - demand for
tank capacity is expected to recover in two to three years, said Jurong Port Tank Terminals'
general manager Loh Wei.
      Jurong Port is also banking on an increase in demand for marine gasoil ahead of
International Maritime Organisation (IMO) fuel standards that start in 2020 and which will
likely cause shipowners to use more low sulphur gasoil to power vessels instead of fuel oil.  
    - MIDDLE EAST AIRLINES: Middle Eastern carriers saw their slowest rate of international
growth in September in over eight years, with a temporary ban on electronics and proposed travel
restrictions hitting demand, according to an airline industry body on Thursday. [nL8N1N874B]
      Demand, measured in revenue passenger kilometres, rose 3.7 percent in September, the
slowest rise since February 2009, the International Air Transport Association said in its
regular monthly traffic update.

LONDON, Oct 31 (Reuters) - Energy trader Gunvor Group has
appointed Muriel Schwab as its new chief financial officer and
she will take up the position by May 1 next year, the company
said on Wednesday. 
    Schwab replaces Jacques Erni who has been Gunvor's CFO since
2013. Erni has been at Gunvor since 2006 and will become an
executive director after a transition period.
    The move is part of the company's leadership revamp that
began earlier this year. [nL5N1UY5UO]
    Schwab was previously regional head of trade and commodity
finance for the Americas at Rabobank in New York and a member of
the trade commodity finance management team. 
    She was previously at Gunvor between 2007 and 2014 and also
has held roles at Taurus Petroleum, Credit Suisse and ING.

SINGAPORE, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Asia's 10ppm gasoil cash premium to Singapore benchmark prices surged nearly
29 percent on Tuesday to reach an almost one-year high of $1.35 a barrel as supplies tightened due to demand,
recent refinery maintenance and outages. 
    - Bad weather had caused supply disruptions in Japan, with Fuji Oil's refinery in Sodegaura seen affected
by a power blackout due to a typhoon. [nL4N1WI1VM]
    - Idemitsu Kosan's refinery in Hokkaido had been previously affected by an earthquake and its crude unit

SINGAPORE, Oct 26 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil differential
slipped on Wednesday on the back of ample supply in the region
but spot demand from Sri Lanka limited the fall, trade sources
said.     
    Spot demand from Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp for a
December cargo could boost sentiment, though the volumes were
not very big, traders said. 
    China's end-September refined fuel stocks were down 6.59
percent from the previous month at their lowest since December
2015, data from the official Xinhua news agency showed on
Wednesday. [nL4N1CW26R]
    Diesel led the fall with a decline of 12.8 percent to about
6.34 million tonnes, according to Reuters' calculations based on
historical figures, the lowest since at least January 2014.
    Diesel was bolstered by incremental demand in the
agricultural sector and infrastructure projects, said China OGP,
a Xinhua-run newsletter.
    Bahrain Petroleum Co (Bapco) likely sold 40,000 to 60,000
tonnes of 10ppm sulphur gasoil for Dec. 6-9 loading at a premium
of $1.50 a barrel above Middle East quotes, traders said, though
this could not be confirmed. 
    Kenya's oil importers are expected to enter the spot market
seeking oil products, which will likely boost gasoil and jet
fuel differentials, traders said.

gasoil and 192,000 barrels of jet fuel for Dec. 11-12 delivery
to Colombo. The tender closes on Nov. 8 and is valid for 72
hours.

SINGAPORE, Aug 15 (Reuters) - Front-month time spreads for Asia's 380-cst fuel oil slipped
to a more than one-week low on Wednesday as industry participants expected improved higher
supplies in August and September to ease supply constraints in the Singapore trading and storage
hub. 
    The 380-cst Sept/Oct time spread was trading at about $5 a tonne on Wednesday, down from
$5.25 a tonne on Tuesday and its lowest since Aug 7. <FO380SGSDMc2>
    Meanwhile, tight supplies of finished grade 380-cst bunker fuels helped to lift ex-wharf
premiums of the fuel to about $10-$12 a tonne this week, up from about $8-$10 a tonne a week
ago, trade sources said. 
    The higher ex-wharf premiums come despite lower spot demand for bunker fuels in Singapore as
shippers seek to minimise the risk of loading batches of contaminated bunker fuels that surfaced
in Singapore around the end of July, sources said. [nL4N1UR4Q4]
    
    AUGUST ARBS HIGHER
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia in August are expected to be higher from the previous
month, with about 6 million tonnes notionally assessed so far, assessments by Thomson Reuters
Oil Research showed on Tuesday. [nPGEtVWwba]
    - In comparison, July inflows closed at a 23-month low of 5.2-5.3 million tonnes. 
    - The higher-than-expected arrivals for August are partly the result of higher arrivals of
Middle East and western cargoes which were attracted by strong Asian price benchmarks as well as
tepid demand in the Middle East where Pakistan did not award most of its July-August tenders,
according to the assessments. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fuel oil inventories at the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fell 10 percent, or 1.06
million barrels (about 158,000 tonnes) to 9.293 million barrels (about 1.387 million tonnes) in
the week ended Aug 13, data from S&P Global Platts showed on Wednesday. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - In the previous week, Fujairah fuel oil stocks were at an eight-month high of 10.353
million barrels (1.545 million tonnes), the highest since the week to Dec 11. 
    - Compared with the same time last year, Fujairah fuel oil inventories were 23 percent
lower, but were above the 2018 weekly average of 8.308 million barrels (1.24 million tonnes),
Reuters calculations showed.    
    
    WINDOW TRADES

of 180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) and 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst HSFO.

    TENDERS
    - Saudi's Samref sold 80,000 tonnes of 650-cst to 700-cst high-sulphur fuel oil loading from
Yanbu on Aug 27-29 to Chevron at an unknown price level.
    - Indonesia's Pertamina has offered 80,000 barrels of vacuum residue loading from Plaju over
Sept 19-20 in a tender closing on Aug 15 with validity to Aug 20.
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
    
    RELIANCE FM 
    - India's Reliance Industries, which operates the world's largest refining complex, has
declared force majeure on gasoline exports from its Jamnagar site, four people familiar with the
matter said on Wednesday, potentially boosting margins for other suppliers of the oil product.
[nL4N1V62K1]
    - The force majeure follows an unspecified issue at a gasoline-producing fluid catalytic

per day (bpd) in the special economic zone in Jamnagar, two of the people said.
    - It was not immediately clear what the issue at the FCC was.
    - The unit is expected to restart within two weeks, the company said in a statement.

SINGAPORE, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Cash premiums for Asia's mainstay 380-cst high-sulphur fuel
oil slipped to a near one-month low on Thursday, as rising supplies helped ease concerns of
tight availability of finished grades of the fuel.
    However, traders said further downside risk would be limited due to a tighter supply outlook
in December amid expectations of lower arbitrage volumes on the last month of the year. 
    Premiums for 380-cst cargoes slipped to $7.82 a tonne to Singapore quotes on Thursday, from
$8.33 in the previous session, and their lowest since Oct. 25. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    Singapore fuel oil inventories jumped 13 percent to a four-week high in the week ended Nov.
21, despite an 18 percent drop in net imports to a two-week low, official data released on
Thursday showed. [nL4N1XX3K5]
    The higher inventory levels were in line with market expectations of increased arbitrage
flows into Singapore in November, compared with the previous month, with more volumes due for
arrival in the second half of the month, trade sources said.
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Onshore fuel oil inventories jumped 2.082 million barrels (about 311,000 tonnes) to 17.903
million barrels, or 2.672 million tonnes, in the week to Nov. 21, data from International
Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed. [O/SING1]
    - Net fuel oil imports came in at 1.121 million tonnes, compared with an 11-week high of
1.359 million tonnes in the week before. Weekly figures like this are volatile, however.
    - Singapore fuel oil net imports have averaged 792,000 tonnes per week in 2018.
    - This week's onshore fuel oil inventories were 24 percent lower than a year earlier.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to China topped the week ended Nov. 21 at 297,000
tonnes, an 11-month high, followed by Hong Kong at 264,000 tonnes, Malaysia at 106,000 tonnes
and Qatar at 41,000 tonnes.
    - Singapore's fuel oil shipment to Qatar in the week to Wednesday marked a second
consecutive week of fuel oil exports to the gas-rich Gulf state. Before that, Singapore never
exported fuel oil to Qatar since at least December 2015, or as far as records go back, official
data compiled by Reuters showed.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Iraq at 533,000 tonnes, followed by
Russia at 286,000 tonnes, the Netherlands at 218,000 tonnes, Saudi Arabia at 192,000 tonnes and
Malta at 172,000 tonnes.
    - Singapore's fuel oil imports from Iraq hit a record high in the week to Nov. 21. Only
Russia and Malaysia exported larger volumes of fuel oil to Singapore in any given week this year
at 658,000 tonnes and 679,000 tonnes, respectively.

LONDON, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Spot trade in the West African
market remained fairly sluggish on Thursday, as buyers waited
for the bulk of the Nigerian export plan for January to emerge,
while loadings in Angola are set to fall for a second month in a
row that month.
    * Angola's final loading programme for January contains just
43 crude oil cargoes, up one from the preliminary schedule and
down from 46 cargoes in December, a source familiar with the
matter said. [O/LOAD]
    * The programme includes six spot cargoes.
    * Angola will export fewer cargoes in 2018 than at any time
since 2011, based on monthly loading programmes.
    * Traders said the Nigerian January loading schedules for
major grades such as Bonny Light and Forcados had not yet been
released. The January Qua Iboe programme, which emerged earlier
this week, lists seven cargoes, down from December's eight.
    * Both Qua Iboe and Bonny Light were last indicated around
$1.70 a barrel above dated Brent, unchanged over the last week,
although buyers were said to find this level far too pricey
given the number of unsold cargoes still in the market, traders
said.
    * Almost a third of the cargoes in the December Nigeria
programme were still said to be available for sale, marking the
largest overhang in several months in the West African market,
according to Reuters calculations.
    * Taiwan's CPC issued a buy tender for crude loading in
January or to be delivered in February. The tender was due to be
awarded on Tuesday and the rest is expected to emerge on
Wednesday.
    * Thailand's PTT is looking to purchase between 300,000 and
1 million barrels of light sweet crude for arrival between mid
January and mid February, in a tender that closes on Thursday.

SINGAPORE, March 2 (Reuters) - The jet fuel cash differential slipped from multi-year highs
on Friday as temperatures in Japan rose, indicating winter demand may ease, traders said.
    
    JET FUEL DEMAND
    * Japan is set to import 10 to 12 medium-range cargoes of jet fuel in February, likely the
highest on record, traders said, due to a cold winter and refinery maintenance curbing supply.
      But with the temperature rising late this week, imports of jet fuel could slip to four to
five cargoes in March and exports of the fuel may resume in April, one of them said.
      A backwardated market structure has also prompted many to give up storage space, creating
a very low inventory of jet fuel, which had in turned tightened the spot market, the trader
added.
      Japanese oil refiner Idemitsu Kosan said in February that it shut a 60,000 barrels-per-day
(bpd) residue hydro desulphurisation unit at Aichi refinery due to a problem, adding that there
is no schedule yet for resuming the unit.
      This has caused tightness in the market for jet fuel cargoes, traders said.
      Scheduled refinery maintenance in South Korea and Taiwan are also causing supply
tightness, they added.     
    
    INDIA
    * India's Essar Oil may have sold up to 44,000 tonnes of 500 ppm sulphur gasoil for loading
over March 29 to 31 at parity to Singapore quotes, traders said, though this could not
immediately be confirmed.
      The cargo size is smaller than what the refiner typically offers.     

    RUSSIA
    *  Russia's exports of ultra-low sulphur diesel (ULSD) from the Baltic Sea port of Primorsk
is expected to fall in March by 7.3 percent on a daily basis to 1.415 million tonnes, from 1.378
million tonnes planned for February, which is three days shorter, trade sources said.

LONDON, Sept 12 (Reuters) - European diesel stocks are
expected to fall by about 2 million tonnes in September as
imports from the United States plunge in the wake of Hurricane
Harvey which crippled refining operations on the Gulf Coast,
traders said on Tuesday.

SINGAPORE, Sept 13 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differentials on Wednesday spiked to a
near two-year high on continued buying from Winson Oil, traders said. 
    
    - WINSON OIL BUYS MORE: Winson Oil bought 450,000 barrels of gasoil on Wednesday, bringing
its total tally to over 9 million barrels since the start of September, trade data showed.
      At least three to four long-range tankers have been chartered by Winson Oil to store
gasoil for a period of two to three months in Asia, shipbrokers said.
      Winson Oil has also bought a super-tanker, known in the trade as a very large crude
carrier (VLCC), to store fuel off Singapore waters. The vessel is Winson Oil's second VLCC.
      Unipec has chartered a newly built VLCC, Coshonour Lake, to load gasoil from Tianjin in
northern China in the second half of September, likely to head to Europe, a person close to the
matter said. The person spoke on condition of anonymity as he was not allowed to speak to media.
    - INDIA OFFERS GASOIL: India's Essar Oil has offered up to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for loading from Vadinar over Oct. 9 to 13 in a tender that closes on Sept. 14. India's
exports of diesel are expected to slow over the fourth quarter as domestic demand could pick up
post-monsoon, traders said. 
    - CHINA POLLUTION CRACKDOWN: China's crackdown on pollution is choking output of chemicals,

SINGAPORE, Sept 8 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil and jet fuel cracks were bid up during
Singapore trading hours to their highest levels in nearly two years on Friday, boosted by strong
demand for spot cargoes and a tighter supply outlook, trade sources said.
        
    - CRACKS FIRM: The October gasoil crack to Dubai crude <GOSGCKMc1> rose for a fifth
consecutive session, reaching $15.82 a barrel on Friday, up from $15.22 in the previous session
and its highest since September 2015. 
    - The October jet fuel crack to Dubai crude <JETSGCKMc1> rose 48 cents a barrel from the
previous session to $15.17, its highest since November 2015. 
    - In addition to a surge in demand for arbitrage cargoes into the United States after
Hurricane Harvey, industry sources also pointed to improved demand from China for gasoil as it
lifts its fishing ban in mid-September. [nL4N1LG30C]
    - Asian jet fuel and gasoil supplies are also expected to tighten in the near term amid
scheduled turnarounds in September and October in northeast Asia, adding to supply shortages
caused by Harvey. At its peak the storm knocked out nearly a quarter of U.S. refining capacity. 
  

    - BUYING SPREE: Demand for physical cargoes continued on Friday, with 1.65 million barrels
changing hands through 11 deals in the Platts window. 
    - On Thursday 3.1 million barrels of gasoil were traded in Singapore through 18 deals, the
highest in number and volume since at least the start of the year. [nL4N1LO412]
    - Physical trade activity has soared since the start of the month. A total of 9.65 million
barrels of gasoil has exchanged hands in the Platts window at an average of 13 trades per day. 
    - By comparison, the last four trading days of August saw a total of 1.135 million barrels
of gasoil traded in the window at an average of less than two deals a day.

SINGAPORE, Sept 12 (Reuters) - Cash premiums of Asia's mainstay 380-cst fuel oil extended
loses on Tuesday as buying interest receded to the point where no deals were reported in the
Platts window, traders said. 
    The lack of physical buying interest is a sharp contrast from the intense trading
activity seen in the previous week. 
    Meanwhile, the East-West (EW) arbitrage spreads also extended loses, narrowing the
opportunity to secure new fuel oil bookings from northwest Europe, sources said. 

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - One cargo trade was reported in the Platts window, after Mercuria bought 20,000 tonnes
of 180-cst fuel oil from P66.
    - Trafigura, September's top buyer of fuel oil cargoes in the window, was absent from the
window for the first time this month. 
    - Trafigura has bought 1.031 million tonnes of fuel oil cargoes in the window since the
start of the month. Hin Leong was the second largest purchaser of fuel oil cargoes in
September with 220,000 tonnes. 
    - The top suppliers in September were Mercuria with 822,000 tonnes and PetroChina with
380,000 tonnes. 
    - A total of 1.5 million tonnes of HSFO traded in the window in the first week of
September compared with 1.4 million tonnes in August.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 

    ARBITRAGE SPREADS
    - Broker sources said both the October and November EW arbitrage spreads were about 50
cents a tonne lower on Tuesday from the previous session at about $15.50 a tonne and $17.75 a
tonne, respectively. 
    - Reuters data shows the October <FOSGEWMc2> and November <FOSGEWMc3> arbitrage spreads
both slip for two consecutive sessions after both spreads reached a near one-week high at the
end of the previous week. 
    - Industry sources said the arbitrage window was possibly being offered down as some
suppliers lock in fresh cargoes for arrival into Singapore. 
        
    TENDERS
    - Bahrain's Bapco sold two 380-cst cargoes, each 80,000 tonnes in volume, for late-Sept
delivery from Sitra, each at a premium less than $2 a tonne to Arabian Gulf 380-cst quotes.
[nL4N1LT2QL]
    - Industry sources said PetroChina was possibly awarded the first cargo for Sept. 20-23
loading while Litasco was awarded the second for Sept. 24-27 loading, but this could not be
confirmed. 
    - One tanker report showed Litasco fixed the PVT Athena aframax vessel to load 80,000
tonnes of fuel oil from Bahrain on Sept. 24 heading East, while a tanker broker said
PetroChina was enquiring about a vessel to load a similar sized cargo from Bahrain to
Fujairah or the East on Sept. 20-23. 
           
    OTHER NEWS
    - Iraq's Oil Marketing Company (SOMO) postponed its plan to switch its price benchmark
for Basra crude in Asia to DME Oman futures from January 2018, according to a letter seen by
Reuters. [nL5N1LS5VX]

for Basra crude to DME Oman futures from the average of Platts' Oman-Dubai prices with effect
from January 2018, according to the letter dated Sept. 10, and sent by Falah Alamri, the
former head of the state oil marketer.
