LONDON, Sept 12 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins
dropped to their lowest since Aug. 29 as exports from the region
slowed sharply in the wake of Hurricane Harvey.
    * Several new gasoline cargoes have been booked out of the
region for North America and West Africa in recent days but the
flow remains significantly lower than in previous weeks.
    * Some 700,000 tonnes of gasoline and blending components
have been booked to sail on the transatlantic route in recent
weeks. 
    * Refineries on the U.S. Gulf Coast are slowly starting up
again after being shut down ahead of Hurricane Harvey. Six
refineries are restarting along the Texas Gulf Coast, according
to their owners, some of them after dealing with several feet of
floodwater in their facilities. [nL2N1LS1X2]
    * Several cargoes heading to the New York Harbour region
were redirected to Latin America after a rush of cargo bookings
to the region in the wake of the hurricane, traders said.

bids or offers.

fob Amsterdam-Rotterdam, compared with trades at $576-$599 a
tonne on Monday. Shell, NIC and Total sold to BP and Gunvor.

afternoon window. Offers came in at $603 a tonne fob ARA.

from $534 a tonne on Monday.

end of May at around $12.52 a barrel.

sharply on Thursday as ARA stocks rose, mirroring a rise last
week in the United States.

CHICAGO, April 19 (Reuters) - A shipment of Paraguayan corn
was due to arrive next month at the U.S. port of Wilmington,
North Carolina, a U.S. grains trader said on Wednesday.
    The vessel Nord Bering was moored at the Brazilian port of
Paranagua, according to Thomson Reuters Eikon data. It was
scheduled to arrive in Wilmington by May 20, according to the
port website.
    The grain was shipped to Brazil from land-locked Paraguay
before being loaded onto the U.S.-bound vessel, said the U.S.
trader, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not
authorized to speak to the media. If loaded to its 61,000 tonne
capacity, the shipment would be the biggest-ever U.S. import of
Paraguayan corn, according to U.S. Department of Agriculture
data.

180-cst fuel oil <FO180-SIN-DIF> to their highest since December on Monday amid robust
demand for the lower viscosity fuel. 
    Industry sources said fewer arrivals of cutter stocks into Singapore, which are used to
blend high-viscosity material into lower viscosity fuel oils, have also been boosting
premiums of 180-cst fuel oil since the start of May. [nL4N1I62FR]
    
    WINDOW TRADES

tonnes of fuel oil, the most in number since April 17.

tonnes together with four 180-cst fuel oil trades totalling 80,000 tonnes.

which each bought one.

traded in the window since the start of May.

session to $4.32 a tonne to Singapore quotes, the highest since Dec. 28.

swaps largely unchanged.

on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) on Monday. 
    - The ICE-traded 380-cst June/July contract was 5 cents a tonne lower from the previous
session at 45 cents a tonne by 7:00 p.m. Singapore time (1100 GMT) after trading about
220,000 tonnes in contracts. 
    
    OTHER NEWS

refinery to Washington in the U.S. west coast in what traders say is an unusual move.

refinery.

SINGAPORE, May 4 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil differentials fell on Thursday amid thin
liquidity as underlying crude oil prices fell, traders said. 
    
    - STOCKS: Singapore middle distillates stocks slipped by 3.6 percent to a two-week low
of 11.732 million barrels in the week to May 3, latest data from International Enterprise
showed. [nL4N1I62ED] 
    India, South Korea and the United Arab Emirates shipped more cargoes to Singapore last
week than the week before as the arbitrage to ship the cargoes west is not profitable,
traders said.
    Still, higher exports of the fuel to Australia, Myanmar, New Zealand and Sri Lanka drew
down the stocks, the data showed. 
    - SOUTH AFRICA: Larger-than-usual demand from South Africa's PetroSA supported gasoil
margins, traders said.
    PetroSA is seeking up to 247,000 tonnes of gasoil and gasoline for delivery over June
to October, a tender document showed. The tender closes on May 8 and is valid until May 11.
    PetroSA usually imports oil products in the spot market when there is a sudden spike in
domestic demand or supply disruptions from local refineries, traders said. It was not
immediately clear why the company was seeking term cargoes. 
    - IRAQ REFINERY: Iraqi's oil ministry on Thursday asked foreign companies and investors
to bid for a project to build and operate a 300,000-barrel-per-day export-oriented refinery
in Fao, near the southern city of Basra. [nL8N1I62IZ]
    Bidding documents provide for two investment models -- build-own-operate and
build-operate-transfer, the ministry said in a statement.

four-month high as suppliers sought to lock in replacement cargoes for June amid easing
Singapore supplies [O/SING1] as a result of robust demand for cargoes in the Platts window

limited at current price levels.

session.

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, May 4 (Reuters) - The front-month visco spread, the differential between
the price of 180-cst and 380-cst fuel oil, rose towards a two-year high on Thursday as
bidding interest for the low-viscosity fuel soared amid concerns over a tightening of
cutter stocks, which are used to blend high-viscosity material into bunker fuels.
    Industry sources said that availability of the blend-stock had started to show signs
of tightness in the past couple of weeks. 
    
    SWAPS MARKET
    - Reuters data showed the June visco spread jump $2.25 a tonne from the previous
session to $9.50 a tonne on Thursday, its highest since July 2015.
    - On the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), time spreads of 380-cst fuel oil, from
May/June to Sept/Oct, all posted gains over the previous session in trading volumes in
excess of a million tonnes by 5:30 p.m. Singapore time (0930 GMT).
    - The ICE 380-cst July/Aug contract, pegged at a 65 cent premium, posted the largest
gains on Thursday over the previous session of 40 cents a tonne. 
    - Meanwhile, the ICE 380-cst June/July contract, also pegged at a 65 cents per tonne
premium, was the most actively traded time spread with about 640,000 tonnes in contracts
changing hands. 

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Four cargo trades were reported in the Platts window on Thursday. These were one
20,000 tonne cargo of 380-cst fuel oil and three cargoes of 180-cst fuel oil totalling

SINGAPORE, Oct 8 (Reuters) - Asia's cash differentials for 10ppm gasoil rose on Monday due
to stronger demand in the region, while refining margins for the industrial fuel gained on
weaker crude prices.
    Cash premiums for 10ppm gasoil <GO10-SIN-DIF> climbed to 54 cents a barrel to Singapore
quotes, compared with a premium of 45 cents a barrel a day on Friday. 
    The gasoil market remains firm as supply available is quite limited on the back of steady
demand at present, but the arbitrage opportunities are still closed, trade sources said. 
    The gasoil price spread between east and west widened to its maximum in more than two weeks
on Monday though it was still not profitable to ship cargoes from east to west, traders said.
    The exchange of futures for swaps (EFS) <LGOAEFSMc1> widened to minus $6.61 a tonne on
Monday, from minus $4.46 a tonne on Friday, Reuters data showed. Arbitrage is usually profitable
when the EFS trades at about minus $15 a tonne and below.
    Refining margins, or cracks for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10SGCKMc1> were at
$16.30 a barrel over Dubai crude during Asian trading hours Monday, up from Friday's $16.03 a
barrel.
    Meanwhile, jet fuel cracks <JETSGCKMc1> inched higher to $16.06 a barrel over Dubai crude,
from $15.79 a barrel in the previous session.
    Cash discounts for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> narrowed to 21 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes
on Monday as the prompt-month spread slimmed its contango structure. Jet cash discounts were at
42 cents a barrel on Friday.

24-28 loading at a premium of 55 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes.

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, May 15 (Reuters) - Lower deal values in the Platts window on Monday saw
cash premiums of 380-cst fuel oil <FO380-SIN-DIF> fall to their lowest in May, while
near-dated 380-cst time spreads on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) gave back gains
made in the previous week in low traded volumes. 

    PAPER MARKETS
    - The ICE-traded 380-cst June/July spreads contract fell by 45 cents a tonne from the
previous session to 5 cents a tonne, after trading about 260,000 tonnes in contracts by
5:00 p.m. Singapore time (0900 GMT) on Monday.
    - Industry sources said the spreads contract lost as much as 40 cents a tonne earlier
in the day before physical trade in the Platts window began amid relatively low volumes of
less than 100,000 tonnes in contracts. 
    - Given firm demand for 380-cst fuel oil cargoes and expectations of narrower supplies
from around June, sources said they expected time spreads to recover from Monday's losses.
    - Open Interest (OI) levels for the ICE 380-cst June contract rose to just over 10.5
million tonnes, the highest OI level for any month this year. 
    - Previously, the 380-cst March contract held the highest OI levels for the year at
just under 10 million tonne.

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Eight cargo trades were reported in the Platts window on Monday totalling 100,000
tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil through five cargoes, along with three 20,000 tonne cargoes of
180-cst fuel oil.
    - While volumes in the window remain elevated, Monday's deal values were lower
compared with the previous session. 
    - Monday's deals were concluded at a premium range between 76 cents and $1.35 a tonne
to Singapore quotes, down from Friday's deal premiums between $1.3 and $2 a tonne. 
    - A total of 1.16 million tonnes of fuel oil have traded in the window since the start
of May, compared to 3.821 million tonnes in April.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    VESSEL CHARTERS
    - Koch has fixed a VLCC, the MT Artois, to load up to 270,000 tonnes of fuel oil in
Rotterdam on May 31 for delivery into Singapore by July 9, industry sources said. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Russian oil producer Surgutneftegaz has awarded Trafigura with up to 3.7 million
tonnes of fuel oil via tenders, produced at Kirishi refinery, for delivery from the Baltic
Sea port of Ust-Luga in July-December 2017, industry sources told Reuters on Monday.
[nL8N1IH351]
    - The UAE's ADNOC is offering up to 425,000 tonnes of straight-run fuel oil (SRFO)
through five 85,000 tonne cargoes for delivery on July 2-4, July 7-9, July 13-15, July
19-21 and July 25-27 from Ruwais. The tender closes on May 16. [nL4N1IH34S]
    It was unclear why ADNOC was offering five cargoes of SRFO in July, which is higher
than the usual 3-4 cargoes it has been offering since the start of the year after a fire
at its Ruwais refinery damaged a secondary processing unit. [nL3N1HB33O]

SINGAPORE, April 4 (Reuters) - Asia's prompt-month viscosity spread extended gains for a sixth
consecutive session to a near three-year high on Wednesday after almost three weeks of steady gains.
    The April viscosity spread settled at $10.75 a tonne on Wednesday, up from $9.75 a tonne in the
previous session and its highest since June 2015. <FOVISSGDFMc1>
    Concerns of tight blendstock supplies over the coming month have helped boost the low-viscosity
fuel oil market in recent weeks, trade sources said. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil inventories slipped 1.4 percent to a four-week low
of 7.049 million barrels (about 1.052 million tonnes) in the week to April 2, data via S&P Global
Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - The 100,000 barrel (15,000 tonne) drop in Fujairah fuel oil stocks marks the second straight
week of inventory declines in the Middle East storage hub.
    - Compared with year-ago levels, Fujairah fuel oil inventories are 38 percent lower.
    - On average, fuel oil stocks there have totalled 9.662 million barrels (or 1.442 million
tonnes) per week since records began in January 2017.
    
    ARBITRAGE FLOWS
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for April is expected to close under last month's 13-month
high of 6.9-7.0 million tonnes, with 5.8-5.9 million tonnes notionally assessed so far, on lower
arrivals from all three supply regions - the West, the Middle East and Asia - assessments by Thomson
Reuters Oil Research showed on Tuesday. [nPGEdbw8va]
    - Inflows from the West closed at 3.6-3.7 million tonnes for April, while May arrivals are also
expected to be lower-to-steady to April arrivals amid a weak price environment burdened by March's
heavy supplies, the assessments showed. 
    - CSSSA, Total's shipping arm, is making enquiries into chartering a very large crude carrier
(VLCC) vessel to load fuel oil from Rotterdam on April 20-25 for discharge into Singapore, ship
broker reports showed on Wednesday.

million, tanker broker sources said.

highest in nearly a month, helped by higher deal values and tighter supplies on the back of
seasonal refinery turnarounds in the region.

Zone (FOIZ) for the week ended April 2, according to data published on Wednesday via industry
information service S&P Global Platts.

Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]

average of 3.031 million barrels since records began in January 2017, Reuters calculations
showed.

lower.

cooperation between OPEC and non-OPEC countries may be set up once the current deal on oil

SINGAPORE, June 13 (Reuters) - Asia's prompt-month time spread slipped on Wednesday, narrowing
its backwardated structure to a more than three-week low of $2.75 a tonne, but market sentiment was
still supportive on expectations of tight supplies of finished grade fuel oil into July, trade
sources said. <FO380SGSDMc1>
    Meanwhile, a highly competitive market environment kept ex-wharf premiums for 380-cst fuel oil
steady at about $2-$3 per tonne to Singapore quotes this week despite improved demand, trade sources
said. 
    Around the end of May, ex-wharf premiums were trading at a narrower premium of $0-$2 a tonne.
    
    ARBS 
    - Vitol provisionally booked the Saham VLCC tanker for a $3.15 million fee to load up to 270,000
tonnes of fuel oil from Rotterdam on June 27 for discharge into Singapore on Aug. 11, shipping data
in Thomson Reuters Eikon showed. 
    - Weak arbitrage economics over the past two months have resulted in few fuel oil shipments
along the Rotterdam to Singapore voyage, trade sources said. 
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for June are expected to close significantly below May's
six-month high of about 6.6-6.7 million tonnes, with only 5.4-5.5 million tonnes notionally assessed
so far, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed on Tuesday. [nPGELFTwla]
    - The tighter flow volumes were largely due to lower Western arbitrage supplies which were
assessed at an eight-month low of less than 3 million tonnes, the assessments showed.    
    
    BUNKER SALES
    - Singapore marine fuel sales climbed to a four-month high of 4.283 million tonnes in May, up
1.2 percent from the previous month and 2.5 percent higher than a year ago, official data showed on
Wednesday. [nL4N1TF2X7]
    - The strong volumes sold in May were largely in line with industry expectations and come
despite sharply higher bunker fuel prices due to rising crude oil prices and shortages of finished
grade bunker fuel oil during the month. [nL3N1S22HA]
    - Sales of the 380-centistoke (cst) high-sulphur fuel oil fell to a three-month low of 2.948
million tonnes in May, 6 percent lower from a year earlier, and 3 percent lower from April.
    - However, sales of the less-expensive high-viscosity 500-cst marine fuel passed the
1-million-tonne mark for the first time ever, climbing to a record high of 1.01 million tonnes.
     
    WINDOW TRADES

380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO).
    - PetroChina bought two cargoes, one 40,000 tonne cargo from Trafigura and a 20,000 tonne cargo
from Socar. 
    - Gunvor bought the remaining two 20,000 tonne cargoes, also taking one from Socar and one from
Trafigura.

LONDON, Sept 17 (Reuters) - Angola will export less crude
oil in November than in October, based on a preliminary loading
schedule on Monday that showed shipments will likely fall to
their lowest since August.

number of cargoes to 44 in November and equates to a daily rate
of 1.41 million barrels per day, from October's final 49 cargoes
and 1.52 million bpd.

bpd rate, which in turn was a 12-year low. 
    The schedule included four cargoes of new grade Gindungo,
which comes from Total's <TOTF.PA> Kaombo oil field.     
    Meanwhile, BP was again actively bidding for Nigerian
cargoes loading in late October and early November, although, in
the absence of any November loading programmes, made no
purchases, traders said.
    BP bid for one cargo of Forcados loading between Oct 13-17,
as well as for two additional cargoes, one Forcados and one
Bonga, loading Nov 6-11. BP was believed to have started bidding
around $1.50 a barrel above the dated Brent price, but escalated
this as high as $1.65.
    Several traders said no other cargoes were on offer,
although with only days to go until the release of the November
loading programmes, it was not unusual for bids and offers to
dry up.

    Sept 17 (Reuters) - U.S.-based Cheniere Energy Inc <LNG.A>
said on Monday that it has signed a 15-year agreement to supply
liquefied natural gas (LNG) to the world's largest oil trader
Vitol Group that has been steadily ramping up its presence in
that market.
    The move by Vitol is part of a long-term objective shared by
many major commodity traders to increase their traded gas
volumes as emerging markets seek cleaner fuels for power
generation.      
    China in particular has soaked up what many analysts
expected to be a significant LNG glut this year as it replaces
some of its coal furnaces with gas-fuelled ones.
    Part of the drive for traders is that the LNG market is
becoming increasingly liquid with more spot deals, presenting
arbitrage opportunities and supply imbalances that traders
thrive off.
    Cheniere said it will sell 700,000 tonnes of LNG per year to
Vitol, starting in 2018 with a purchase price pegged to the
Henry Hub monthly average, plus a fee. [nBw2ypmb4a] 
    On Monday, Vitol's Chief Executive Russell Hardy told a
conference in Barcelona that he expected global LNG traded
volumes, currently at 300 million tonnes, to double in the
coming years, as new importing countries build
facilities.[nL5N1W3019]
    Last year, Vitol's LNG traded volumes tripled to 7.4 million
tonnes up from 2.6 million tonnes in 2016. [nL8N1R8331]
    The United States has become a major LNG exporter in the
last two years, mostly due to the ramp-up of Cheniere's Sabine
Pass terminal in Louisiana. Houston-based Cheniere is also
building the Corpus Christi terminal in Texas.
    Earlier this year, Cheniere signed a similar agreement with
rival Trafigura, a major Swiss-based commodities trader, for 1
million tonnes. [nL3N1PB4JG]
    Along with long-term supply deals, Vitol has been competing
to build LNG import infrastructure in Southeast Asia, pitting
itself against Gunvor and Trafigura in Pakistan and Bangladesh.
[nL8N1QW6ES]

northwest Europe slipped to their  lowest level since

SINGAPORE, Nov 7 (Reuters) - The front-month 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil barge crack
firmed on Wednesday, bringing its discount to Brent crude to the narrowest in more than 15
months amid weaker crude prices and a persistent shortage of fuel oil supplies, trade sources
said. 
    While fuel oil arbitrage volumes into Singapore were expected to improve in November in
comparison to October, most arrivals are due for arrival in the latter end of the month, the
sources said, keeping prompt prices elevated for now. 
    The December 380-cst fuel oil crack to Brent crude was trading at about minus $5.80 a barrel
on Wednesday, compared with a discount of $6.15 a barrel on Tuesday, broker sources said. 
    The front-month crack discount was last narrower in July 2017, according to Refinitiv data
in Eikon. <HFOFARAACMc2>
    
    WINDOW TRADES
    - Two cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, including one 20,000 tonne
cargo of 180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) and another 40,000 tonne cargo of 380-cst HSFO.
    - P66 sold the 180-cst HSFO cargo to Hin Leong at $485 a tonne. 
    - Mercuria sold the 380-cst HSFO cargo to BP at a $9 per tonne premium to Singapore quotes. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fuel oil inventories at the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fell 5 percent, or 362,000
barrels (about 54,000 tonnes), to a six-week low of 6.666 million barrels (0.995 million tonnes)
in the week ended Nov. 5, data from S&P Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - Fujairah fuel oil inventories are now 23 percent lower from the same time last year.
    - In 2018, Fujairah's fuel oil stocks averaged 8.144 million barrels (1.216 million tonnes)
compared with 9.974 million barrels (1.489 million tonnes) in the year before, Reuters
calculations showed.
        
    SHANDONG OVERHAUL
    - China's Shandong province, home to a fifth of China's oil refining capacity, is planning
to consolidate dozens of small refineries and build mega-petrochemical complexes, as part of a
new plan to overhaul energy intensive industries. [nL4N1XH32Q]
    - The province, home to 90 percent of China's private refiners, wants to reduce total crude
processing capacity from 130 million tonnes per year, or 2.6 million barrels of oil per day
(bpd), to 90 million tonnes. 
    - It will merge refiners with less than 3 million tonnes annual capacity by 2022, and later
target those with up to 5 million tonnes, or about 100,000 bpd, before 2025. 
    - It also wants to significantly reduce the output of diesel and gasoline by 2025. 
    - The move is seen as positive for China's independent refining industry, currently facing
fierce competition in local fuel markets and subject to frequent shutdowns due to environmental
scrutiny. 
    
    VENEZUELA CRUDE EXPORTS

activity in the Singapore window on Thursday to its highest levels in more than a week, but weighed
on fuel cash differentials. 
    Cash premiums of 380-cst fuel oil <FO380-SIN-DIF> slipped for a second straight session to its
lowest in more than one week on Thursday, while cash differentials of 180-cst fuel oil
<FO180-SIN-DIF> flipped to a narrow discount after trading at a premium for more than a week. 
    This came after official data showed Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories climb to a four-week
high in the week ended Jan. 31. 
          
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Five cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of
180-cst fuel oil and another 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories rose 1 percent to a four-week high of 22.516
million barrels (about 3.36 million tonnes) in the week ended Jan. 31 despite fewer net imports,
data from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed on Thursday. [O/SING1]
    - Net fuel oil imports into Singapore fell to 626,000 tonnes in the week to Jan. 31, down 41
percent from the week before,
    - Net imports were weighed down by higher fuel oil exports from the city-state which climbed to
681,000 tonnes, up 135 percent from a nine-week low seen in the week before. [nL4N1PK32W]
    - Onshore fuel oil inventories were 3 percent higher compared with year-ago levels.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Hong Kong topped the week at 218,000 tonnes, followed
by South Korea with 97,000 tonnes and China with 45,000 tonnes, the data showed.
    - Net exports of Singapore fuel oil to China were at a five-week low ahead of the Lunar New Year
celebrations in February.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Iraq at 190,000 tonnes, followed by
Malaysia at 171,000 tonnes, the United States at 154,000 tonnes and Brazil at 116,000 tonnes,
according to the data.
    - Fuel oil inventories in Singapore averaged 23.367 million barrels (3.49 million tonnes) a week
since the start of 2017.

    Liquidity in the Platts market on close continued to be robust on Thursday, traders said. 
    Glencore sold 200,000 barrels of 50ppm sulphur diesel for loading from Fujairah, Ruwais or
Sitra over Nov. 9 to 13 to Trafigura at a premium of 80 cents a barrel to the average of Nov. 9
to 15 Middle East quotes, they said. [nL4N1CQ3L2]
    Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks fell nearly 5 percent to a two-week low of
12.895 million barrels in the week to Oct. 19, latest data from International Enterprise showed.
    The inventory is likely to be drawn down further in the coming weeks as several refineries
undergo maintenance in Asia and the Middle East, curbing supply, traders said. 
    Japan's JX Nippon Oil shut a condensate splitter and reformer at its Kashima plant on
Thursday after a fire, the company said. [L4N1CQ3AT]
    This could reduce supply of oil products if the shutdown is prolonged, traders said. 
    Bangladesh Petroleum Corp (BPC) has issued an international tender to import oil products as
part of efforts to buy at cheaper rates by moving away from direct-term deals with suppliers of
fuel products. [nL4N1CQ2PW]
    BPC is seeking 965,000 tonnes of 500 ppm sulphur gasoil, 120,000 tonnes of 180-centistoke
high sulphur fuel oil and 90,000 tonnes of jet fuel, a tender document showed.
    A shortfall in supplies of natural gas has forced the south Asian country to burn oil, a
costlier option, to generate electricity.
    The state-owned firm is also in talks with 11 companies for refined oil product imports
through term deals for the first half of next years, another BPC official said.
    The buy tender is expected to further boost the Asian gasoil margins, which have gained
momentum due to recent curbs in supply from several refineries undergoing maintenance in Asia,
traders said. 
    Glencore Singapore Pte has advised Platts that it wishes to participate in Platts' market on
close pricing process for Middle East physical fuel oil, gasoil, gasoline and kerosene, the oil
pricing agency wrote in a note to its subscribers on Thursday.

Oct 13 (Reuters) - * Flows of Norwegian crude to the United
States and Canada look set to hit their highest in eight months
in October, thanks to the weakness in physical North Sea crude
prices.    
    * Reuters Trade Flows data shows shipments of Norwegian
crude loading at the ports of Sture and Mongstad are set to rise
so far to 3.1 million barrels, up from September's 2.85 million
barrels.
    * Overall, so far in 2016, shipments of North Sea crude to
Canada have trebled, to 9.9 million barrels compared with this
time last year, while flows to the United States have fallen to
around 9.89 million barrels from close to 15 million barrels in
October 2015.
    * Most of this increase is derived from flows of Oseberg
crude, for which exports to Canada have risen tenfold to nearly
5.1 million barrels in the year to date, compared with 2015.
    * Nearly 1.2 million of that total will have shipped in this
month alone, when Oseberg differentials <BFO-OSE> have fallen to
their lowest levels since last July, one trading source said.
    * The dated Brent benchmark, as opposed to ICE Brent futures
<LCOc1>, has fallen to its lowest in nearly three months,
helping Norwegian crude exports.

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, Oct 12 (Reuters) - The near-term time spreads of Asia's 380-cst fuel oil softened on Wednesday, weighed
down by weaker sentiment, industry sources said. 
    The balance of Oct/Nov time spreads for 380-cst fuel <FO380SGSDMc1> were 50 cents lower to minus 25 cents a tonne to
Singapore quotes. The Nov/Dec spreads were also 50 cents lower, slipping 50 cents from the previous session and were
trading at parity to each other on Wednesday. 
    Despite the softening of the fuel oil forward curve in Singapore, European swaps were even weaker with the prompt
month Rotterdam high-sulphur barge spreads trading $1 lower on Wednesday to 50 cents a tonne, prompting a rise in
East-West (EW) arbitrage spreads, traders said.
    The EW spread for the front month <FOSGEWMc1> - the price difference between FOB Singapore 180-cst high-sulphur fuel
oil and FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil with maximum 3.5 percent sulphur - rose by 75 cents from the previous session to
$25.75 a tonne. 
    This marks a fifth consecutive session of gains for EW spreads and a third consecutive session of setting fresh
multi-month highs that began this week.
    The last time EW spreads were higher was on April 6 when it traded at $28 a tonne. 
    The strengthening of the EW spreads is likely to prompt traders to lock in arbitrage cargoes from the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp oil hub into East Asia for arrival in late November, traders said. 
    Western fuel oil arrivals into East Asia for November have so far been provisionally pegged at 2.8 to 3.0 million
tonnes, with full-month projections likely to edge up slightly versus October volumes of 3.8 to 4.0 million tonnes,
according to the latest assessments by Thomson Reuters Supply Chain and Commodities Research released on Tuesday.

    SINGAPORE, Oct 18 (Reuters) - A total of 40,000 tonnes of
benchmark 180-cst fuel oil exchanged hands in the Platts window
on Tuesday, the highest volume in more than two months after
some suppliers lowered price levels, industry sources said.
    Vitol lifted two 20,000 cargoes from Mercuria at a premium
of about $1.50 a tonne to Singapore quotes in the Platts
Market-on-Close (MOC) window, sources said, whereas Hin Leong
paid Chevron a premium of $2.25 a tonne for 20,000 tonnes on
Friday.
    The last time 40,000 tonnes or more of 180-cst fuel traded
in the Platts window in a single day was Aug. 3, data compiled
by Reuters showed.
    The lower transaction price levels weighed on 180-cst fuel
premiums, knocking them 31 cents lower on Tuesday to $1.69 a
tonne above Singapore quotes. 
    Traders said the weaker 180-cst fuel oil cash premiums were
the result of softer spot demand and a slight increase in
replenishment cargoes.
    The weaker 180-cst complex was also reflected in prompt
month time spreads. The Nov/Dec spread traded 25 cents lower on
Tuesday from the previous session at a discount of 25 cents,
well below the $1.27 a tonne average premium for September.

    SINGAPORE, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Deal activity in the Singapore fuel oil market picked up
on Thursday as demand in the world's largest bunkering hub showed signs of weakness,
industry sources said. 
    Sales of marine fuels in Singapore fell 9.4 percent in September from a month ago,
sinking to an eight-month low as fewer ships came to the city-state for refuelling,
official data released on Thursday showed. [nL4N1CJ3GM]
    Five cash deals were reported in the Platts window on Thursday totalling 100,000 tonnes
of 380-cst fuel oil, the most in number and volume since Sept. 14, industry sources said.
    Cash differentials of the 380-cst fuel oil <FO380-SIN-DIF> flipped into a discount of
34 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes, down from a premium of 12 cents a tonne in the
previous session. Cash differentials were weighed down by suppliers' eagerness to offload
cargoes to help offset slowing bunker fuel demand, industry sources said. 
    Despite the slow down in bunker fuel demand, onshore inventories of Singapore fuel oil
still managed to find an outlet abroad, dropping 1.624 million barrels (or about 242,000
tonnes) in the week to Oct. 12, the latest official data showed. Onshore fuel oil
inventories now stand at a total of 23.69 million barrels (or 3.54 million tonnes).

refining margins eased on Wednesday but strong demand to export
the motor fuel on transatlantic journeys and to West Africa
limited losses.

planning to export gasoline from Europe to North America and
West Africa.
    * Traders were also seeking to move reformate from ARA to
China, as demand for the blendstock from Asian markets nudges
higher. 
    * Interest in moving naphtha from the Baltic and other
European locations to Brazil also emerged. 
    * Qatargas began operations at its Ras Laffan 2 condensate
splitter over the weekend after technical issues delayed a
planned September start-up of the unit. [nL4N1CI1DA]

LONDON, Oct 18 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe were little changed at above $10 a barrel on
Tuesday, and were supported by seasonal refinery turnarounds and
overseas demand.
        
    * Seasonal refinery turnarounds in Europe and other regions
are limiting gasoline supplies and boosting margins. 
    * Margins are also supported by demand to export the motor
fuel from Europe to the U.S., with several new spot bookings
emerging along the route in recent days. 
    * Colonial Pipeline said on Monday it would cut shipping
volumes while it works to restart the section of its main
gasoline conduit that was damaged after its biggest leak of the
fuel in nearly two decades in Alabama last month. [nL1N1CN0SZ]
    * Naphtha supply are expected to lengthen following an
incident on a petrochemical plant in Germany.  
    * At least two people died and roughly two dozen were
injured in an explosion at BASF's biggest German plant on
Monday. BASF shut down more than 20 facilities, including its
two steam crackers after the blast. [nF9N1C400Q] 
    * The plant consumes at least 150,000 tonnes a month of
naphtha when fully operational, traders said. 
    * India's fuel demand fell 0.7 percent y-o-y in September,
with gasoline down 3.4 percent. [nENNGA40SN]
    * Registered fuel sales in Poland have risen 14 percent
since the introduction of new legislation on Aug. 1 to curb
black market sales, an industry body and the authorities said.
[nL8N1CN46G]
    * PBF plans to shut down its 65,000 barrel-per-day fluid
catalytic cracking unit at its Delaware City refinery on March 3
for up to 45 days of planned work, according to a source
familiar with the plant's operations. [nL1N1CN1LI]

SINGAPORE, Oct 12 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil differential edged higher on
Wednesday with the market structure between October and November becoming
parity, on a buying spree in Singapore, trade sources said.
    There was a flurry of activity in the Singapore gasoil cash market with
600,000 barrels exchanging hands, traders said. The main buyers were Winson Oil
and BP, while the sellers were Trafigura and Lukoil, they added. 
    It was not immediately clear where they were planning to ship the cargoes
to.
    Glencore's shipping unit, ST Shipping, has chartered a newly built very
large crude carrier (VLCC) to ship gasoil from South Korea possibly to Africa in
a rare move, shipbrokers and traders said. [nL4N1CI26N]
    Shipping data in Thomson Reuters Eikon shows that the brand-new, 299,011
deadweight tonne (DWT) Gener8 Oceanus VLCC, now off the southeast coast of
Taiwan en route to Singapore, and with a carrying capacity of about 2.2 million
barrels, has been chartered to load gasoil.
    Several broker and trading sources said the ship, which was delivered to
ship owner Gener8 Maritime Inc by South Korean shipbuilder Hyundai Mipo Heavy
Industries on Sept. 12, was chartered by Glencore's shipping arm ST Shipping.
    One of the brokers said the ship would load more gasoil in Singapore before
heading to Africa, though this could not be confirmed with ST Shipping or
Glencore.
    Separately, Koch Supply and Trading is expected to lease the 320,000 DWT
VLCC Eco Seas on a time charter of about three months, although it was not
immediately clear if it will load gasoil or crude initially.
    The cargoes were likely fixed when freight rates for VLCCs were lower, but
rates have since soared due to seasonal demand and increased cargoes from West
Africa, shipbrokers said.
    JBC Energy expects diesel demand in China to decline by 160,000 barrels per
day, a marked slowdown from previous years. 
    This will likely translate into more diesel exports from the country,
traders said, though demand could return if the pick-up in mining sustains.

SINGAPORE, Oct 19 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil differentials edged higher on Wednesday on the
back of reduced supply as several refineries undergo maintenance, traders said.
    The regrade -- the price difference between jet fuel and gasoil -- turned negative, which
gives refiners an incentive to maximise gasoil production over jet fuel, they added.     
    Japan's operating rate increased by 3.7 percent on the week to 77.8 percent in the week to
Oct. 15, Reuters calculates using data from the Petroleum Association of Japan. <O/JAPAN1>
    But Japan's Showa Shell Sekiyu said on Wednesday that it plans to refine 3.7 percent less
crude oil for the domestic market from October to December compared with the same period last
year.
    Showa Shell expects to process 468,600 barrels per day (6.854 million kilolitres) of crude
over the three months, the company said.
    Sales of kerosene in Japan increased by 12.8 percent on the week while jet fuel sales edged
2 percent higher, the PAJ data showed. 
    Gasoil sales, however, fell by 5.5 percent.
    India's diesel demand declined to 1.3 million barrels per day (bpd) in September, down
170,000 bpd from a year ago and its steepest fall in the past decade, as severe flooding crimped
construction and agricultural activities, Energy Aspects said in a note.
    Exports of the fuel are likely to remain high until the rains subside, it added.
    Traders said that demand is expected to recover once the monsoon season ends, in turn
curbing diesel exports.

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, Oct 14 (Reuters) - The prompt month arbitrage window for Western fuel oil
cargoes into East Asia snapped six consecutive sessions of gains on Friday on strength in
Rotterdam barge spreads following a drop in fuel oil inventories in North West Europe (NWE),
industry sources said.     
    The October East-West (EW) spread <FOSGEWMc1> - the price difference between FOB
Singapore 180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil and FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil with maximum 3.5
percent sulphur - fell $1 on Friday to $25.25 a tonne.
    The October EW spread rallied over the past week, settling at a more than six-month high
of $26.50 a tonne on Thursday. The last time EW spreads were higher was on April 6 at $28 a
tonne.
    This came as fuel oil stocks in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) oil hub sank to
their lowest levels since November 2014, the latest PJK data showed. [ARA/]
    ARA fuel oil inventories <STK-FO-ARA> fell 39 percent, or 325,000 tonnes, from the
previous week to 513,000 tonnes in the week to Oct. 13. 
    This followed a 1.624 million barrel (or about 242,000 tonnes) decline in onshore
Singapore fuel oil inventories in the week to Oct. 12 to a total of 23.69 million barrels
(or 3.54 million tonnes), official data released on Thursday showed. [O/SING1]
    In the physical markets, three cash deals were reported in the Platts window after
Singapore-trader Hin Leong snapped up two 20,000-tonne cargoes of 380-cst fuel at a discount
of 50 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes and another 20,000-tonne cargo of 180-cst fuel oil
at a $2.25 a tonne premium to Singapore quotes, sources said. 
    All three traded cargoes are due for delivery at the front of today's trading window
between Oct. 29 and Nov. 2. 
    Hin Leong bought on Thursday a similar 380-cst fuel oil cargo at the front of the window
at a premium of about 10 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes, sources said.
    The lower deal price weighed down on cash discounts of the 380-cst fuel oil
<FO380-SIN-DIF> which slipped 26 cents from Thursday to 60 cents a tonne below Singapore
quotes. 
    
    TANKER RATES:
    Freight rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs), which rose to multi-month highs
this week, are likely to hold firm as owners tread water before the release of further
Middle-East and West Africa cargoes, ship brokers said on Friday. [nL4N1CH308]
    Charter rates for an 80,000-dwt Aframax tanker from Southeast Asia to East Coast
Australia <.BAIJ> rose to around W73.75 on Thursday, the highest since Aug. 9, from W65.75
last week.
    That was due to increased chartering activity as a result of more fuel oil heading from
Europe to Singapore and China, said Ashok Sharma, managing director of broking house BRS
Baxi Far East in Singapore.

    - VTTI, the storage arm of the world's largest independent oil trader Vitol [VITOLV.UL],
is scouting for investment opportunities in Southeast Asia to cater to the region's rising
demand for tank space, the head of its Asia business unit said. [nL4N1CK17H]

LONDON, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe edged higher on Friday amid thin trade,
supported by recent declines in regional and global stocks and
refinery maintenance.
    
    * Gasoline stocks in the United States, Singapore and ARA

* At least four tankers diverted to U.S., Caribbean
    * Brimming European storage limits imports
    * Lower U.S. refinery output boosts prices

    By Ron Bousso
    LONDON, Feb 16 (Reuters) - Tankers carrying diesel from the
Middle East and Asia are being diverted from Europe to the U.S.
East Coast, with refinery cuts across the Atlantic offering a
selling opportunity as European storage brims and demand sags.
    The United States has become in recent years one of the
world's largest exporters of diesel and jet fuel and imports of
the products are rare, even though imports of high-sulphur
gasoil to the U.S. East Coast occur during winter.
    But U.S. refinery output cuts in recent weeks, including
Exxon Mobil Corp's <XOM.N> Baytown plant in Texas, the nation's
second largest, has offered better prospects in the New York
Harbour areas than in Europe, the world's biggest diesel demand
hub, traders said.[nL2N15Q3IH][nL2N15R03B]
    In Europe, diesel and gasoil storage levels in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub are near record highs as
imports into the region from huge refineries in the Middle East
and Asia continue to flood the market. [ARA/]
    In recent days, several tankers en-route to Europe from the
East have been diverted across the Atlantic, according to
traders and Reuters ship tracking.
    The 90,000-tonne long-range Raysut tanker, chartered by
Litasco, the trading arm of Russian oil company Lukoil
<LKOH.MM>, loaded with diesel on Jan. 25 at the Ruwais refinery
in the United Arab Emirates and set sail to Europe, only to be
diverted towards New York in recent days.
    Similarly, the 38,000-tonne Front Dee and Arendal tankers
which loaded gas-to-liquids (GTL), a fuel used with diesel and
jet fuel, are now heading to New York after crossing the
Mediterranean.
    The 60,000-tonne Marilee tanker chartered by trading house
Castleton loaded jet fuel from the Reliance Industries Ltd
<RELI.NS> 580,000 barrels per day Jamnagar refinery in India,
and is currently heading to Freeport in the Bahamas, where the
company has storage.
    The European diesel market has been under huge pressure in
recent months due to swelling storage levels and high imports
that have led traders to store product on tankers, order ships
to take longer routes to Europe and even make U-turns in mid
Atlantic ocean.[nL8N1443F4]
    And while European coastal storage levels are nearly full,
experts and traders emphasized there was still ample space on
the U.S. East Coast.[nL8N1520NK]
    Independent U.S. refiners including Valero Energy Corp
<VLO.N>, PBF Energy INC <PBF.N>, Philadelphia Energy Solutions
and Monroe Energy, a unit of Delta Air Lines Inc <DAL.N>, are
curbing output, capitulating to record stockpiles and sluggish
winter demand that have hurt profits.

in northwest Europe climbed towards $10 a barrel as oil prices
rallied and supplies in the region were expected to tighten.
    Planned maintenance around the world next month is expected
to limit flows into the region, offering some support to the
market in March and April, traders said.
    Price pressure remains, however, because of large imports
while storage nears maximum levels in many parts of Europe.    
    In the cargo market, more than 2 million tonnes of diesel is
expected to reach the region from Asia and the Middle East this

diesel were awaiting orders to discharge off the coast of

where Tupras issued a tender to buy 30,000 to 60,000 tonnes of
diesel for Feb. 20-29 delivery into the port of Izmit, a tender
document showed.

northwest Europe declined on Monday amid thin trading and ample
supplies in the region.
    Inland demand was weak, with little buying interest despite
a cold snap that has hit the region. With storage levels near
maximum, end users have little spare room and are buying only to
refill stocks, according to traders.

earlier, traders told Reuters on Monday. The February stock
levels are nevertheless higher than the five-year average of 54
percent. [PROD/DE]

levels, shipments in March were expected to drop as refineries
around the world enter their seasonal maintenance period,
cutting production. The arbitrages from the U.S. Gulf Coast and
Asia were largely closed, according to traders.
    In the cargo market, more than 2 million tonnes of diesel is
expected to reach the region from Asia and the Middle East this
month, traders said.
    Large tankers continued to make their way to the region,
with some taking the longer route around South Africa in order
to delay their arrival in the region. More than 400,000 tonnes
of diesel are awaiting orders for discharging around Europe,
according to shipping data.

LONDON, Feb 15 (Reuters) - North Sea Forties crude
differentials steadied on Monday, after an uptick in supply of
oil through a major pipeline helped improve some tightness that
has developed.
    The flow of oil through the Forties Pipeline System has been
restored to normal levels, after an outage late last week and
through the weekend restricted the amount of crude carried, a
spokeswoman for system operator BP said on Monday. [nL8N15U3P2]
    Lower-than-expected production prompted the deferral of two
cargoes from the February loading programme into March, trade
sources said on Thursday, and more cargoes are being delayed.
    A March-loading cargo, numbered F0301 and originally owned
by BP, has been delayed until later in March, trade sources said
last week.
    Reflecting the tightness in supply of oil for prompt
delivery, the dated Brent curve <BFO-><BFO-2M> is now showing
its smallest contango since late January, as the premium for
further-dated deliveries has almost halved to around $1.74 a
barrel.
    Three weeks ago, the curve was showing its largest contango
in three months. 
    In terms of flows of North Sea crude out of Europe, the VLCC
Ellinis is now underway, heading towards South Korea after
loading at Hound Point last week.
    The supertanker Nave Electron, which had originally been
booked by Vitol, is currently just outside Hound Point, while
the Hakata is moored just off the French port of Antifer in the
English Channel, according to Reuters shipping data. 
    So far this month, if all these fixtures result in a voyage,
some 6 million barrels of Forties will move to Asia, in line
with the flows seen in January.

the country's ability to import cargoes.

SINGAPORE, Oct 5 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil margin jumped
to a three-month high on Wednesday on a spike in underlying
crude oil prices and refinery maintenance in the region curbing
supply, traders said. 
    There are several refineries undergoing maintenance in
Japan, Middle East and Taiwan, which is boosting the margin,
they said.     
    A fire at Pertamina's Cilacap refinery in Indonesia shortly
after midday on Wednesday has been extinguished, officials at
the state owned energy company said. [nJ9N1A7014]
    The fire started during maintenance to an asphalt tank that
was being emptied and may have overheated, Pertamina Refineries
Director Rachmad Hardadi told Reuters.
    The fire did not spread and did not affect the refinery's
normal operation, Hardadi said.
    Still, supplies of jet fuel and diesel were ample. 
    India's Essar Oil sold up to 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel for
Nov. 5-9 loading from Vadinar to BP at a premium of about 30 to
40 cents a barrel above Middle East quotes, traders said.
    This is lower than the premium of 50 to 60 cents a barrel it
achieved for a mid-October loading cargo sold to ENOC earlier,
they added.
    Taiwan's Formosa Petrochemical Corp sold 720,000 barrels of
10ppm sulphur diesel for Nov. 8-12 loading from Mailiao to
Winson Oil at a premium of 25 cents a barrel to Singapore
quotes, traders said.
    Formosa also sold 240,000 barrels of jet fuel for Nov. 1-5
loading to Vitol at a discount of $1 a barrel to Singapore
quotes, they added. 
    The cargoes were likely sold in anticipation of the 500,000
barrels per day (bpd) Mailiao refinery returning from
maintenance in late October, one of them said.
    Taiwan's CPC Corp offered diesel for November, also adding
to the supply glut.
    Demand for global air freight rose for the fifth straight
month in August as European airlines benefited from an increase
in German export orders, the International Air Transport
Association (IATA) said on Wednesday.

SINGAPORE, Oct 4 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil margin slipped
from its one-week high on Tuesday as more Indian supply flooded
the market, but spot demand from Vietnam and Egypt capped the
fall. 
    Spot supply from India continued to enter the market, with
Essar Oil and Indian Oil Corp offering diesel for October and
November, traders said.
    More spot supply from Taiwan is also expected once the
refinery completes maintenance at the end of October, they
added.
    But some spot demand supported sentiment. Vietnam's Saigon
Petro is seeking 20,000 tonnes of gasoil for early November
while Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) is seeking up to
117,000 tonnes of gasoil for October, traders said.     
    Pakistan will lower the sulphur content of diesel imports
from January next year, in line with a global shift toward
cleaner fuels, said two sources familiar with the matter.
[nL3N1CA1Z0]
    Pakistan will require diesel fuel with 500 parts per million
(ppm) sulphur starting from January 2017 from the current 5,000
ppm sulphur gasoil, the sources said this week.
    About 40 percent of Pakistan's refineries have upgraded
their units to produce the low sulphur diesel while the
remaining refineries are still working to finish units to reduce
the amount of sulphur in the fuel, the source said.

    TENDERS
    - Saigon Petro is seeking 10,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for delivery into Cat Lai terminal over Nov. 4 to 6 or
loading from Singapore, Thailand or Malaysia over Nov. 1 to 3. 
     It is also seeking 10,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil
for delivery into Cat Lai over Nov. 24 to 27 or loading from
Singapore, Thailand or Malaysia over Nov. 21 to 24. The tender
closes on Oct. 7, with same-day validity.
    - Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) is seeking 35,000
to 37,000 tonnes of 0.1 percent sulphur gasoil for delivery into
Suez over Oct. 22 to 24. 
    It is also seeking two cargoes of 40,000 tonnes each of 0.5
percent sulphur gasoil for delivery into Ain Sukhna over Oct. 15
to 17 and Oct. 24 to 26. The tender closes on Oct. 10 and is
valid until Oct. 12.
    - Indian Oil Corp has offered 40,000 to 45,000 tonnes of
50ppm sulphur gasoil for loading from Paradip over Oct. 21 to 23
and 13,500 to 16,500 tonnes of 350ppm sulphur gasoil for loading
from Haldia over Oct. 20 to 22. The tender closes on Oct. 4 and
is valid until Oct. 5.
    - Essar Oil has offered up to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm
sulphur gasoil for Nov. 3 to 9 loading from Vadinar. The tender
closes on Oct. 5, with same-day validity.

SINGAPORE, Oct 3 (Reuters) - The spot jet fuel differential in Singapore increased on Monday
on the back of refinery maintenance expected to curb supply, traders said. 
    Japanese oil refiner TonenGeneral Sekiyu KK is likely to shut the 132,000 barrels-per-day
sole crude distillation unit (CDU) at its Wakayama refinery in western Japan soon, an industry
source said on Monday. [nL3N1C90BZ]
    The maintenance was originally set to run from late September to late October, but has been
delayed slightly, the source with direct knowledge of the matter said.
    The CDU is likely to be shut for about a month, the source added.
    Royal Dutch Shell bought larger-than-normal gasoline cargoes from the Singapore cash window
last week, with traders saying the purchases could be linked to a crude distillate unit at its
Bukom refinery in Singapore being shut for maintenance, though this could not be confirmed with
Shell. [nL3N1C63PN]
    However, the fuel supply was ample and kept a lid on margins, traders said. 
    India's Essar Oil offered jet fuel for early November loading, which is expected to weigh on
differentials for the aviation fuel, traders said.
    India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) sold 40,000 tonnes of jet fuel for
Nov. 13 to Nov. 15 loading to BP at a discount of $1.20 to $1.30 a barrel to Singapore quotes,
traders said, though this could not immediately be confirmed. 
    U.S. shale gas will displace a growing portion of the world's expanding energy demand,
cutting into the need for oil products from refineries, BP's head of refining economics said on
Friday. [nL8N1C62AS]

    TENDERS
    - Essar Oil has offered 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel for Nov. 5 to Nov. 9 loading from Vadinar.
The tender closes on Oct. 4, with same-day validity.

    SINGAPORE CASH DEALS: Three gasoil deals, one jet fuel trade.
    - Trafigura sold 150,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for Oct. 18 to Oct. 22 loading to
Shell at a discount of 30 cents a barrel to the average of Oct. 17 to Oct. 21 Singapore quotes.
    - Shell bought 150,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for Oct. 18 to Oct. 22 loading from
Trafigura at a discount of 25 cents a barrel to the average of Oct. 18 to Oct. 22 Singapore
quotes.
    - Winson Oil bought 150,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for Oct. 18 to Oct. 22 loading
from Ocean Energy at a discount of 30 cents a barrel to the average of Oct. 17 to Oct. 21
Singapore quotes. 
    - BP sold 200,000 barrels of jet fuel for Oct. 19 to Oct. 23 loading to PetroChina at a
discount of 70 cents a barrel to the average of Oct. 18 to Oct. 24 Singapore quotes.

LONDON, Oct 5 (Reuters) - U.S. crude stockpiles fell last
week for the fifth time in a row, although overall oil
inventories remained at their highest in this century, the U.S.
Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday. The drop
boosted oil futures to their highest since June. [nL2N1CB0VO]
[O/R]
    * Increased exports from Nigeria and Libya were weighing on
physical prices, and an excess was building in the Atlantic
basin. Tullow sold a cargo of Jubilee crude, whole Sinochem sold
a cargo of Zafiro. 
    * Chinese loadings of West African crude oil are set to
accelerate over the course of October, hitting their highest
since April, according to a Reuters survey of shipping fixtures
and traders on Wednesday. [nL5N1CB4ZL]

     Sellers of Angolan crude were reducing offers for some
grades in a bid to shift lingering cargoes.
    
    NIGERIA 
    * Trading picked up on Wednesday, but sources said
differentials had fallen further to facilitate the deals.
    * ENI had sold a cargo of Qua Iboe to Litasco, but other
traders said the deal concluded at a premium below $1 per
barrel. The trade could not be confirmed at source.  
    * Neither the Los Angeles Spirit, which was waiting to load
Qua Iboe, nor the Everbright, which was waiting to load
Forcados, had loaded by Wednesday evening. 
    
    ANGOLA 
    * After a brisk trading the previous week, Angolan sales
slowed notably due in part to a national holiday in China that
limited buying interest. 
    * State oil company Sonangol had lowered offer levels on its
remaining cargoes, showing Nemba at dated Brent minus 50 cents,
a 30 cent decrease, and Girassol at dated minus 10 cents,  10
cents lower.
    * Traders said successful sales would only come at lower
prices, particularly for Nemba, which was competing with renewed
Nigerian exports. 
    * Unipec offered its own cargo at a $1 per barrel discount
to dated Brent and did not find a buyer, suggesting even that
price was not attractive. 
     
    TENDERS
    * Indonesia's Pertamina issued a tender to buy
December-arrival crude oil, traders said. 
    * A tender from Uruguay's ANCAP to buy 1 million barrels of 
medium to light, sweet crude for delivery Dec. 10-14 closed on
Wednesday. The company bought a Nemba cargo last month.
[nL2N1C91U6]     
    * Indian Oil Corp. is running a tender to buy
December-loading cargoes, which closes later this week.

SINGAPORE, Oct 10 (Reuters) - Spot gasoil demand from Iraq, Vietnam and Indonesia supported
the Asian gasoil margin, industry sources said on Monday.
    Indonesia's Wilmar Trading was seeking a spot cargo for November while Vietnam's top fuel
importer Petrolimex also sought three cargoes for November, the sources said.
    Iraq's State Oil Marketing Company sought nearly 2 million tonnes of gasoil for 2017, about
8 percent higher than it sought for 2016, traders said.     
    Pakistan State Oil bought 10,000 tonnes of jet fuel for delivery in November from BB Energy
at a premium of about $4.85 a barrel above Middle East quotes, traders said.
    Ceylon Petroleum Corp (Ceypetco) was another buyer, industry sources said, purchasing a
total of 618,000 barrels of gasoil and gasoline for delivery in November from PetroChina
Singapore.
    Ceypetco will pay a premium of $2.58 a barrel to Singapore quotes for 52,000 barrels of
10ppm sulphur diesel and a premium of $2.20 a barrel for 255,000 barrels of 92-octane gasoline
for delivery over Nov. 1-2, the sources said.
    It will also pay a premium of $1.62 a barrel to Singapore quotes for 217,500 barrels of
500ppm sulphur gasoil and a premium of $3.80 a barrel for 93,500 barrels of 95-octane gasoline
for delivery over Nov. 8-9, they added.
    Taiwan's CPC Corp is likely to have sold a 10ppm sulphur diesel cargo for loading in
November at a premium of about 50 cents a barrel, traders said, though this could not
immediately be confirmed. 
    Jet fuel prices will remain elevated over the next five years as the crude oil market
rebalances and global aviation demand remains strong, BMI Research said in a note on Monday.
[nL4N1CG0HY]
    However, analysts sais they expect the supply of jet fuel in Asia to remain high, with
Chinese exports continuing to flood the market.

    - Iraq's State Oil Marketing Company is seeking 1.989 million tonnes of 500 ppm sulphur
gasoil for delivery into Khor Al-Zubair terminal between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2017. The tender
closes on Oct. 19, with offers to remain valid for 20 days. 
    - Indonesia's Wilmar Trading is seeking 40,000 tonnes of 0.3 percent sulphur gasoil for

is valid until Oct. 12.

SINGAPORE, Oct 7 (Reuters) - The Asian jet fuel differential edged up on Friday as refinery
maintenance curbed supply, industry sources said.
    Potential demand from the United States could also support.
    While there have been no additional cargoes fixed to ship jet fuel from Asia to the U.S. as
hurricane Matthew strikes the east coast, Valero and China Aviation Oil have chartered vessels
to ship jet fuel from Asia to the United States West Coast, a shipbroker said.     
    Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp will hold a partial maintenance at its sole 50,000
barrels-per-day oil refinery in November, two company sources said. [nL3N1CD1JC]
    It will be changing a catalyst at the refinery, which will reduce production of gasoil and
gasoline, one of them said.
    The maintenance will start from Nov. 3, and continue for about 20 days, the second source
said.
    Sri Lanka will build a second refinery with a capacity of at least 100,000 barrels per day

SINGAPORE, Sept 6 (Reuters) - Cash differentials on 380-cst fuel oil jumped as the
number and volume of deals for cargoes of the fuel in the Platts trading window hit the
highest since April. 
    The 380-cst premium <FO380-SIN-DIF> jumped $1.17 a tonne from the previous session to
a two-month high of $1.38 a tonne to Singapore quotes on Wednesday, and sharply higher
from the 27 cent a tonne discount at the start of the week. 
    Gains in the 180-cst fuel oil cash differential <FO180-SIN-DIF> were less pronounced
but still managed to flip from a discount of minus 17 cents a tonne in the previous
session to a premium of 13 cents a tonne on Wednesday. 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Fifteen cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 246,000 tonnes of
380-cst fuel oil and another 60,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil.
    - The number and volume of physical trades on Wednesday were the highest since April
17 when 320,000 tonnes of fuel exchanged hands through 16 trades. 
    - Hin Leong was the lead buyer of fuel oil cargoes, lifting a total of 120,000 tonnes,
followed by Trafigura (103,000 tonnes), Mercuria (60,000 tonnes) and Coastal (23,000
tonnes).
    - As in the previous two sessions, Mercuria was the top supplier of cargoes in the
window, selling a total of 146,000 tonnes, followed by PetroChina (100,000 tonnes), Gunvor
(40,000 tonnes) and Trafigura (20,000 tonnes). 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    ARBS EXTEND GAINS 
    - The October east-west (EW) arbitrage spread on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)
extended gains on Wednesday, lifted by ample fuel oil inventories in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub. 
    - The ICE-traded October EW spread rose 50 cents a tonne form the previous session to
$16.75 a tonne by 6 p.m. Singapore time (1000 GMT). 
    - While the wider arbitrage spread makes fuel oil shipments from northwest Europe into
Singapore more economically viable, tanker brokers said new VLCC vessel charters to ship
fuel oil along that route remain limited. 
    - In the week to Aug. 31, ARA fuel oil inventories jumped to 1.37 million tonnes,
their highest level since at least 2013 for this time of year. [ARA/]
    
    TENDERS
    - India's IOC is seeking up to 15,000 tonnes of 130-cst to 180-cst high-sulphur fuel
oil with 0.97 density for import into New Mangalore on Oct. 7-10 in a tender closing on
Sept. 11. [nL4N1LN2BL]
    
    FUJAIRAH INVENTORIES
    - In the United Arab Emirates, the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil
inventories were 0.5 percent lower in the week to Sept. 4 at a total of 10.734 million
barrels (about 1.6 million tonnes), data via S&P Global Platts showed. [nL4N1LN2T5]
    - Fuel oil inventories in the Fujairah oil hub are now at a two-week low after
slipping just 53,000 barrels (about 8,000 tonnes) from a week earlier. 
    - Weekly fuel oil inventories in Fujairah averaged 10.6 million barrels (or 1.58
million tonnes) since records began in January.

SINGAPORE, Oct 31 (Reuters) - Aggressive offers continued to weigh on the break-bulk ex-wharf
premiums of Asia's 380-cst fuel, with some suppliers seeking to stimulate demand, industry sources
said. 
    Demand for spot 380-cst ex-wharf fuel oil has been sluggish in recent weeks amid rising outright
prices of 380-cst bunker fuel which has climbed to its highest level since June 2015, keeping some
buyers at bay, sources said. <FO380-SIN>
        
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Two cargo trades were reported in the Platts window totalling 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil.
    - A total of 1.56 million tonnes of fuel oil have traded in the window in October, against 2.262
million tonnes in September.
    - Hin Leong has been the primary buyer of fuel oil cargoes throughout October, with 640,000 tonnes
purchased in the window throughout the month. BP was the second largest buyer with 420,000 tonnes, all
of which it bought in the first two weeks of the month. 
    - Vitol was the third largest buyer this month, lifting a total of 300,000 tonnes of the fuel in
the window, 260,000 tonnes of which was 180-cst fuel oil. 
    - Mercuria was the top supplier of fuel oil cargoes having sold 580,000 tonnes in the window this
month, followed by Gunvor which sold 220,000 tonnes of fuel, all of which were 180-cst fuel oil
cargoes. 
    - In addition to being the top buyer this month, Hin Leong also sold 180,000 tonnes of fuel oil,
making it the third largest supplier in the window this month.

    - Indonesia's Pertamina is offering one or two 200,000-barrel cargoes per month of decant oil with

of 2018, industry sources said. [nL4N1N63EG]
    - Pertamina's offer closes on Oct. 31 and remains valid until Nov. 7.

millions (ppm), typically used by tractors and ships, from Nov. 1, in its latest effort to clean up

used by automobiles. [nL3N1JR3E9]

differential rose on Tuesday as a continued buying spree from
Winson Oil and Unipec absorbed excess cargoes in the Singapore
oil market, traders said.

bought 1.05 million barrels of gasoil after buying 1.5 million
barrels of the fuel on Monday, traders said.
       Unipec, the trading arm of Sinopec, snapped up 900,000
barrels of gasoil, bringing their total purchases this week to
1.05 million barrels. 
       The end of a fishing ban in mid-September in the South
China sea and a recovery in demand in Asian cities as monsoon
rains subside are expected to boost prices for the fuel, traders
said.
       Both companies could be stocking up to prepare for that,
the traders said, though this could not be confirmed directly
with the companies.

deal on a free-on-board (FOB) Karimun basis on Tuesday.

(ppm) sulphur gasoil to Winson Oil for loading from Karimun in
Indonesia over Sept. 20 to 24. 
    
    - INDONESIA'S GASOIL EXPORTS: Potential exports of gasoil
from Indonesia's state-owned refiner Pertamina are likely to be
of a high sulphur grade, two sources familiar with the matter
said. [nL4N1LM30K] 
      Pertamina will likely propose to ship gasoil with a
sulphur content between 1,400 ppm and 2,500 ppm, the grades
produced by its refineries, one of the sources said.
      The cargoes will be shipped in lots of 200,000 barrels,
though overall volumes will depend on market fundamentals and on
how much is available, the source said, declining to be named as
he was not authorised to speak with media.
      Pertamina received a licence from the government about two
to three weeks ago to export gasoil for the first time, sources
said on Monday. [nL4N1LM14J]

United States or Latin America after Hurricane Harvey have been
failed, shipbrokers said.

hub were resuming, although many still had restrictions on
vessel draft, according to U.S. Coast Guard updates. Key fuel
pipelines planned to restart as more of the oil refineries that
feed them ramped up production. [nL8N1LL3CB]

their so-called upgrading capacity, which uses fuel oil, the
residue oil left over after crude oil is initially processed, to
manufacture fuels including gasoline and diesel.

fuel to a two-month high.

prompt-month time spreads <FO380SGSDMc1> also rose to about $2 a

inventories in Singapore rising to a more than five-month high

the week to Sept. 6, the highest since the week to March 22,
official data shows. [O/SING1]

into Singapore to a four-week low of 720,000 tonnes.

same time last year.

totalling 295,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.

By Florence Tan
    SINGAPORE, Oct 31 (Reuters) - China's state oil major
Sinopec is evaluating two projects in the United States that
could boost Gulf Coast crude oil exports and also expand storage
facilities in the Caribbean, two people familiar with the matter
said on Tuesday, with U.S. President Donald Trump set to visit
Beijing next week.
    With U.S.-China energy trade likely to feature prominently
during Trump's visit, the people said one of the projects could
see Sinopec <600028.SS> <0386.HK> partnering with U.S.
commodities trader Freepoint Commodities LLC and U.S. private
equity firm ArcLight Capital Partners LLC.
    The trio is mulling building a pipeline to move shale oil
from the Permian basin in Texas to the U.S. Gulf Coast for
export, the people said. 
    This project also includes the construction of a terminal
that can load 2 million barrels of crude onboard a Very Large
Crude Carrier (VLCC), they said. This will reduce a big chunk of
logistics costs incurred for U.S. crude exports, making the oil
more competitive in Asia, the sources said.
    They declined to be identified because they were not
authorised to speak to media.
    The three companies have also been exploring an expansion of
oil storage at Limetree Bay (LB) Terminals in St. Croix, U.S.
Virgin Islands in the Caribbean, and restarting an idled
refinery at the same site, they said.    
    Sinopec, which is Asia's largest oil refiner, ArcLight and
all Freepoint declined to comment.

standards for its imported gasoline, diesel and kerosene from

to protect citizens from toxic fuel.

ppm sulphur, while gasoline and kerosene can contain a maximum

By Roslan Khasawneh
    DUBAI, April 12 (Reuters) - The near-dated market structure of 380-cst fuel oil slipped
into contango on Wednesday, erasing steady gains made in the previous week, as ample prompt
supplies of the fuel weighed on sentiment despite slowing fuel oil flows into Asia. 
    
    ARB SUPPLY
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for April to fall below the Q1 average of 7.1-7.2
million tonnes, with 6.3-6.4 million tonnes notionally assessed so far, assessments by
Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed on Tuesday. 
    - Arrivals for May are expected to be similarly thin, with less than 3 million tonnes
of Western arrivals seen so far, but the downside is mitigated by heavy inflows from the
Middle East, with over 1.8 million tonnes already notionally assessed. 
    
    FUJAIRAH INVENTORIES
    - In the United Arab Emirates, the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil
inventories were up 2 percent, or 182,000 barrels, from the previous week to a total of
11.63 million barrels (about 1.74 million tonnes) in the week to April 10, data via S&P
Global Platts showed. [nL3N1HK3EP]
    - Current inventories of the fuel in the Arabian Gulf oil hub are just under 700,000
barrels down from the three-month high recorded in the week to March 27, despite a 7
percent drop in Fujairah's fuel oil stocks in the previous week. [nL5N1H63E5]
    
    SWAPS MARKET
    - Concerns about ample prompt supplies dragged near-dated time spreads into contango on
Wednesday, reflecting weakening sentiment. 
    - 380-cst balance-of-April/May time spread was pegged at about minus 20 cents a tonne
while the May/June contract slipped to around minus 40 cents a tonne by 1800 Singapore time
(1000 GMT).
    - By comparison, the 380-cst balance-of-April/May time spread was trading at a premium
of about 80 cents per tonne on Friday after official data showed a draw in fuel oil
inventories in Northwest Europe and Singapore during that week. 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Thirteen cargo trades were reported in the Platts window on Tuesday totalling 260,000
tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.     
    - Pricing of the traded cargoes was mixed across the different laycans, ranging from a
low of 10 cents per tonne discount to Singapore quotes in the middle of the trading window
to a high of $1.60 a tonne premium to Singapore quotes at the front of the window.  
    - A total of 1.94 million tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil have traded in the window since
the start of April.    
    - Please click on <O/AS> for more details. 

    OTHER NEWS
    - OPEC states cut oil output in March by more than they pledged under supply curbs,
according to figures the exporter group uses to monitor its supply, extending a record of
higher-than-expected adherence to its first production cut in eight years. [nL8N1HJ4N2]

LONDON, April 11 (Reuters) - European gasoline barge crack
swap hit its highest level since the start of June last year as
inventories in the United States fall, bringing rising imports
from Europe ahead of the summer driving season.
    
    * The barge swap hit a high of $13.14 a barrel on Tuesday.  
    * A trader said the decrease in U.S. stocks was also due to
demand from Latin America and West Africa. 
    * Demand for naphtha in Asian petrochemical crackers has
started to wane in favour alternative propane and butane prices
that have become seasonally cheaper. [nL3N1HI345]
    * Part of the unwanted naphtha is expected to be mopped up
by greater gasoline blending as demand rises and by a few
crackers returning from maintenance. 
    * U.S. data showed gasoline stocks fell 618,000 barrels,
compared with analysts' expectations for a 1.4 million-barrel
drop. <EIA/S>
    * OPEC appears to be slowly winning the battle against a
global overhang of crude and oil products as inventories in
onshore and floating storage decline. [nL8N1HF516]
    * Crude oil intake at Europe's refineries in March fell 0.6
percent compared with February to 10.3 million barrels per day
as refinery turnarounds gathered pace, data from industry
monitor Euroilstock showed on Tuesday. 

    GASOLINE 
    * No barges of benchmark Eurobob gasoline during the
afternoon session but a bid surfaced at $567 a tonne fob ARA,
the same level as a deal done on Monday.
    * Elsewhere during the day, 12,000 tonnes traded at
$565-$572 a tonne fob Amsterdam-Rotterdam, in line with the
previous day. Gunvor sold all the barges to Shell, BP, Freepoint
and Interchem. 
   * One barge of premium unleaded gasoline traded at $579 a
tonne fob ARA at the upper end of discussions in the previous
session.
   * The May swap traded at $575 a tonne at the close, up from
$572 a tonne on Monday.
    * Brent crude futures <LCOc1> were down by 32 cents at
$55.66 a barrel by 1607 GMT.
    * Gasoline barge refining margins stood at $13.78 a barrel,
up slightly from $13.35 a barrel on Friday.
    * U.S. front-month RBOB gasoline futures <RBc1> were 0.82
percent higher at $1.7437 a gallon.
    * The RBOB crack versus U.S. crude <RBc1-CLc1> stood at
$20.32 a barrel, down slightly from $20.76 a barrel at the
close.
    
    NAPHTHA <NAF-C-NWE>

being lifted.

time, the prompt time spread was unchanged from Monday's settlement of 50 cent a tonne
premium but its bid-offer spread widened to minus 50 cents a tonne and plus 50 cents a
tonne, respectively.

becoming commonplace as Uniper ramps up its Fujairah facility with an ULSFO production
capacity of approximately 300,000 tonnes per month, commissioned since the start of the
year.

taxes, China's independent oil refiners are branching out into new sectors from clean

LONDON, April 7 (Reuters) - Diesel refining margins in
northwest Europe rose on Friday supported by strong demand and
concerns that imports from the U.S. Gulf Coast could dwindle as
West Africa draws more.
    
    * The arbitrage from the U.S. Gulf Coast remained closed as
Latin America continued to draw most of the export volumes.
Exports to Europe were expected to reach around 1 million tonnes
in April, according to traders.
    * The transatlantic arbitrage could come under further
pressure in the coming months after Nigeria said it would raise
quality standards on its imported gasoline, diesel and kerosene
from July 1.[nL8N1HF2NU]
    * All imported diesel from July 1 can contain a maximum of
50 ppm sulphur, while gasoline and kerosene can contain a
maximum of 150 ppm, according to officials.
    * Imports from Asia and the Middle East were expected to
remain stable in April from the previous month at 1.5 million
tonnes, despite a heavy refinery maintenance programme.
    * Exports from Russia were also little changed in recent
weeks, with larger volumes from the Baltic Sea, particularly the
port of Ventspils, set to discharge in ARA, traders said.
    * At the same time, demand for cargoes in northern Europe
has been relatively strong in recent weeks.
    * ARA gasoil stocks, which include diesel and heating oil,
were down to 3.261 million tonnes in the week to Thursday from
3.286 million tonnes, data from Dutch consultancy PJK

tender to buy a cargo of vacuum gasoil (VGO), two cargoes of

Friday.[nL1N1HF0GF]
