SINGAPORE, Dec 7 (Reuters) - Asia's prompt-month 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) time
spread and cash premium fell on Friday as physical trade activity fizzled in the Singapore
trading window following a week of intense buying appetite for cargoes of the fuel. 
    Rising fuel oil inventories in Singapore and the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) refining
and storage hubs this week also helped dampen market sentiment. 
    The 380-cst fuel oil cash premium slipped to $5.65 a tonne to Singapore quotes, down from
$5.95 a tonne in the previous session <FO380-SIN-DIF>. 
    Strong buying interest on Monday had boosted the premium to a two-week high of $8.97 a tonne
to Singapore quotes.
    Similarly, the 380-cst Dec/Jan time spread slipped to around $8 per tonne on Friday, down
from about $8.75 a tonne in the previous session, broker sources said. 
    The prompt-month time spread was last lower on Nov. 28 at $7.75 per tonne, data in Refinitiv
Eikon showed. <FO380SGSDMc0>
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - One cargo trade was reported in the Singapore trading window totalling 20,000 tonnes of
380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO).
    - Repsol sold the cargo to Hin Leong at a premium of $3 per tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    - Trafigura, which has bought a total 460,000 tonnes of HSFO cargoes in the window so far
this month, did not buy any cargoes on Friday but did have outstanding bids for 380-cst HSFO
cargoes. 
    - A total of 800,000 tonnes of HSFO cargoes have traded in the window in the first week of
December, up from a total of 760,000 tonnes in the whole of November. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
        
    INVENTORIES
    - Fuel stocks independently held in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) refining and
storage hub rose by 18 percent to 1.1 million tonnes in the week to Dec. 6, data from Dutch
consultancy PJK International showed. [nL8N1YB52V]
    - ARA fuel oil imports in the week to Thursday originated from France, Poland, Russia and
the UK while exports were headed to Singapore, the data showed.
    - ARA fuel oil inventories were 9 percent lower than year-ago levels but above the five-year
average of 969,000 tonnes for this time of the year. <STK-FO-ARA>
    - In Singapore, fuel oil inventories climbed for a third straight week to a near six-month
high of 19.838 million barrels, or 2.961 million tonnes, in the week ended Dec. 5, lifted higher
by steady net import volumes during the week, official data showed. [nL4N1YB383]
    - By contrast, fuel oil inventories at the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) slipped 3
percent to a nine-month low of 6.001 million barrels, or 896,000 million tonnes, in the week
ended Dec. 3, data from S&P Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - In the United States, fuel oil inventories <RFO-STK-T-EIA> were just 0.2 percent lower to
a two-week low of 28.634 million barrels, or about 4.27 million tonnes, in the week to Nov. 30,
the latest data from the Energy Information Administration showed. [EIA/D]

validity.
    - Kuwait's KPC is offering up to 80,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4.2
percent sulphur content for Dec. 19-20 loading in a tender closed on Dec. 6.
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
    
    THIN MARGINS
    - Oil refiners' profits in Asia have slumped to the lowest in more than four years after
refineries ramped up output in the fourth quarter and churned out excess fuel in anticipation of
stronger demand during winter. [nL4N1YB3N1]
    - Oil inventories are building as new refineries in China and Vietnam are running at full
tilt, adding to Asia's supplies.
    - The margins at a typical Singapore complex refinery, a reference for profits at refineries
across Asia, fell to $2.49 a barrel on Thursday, the lowest since August 2014, Refinitiv Eikon
data showed. <DUB-SIN-REF>

SINGAPORE, Aug 2 (Reuters) - Asia's 380-cst prompt time spread was steady on Thursday, hovering
near a three-year high hit earlier in the week, as near-term fundamentals remained supportive. 
    This followed official data showing Singapore fuel oil stocks drop to a nine-year low this week.
[nL4N1UT37K] 
    Bullish fundamentals propped up Asia's fuel oil market over the summer months as strong demand,
particularly in the Middle East, and lower output contributed to low arbitrage volumes into the
Singapore hub. 
    However, some trade sources said they expected supplies into Singapore to gradually normalise
from September onwards as utility demand subsides after the scorching summer. 
    The 380-cst Aug/Sept time spread was about $9.75 a tonne on Thursday, while the following
Sept/Oct time spread was at a narrower premium of about $5.80 a tonne, according to broker sources.
<FO380SGSDMc1> <FO380SGSDMc2>
    Cash premiums for 380-cst cargoes were also lower on Thursday as some suppliers lowered their
offers for cargoes of the fuel in comparison with the previous session. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Singapore's weekly onshore fuel oil inventories continued to shrink after falling 1.397
million barrels (about 209,000 tonnes) to 14.799 million barrels (2.209 million tonnes) in the week
ended Aug. 1, official data showed on Thursday. 
    - Residual fuel stocks are now at their lowest since July 2009 after falling 8.6 percent in the
week ended Aug. 1, the data showed. <STKRS-SIN>
    - The shrinking fuel oil stocks in Singapore came as no surprise to trade sources, which pointed
to months of below-average arbitrage resupplies into Singapore as cargoes were diverted to the
Middle East to meet strong seasonal demand.
    - Fuel oil imports into Singapore hit 693,000 tonnes, their lowest in more than six months, in
the week ended Aug. 1, the data showed.
    - Net fuel oil imports into Singapore in the week ended Aug. 1 were at 244,000 tonnes compared
with a 2018 average of 760,000 tonnes per week.
    - Compared with a year ago, the latest onshore fuel oil inventories were 36 percent lower.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Hong Kong topped the week ended Aug. 1 at 135,000
tonnes, followed by Bangladesh at 61,000 tonnes and Guam at 39,000 tonnes.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Colombia at 162,000 tonnes, followed by
Indonesia at 95,000 tonnes, Malaysia at 83,000 tonnes and Saudi Arabia at 80,000 tonnes.
    - Fuel oil imports into Singapore in the week ended Aug. 1 from Iraq were absent for the first
time since early-May, while imports from the Netherlands were absent for a second consecutive week.
    - In the United States, fuel oil inventories <RFO-STK-T-EIA> climbed for a third straight week
to 28.72 million barrels in the week ended July 27, up 1.2 percent from the previous week, data from
the Energy Information Administration showed last week. [EIA/D]
             
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - One cargo trade was reported in Singapore trading window, totalling 20,000 tonnes of 380-cst
high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO).
    - Hin Leong bought the cargo from PetroChina at a premium of $4 a tonne to the average of
first-half August 380-cst Singapore quotes. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
     
    TENDERS
    - South Korea's EWP bought 40,000 tonnes of 540-cst low-sulphur fuel oil (LSFO) with a maximum
0.3 percent sulphur content for import into Ulsan over Aug 13-17 from Hanwha at a premium of about
$75 a tonne to Singapore 180-cst quotes on a CFR basis.

LONDON, Oct 2 (Reuters) - Spot trade slowed on Tuesday as
public holidays in China kept bidding at bay, although the
backdrop for the West African market was healthy with flows to
Asia set to reach their highest in two months in October.
    
    ANGOLA AND NIGERIA
    * The Angolan November programme had about 10 cargoes left,
down from about a dozen late last week, traders said. The
programme originally planned 46 cargoes for the month.
    * Cabinda was last on offer for loading mid-November at a
premium of about $1.00 a barrel to dated Brent, broadly
unchanged on the day, as was late November-loading Girassol that
was offered at around dated Brent plus $1.45.
    * The Nigerian market is still stuck with an overhang of
close to 20 unsold cargoes from the 58-strong October loading
programme, traders said, while the November programme, the
largest in six months, has seen fairly muted demand so far.
    * China's financial markets, including commodities, are
closed during the week of Oct. 1-5 for the National Day holiday.
    
        
    RELATED NEWS
    * Shipments of West African oil to Asia are set to hit a
two-month high in October as Chinese refineries scramble for
alternatives to Iranian crude before U.S. sanctions take effect
on Nov. 4. 
    Loadings for Asia will rise to 2.52 million barrels per day
(bpd) in October, equivalent to 75 percent of total output from
Angola, Nigeria, Republic of Congo, Ghana and Equatorial Guinea,
based on Reuters calculations, shipping brokers and Refinitiv
Eikon data. [O/WAFRICA1]
    * Russian President Vladimir Putin is to meet OPEC
Secretary-General Mohammad Barkindo on the sidelines of an
energy forum in Moscow this week, RIA news agency quoted the
Kremlin as saying. [nR4N1WD012]
    *  With oil prices hitting fresh four-year highs,
long-dormant proposals to allow the United States to sue OPEC
nations are getting a fresh look in Congress, although they were
once considered a longshot to becoming law. [nL2N1WH1RX]

crude, 2 million barrels for delivery from Nov. 6-20 and another

3 and the results are due by Oct. 5.

crude for November delivery, traders said.

SINGAPORE, Oct 2 (Reuters) - Asia's cash differentials for 10ppm gasoil climbed to their
highest in over a week on Tuesday, buoyed by stronger buying interests amid limited supply,
while the prompt-month spread widened its backwardated structure.
    Cash premiums for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10-SIN-DIF> rose to 84 cents a barrel
to Singapore quotes during Asian trade on Tuesday, compared with a premium of 80 cents a barrel
on Monday.
    The current high cash differentials for gasoil would likely sustain because the region is
quite strong lately due to some turnarounds in North Asia, trade sources said, adding supply
available is quite limited at present.
    The Oct/Nov time spread widened in backwardation to $1.45 a barrel on Tuesday, from $1.10 a
barrel on Monday. 
    Backwardation, when the front-month contract is more expensive than subsequent months, makes
it uneconomical to store the product, resulting in a drawdown in inventories. It is usually seen
as a sign that the market is rebalancing and prices are likely to head higher in future months.
    Refining margins for 10ppm gasoil <GO10SGCKMc1> climbed to $16.82 a barrel over Dubai crude
during Asian trading hours, compared with $16.68 per barrel a day earlier.
    Meanwhile, refining margins for jet fuel <JETSGCKMc1> inched down to $16.02 a barrel over
Dubai crude, compared with Monday's $16.18 a barrel, their highest in over three weeks.
    Cash discounts for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> narrowed to 67 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes,
compared with a discount of 70 cents on Monday.
    The physical market for jet fuel in the Singapore window remained subdued with no bids or
deals on Tuesday. 
    
        
    SINGAPORE CASH DEALS
    - Five gasoil deals, no jet fuel trade.
    - Total sold 155,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil to Winson Oil for Oct. 21-25 loading at a
premium of 85 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes.
    - Shell sold 165,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil to Lukoil for Oct. 17-21 loading at a premium
of 70 cents a barrel to the balance of October Singapore quotes.
    - BP bought 150,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil from Shell for Oct. 17-21 loading at a premium
of 40 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes.
    - Singapore trader Hin Leong sold 160,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil to Winson Oil for Oct.
17-21 loading at a premium of 60 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes.
    - Hin Leong also sold 220,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil to BP for Oct. 19-23 loading at a
premium of $1.70 a barrel to November Singapore quotes..

BENGALURU, Aug 2 (Reuters) - Asia's cash differentials for 10ppm gasoil climbed on Thursday
as middle distillate inventories in Singapore dipped, but traders were concerned near-term
demand may not be sufficient to meet growing supplies in the region.
    Backed by a stronger bid, cash premiums for gasoil with 10 ppm sulphur content
<GO10-SIN-DIF> rose to 8 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes, against a premium of 5 cents on
Wednesday.
    Gasoil exports from China and India will remain vital for the wider Asian markets over the
next couple of months as Chinese refineries returning from planned turnarounds add to supply,
while India will likely experience a seasonal dip in domestic sales during the monsoon, market
analysts said.
    India used about 42.6 million tonnes of diesel during January to June this year, up more
than 6 percent from the corresponding period last year. However, the country's consumption of
the transportation fuel usually drops as travel is affected by heavy monsoon rains.
    India's diesel exports in June was up 20 percent from the same month last year, and 23
percent higher than May, government data showed on Wednesday. This follows China's June diesel
exports that were up 23 percent from a year ago, as reported last week. [nL4N1US4WC][nB9N1RY01N]
    Meanwhile, cash premiums for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> were at 12 cents a barrel to Singapore

Dubai crude during Asian trade, from $14.35 on Wednesday.

to minus $11.72 a barrel in the previous session. <HFOFARAACMc2>

    SINGAPORE, May 2 (Reuters) - Bullish fundamentals in the physical and paper markets helped
boost Asia's fuel oil market complex on Tuesday, boosting 380-cst cash premiums to a near 2017
high while widening premiums across the fuel's near-term forward curve. 

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums <FO380-SIN-DIF> rose $1.14 a tonne from the previous session
to $2.59 a tonne to Singapore quotes, its highest since Jan. 16.
    - Traders attributed the rising premiums to higher costs of delivered arbitrage cargoes into
Singapore, as well as, fewer and less aggressive supplier offers. 
    - Traders pointed to Shell's sale of 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil to Socar at a
relatively high premium of $3 a tonne premium to Singapore 180-cst quotes was among the most
notable trades on Tuesday.
    - Mercuria on Tuesday also bought 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil from Shell at $304 per
tonne, equivalent to a premium of about $2 a tonne to Singapore quotes.
    - Prior to Tuesday's trades, the last time 180-cst fuel oil was traded in the window was on
April 24 when Vitol sold to Trafigura 40,000 tonnes of the fuel at a premium of about $2.15 a
tonne to Singapore quotes.
    - Five cargo trades were reported in the Platts window totalling 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst
fuel oil as well as 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil.
    - While still actively bidding for 380-cst cargoes, PetroChina did not buy any fuel oil
cargoes in the window for the first time since March 30. 
    - Please click on <O/AS> for more details. 
    
    SWAPS MARKET
    - Bullish sentiment was also evident in the swaps market after most near-dated 380-cst fuel
oil time spreads, from May/June through to Oct/Nov, posted gains on the Intercontinental Exchange
(ICE) by 6 p.m. Singapore time (1000 GMT).
    - The ICE-traded 380-cst May/June contract posted the largest gains, rising 85 cents a tonne
from the previous session to $1.75 a tonne.
    - The lower viscosity 180-cst May/June contract also rose 85 cents a tonne on ICE, trading at
$1.75 a tonne during the same time. 
    
    REFINERIES
    - Kuwait's new al-Zour refinery is expected to produce up to 225,000 barrels per day (bpd) of
low-sulphur fuel oil to meet domestic requirements for power generation. [nL4N1I41U9]
    - After the start-up of its Clean Fuel project by 2018, which will upgrade its other existing
refineries, Kuwait will have to import fuel oil for power generation until the commissioning of
the al-Zour refinery in 2019. [nL5N1HB2YE]
        
    NEW PRICE ASSESSMENTS 
    - S&P Global Platts <SPGI.N> will launch new low-sulphur marine gasoil (MGO) and diesel oil
(MDO) prices at several bunkering ports in Asia from June 2017. [nL4N1I40Y1] 
    - This is to cater for rising sales of the fuel sold in Singapore and as sulphur limits are
expected to tighten globally in the years ahead, the company said.

inventories at the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp hub.

in Scotland was successfully contained on Tuesday after
emergency services rushed to the scene, police said.
[nL8N1I44QM]

hydrocracking unit (HCU) at its 235,000 barrel per day (bpd)
Convent, Louisiana, refinery on Tuesday due to a leak, sources
familiar with plant operations said. [nL1N1I40K0]

barrel per day (bpd) condensate splitter in the Netherlands from

Industries, Vitol said in a statement on Tuesday. nL4N1I437X]

Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub fell 7.6 percent in the
week ending April 28, data from Dutch consultancy PJK
International showed on Friday.[ARA/]
    * Gasoline inventories in the refining and storage hub stood
at 1.09 million tonnes amid rising exports to the United States,
PJK's Jacob van den Berge said.

month when arbitrage to the United States was open. But rising
stocks in the United States has shut the arbitrage this week.

dragged. [nL4N1I40QN]

started around mid-March.

    SINGAPORE, May 3 (Reuters) - 380-cst cash premiums extended gains made in the previous
session to reach a four-month high on Wednesday, lifted by persistent bidding interest
amid reducing stocks after weeks of aggressive supplier offers in the Platts price
assessment window. 
    Meanwhile a shortage in prompt supplies of blend stock has boosted viscosity spreads
and prompt-month 180-cst fuel time spreads as blenders seek cutter supplies.  
        
    SWAPS MARKET
    - On the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), time spreads of 180-cst fuel oil for the
May/June contract jumped $2 a tonne from Tuesday's settlement, trading at $3.75 a tonne by
5:30 p.m. Singapore time (0930 GMT).
    - The May visco spread, the differential between the price of 180-cst and 380-cst fuel
oil, also rose sharply to $9.50 a tonne on Wednesday, up $2.25 a tonne from the previous
session.
    - The more actively traded 380-cst May/June contract rose 25 cents a tonne from the
previous session to $2 a tonne by the same time on ICE.
    - Traders, however, noted that the traded volumes of time spreads and visco spreads on
ICE were relatively low and did not exceed 50,000 tonnes in contracts each. 

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums <FO380-SIN-DIF> rose 62 cents a tonne from the
previous session to $3.21 a tonne to Singapore quotes, its highest since Jan. 3.
    - Seven cargo trades were reported in the Platts window on Wednesday totalling 120,000
tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil as well as 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Indonesia's Pertamina is offering 80,000 barrels of vacuum residue for loading at
Plaju on May 24-25. [nL4N1I51V0]
    - India's Reliance is offering 40,000 tonnes of carbon-black feedstock for May 20-21
for loading at Sikka. [nL4N1I51OM] 
    - India's IOC is offering up to 32,000 tonnes of vacuum gasoil (VGO) and up to 2,000
tonnes of 180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil from Haldia. Buyers have the option of lifting
16,000 tonnes of VGO with 1,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil on May 26-28, along with an
option second set of similar cargoes over June 4-6. [nL4N1I51NP]
        
    FUJAIRAH INVENTORIES
    - In the United Arab Emirates, the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil
inventories were virtually unchanged in the week to May 1 at 10.885 after rising just
6,000 barrels from the previous week, data via S&P Global Platts showed. [nL4N1I52C4]

LONDON, Sept 18 (Reuters) - Benchmark gasoline refining
margins in northwest Europe flattened on Monday after falling
sharply on weaker demand from the United States and the
continuing recovery in refining operations in the U.S. Gulf
Coast oil hub. 

    * Refinery operations across the U.S. Gulf Coast continued
to resume over the weekend and on Monday, with the Exxon
Beaumont refinery restarting its secondary units and Shell
restarting its 325,700 barrel per day (bpd) Deer Park refinery
in Texas on Sunday. [REF/OUT]
    * The restarts put a damper on oil exports from Europe to
the United States after they had spiked in the aftermath of
Hurricane Harvey. The storm knocked out nearly a quarter of U.S.
refining capacity. 
    * Demand remained strong in Latin America, particularly
Mexico and Brazil, which have struggled to run their own
refineries at nameplate capacity.
    * Demand was also strong in the Middle East, traders said,
amplified by refinery maintenance in the region. 
    * China's refined fuel production rose in August for nearly
all products, with kerosene up 5.3 percent year on year.
[nL4N1LZ1NJ]

    GASOLINE 
    * No barges traded in the afternoon window, and there were
no bids or offers.
    * Elsewhere, 18,000 tonnes traded at $577-$587 a tonne fob
Amsterdam-Rotterdam, compared with $577-$591 a tonne fob on
Friday.
    * There were no trades of premium unleaded gasoline in the
afternoon window. An offer came in at $592 a tonne fob ARA, but
there were no bids.
    * No cargoes traded. BP offered one cargo fob Thessaloniki
at $595 a tonne. 
    * The October swap stood at $548 a tonne at the close, down
from $551.50.
    * The benchmark EBOB gasoline refining margin fell to $13.91
a barrel at the close, down from $14.15 the previous day.  
    * Brent crude futures <LCOc1> were down 46 cents at $55.16 a
barrel by 1604 GMT.
    * U.S. front-month RBOB gasoline futures <RBc1> were up 0.37
percent at $1.6679 a gallon. 
    * The RBOB crack versus U.S. crude <RBc1-CLc1> was up 3.72
percent at $20.64 a barrel.

    NAPHTHA <NAF-C-NWE>

SINGAPORE, Sept 15 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil cash differentials continued to climb on Friday
at near three-year highs even as Unipec, the trading arm of China's Sinopec, planned to ship
excess fuel cargoes west, trade sources said.     
    
    - UNIPEC TO SHIP DIESEL IN VLCC: Unipec is planning to load a very large crude carrier
(VLCC) containing 10ppm sulphur diesel from its Tianjin refinery in the second half of September
to head to Europe, two sources familiar with the matter said. [L4N1LW3PJ]
    - CHINA OIL PRODUCT QUOTA: China added the nation's largest jet fuel distributor to its list
of approved exporters for the fourth quarter, breaking the grip of the country's four oil majors
on the lucrative export market and giving independent refiners indirect access to sales abroad.
     China issued a new batch of refined fuel export quotas to five state-run companies under
the general trade category for a total of 3.356 million tonnes, according to trading sources
with knowledge of the permits.
     The new issues compared with a previous round under the same category at 6.29 million
tonnes and would bring total fuel export quotas to 35.72 million tonnes for 2017 under both
general trade and tolling schemes.
     State-run China National Aviation Fuel Company (CNAF), the dominant jet fuel distributor,
was awarded for the first time export quotas totalling 200,000 tonnes, said a CNAF trading
executive.    
    - VIETNAM BUYS GASOIL: Vietnam's top fuel importer Petrolimex bought two cargoes of 35,000
tonnes each of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for October delivery at a premium of 60 cents a barrel
free-on-board (FOB) Singapore, Malaysia or Thailand, traders said.
      This is 40 cents higher than the importer paid for September cargoes, they added.      
    - THAILAND OFFERS GASOIL: Thailand's PTT offered 35,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for
loading in Oct. 8-10 in a tender that closes Sept. 18, traders said.
    - INDIA OFFERS JET FUEL: India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals (MRPL) has offered
40,000 tonnes of jet fuel for loading Oct 17-19 in a tender that closes on Sept. 20. 
    - YUNNAN PIPELINE: PetroChina this week started pumping diesel fuel into a new pipeline
connecting the Chinese state oil major's newly refinery in southwestern Yunnan province, parent
company CNPC said on its website on Friday. [nL4N1LW0C1]
      The new oil product pipeline has a total length of 951 km (590.92 miles), composed of
three trunk lines and one branch line, with total annual transport capacity of 7.22 million
tonnes. 
    
    - SINGAPORE CASH DEALS: Five gasoil deals and no jet fuel trades. <O/AS>

SINGAPORE, Sept 15 (Reuters) - Unipec, the trading arm of
China's state-owned Sinopec <600028.SS>, is shipping its first
very large crude carrier (VLCC) of diesel from China to Europe,
two sources close to the matter said on Friday.
    The company is loading the vessel with 10 parts-per-million
(ppm) diesel from its refinery in the northern port city of
Tianjin, near Beijing, in second-half September to head to the
Mediterranean or northwest Europe, one of the sources said.
    It will also match the more stringent winter specifications
required by Europe, the source said.

SINGAPORE, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Asia's physical and paper fuel oil markets were boosted
on Thursday as official weekly data showed Singapore fuel oil inventories fell 11 percent,
ending the five-week run of inventory builds. 
    The decline in inventories helped improve the market outlook, widening near-dated time
spreads <FO380SGSDMc1>, arbitrage spreads <FOSGEWMc2> and cracks <FO180SGCKMc1> in the
paper market, as well as boosting cash premiums for spot fuel oil cargoes, industry
sources said.

total of 3.5 million tonnes in the week to Sept. 13, official data showed. [O/SING1]
    - Weekly net imports into Singapore fell 20 percent to a five-week low of 575,000
tonnes. 
    - Compared with the same time last year Singapore's fuel oil stocks are now 9 percent
higher. 
    - On Wednesday fuel oil inventories in the Fujairah oil hub slipped 0.7 percent in the
week to Sept. 11 to a total of about 1.59 million tonnes. [FUJAIRAH/]

which are 180-cst fuel oil cargoes.     
    - Trafigura sold Thursday's fourth 380-cst cargo to BP. 
    - This comes after Trafigura in September bought a total of 1.031 million tonnes of
380-cst fuel oil in the window.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details.

LONDON, Sept 22 (Reuters) - Benchmark diesel refining
margins in northwest Europe ended the week slightly lower but
held near two-year highs as supplies in the region were set to
tighten significantly.
    * Europe is set to export a record volume of diesel in
September as Latin American buyers struggle to recover from a
drop in U.S. supplies in the wake of Hurricane Harvey, according
to shipping data and traders. [nL5N1M24W9]
    * At least 600,000 tonnes of diesel and heating oil are
expected to sail from Europe and the Mediterranean to Brazil and
Argentina in September.
    * ARA gasoil stocks declined in the week to Thursday to
2.589 million tonnes from 2.634 million tonnes, data from Dutch
consultancy PJK International showed. [ARA/]
    * Buying interest in the ARA region as well as inland
markets has been low this week due to high diesel and heating
oil prices and a strong backwardation, traders said.
    * Still, a drop in imports is expected to lead to a sharp
draw in diesel stocks this month.
    * Increasing efficiency of fossil-fuel powered cars is a
bigger threat to gasoline demand than electric cars, energy
consultant FGE told the Platts refining summit in Brussels. FGE
forecasts that from 2016 to 2040, fuel economy gains will slash
11.3 million barrels per day (bpd) from global gasoline
consumption, more than twice the 5.3 million bpd cut by the
addition of hybrid cars, plug-in hybrids and battery electric
vehicles. [nL5N1M24BV]
    * Nigeria's efforts to cut sulphur levels in its fuel
imports are unlikely to succeed this year, the head of a major
Nigerian downstream company told the Platts refining conference
in Brussels. [nL5N1M31ZL]

SINGAPORE, Sept 22 (Reuters) - Firm buying interest and few supplier offers in the Platts
window on Friday helped boost cash premiums of Asia's 380-cst fuel oil <FO380-SIN-DIF> to their
highest since June 29.
    In the paper markets, the front-month fuel oil crack <FO180SGCKMc1> slipped to a near
two-month low on rising crude oil prices but bullish sentiment continued to lift 380-cst
front-month time spread <FO380SGSDMc1> higher, industry sources said. 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Three cargo trades were reported in the Platts window totalling 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst
fuel oil.
    - Hin Leong bought 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil from Vitol in two cargoes and Total
sold it the third 20,000-tonne cargo. 
    - Friday's cargo trades were executed at a premium range between $2.25 to $2.35 a tonne to
Singapore quotes, sources said. By comparison, on Monday two 380-cst cargoes were traded at a $1
a tonne and $1.50 a tonne premium to Singapore quotes. 
    - There were just two standing supplier offers for 380-cst cargoes by the close of the
trading window versus nine bids. By comparison, there were seven standing offers against six
bids for 380-cst cargoes on Monday.
    - A total of 2.042 million tonnes of fuel oil have traded in the window since the start of
the month, against 1.402 million tonnes in August.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Kuwait's KPC is offering another unexpected fuel oil cargo totalling 80,000 tonnes for
Oct. 1-2 loading in a tender closed on Thursday and valid until today. [nL4N1M338L]
    - An industry source who has seen the specification sheet of the cargo said it was described
as 380-cst heavy fuel oil but had the characteristics of straight-run fuel oil (SRFO). 
    - The source said the cargo will be supplied from different tanks but the majority of the
cargo was comprised of SRFO that was blended with a small proportion of cracked 380-cst fuel
oil. 
    - At the start of the month, KPC unexpectedly offered a similar cargo with a similarly
prompt delivery notice. [nL4N1LP3C9]
    - KPC's scheduled decommissioning of the Shuaibah refinery on April 1 reduced Kuwaiti fuel
oil supplies by about 250,000 tonnes per month, resulting in almost no fuel oil exports.
[nL5N1HB2YE] [nL3N1H758B]
    - Prior to decommissioning KPC's Shuaibah refinery on April 1, KPC typically exported
380-cst HSFO, but rarely SRFO cargoes, sources said.
    - India's HPCL is offering 30,000 tonnes of 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) with a
maximum 4.5 percent sulphur content for delivery on Oct. 10-13 from Mumbai. The offer closes
today. [nL4N1M32US]
    
    SOUTH KOREAN EXPORTS 
    - Two South Korean refiners are exporting excess cargoes of residual fuel oil to nearby
China, displacing some Singaporean sales of the commodity which can be used in ships and power
stations, three trade sources said. [nL4N1LW3YF]
    - Sources estimate GS Caltex has exported between 100,000-200,000 tonnes of fuel oil, mostly
to China, as a result of a fire at its Yeosu refinery in August.
    - S-Oil is estimated to have exported 120,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil into China in
September for use as a marine fuel.

SINGAPORE, Sept 19 (Reuters) - Cash premiums of Asia's 380-cst fuel oil narrowed for a
second consecutive session on Tuesday following lower deal values, while the front-month
time spreads of the mainstay fuel were offered down amid limited trade activity, industry
sources said. 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Three 20,000-tonne 380-cst fuel oil cargo trades were reported in the Platts window on
Tuesday.
    - Coastal was both a buyer and seller of 380-cst fuel oil cargoes in the window, sources
said. 
    - Trafigura sold 20,000 tonnes of the fuel to Coastal at a premium of $1.25 a tonne to
Singapore quotes for Sept. 4-8 loading and then Coastal sold to Hin Leong a similar cargo
loading over the same laycan at a lower premium of $1 a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    - The third 20,000 tonne cargo was sold by Mercuria to Coastal for loading over Sept.
9-13 at a premium of $1.25 a tonne to Singapore quotes, sources said. 
    - A total of 1.862 million tonnes of high-sulphur fuel oil has traded in the window
since the start of the year, compared with 1.4 million tonnes in August.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    380-CST RECENT HIGHS 
    - Market sentiment was improved last week by firm buying interest for physical cargoes
and declining fuel oil inventories across key storage hubs including Singapore and northwest
Europe, sources said. [nL4N1LW3YE]
    - By Friday, 380-cst cash premiums <FO380-SIN-DIF> rose to $1.58 a tonne to Singapore
quotes, their highest since July 4, while the front-month 380-cst time spread <FO380SGSDMc1>
had climbed to $2.25 a tonne, its highest since June 29.  
    - On Tuesday, 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums fell 32 cents a tonne from the previous
session to $1.15 a tonne to Singapore quotes, a four session low. 
    - The 380-cst Oct/Nov time spreads had slipped to about $2.05 a tonne on Tuesday by 5.45
p.m. Singapore time (0945 GMT), 15 cents lower than the previous session amid limited trade
volumes, sources said.     
        
    OTHER NEWS
    - Shippers are sending oil cargoes originally bound for Venezuela to other spots in
Latin America and the Caribbean in advance of coming hurricanes that threaten to further
disrupt oil flows in the region, according to traders and Reuters data. [nL2N1LW275]
    - Iraq does not see the need for more output cuts now, but if there is a need the
country will support consensus within the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
(OPEC), Iraq's oil minister Jabar al-Luaibi said on Tuesday. [nD5N1IQ000]

SINGAPORE, Sept 21 (Reuters) - Market sentiment in Asia's fuel oil market was positve on
Thursday despite official data showing a 5 percent rise in onshore Singapore fuel oil stocks to a
two-week high over the past week. 
    Industry sources said the front-month time spreads <FO380SGSDMc1> and East-West arbitrage
spreads <FOSGEWMc1> held near their recent highs, but rising crude oil prices had weighed on the
fuel oil crack. 
    The October 180-cst crack to Dubai crude <FO180SGCKMc1> fell to a near two week low of minus
$1.80 a barrel on Thursday, down 36 cents a barrel from the previous session. 

    SINGAPORE INVENTORIES
    - Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories climbed to a total of 3.5 million tonnes in the week
to Sept. 20, up 5 percent or 169,000 tonnes from the previous week, IE Singapore data showed.
[O/SING1]
    - This came as weekly fuel oil exports from Singapore sank to their lowest since week to Feb.
1 totalling 352,000 tonnes over the past week, according to IE Singapore data. [IEOIL]
    - Weekly net imports into Singapore were 16 percent down to a six-week low of 482,000 tonnes.
    - Fuel oil stocks are now 1 percent higher year-on-year.

fuel oil through four deals in addition to one 20,000 tonne cargo of 380-cst fuel oil.

September, against 1.402 million tonnes in August. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details.

[nL4N1M242X]

SINGAPORE, Sept 20 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differentials eased on Wednesday as oil
traders Winson Oil and Unipec slowed down their buying spree of gasoil cargoes in Singapore,
trade sources said.
    
    - SRI LANKA SEEKS: Ceylon Petroleum is seeking a combination cargo of 150,000 barrels of
500ppm sulphur gasoil and 160,000 barrels of jet fuel for Nov. 18 to 19 delivery. The tender
closes on Oct. 4 and is valid for up to 72 hours. 
    - TANKER RATES: Freight rates for oil product tankers in Asia hit a multi-month high this
week on reduced availability as vessels were diverted to ship fuel to the United States and
Mexico in the wake of Hurricane Harvey. [nL4N1LZ2UN]
      Some bigger tankers are also being used as temporary storage for gasoil as traders hold
fuel on expectations of tighter supply and improved demand in the fourth quarter. This has
compounded the shortage of vessels.
    - OIL STORAGE: Singapore port operator Jurong Port and independent oil storage operator
Oiltanking officially launched an oil storage facility with a total capacity of 480,000 cubic
metres on Wednesday. [nL4N1M13BL]
      Located on 16 hectares (39.5 acres) of land in Jurong Port, the terminal will store clean
petroleum products and will be supported by four jetties with a draft limit of up to 17.6 metres
capable of handling vessels up to 180,000 deadweight tonnes (DWT).
      Construction of the terminal, known as Jurong Port Tank Terminals, started in May and is
on track to be completed by 2019, Jurong Port said in a press statement.
    - RELIANCE EXPANSION: India's Reliance Industries, operator of the world's largest refining
complex, is considering expanding its oil processing capacity by over 40 percent by 2030,
according to two sources familiar with the matter.
      Reliance may expand the capacity at its dual refinery complex in Jamnagar in the western
Indian state of Gujarat by 30 million tonnes a year to 100 million tonnes per year, according to
the sources, who saw the expansion plans in a presentation by the company on potential energy
scenarios to 2030. [nL4N1LZ47Z]

LONDON, Sept 21 (Reuters) - Benchmark diesel refining
margins in northwest Europe rose on Thursday as stocks in the
region continued to decline due to lower imports.

2.589 million tonnes from 2.634 million tonnes, data from Dutch
consultancy PJK International showed.[ARA/]
    * Buying interest in the ARA region as well as inland
markets has been low this week due to high diesel and heating
oil prices and a strong backwardation, traders said.
    * Still, a drop in imports is expected to lead to a sharp
draw in diesel stocks this month.
    * Hurricane Harvey's crippling impact on U.S. oil refinery
operations this month and the challenge buyers faced in filling
the gap in gasoline supplies has exposed a shortage of spare
refining capacity around the globe. [nL5N1M20QE]

LONDON, Sept 13 (Reuters) - Benchmark diesel refining
margins in northwest Europe rose on Wednesday supported by
stronger demand in the region and an expected sharp tightening
of supplies in the Atlantic basin.

    * Buying activity in the ARA hub increased following the
expiry of the September low sulphur gasoil futures contract on
Tuesday, traders said.
    * A strong backwardation in the front end of the market has
led traders to offer larger volumes from storage tanks. 
    * At the same time inland buyers in Germany have started
stocking up on heating oil for winter, traders said.
    * U.S. distillate stockpiles, which include diesel and
heating oil, fell last week by 3.2 million barrels, which
compared with expectations for a 1.5 million-barrel drop, EIA
data showed. [EIA/S]
    * European diesel stocks are expected to fall by some 2
million tonnes in September as imports from the United States
plunge in the wake of Hurricane Harvey, which crippled refining
operations on the Gulf Coast, traders said on
Tuesday.[nL5N1LT4LP]
    * Diesel imports from the Gulf Coast, a major source of
supply for Europe, are expected to drop to about 500,000 tonnes
in September, far lower than the 1.5 million to 2 million tonnes
seen in previous months, according to traders and shipping data.
    * Imports of diesel from Asia and the Middle East were
expected to reach around 1.4 million tonnes in September,
slightly offsetting the lower imports from other regions,
traders said.
    * Nigeria and several other West African states are not
expected to implement rules banning imports of sulphur-heavy
fuels until Dec. 1 at the earliest after missing summer
deadlines, drawing the ire of health campaigners pushing for
cleaner air.[nL8N1LI4MA]

month, traders said 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums and time spreads were holding firm near

sources said.

fuel this year headed for their homeland despite declaring other destinations, a ploy that U.S.
officials say is often used to undermine sanctions.

Reuters ship-tracking data. Changing a ship's destination once underway is not forbidden and it
is unclear whether any of the ships unloaded fuel in North Korea.

state tactics to circumvent the international trade sanctions imposed over Pyongyang's nuclear
weapons programme.

Thursday after extending gains for a fourth consecutive session, fuelled by bullish
fundamentals and falling crude oil prices.

high. However, it was largely ignored by traders since the inventory build was a
result of floating storage being discharged into onshore tanks.

<FO180SGCKMc1> rose to a premium of 59 cents a barrel, up from 27 cents a barrel in
the previous session, Reuters data showed.
    - Prior to Wednesday, the last time the residual fuel has been at a premium to
Dubai crude was in January 2012 and before that in July 2003.
    - The July margin for FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil to Brent crude on the
Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) also extended gains, narrowing its discount to
around $3.70 a barrel by 1630 Singapore time (0830 GMT).

the summer when demand for the fuel used in power generation peaks. [nL3N1JJ1YQ]

differentials for gasoil, traders said on Tuesday. Traders were also eyeing the impending

50ppm sulphur diesel and 74,332 tonnes of jet fuel for delivery into the Mozambican ports of
Maputo, Beira, Nacala and Pemba in the second half of 2017, traders said. [nL3N1JO2Q2]
      The tender closes on July 14.

500ppm from mid-2017, one of the traders said.

for delivery in August, including 148,234 tonnes of jet fuel and 281,554 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur
diesel, a tender document showed.

    - PETROSA: South Africa's PetroSA is seeking two cargoes of 42,000 tonnes each of 50ppm
sulphur diesel for delivery in September and October in a tender that closes on June 28.
<MDIS/TENDA>
    - INDIAN SPOT DEMAND CONTINUES: Indian Oil Corp has offered 38,000 to 40,000 tonnes of 40ppm
sulphur diesel for delivery in July, and has offered a 1 percent sulphur light diesel oil cargo
also for the same period, traders said. 
      India's diesel imports continued despite the start of the monsoon due to heavy refinery
maintenance as refiners change specifications to meet new sulphur standards, they added.

production over the next four years as demand for aviation strengthens, analysts from BMI
Research said in a note on Tuesday.

strong across the main markets in Asia, North America and Europe, a good indicator for the next

SINGAPORE, June 23 (Reuters) - Continued jet fuel purchases by Chinese traders in Singapore
supported the cash differentials for the aviation fuel, traders said on Friday. 
    
    - SAIGON PETRO TENDER: Vietnam's Saigon Petro is seeking 10,000 tonnes of diesel for
delivery in mid-July, traders said. 
      It last bought five diesel cargoes for delivery in June and July at a premium of 70 cents
a barrel to Singapore quotes, traders have said. <MDIS/TENDA>
    - INDIAN OIL OFFERS: Indian Oil Corp has offered five cargoes of up to 28,000 tonnes each of
high-sulphur gasoil for loading over July to October, traders said.
      IOC is having extensive maintenance until the end of the year to upgrade its units as the
country moved towards Euro IV fuels in April this year. This has, in turn, increased exports of
high-sulphur gasoil from the country and boosted low-sulphur diesel, traders said. <REF/A>
    - ADNOC TERM TALKS: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company's term talks to sell diesel for its term
contract for cargoes loading from July has stalled, a trader said.
      Talks stalled due to uncertainty involving the situation in Qatar, the trader added,
though this could not be confirmed. 
    - CHINESE DEMAND: Some of China's top oil refineries are having to take the highly unusual
step of cutting operations during what is typically the peak demand summer season when hot
weather drives up power usage and families take to the road during school holidays.
      Almost 10 percent of China's refining capacity is set to be shut down during the third
quarter, signaling that demand growth from the world's top crude importer is stuttering further.
      To whittle down the surplus weighing on the domestic market, analysts expect China to
export refined product, putting more pressure on a well-supplied global market. [nL3N1JI3C7]
     - NEW REFINERY: Indonesian engineering firm PT Intim Perkasa has expressed an interest in
building a refinery in Nigeria, the West African country's state oil company said on Wednesday. 
     Nigeria has been seeking investment in the sector to reduce reliance on imported oil
products that consume a large portion of the OPEC member's scarce foreign currency reserves.

LONDON, June 27 (Reuters) - Diesel differentials in
northwest Europe were little changed on Tuesday in thin trading
activity.    
    * A lack of prompt barge availability due to high demand
from inland buyers kept a lid on trading activity, traders said.
    * Inland demand has been high due to prolonged refinery
maintenance in Germany and Switzerland. 
    * Varo said its 68,000 barrel per day Cressier refinery had
restarted following a maintenance shutdown. 
    * Latin American refinery outages underpinned the market by
attracting diesel cargoes from the U.S. Gulf that could have
otherwise landed in Europe. 
    * Venezuela's largest refining complex plans to operate next
month at 42 percent of its 955,000-barrel-per-day capacity, a
level that would require state-run oil company PDVSA to keep
increasing fuel purchases, according to internal documents seen
by Reuters. [nL1N1JO0OL]
    * Global jet fuel consumption will outstrip production over
the next four years as demand for aviation strengthens, say
analysts from BMI Research. [nL3N1JO1BC]
    * Traders said that BB Energy won the most recent Midor
tender to sell two jet fuel cargoes and the Sonatrach tender to
sell one cargo. Kenya's oil importers are seeking nearly 580,000
tonnes of oil products for delivery in August. [O/TEND]
    * Kenya's importers are seeking 148,234 tonnes of jet fuel
and 281,554 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur gasoil.
    * Mozambique's Importadora Mocambicana de Petroleos is
seeking 685,058 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur gasoil and 74,332 tonnes
of jet fuel for delivery in the second-half of this year,
traders said.

  GASOIL <EURO/DIFF/GO>    
    * Barges of 0.1 percent sulphur content traded at discounts
of $11.50 a tonne fob ARA to the July ICE Low Sulphur Gasoil
futures, slightly weaker than the day earlier.
    * No cargo trades were reported.
    * No barges of 50 ppm sulphur gasoil traded.     
    * July Low Sulphur Gasoil futures were $13.50 a tonne higher
at $423 by 1548 GMT.
    * The July contract was trading flat to the August contract,
compared with a 25 cent contango the previous day.
    * Benchmark diesel margins stood at $9.94 a barrel, up from
$9.20 a barrel at Monday's close.  

    DIESEL <ULSD10-BD-ARA>

    * Vitol sold to Glencore one cargo cif Le Havre at a

    SINGAPORE, June 28 (Reuters) - The July East-West arbitrage spread continued to fall on
Wednesday, weighed down by bullish market fundamentals in northwest European markets,
making shipments into Asia increasingly uneconomical over the near term. 
    Western fuel oil flows into East Asia for July closed at 3.1 to 3.2 million tonnes, the
lowest in 12 months and well below June's four-month high of 5.1 to 5.2 million tonnes, the
latest assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed. [nPGEmXWxla]
    
    ARB SPREADS  
    - Broker sources pegged the July EW spread at about $13.25 a tonne by 7 p.m. Singapore
time (1100 GMT) on Wednesday, down from around $13.50 a tonne at around the same time in
the previous session.
    - Earlier in the day, the EW arbitrage spread tried to push higher reaching $14 a tonne
but was quickly sold down, sources said.
    - Despite expectations for tighter arbitrage flows into Asia in the coming two months,
sources said the EW spread has been weighed down by tight European supplies. 
    - European barge time spreads for July/Aug <HFOFARAASMc1> were at a premium of $3.50 a
tonne on Wednesday, up 25 cents a tonne from the previous session. 
    - The July/Aug barge time spread on Monday settled at a near 10-month high of $3.75 a
tonne. 
    
    FUJAIRAH INVENTORIES
    - In the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil
inventories rose nearly 4 percent in the week to June 26 to a total of 12.136 million
barrels, data via S&P Global Platts showed. [nL3N1JP38Y]
    - Fujairah's fuel oil inventories are now at their second highest since stocks
reporting began in mid-January, slightly below the record 12.328 million barrels seen in
the week to March 27. 
    - In spite of the rise, traders said pressure over bunker fuel sales in Fujairah is
gradually easing after the Port of Fujairah lifted restrictions on vessels sailing to and
from Qatar from entering its ports in a notice dated June 12.
    - Qatari-flagged, owned or operated vessels are still barred from calling at any UAE
ports.
    - In response to this ongoing ban, Qatar Petroleum last week said it made available a
vessel-borne fuelling facility for all ships lifting any Qatari seaborne imports or
exports. [nL8N1JG2V2]
            
    TENDERS
    - India's IOC offered up to 35,000 tonnes of 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil for loading
in Chennai on July 22-24 in a tender closing on Wednesday. [nL3N1JP3J2]
    
    WINDOW TRADES
    - No cargo trades were reported in the Platts window.
    - The last time no cargo trades were reported in the window was three weeks ago on June
7.

SINGAPORE, June 20 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differentials may weaken over the
coming weeks as demand from China is expected to fall as an annual fishing ban starts and as the
beginning of monsoon rains dent demand in India, traders said on Tuesday.
    
    - GASOIL DIFFERENTIALS MAY WEAKEN: A fishing ban in the South China sea which takes place
between May and September may dent demand for gasoil from fishing boats which in turn may weaken
the cash differentials for the 500ppm sulphur gasoil, a North Asian trader said.
      He added that the start of monsoon in India may also curb imports of diesel into the
country, in turn putting pressure on cash differentials for the grade.  
    - TAIWAN REFINERY: Taiwan's Formosa Petrochemical Corp plans to shut its No. 2 crude
distillation unit (CDU) with a capacity of 180,000 bpd from July 10 for about three to four
weeks, a company spokesman said. [nL3N1JH1W5]
     The operating rate of the refinery will be lowered to 400,000 bpd, or about 74 percent, in
July from the current 500,000 bpd, he said. This could cut Formosa's diesel exports, traders
said. 
     Formosa is also planning to shut its No. 1 residue desulphuriser unit with a capacity of
80,000 bpd to replace a catalyst, in late September. 
    - SRI LANKA IMPORTS:  Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp has re-issued its term tenders to
buy gasoil, jet fuel and gasoline by seeking more volumes for delivery over August 2017 to March
2018, traders said. 
    - INDIAN OIL OFFERS: Indian Oil Corp has offered 4,000 to 4,500 tonnes of light diesel oil
(LDO) with 1 percent sulphur for loading over July 10 to 12 from Budge Budge in a tender that
closes on June 21, traders said. 
    - INDIAN JET FUEL: India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Corp (MRPL) has offered
40,000 tonnes of jet fuel for loading over July 27 to 29 in a tender that closes on June 28,
traders said. 
      MRPL last sold a mid-July loading jet fuel cargo to Litasco at a discount of $1.25 a
barrel to Singapore quotes, traders said. <MDIS/TENDA>

LONDON, May 9 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe extended gains on Tuesday as crude futures
traded lower for a second consecutive session. Planned and
unplanned refinery maintenance in Europe also supported margins.
  
    * Planned refinery turnarounds in Italy, Israel, Spain,
Poland, and Hungary were helping to keep supplies of oil product
in check, traders said. 
    * An unplanned shutdown at Total's Feyzin refinery due to
strike action was also tightening the market. [REF/E]
    * This comes amid relatively weak arbitrage economics to
other regions. 
    * While more tankers were booked in recent days to ship
gasoline and blending components to the U.S. East Coast, traders
said the arbitrage window was shaky as inventories in that
country grew and its refiners cranked up output following
seasonal maintenance.
    * West Africa was facing an excess of cargoes, though deals
to swap crude oil for products - expected to be finalised any
day - could lead to some new bookings. 
    * Crude oil intake at Europe's refineries in April rose 6.5
percent from a year ago to 10.549 million barrels per day, data
from industry monitor Euroilstock showed on Tuesday.
[nL9N1CH036]

GASOLINE 
    * No trades of benchmark Eurobob gasoline emerged during the
afternoon trading window.
    * Elsewhere, 5,000 tonnes traded at $509-$509.50 a tonne fob
Amsterdam-Rotterdam, compared with trades at $504-$506 a tonne
on Monday.
    * Vitol sold a barge of premium unleaded gasoline to Total
at $504 a tonne fob ARA, this compared with an offer at $503 a
tonne on Monday.
    * The June swap stood at around $503 a tonne at the close,
unchanged.
    * Brent crude futures <LCOc1> were 39 cents lower at $48.95
a barrel by 1551 GMT.
    * Gasoline barge refining margins firmed to $13.715 a barrel
from $12.475 a barrel on Monday. 
    * U.S. front-month RBOB gasoline futures <RBc1> were 1.3
percent lower at $1.4981 a gallon.
    * The RBOB crack versus U.S. crude <RBc1-CLc1> stood at
$16.85 a barrel, down from $17.32 a barrel at the close on
Monday.

LONDON, May 9 (Reuters) - Benchmark diesel barge
differentials in northwest Europe rose on Tuesday to their
highest since early January supported by lower imports and
refinery maintenance in the region.
    * Demand for diesel in inland markets, particularly in
Germany, was strong, traders said. Most buying was done locally
however with ARA barge activity relatively slow.
    * The arbitrage from the U.S. Gulf Coast remained closed
with only a slow flow of tankers on the route, which is expected
to reach around 500,000 tonnes in May so far, traders said.
    * The Mediterranean diesel market remained tight due to a
number of refinery outage and lower imports from the East and
West.
    * The arrival in Northwest Europe in recent days of several
jet fuel tankers from India, the Middle East and Asia Pacific
was putting downward pressure on prices in the region, traders
said.  
    * India's record jet fuel exports may fall this year as an
expanding middle class and cheaper air travel boost local
consumption, refinery executives and analysts told Reuters,
potentially raising ailing profit margins for the
fuel.[nL4N1IA1H3]

SINGAPORE, May 9 (Reuters) - Unexpected spot demand from India supported the
Asian gasoil cash differentials on Tuesday, traders said. Summer demand from the
Middle East is also expected to boost differentials further, they added. 
    
    - INDIAN GASOIL DEMAND: Indian Oil Corp is seeking up to 80,000 tonnes of gasoil
for import in May in an unusual move, a tender document showed. 
     It is seeking two cargoes of 38,000 tonnes to 40,000 tonnes each of euro IV
diesel for delivery in May. IOC is typically well-balanced in its gasoil supply and
demand, but may be importing due to a recent shift towards Euro IV fuel standards in
India, one trader said, though this could not be confirmed.
    - MIDEAST SUMMER DEMAND: Spot demand from the Middle East is also expected to
boost gasoil differentials, traders said.
    Saudi Arabia may have bought gasoil from India to import into the Red Sea, one of
the traders said, though this could not immediately be confirmed. 
    - PAKISTAN CANCELS JET: Pakistan State Oil has cancelled a tender to buy jet fuel
for delivery in June amid a border dispute between the South Asian country and
Afghanistan, a source at the company said. [nL4N1IB3R8]
    PSO initially sought to buy a cargo of 10,000 tonnes of jet fuel for delivery in
June but this has now been cancelled due to restrictions in shipping oil across the
border, the source said.
    PSO has also cancelled a tender to buy gasoil for June due to sufficient
inventory, he said. 
    - INDIA'S JET FUEL EXPORTS TO FALL:  India's record jet fuel exports may fall
this year as an expanding middle class and cheaper air travel boost local
consumption, refinery executives and analysts told Reuters, potentially raising
ailing profit margins for the fuel.

LONDON, May 8 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe jumped higher on Monday as crude oil futures
slid nearly 1 percent lower in afternoon trading. The crack gain
came despite worries over whether demand in the crucial U.S.
market would be enough to absorb summer production.   
    * While more tankers were booked in recent days to ship
gasoline and blending components to the U.S. East Coast, traders
said the arbitrage window was shaky as inventories in that
country grew and its refiners cranked up output following
seasonal maintenance.
    * U.S. gasoline demand has faltered in recent weeks, and
that along with inventories in the Gulf Coast flagged worries
about the market for Europe's exports.
    * West Africa was also facing an excess of cargoes, though
deals to swap crude oil for products - expected to be finalised
any day - could lead to some new bookings. 
    * China's refiners processed less oil in April during a
heavy maintenance season, while exports of refined fuel fell by
a quarter from a month earlier due to quota reductions.
[nL4N1IA1UR]

Saudi Aramco on downstream investments, including a 1.2 million
bpd mega project on its west coast. [nL4N1IA2AP]

SINGAPORE, April 29 (Reuters) - The discounts of Asian 380cst fuel oil narrowed slightly on
Friday, returning to the same levels at the start of the week. 
    Cash discounts of 380cst fuel oil contracted to $1.48 a tonne below Singapore quotes, up 13
cents from the previous day and just 1 cent lower from Monday's minus $1.47. 
    Differentials of the 380cst fuel oil have traded within a tight range throughout April, with
little volatility compared to previous months, settling between a 21 cent high and a minus $1.97 low
to Singapore quotes. By contrast, the February range for 380cst cash differentials stood between
plus 78 cents and minus $5.35, while March drifted between plus $3.58 and minus $2.54. 
    Friday's narrower cash discounts followed slightly firmer buyers bids in the Platts window which
concluded in three cash deals being reported. 
    Two of Vitol's bids, each for 20,000 tonnes of 380cst high-sulphur fuel oil, were lifted by
Gunvor and BP at a discount of $1.75 a tonne to Singapore quotes. Glencore bought the third cargo of
20,000 tonnes of 380cst fuel oil when its bid was picked up by Coastal at a discount of $1.50 a
tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    The front-month time spreads of the 380cst fuel oil deepened their contango marginally, slipping
25 cents to minus $1.50 a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    In related news, the sales and operation licences of Seaquest Tanker and Vermont UM Bunkering
were revoked by Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) because of erroneous record keeping on
their tankers, the MPA said in a statement on Thursday. [nL3N17V3UB]
    The MPA took away the licences after finding discrepancies and wrongful declarations in the
records kept on board their bunker vessels, the statement said.
    
    RELATED MARKET NEWS:
    - Saudi Arabia's oil output will edge up close to record highs in the coming weeks to meet
summer demand for power but is unlikely to be pushed to the limit and flood global markets,
Saudi-based industry sources said. [nL5N17V3V9]
    Production may rise to around 10.5 million barrels per day (bpd) during the summer, the sources
said.
    - Dozens of tankers with unsold crude have been amassing at sea in the past few weeks,
reminiscent of 2015 when a recovery in oil prices was scuppered by rising physical supply.
[nL5N17V5XP]
 
    TENDERS & AWARDS:
    - Taiwan's Fermosa awarded a 40,000 tonne cargo of 380cst high-sulphur fuel oil to Shell for
loading May 10-12 from the port of Mailiao, industry sources said. [nL3N17W2TH]
    The contractual price of the deal could not be confirmed.

SINGAPORE, Oct 24 (Reuters) - The Asian jet fuel cash
differential flipped to a premium on Tuesday as the outlook for
airline travel was expected to be robust and supply tight as
refiners in North Asia focus on heating fuel kerosene
production, limiting jet fuel supply. 
    
    - AIR PASSENGERS TO DOUBLE: The International Air Transport
Association (IATA) said on Tuesday it expected 7.8 billion
passengers to travel in 2036, nearly doubling the 4 billion air
travellers expected to fly this year. This is expected to boost
jet fuel demand. 
    - SOUTHEAST ASIA OIL DEMAND TO GROW: Southeast Asian demand
for oil will keep growing until at least 2040 as emerging
nations there rely on the fuel to transport their rapidly
growing populations, ship goods and make plastics, the
International Energy Agency said on Tuesday.
      Oil usage in the region will expand to about 6.6 million
barrels per day (bpd) by 2040 from 4.7 million bpd now, with the
number of road vehicles increasing by two-thirds to about 62
million, the agency said in a report. It did not make any
forecasts beyond 2040.
      Oil will continue to meet about 90 percent of
transport-related demand in Southeast Asia, especially for
trucks and ships, Keisuke Sadamori, the IEA's director of energy
markets and security, said at the Singapore International Energy
Week. [nL4N1MZ1FA]    
    - CHINA SHIPMENTS TO NORTH KOREA: Diesel shipments in
September remained slow after China National Petroleum Corp
(CNPC) suspended sales of gasoline and diesel at the end of June
to North Korea over concerns CNPC would not get paid for its
goods, according to data from the General Administration of
Customs. [nL4N1MZ2QP]
      The measures are still in place, sources familiar with the
matter say. China's diesel sales for the month were the smallest
since May.

SINGAPORE, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Asia's fuel oil crack rose to multi week highs on Monday, boosted
by expectations of tighter supplies by the end of the year partly because of limited arbitrage
bookings and lower output from key producers, including Russia and Venezuela, trade sources said. 
    In addition to higher freight rates making arbitrage flows into Asia less profitable, some of
the sources pointed to the reluctance of suppliers to import more cargoes as the current fiscal year
draws to an end. 
    Softer crude oil prices also helped lift fuel oil cracks. [O/R]

    CRACKS
    - The November 180-cst fuel oil crack to Dubai crude <FO180SGCKMc> narrowed to minus $1.91 a
barrel, its narrowest discount since Sept. 21. 
    - Similarly, the November 180-cst discount to Brent crude <FO180BRTCKMc1> narrowed by 26 cents a
barrel from Friday to minus $3.90 a barrel on Monday, its narrowest discount since Sept. 25. 
       
    RUSSIA DATA
    - Russian refinery runs were 5 percent down in September from the previous month and down 0.9
percent from the same time last year, official data showed. [nENNHAB0SR]
    - Russian fuel oil output stood at 3.519 million tonnes in September, down 8.3 percent from
August and 17.7 percent lower from September 2016, based on absolute figures, the data showed.
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - One cargo trade was reported in the Platts window totalling 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil.
    - Gunvor sold the 180-cst cargo to Vitol for prompt delivery on Nov. 7-11 at a premium of $1.25
a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    - The last time 180-cst fuel oil was traded in the window was on Oct. 12 when Vitol bought a
similar cargo from Reliance at $333.65 a tonne, or the equivalent of about 5 cents a tonne above
Singapore quotes. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - The UAE's Adnoc has sold five 85,000-90,000-tonne cargoes of straight-run fuel oil for loading
over November at premiums of about $23-$25 a tonne to Singapore 180-cst quotes, trade sources said. 
    - The cargoes were awarded to Lukoil, PetroChina, Mercuria, GS Caltex and SK Energy, however the
specific loading dates most companies were allocated could not be confirmed.
    - Buyers are to take delivery of the cargoes from Adnoc's refinery in Ruwais on Nov. 1-3, 8-10,
14-16, 20-22 and 25-27.  
    - Lukoil has chartered the Stavanger Bliss aframax vessel to load fuel oil on Nov. 1-3 from
Ruwais for discharge at an unspecified destination in Asia, according to one tanker report. 
    - Bahrain's Bapco sold 60,000-80,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4 percent sulphur
content to Aramco Trading (ATC) for Nov. 20-23 loading from Sitra at an unknown price level, sources
said. [nL4N1MY20F]
        
    OTHER NEWS
    - Struggling commodities trader Noble Group <NOBG.SI> agreed to sell its Americas-focused oil
liquids business to Vitol for about $580 million as part of a debt-cutting strategy, and warned of a
big loss for its third quarter. [nL4N1MX0X3]

LONDON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Diesel refining margins in
northwest Europe weakened on Monday as supplies in the region
were expected to rise in the coming weeks.

    * The 2 million barrel tanker Coshonour Lake was heading to
Europe with a cargo of diesel after leaving the port of
Singapore on Monday, according to Reuters shipping data and
traders.[nL8N1MY228]
    * The 245,000 tonne cargo is expected to arrive at the
Straits of Gibraltar on Nov. 26, according to Reuters data.
    * The vessel left the port of Tianjin in northern China in
late September and loaded part of its cargo in Taiwan before
heading to Singapore, where it is now almost fully loaded,
according to the data.
    * At least four diesel cargoes booked to go from the U.S.
Gulf Coast to Latin America have been diverted in recent days to
Europe, according to traders and shipping data.
    * At the same time, a number of cargoes have been booked in
recent days to deliver diesel from Europe to Latin America,
continuing a flow that grew in the wake of Hurricane Harvey.
    * China's diesel exports in September fell to the lowest
monthly level since January as domestic demand picked up ahead
of winter and refiners ran out of quotas.
    * Outbound diesel shipments <DL-CNEXP> in September were
down 26.1 percent from a year earlier at 1.18 million tonnes,
according to data released by the General Administration of
Customs on Monday.

SINGAPORE, Oct 25 (Reuters) - The Asian diesel cash differential slipped on Wednesday on the
back of more spot supply from Russia and India, and as China is expected to increase its exports
of the fuel with refiners applying for more export quotas, trade sources said. 
    
    - INDIA, RUSSIA OFFER DIESEL: India's Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPCL) has offered its
second 50ppm sulphur diesel cargo for Nov. 1 to Nov. 4 loading from Mumbai through a tender,
trade sources said. 
      Last week, BPCL sold a low sulphur diesel cargo through an export tender for the first
time as its refineries upgrade units and due to higher inventory of the fuel, sources have said.
      The state-owned refiner, which was once a net importer of diesel, is typically
well-balanced with its diesel stocks and rarely ships the fuel out of the country.
      Russia's Rosneft Oil Company has offered up to 200,000 tonnes of low viscosity marine
diesel oil for loading over November to December, in a tender that closes on Oct. 27 with bids
to remain valid until Nov. 6. [nL4N1N03IM]
    - CHINESE REFINERS APPLY FOR QUOTA: China National Offshore Oil Company, or CNOOC, has
joined the country's top two refiners to apply for additional quotas to export refined oil
products under a fifth batch of issues for 2017, three sources said. [nL4N1N03MH]
      CNOOC applied for about 1.2 million tonnes of fuel quotas, while Sinochem Corp applied for
a small portion of around 300,000 tonnes. 
      The quotas, valid until the end of 2017, are expected to be issued within days.
    - SOUTH AFRICA SEEKS: South Africa's PetroSA is seeking 11,000 tonnes of diesel for delivery
in late November to early December in a tender that closes on Oct. 26, trade sources said. 
    - KENYA BUYS: Kenya bought the bulk of its gasoil and jet fuel cargoes for December to
January delivery from Gapco, industry sources said. <MDIS/TENDA> 
    - JAPAN WEATHER: Japan will see average to warmer weather between November and January, the
official forecaster said on Wednesday, potentially reducing the need for heating fuel kerosene.
[nL4N1N02TU]
      Eastern Japan, including the most densely populated Tokyo, will have a 40 percent chance
of average temperatures for the period, the Japan Meteorological Agency said in its monthly
three-month forecast.

amid rising fuel oil inventories across key storage hubs over the past week as well as strength in
crude oil prices, trade sources said.

by comments from Saudi Arabia's crown prince backing the extension of OPEC-led output cuts. [O/R]

<STK-FO-ARA>

LONDON, Oct 24 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe declined on Tuesday as a recent Chinese buying
spree fizzled out.
    * A naphtha leakage at Statoil's <STL.OL> Mongstad refinery

unit remains shut and the company is investigating the causes of
the accident, a company spokeswoman said on Tuesday.[nL8N1MZ23P]
    * Over 800,000 tonnes of gasoline and blending components
were expected to be exported from Europe to Asia in October
after Chinese demand rose in September and October ahead of year
end.
    * Chinese buying for mixed aromatics has nevertheless
weakened in recent days, traders said.
    * At the same time, over 300,000 tonnes were booked over the
past week to go to the Middle East, according to shipping
reports, due to a busy refinery maintenance programme in the
region.

lull in export activity from Europe as supplies in the New York
Harbour have been tight.

SINGAPORE, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Additional spot cargoes from India could weigh on cash
differentials for Asian gasoil, trade sources said. 
    
    - INDIA OFFERS DIESEL: Indian Oil Corp has offered up to 80,000 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur
diesel for loading in November, in a tender that closes on Friday.
    The offer follows an earlier sell tender by another state-owned refiner Bharat Petroleum
Corp Ltd (BPCL) on Thursday.
    Export tenders from state-owned refiners are unusual but are likely prompted by recently
completed upgrading to meet changes in sulphur standards for domestic fuel, traders said.
    - CHINA DIESEL INVENTORY: China's diesel inventory at the end of September fell to the
lowest level since November while crude stocks were unchanged, the official Xinhua news agency
said on Friday, showing eased oversupply in fuel in the domestic market. [nL4N1N21XH]
    Diesel inventory fell 10 percent from August to 6.60 million tonnes, leading a decline in
overall refined products stocks. Kerosene stocks fell 4 percent to 2.18 million tonnes, the
lowest in 10 months, Xinhua data showed.
    Increasing industrial activities and mining projects boosted demand for diesel, Xinhua said.
    - ARA STOCKS SLIDE: Gasoil stocks held in independent storage tanks in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp storage and refining hub fell over 11 percent in the week to
Thursday to 2.24 million tonnes, due to exports, according to data from Dutch consultancy PJK
International. [nL8N1N18I4]

SINGAPORE, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Cash differentials for jet fuel and diesel rose on Monday
ahead of an expected rise in demand during winter for heating purposes and on lower exports from
China, industry sources said. 
    
    - CHINA DIESEL EXPORTS: China's diesel exports in September fell to the lowest monthly level
since January as domestic demand picked up ahead of winter and refiners ran out of quotas.
      Outbound diesel shipments <DL-CNEXP> in September were down 26.1 percent from a year
earlier at 1.18 million tonnes, according to data released by the General Administration of
Customs on Monday.
      Kerosene exports <JET-CNEXP> were down 6.7 percent at 1.01 million tonnes, taking the
total for the year so far to 9.08 million tonnes, up 0.2 percent, the data showed.
    - DIESEL SHIPMENTS TO EUROPE: The 2 million barrel tanker Coshonour Lake was heading to
Europe with a cargo of diesel after leaving Singapore on Monday, according to Reuters shipping
data and traders.
      The 245,000-tonne cargo is expected to arrive at the Straits of Gibraltar on Nov. 26,
Reuters data shows.
      The vessel left the port of Tianjin in northern China in late September and loaded part of
its cargo in Taiwan before heading to Singapore, where it is now almost fully loaded, the data
shows.    
    - BANGLADESH AND INDIA DIESEL DEAL: Bangladesh on Sunday signed a long-term sales and
purchase agreement with an Indian refiner to import gasoil to meet the country's energy demand,
officials said.
      The deal between Bangladesh Petroleum Corp (BPC) and Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) was
signed in the presence of India's External Affairs Minister Sushma Swaraj, who arrived in Dhaka
on Sunday on a two-day visit to discuss bilateral issues.
       The deal with NRL, which is majority owned by refiner Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPCL),
is the country's first long-term agreement with any Indian supplier.
       BPC will take up to 250,000 tonnes of gasoil each year from NRL for the first three years
of the deal. The fuel will be transported to BPC's northern fuel depot via a 131km (79 mile)
pipeline to be built by India.
       Import volumes will be increased in line with demand, a senior BPC official said, adding
that the deal would come into effect when the pipeline is built.

LONDON, Oct 25 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe rose sharply on Wednesday after a larger than
expected draw in U.S. inventories.

barrels last week, compared with analysts' expectations in a
Reuters poll for a drop of 17,000 barrels, Energy Information
Administration data showed on Wednesday. [EIA/S]
    * Cracks were also buoyed by a rise of around $1 in U.S.
renewable fuel credits hit in early trading on Wednesday,
traders said. 
    * Prices continue to surge in the wake of the U.S.
Environmental Protection Agency's decision to back off programme
reforms.[nL2N1N0142]
    * The rise in credit prices helped boost U.S. gasoline
margins <RBc1-CLc1> to a session high of $18.83 a barrel, a
nearly 6 percent jump, before falling back.

refinery remains partly shut following a naphtha leak on
Tuesday, and the timing of return to normal operations was
unclear, a spokeswoman said on Wednesday. [nL8N1N0341]

diffs see the largest rise of an average 46 cents.

diffs see the largest rise of an average 46 cents.

SINGAPORE, Jan 31 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil and jet fuel
differentials held firm on Tuesday as refinery maintenance in
Malaysia supported, traders said.    
    Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas) has shut a secondary
unit at its 270,000 barrels-per-day Melaka refinery in the
country's west coast for planned maintenance, industry sources
said. [nL4N1FL1JN]
    It shut a hydrotreater in mid-January for planned
maintenance and is expected to restart the unit in mid-February,
they added. 
    The company has probably lowered its operating rates as a
result, which will lower exports of gasoil, traders add. 
    Japan's monthly oil sales hit their lowest level in nearly
half a century in December, resuming a decades-long slowdown as
consumers in the world's third-biggest economy continue to seek
alternative sources of energy. [nL4N1FL11H]
    Nevertheless colder weather pushed up demand for kerosene
with sales last month up 4.4 percent on a year ago and up 45.6
percent from November, monthly oil data from the Ministry of
Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) showed on Tuesday. 
    As a result, jet fuel exports in December fell 15.9 percent
from November as refiners maximised yield to produce more
kerosene for heating. Gasoil exports, however, rose 13.2 percent
month-on-month, adding to the glut in Asia.
    Swiss oil trader Trafigura placed the lowest offers for a
tender by Pakistan State Oil Company (PSO) seeking 110,000
tonnes of gasoil and 20,000 tonnes of jet fuel for delivery in
March, traders said. [nL4N1FL1WM]
