SINGAPORE, Nov 1 (Reuters) - Differentials for ultra low sulphur diesel could weaken further
in the coming weeks as China may step up exports of the fuel after refiners won extra quotas and
as India steps up its exports, industry sources said. 
    
    - CHINA GETS MORE QUOTAS: China has approved five million tonnes of fuel export quotas for
the rest of 2017 in the fifth release this year after refiners asked for additional permits to
ship out surplus fuels, three traders with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.
[nB9N1MZ00B] 
    The quotas will bring the total of permits this year to about 42.5 million tonnes, roughly
12 percent more than the actual exports of gasoline, diesel and jet kerosene combined for last
year. 
    Of the total, CNPC won about 2.2 million tonnes, Sinopec 1.3 million tonnes, CNOOC 1.2
million tonnes and Sinochem 300,000 tonnes, the traders said.
    One trader said 60 percent of the quotas were allotted to diesel, the rest to gasoline and
jet kerosene.
         
    - INDIA TO EXPORT MORE DIESEL: India's state-owned refiners are exporting low-sulphur diesel
in a seldom seen flow of products as crude processing capacity returns amid a drop in demand due
to a new sales tax and as regional flooding cuts fuel use, industry sources told Reuters.
[nL4N1N62Q6] 
    The exports are expected to continue until year-end, likely weighing on low-sulphur cash
differentials, they added. 
    Demand growth has also been hit by a recently implemented goods and services tax (GST) that
has curbed production and fuel demand, a refining source said, declining to be named as he was
not authorised to speak with media. 
    Heavy floods in parts of India and monsoon rains, which reduce the need to use
diesel-powered irrigation pumps, also cut into demand, a second refining source said.    
    
    - EMARAT SEEKS JET FUEL: Emirates General Petroleum Corp (Emarat) is seeking 40,000 tonnes
of jet fuel for delivery in early December, traders said.     
    
    - BANGLADESH SEEKS GASOIL: Bangladesh Petroleum Corp (BPC) issued an international tender on
Wednesday to import refined oil products for the first half of 2018, officials said.
[nL4N1N72O3] 
    The state-owned company is seeking 780,000 to 980,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil,
100,000 tonnes of jet fuel, 120,000 to 160,000 tonnes of 180-cst high sulphur fuel oil and
30,000 tonnes of 95-octane gasoline. 
    The tender closes on Nov. 13 and is valid for 75 days to Jan. 26, 2018.           
    
    - SOUTH KOREA UPGRADES REFINING UNIT: The owner of top South Korean oil refiner SK Energy
said on Wednesday it would spend about 1 trillion won ($898 million) to build a new
desulphurisation unit by 2020, part of a push to churn out cleaner shipping fuels. [nL4N1N72UU]

    SINGAPORE, Dec 1 (Reuters) - Cash premiums and time spreads in Asia's fuel oil market
rallied on Thursday as supplies of on-specification cargoes continued to weigh as
suppliers were lured into lifting buyers' aggressive bids as they sought to replenish
supplies, traders said. 
    This followed a 1.53 million barrel (about 229,000 tonnes) drop in onshore
inventories of Singapore fuel oil in the week to Nov. 30 to a total of 22.32 million
barrels (3.33 million tonnes). [/SING1]

    A total of nine cash deals were reported in the Platts window on Thursday, the most
since Aug. 3, totalling 65,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil and another 120,000 tonnes of
380-cst fuel, sources said. 
    Total, Coastal and Chevron sold six 20,000 tonne cargoes of 380-cst fuel to
PetroChina at a premium of $3 a tonne across the window. 
    In addition to the higher cargo premiums seen in Thursday's deals, traders said the
boost in outright fuel oil prices following the rally in crude prices in the previous
session also contributed to the spike in deal activity. 
    
    RELATED NEWS:

Light crude for Asia to the lowest in at least two months to track weakness in Middle
East oil benchmark Dubai, trade sources said on Thursday. [nL4N1DW27P]
    - Trading volumes of Brent crude oil futures smashed records on Thursday after some
of the world's top producers on Wednesday struck a deal to cut output for the first time
since 2008, seeking to bolster prices stuck at historically modest levels. [nL4N1DW2GR]

SINGAPORE, Dec 1 (Reuters) - Winson Oil and Hin Leong turned gasoil sellers on Thursday for
the first time since they started a buying spree of the cargoes in mid-September, traders said.
    Winson Oil and Hin Leong sold 3.13 million barrels of gasoil out of a total 3.43 million
barrels traded in the Platts' market on close assessment process, they said.
    Winson Oil and Hin Leong bought over 16 million barrels of gasoil from mid-September to late
November, keeping differentials for the benchmark 500ppm sulphur gasoil firm, they added. 
    There have been few vessel movements of gasoil from these companies out of Asia, suggesting
that most of the cargoes are in storage, a shipbroker said. 
    Hin Leong and Winson Oil officials were not immediately available for comment.    
    Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks jumped 11 percent to a 10-week high of 14.897
million barrels in the week to Nov. 30, data from International Enterprise showed. <O/SING1> 
    Diesel imports from Saudi Arabia and China into Singapore increased from the week before
while exports of the fuel to Indonesia, Australia, Malaysia and Myanmar fell, contributing to
the build in stocks, the data showed.
    India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) sold 40,000 tonnes of jet fuel for
Jan. 1-3 loading to Emirates National Oil Company (ENOC) at a discount of $1.20 a barrel to
Singapore quotes, traders said.
    Thailand's PTT and Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp have yet to finalise their term deals
for gasoil while Taiwan's CPC Corp is yet to award a spot tender to sell gasoil for January,
traders said.
    India's Essar Oil sold a gasoil and jet fuel cargo for late December loading, though details
on price and buyers could not immediately be confirmed. 
    Arbitrage economics to ship diesel and jet fuel from east to west are looking more
favourable, traders said.

SINGAPORE, Dec 6 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil differentials
edged higher on Tuesday on firm demand from India and Europe,
while robust trade also boosted liquidity in Singapore, trade
sources said.     
    India's diesel demand has likely firmed after the monsoon
season, with exports expected to reduce over the next few
months, traders said.
    India's MRPL did not issue a sell tender for diesel, likely
reflecting this rise in domestic demand, they added.
    Winson Oil and Hin Leong continued their selling spree of
gasoil cargoes in Singapore, selling nine out of ten cargoes
during Platts' pricing process, they said.
    Some spot demand from Indonesia appeared, with Pertamina
seeking cargoes for December, but the volumes were too small to
boost margins, one of them said.
    Pertamina cancelled its previous tender seeking gasoil for
December delivery, an industry source said. The reason for the
cancellation was not immediately clear. 
    Supply of diesel in Asia was also ample with Taiwan's
Formosa Petrochemical Corp offering 720,000 barrels of the fuel
for January.
    Arbitrage economics to ship diesel and jet fuel from Asia to
the west was looking more profitable and could boost flow
between the regions, traders said.     
    West African countries such as Nigeria, Ghana, Ivory Coast,
Benin and Togo are moving towards 50ppm sulphur diesel from the
current 0.3 percent sulphur gasoil.
    This will likely reduce the demand for high sulphur gasoil
from Asia, traders said.
    Trafigura sometimes ships gasoil from Korea to West Africa,
they added.

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, Dec 2 (Reuters) - The discount for Asia's benchmark 180-cst fuel oil to
Dubai crude oil was at its widest in five weeks on Friday partly on the back of stronger
crude prices after this week's agreement by OPEC to reduce a global supply overhang.
    Singapore's Dec. 180-cst fuel oil discount to Dubai crude <FO180SGCKMc1> widened by
$1.25 a barrel to minus $3.27 cents a barrel, its widest discount since Oct. 24.
    Oil prices steadied at around $53.50 a barrel on Friday after the biggest weekly rally
since 2009 following OPEC's decision this week to cut crude output in order to rein in a
global glut. [nL4N1DX154] [nL8N1DW115]
    The refining margin was also weighed down by selling pressure in the last two sessions
from at least one major producer of the industrial fuel, two industry sources said. 
   The widening discount for the refining margin marks a shift from weeks of narrower
discounts which were related to supply issues in major producers like Russia and Venezuela
as well as strong demand. [nL4N1DU3HD]
    In other products, traders said premiums of the near-dated time spreads for 380-cst
fuel oil on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) were slightly lower on Friday following
sharp gains in the previous session. 
    The ICE traded 380-cst Jan/Feb time spreads in particular saw an uptick in trading
volumes, trading about 750,000 tonnes in contracts on Friday by 1700 Singapore time (0900
GMT) but were trading only 15 cents a tonne lower at $1.85 a tonne. 
    In the physical market, activity also picked up, with a total of 60,000 tonnes of the
180-cst fuel and another 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst grade changing hands in the Platts
window as suppliers sought to lock in profits following the spike in flat prices following
the rally in crude.
                
    RELATED NEWS:
    - Russian President Vladmir Putin played a crucial role in helping OPEC rivals Iran
and Saudi Arabia set aside differences to forge the cartel's first deal with non-OPEC
Russia in 15 years. [nL8N1DW1IS]
    -  The oil price rally sparked by an OPEC-Russia deal to cut output is likely to be
short-lived, say traders in Asia, because the agreement may only draw more supplies from
storage tanks and more crude shipments from the United States. [nL4N1DW2WQ]

SINGAPORE, Dec 5 (Reuters) - Spot demand from Vietnam and
Egypt boosted differentials for the benchmark 500ppm sulphur
gasoil grade on Monday, traders said.
    Vietnam's top fuel importer Petrolimex sought 105,000 tonnes
of gasoil for delivery in January while Egyptian General
Petroleum Corp (EGPC) sought cargoes for December, they said.   
 
    Taiwan's CPC Corp sold 250,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for January loading at parity to Singapore quotes and
250,000 barrels of 0.25 percent sulphur gasoil at a discount of
$1 a barrel to Singapore quotes, industry sources said.
    The buyers of the cargoes could not immediately be
confirmed. 
    India's Essar Oil likely sold up to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm
sulphur gasoil for Dec. 27 to 31 loading at a premium of 75
cents a barrel to Middle East quotes, traders said, though this
could not immediately be confirmed. 
    South Korea's GS Caltex finalised its 2017 gasoil and jet
fuel term contracts with at least one buyer, traders said.
[nL4N1E032Q]
    It set the 500ppm sulphur gasoil term price for next year at
a discount of 30 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes, up from
this year's minus 60 to 70 cents a barrel, they said.
    For 10ppm sulphur diesel, the refiner set the premium at
about 40 to 45 cents a barrel, down from 2016's 50 cent premium,
they said.
    GS Caltex set the term price for its 2017 jet fuel contract
at a discount of 20 cents a barrel, up from this year's minus 30
cents a barrel, they said.
    Oil pricing agency Platts plans to lower the sulphur content
of its benchmark gasoil assessment in Singapore and the Middle
East from January 2018, in line with a global shift towards
cleaner fuels, the company said. [nL4N1E03A8]

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, Dec 6 (Reuters) - Asia's fuel oil market complex firmed on Tuesday lifted
by a persistent inflow of off-specification arbitrage cargoes, prolonging a supply
shortage that has been exacerbated by robust regional demand for the industrial fuel,
industry sources said. 
    Near term fuel oil refining margins, East-West arbitrage spreads and inter-month
time spreads were bid up on Tuesday as more supplies of off-specification arbitrage
cargoes arrived into Singapore over the past week, trading sources said. 
    Traders said Western arbitrage arrivals into Singapore have consisted of several
cargoes of high-viscosity and high-density fuel oil that would need to be blended into
specific end-user requirements before being delivered to their customers. 
    Traders said colder weather in Northern Asia was stoking demand for power generation
while regional demand for bunker fuels was also robust. 
    Bunker fuel premiums in China, for example, were on the rise recently amid a
tightening supply of marine grade fuel oil supplies. 
    Sources said the fuel oil complex was also supported by continued strength in the
crude oil market following the previous week's OPEC-Russia deal to reduce a global
overhang in supplies.
    In the physical markets, Vitol and Lukoil each supplied Mercuria with a 20,000 tonne
cargo of the 180-cst fuel oil in the Platts window at $323 a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    On Monday, Mercuria bought 60,000 tonnes of the 180-cst fuel for between $316-$317 a
tonne. 
    No cash deals for the 380-cst fuel oil were reported in the Platts window on Tuesday
amid fewer suppliers offers. 

    RELATED NEWS:
    - OPEC's oil output set another record high in November before a deal to cut
production, a Reuters survey found on Monday, lifted by higher Iraqi exports and extra
barrels from two nations exempted from cutting supply - Nigeria and Libya. [nL5N1E03QP]
    - Saudi Aramco has cut the January price for its Arab Light crude for Asian
customers to the lowest in four months as it holds to a strategy of preserving market
share in the world's fastest-growing demand centre. [nENNGBP0RZ]

previous session, amid higher crude prices, broker sources said. [O/R]

tightening fuel oil supplies into 2018 amid shrinking output and fewer arbitrage bookings into Asia,
as well as firm demand for the industrial fuel. [nL4N1N73WK]

months. <FOVISSGDFMc1> <FO180-SIN-DIF>

premiums and time spreads, sources said. <FO380-SIN-DIF>

SINGAPORE, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Cash premiums for cargoes of Asia's mainstay 380-cst
high-sulphur fuel oil slipped on Thursday for a fourth straight session to a three-week low. 
    Falling crude oil prices kept buyers at bay in anticipation of lower prices, trade sources
said. 
    The lower crude oil prices, however, failed to boost the front-month 380-cst barge fuel oil
crack, which was at minus $10.09 a barrel on Thursday, down from Wednesday's settlement of minus
$10.02 a barrel, Refinitiv data showed. <HFOFARAACMc2>
    Oil prices slumped to two-week lows as global stock markets fell, with investor sentiment
made more bearish by an industry report showing U.S. crude inventories rising more than
expected. [O/R]
    Meanwhile, Singapore fuel oil inventories climbed to a near three-month high in the week to
Oct. 10, as net imports of the fuel climbed for a fourth straight week, official data released
late on Thursday showed. [nL4N1WR3CY]
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Onshore fuel oil inventories climbed 6 percent, or 1.089 million barrels (about 163,000
tonnes), to 18.653 million barrels, or 2.784 million tonnes, data from International Enterprise
(IE) Singapore showed. [O/SING1]
    - Net fuel oil imports were at a four-week high of 1.216 million tonnes, up 5 percent from
the week before and above the 2018 average net import volume of 794,000 tonnes per week.
    - The increase in inventories also comes as Maersk Oil Trading last week was said to have
leased 120,000 cubic meters of storage space at Tankstore, possibly contributing to the
inventory increase as it filled its new tanks, trade sources said. [nL4N1WO21N]
    - This week's onshore fuel oil inventories were 21 percent lower than a year ago.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Hong Kong topped the week ended Oct. 10 at 69,000
tonnes, followed by South Korea at 48,000 tonnes and China at 48,000 tonnes.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Malaysia at 458,000 tonnes,
followed by Iraq at 335,000 tonnes, Russia at 291,000 tonnes and Kuwait at 92,000 tonnes.
    - Singapore fuel oil imports from Kuwait have been absent for most of the year but in the
week to Oct. 10 were at their highest since late January.
    - In the United States, fuel oil inventories <RFO-STK-T-EIA> slipped 3 percent to a two-week
low of 27.999 million barrels, about 4.18 million tonnes, in the week to Sept. 28, data from the
Energy Information Administration showed on Wednesday. [EIA/D]

in more than five weeks on Thursday amid weaker crude prices, while cash premiums for the
industrial fuel climbed as onshore middle-distillate inventories in Singapore fell to a
three-week low.

$17.29 a barrel over Dubai crude during Asian trading hours, the highest level since early
September. Cracks were at $16.75 on Wednesday.

Singapore quotes, from 67 cents a day earlier.

Singapore quotes, from 9 cents on Wednesday.

up from $16.27 on Wednesday.

the week to Oct. 10, International Enterprise (IE) data showed. [O/SING1]

million barrels a week, compared with a weekly average of about 12 million barrels in 2017,
Reuters calculations showed.

barrelsagainst expectations for a 2 million barrel drop, the API data showed. [API/S]

SINGAPORE, Dec 26 (Reuters) - Strong buying interest for a jet fuel cargo in the Singapore
trading window on Tuesday helped reduce Asia's jet fuel cash differential to its narrowest since
Dec. 1, trade sources said. 
    This came after Hin Leong bought 150,000 barrels of aviation fuel from Total at a premium of 25
cents a barrel to Singapore quotes. 
    The last time jet fuel cargoes traded in the window was on Dec. 18 when two 100,000 barrel
cargoes exchanged hands, one for a discount of 25 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes, and another
for a 20 cent per barrel discount. 
    
    CHINA FLOWS
    - China exported 2.026 million tonnes of diesel in November, up 38 percent from a year ago,
customs data from China's General Administration of Customs showed on Tuesday. [O/CHINA2]
    - For the first 11 months of the year, China exported a total of 15.251 million tonnes of
diesel, 12 percent higher from the same time last year, the data showed.

SINGAPORE, July 4 (Reuters) - India's diesel imports have intensified with a state-owned
refiner entering the spot market on Tuesday to seek its seventh cargo of the fuel for July,
trade sources said. But imports could slow as monsoon season starts in India, they added. 
    
  - INDIA SEEKS MORE: India's Hindustan Petroleum Corp (HPCL) is seeking 60,000 tonnes of 40ppm
sulphur gasoil for delivery into Vizag over July 20-25 in a tender that closes on July 5. 
    This is the state-owned company's seventh cargo requirement for July, though it was not
clear if all previous tenders have been awarded. 
    India's HPCL-Mittal Energy Ltd (HMEL) was expected to start up its 230,000 barrels per day
Bathinda refinery in northern Punjab after it shut for planned maintenance in late April, but
the refinery is still not back in operation, an industry source said, though this could not
immediately be confirmed. 
  - MONSOON COULD CURB: India's diesel demand has been strong despite the start of monsoon
season due to several power outages which has boosted diesel demand in back-up power generators,
an industry source said. 
    It is still early days in India's monsoon season. Once rains intensify, demand for the fuel
in the agriculture sector could slow, the source added. 
  - NEW LOAD POINT: Oil pricing agency S&P Global Platts said on Tuesday it will include
Singapore's Jurong Aromatics Corp as a loading point in its pricing process known as Market on
Close for gasoil and jet fuel from Aug. 1.
    Sellers in the MOC process will be able to nominate JAC as a loading point for cargoes
traded on a FOB Straits basis, it said, following a review last month. [nL3N1JV37I] [nL3N1J221Y]
  - MYANMAR DEMAND: Myanmar's refined fuel consumption growth is set to outperform the rest of
Asia from 2017 to 2026 due to factors including strong economic growth, a rapid rise in car
ownership and a surge in aviation traffic, BMI Research said in a note.
    Already the sixth-largest net fuel importer in Asia, Myanmar's imports are expected to grow
to over 345,000 barrels per day (bpd) by 2026 from an estimated 212,000 bpd in 2017, it added.
[nL3N1JV20B]

SINGAPORE, July 5 (Reuters) - Asian diesel margin on Wednesday climbed to its highest in
two-and-a-half months, bolstered by firm demand from India, which is attracting cargoes to be
shipped from Europe in an unusual move, traders said. 
    
    - BATHINDA REFINERY DELAYS RESTART: India's HPCL-Mittal Energy Ltd (HMEL), part-owned by
steel tycoon LN Mittal, has delayed the full-scale start-up of its Bathinda oil refinery in
northern state of Punjab to end-July, four sources familiar with the matter said. [nL3N1JW21V]
     The refinery was shut on April 30 for about 45 days to raise capacity by about 28 percent
to 230,000 barrels per day. The start-up was first delayed to late June. 
     It may only be fully operational in late July, the sources said.
     HPCL has either bought or is seeking 455,000 tonnes of diesel for July delivery and is
expected to buy another 130,000 tonnes of the fuel in the next two or three weeks, one of the
sources added.
     The cargoes were bought from both oil majors and traders, industry sources said. 
     HPCL bought 250,000 tonnes of diesel for May and June and was largely absent from the spot
market before that.
   - UNUSUAL REVERSE ARBITRAGE: Oil traders are shipping diesel out of Europe to Asia and the
Middle East where strong demand and tighter supplies have boosted prices, in a rare arbitrage
that reverses traditional routes. [nL8N1JW1M3]
     At least three 90,000 tonne diesel cargoes were booked in recent days out of northwest
Europe options to go to Singapore and the Middle East, shipping data showed.
   - PAKISTAN SKIPS GASOIL AND JET FUEL IMPORTS FOR SEPTEMBER: Pakistan State Oil has a high
inventory of gasoil and jet fuel, and does not need to import the fuels for September as of now,
a source close to the matter said. [nL3N1JW2HT] 
      The company has resumed jet fuel shipments to Afghanistan, after they were halted in June
amid a border dispute, the source said.
   - NEW ASSESSMENTS: Oil price agency S&P Global Platts, a unit of S&P Global Inc, will launch
new temporary assessments for 10ppm sulphur gasoil derivatives on Aug. 1, it says in a
subscriber note
    - TAIWAN OFFERS GASOIL: Taiwan's CPC Corp has offered 250,000 barrels of 0.25 percent or
500ppm sulphur gasoil for loading from Kaohsiung in August and 10,000 tonnes of light cycle oil
for loading over July 10 to 31.
     Taiwan's overall gasoil exports in the third quarter, however, are expected to be lower
than last year due to a maintenance in top exporter Formosa's Mailiao plant. [nL3N1JP3ML]

SINGAPORE, Dec 22 (Reuters) - Cracks and time spreads of Asia's high-sulphur fuel oil fell on
Friday as expectations of ample near-term supplies and weaker demand weighed on sentiment, trade
sources said.
    Premiums of the front-month 380-cst fuel oil time spread fell to about 25 cents a tonne, its
lowest level in more than three months. <FO380SGSDMc1>

its discount to minus $6.04 a barrel on Friday, from minus $5.77 a barrel in the previous session.
<FO180BRTCKMc1>

    - Fuel oil stocks in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) oil hub slipped 8 percent, or 98,000
tonnes, from the previous week to a total of 1.268 million tonnes in the week ended Dec. 21, data
from Dutch consultancy PJK International showed. [ARA/]
    - Compared with the same time last year, ARA fuel oil inventories are 80 percent higher and are
above the five-year average of 888,000 tonnes for this time of the year. <STK-FO-ARA>
    - Outgoing fuel oil cargoes from the ARA hub over the past week were heading to West Africa,
while incoming cargoes originated from Estonia, France Poland, Russia and the United Kingdom, PJK

3-1/2 month high hit in the previous session on concerns over increasing supplies in the first
quarter of next year. <GOSGCKMc1> 
    China's increased allowances for 2018 oil product exports also helped cap trader sentiment as
some participants expected this would pressure overall refining margins in the new year.
[nL4N1OS2A5]
    Meanwhile, increased demand for spot jet fuel cargoes helped lift jet cash premiums to a near
two-year high. <JET-SIN-DIF>

showed. [ARA/]

week. <STK-GO-ARA>
    - Gasoil stocks rose on slower exports to inland locations because of the Christmas holidays,
PJK's Patrick Kulsen said.
    - Jet fuel stocks stood at 687,000 tonnes in the week to Dec. 28, compared with 665,000 tonnes
in the previous week, the data showed. <STK-JET-ARA>
    - In Singapore, onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks slid to a three-year low of 7.911 million
barrels in the week to Dec. 27, down 7.9 percent from the previous week, the latest data from
International Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed. [O/SING1]
    - The last time Singapore middle distillates stocks were lower was in the week to Dec. 17 in
2014, when they stood at 7.764 million barrels.

SINGAPORE, July 3 (Reuters) - Spot requirements by India state-owned refiners continued to
support Asian gasoil margin, which slipped on Monday but stayed above $11 a barrel, trade
sources said. 
    
    - INDIA SEEKS: India's Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd (HPCL) is seeking 60,000 tonnes of 40ppm
sulphur diesel for loading between July 8 and July 12 from Vizag in a tender that closes on July
3, and is valid until July 4, traders said. 
    - CHINA'S NEW DIESEL SPECS: China's Sinopec said on Monday the company has upgraded 11
refineries in North China to meet the stricter standards for fuel.

diesel and gasoline which meet the national six fuel standards, starting September, it said.
[nL3N1JU3GW]

6.76 million kilolitres (462,000 barrels per day) of crude oil in July-September for the
domestic market, down 3 percent from a year ago. [nL3N1JU1Q2]
    The refining would be done at Showa Shell's four group refineries, which have a total
capacity of 588,000 bpd. 
    - AFRICA BUYS: Kenya's oil importers bought nearly 430,000 tonnes of gasoil and jet fuel for
delivery in August from Vivo Energy, Galana Oil, Hess, KenolKobil and Gapco at premiums ranging
from $5.06 a tonne to $21.91 a tonne above Middle East quotes, traders said. <MDIS/TENDA>
    Tanzania's oil importers are set to buy over 352,000 tonnes of oil products for delivery in
August from Sahara Energy, Addax Energy and Vitol Bahrain, industry sources said. [nL3N1JU3BG]
    The country's Petroleum Bulk Procurement Agency is set to buy 112,152 tonnes of gasoline,
214,700 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur gasoil and 26,080 tonnes of jet fuel and kerosene, they said.

of Primorsk is expected to fall by 6.5 percent on a daily basis to 1.120 million tonnes in July
from 1.155 million tonnes planned for June, trading sources familiar with the loading schedule
said on Monday. [nL8N1JN1CJ]

    SINGAPORE, July 5 (Reuters) - Asia's 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums <FO380-SIN-DIF>
slipped to a near 1-month low on Wednesday amid weaker buying interest, but further falls
are seen limited over the near term by bullish supply and demand fundamentals, two traders
said. 
    Following nearly two weeks of uninterrupted gains, sources also said falling crude
prices on Wednesday may have kept some traders on the sidelines ahead of EIA data released
later in the day. [nL3N1JW1HU]
    
    WINDOW TRADES
    - Two cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, including one 20,000 tonne cargo
of 180-cst fuel and another 20,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Click on [O/AS] for more details.
    
    LOWER ARBS
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for June closed at a 4-month high of around 6.8
million tonnes mainly on spillovers from May and despite lower Middle East and intra-Asia
supplies, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed. [nPGEmXWxla]
    - July arrivals are expected to be lower, with Western arrivals closing at a 12-month
low of just over 3 million tonnes, while Middle East inflows are currently at below-average
levels of just over 800,000 tonnes so far, the assessments showed. 
    - Trader sources currently estimate some 3 to 4 million tonnes of fuel oil will arrive
into Singapore in July and August each. 
           
    TENDERS
    - South Korea's EWP is seeking up to 20,000 tonnes of HSFO with a 540-cst maximum
viscosity and 2.5 percent sulphur content for delivery at Ulsan port between July 21-25 in a
tender closing July 11. 
    - EWP last issued a tender seeking fuel oil in January for 50,000 tonnes of the same
quality fuel for delivery over Feb. 12-16. [nL4N1FG2BH]
    - South Korean utilities typically import several fuel oil cargoes every month for power
generation but have turned to cheaper alternatives like LNG and coal since the start of the
year in the wake of rising oil prices, industry sources said. 
    - Pakistan's PSO is seeking up to 705,000 tonnes of fuel oil for delivery in September
in a tender closing on July 24 and valid until Aug. 7. 
    - PSO's tender includes 10 cargoes of 65,000 tonnes each of 180-cst HSFO on an FOB basis
along with 55,000 tonnes of LSFO on a C&F basis. [nL3N1JW2HT]
    
    FUJAIRAH INVENTORIES
    - In the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil
inventories were nearly unchanged in the week to July 3 at 12.127 million barrels, data via
S&P Global Platts showed. [nL3N1JW3DB]
    - Last week, Fujairah's fuel oil inventories rose to their second highest since stocks
reporting began in mid-January, almost 200,000 barrels below the record 12.328 million
barrels seen in the week to March 27.
        
    NEW MOC MEMBERS
    - S&P Global Platts on Wednesday added World Fuel Services (Singapore) Pte Ltd and Seven
Seas Oil Trading Pte Ltd to its Asia Market On Close (MOC) assessment process for Singapore

    - This follows the inclusion of Fratelli Cosulich Bunkers (S) Pte Ltd in the MOC process
for physical bunkers announced on June 18.

SINGAPORE, Dec 26 (Reuters) - Tumbling crude oil prices
helped the front-month fuel oil crack narrow its discount to
Brent crude on Wednesday but overall trade liquidity remains
thin amid the year-end holidays, trade sources said.
    The January 380-cst barge crack against Brent crude was
trading at about minus $6.40 a barrel on Wednesday, from about
minus $6.70 a barrel in the previous trading session, brokers
said.
    The near dated 380-cst time spreads also firmed on
Wednesday.
    The Jan/Feb 380-cst time spread was trading at about $4.50 a
tonne from about $3.75 a tonne in the previous session, the
brokers said. Similarly the Feb/March 380-cst time spread rose
to $2.75 a tonne on Wednesday from $2.25 a tonne previously. 
    The front-month time-spread the previous Wednesday was at
its lowest level since April at $1.50 per tonne, according to
Refinitiv data in Eikon. <FO380SGSDMc1>
    Oil prices were mixed on Wednesday as the U.S. benchmark
rebounded from steep losses in the previous session, even though
concern over the health of the global economy continued to
overshadow the market. [O/R]
    Brent crude oil futures <LCOc1> were down 0.57 percent, at
$50.18 a barrel at 0748 GMT, and earlier fell to the lowest
since July 2017. They skidded 6.2 percent in the previous
session to $50.47 a barrel.
        
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - One cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading
window 20,000 tonnes of 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO).
    - Mercuria bought the cargo from Shell at a $4 per tonne
premium to Singapore quotes. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - The UAE's ADNOC has offered up to three 90,000-tonne
cargoes of straight-run fuel oil (SRFO) from Ruwais loading over
Jan. 7-9, Jan. 11-13 and Jan. 15-17 in a tender closing on Dec.
27.
    - In November, industry sources said ADNOC was expected to
reduce exports of SRFO from 2019 with completion of repairs to
the 127,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) residue fluid catalytic
cracker (RFCC) at its Ruwais refinery that was damaged in
January 2017. [nL4N1XN2RD]
    - In 2017, ADNOC exported about four to five cargoes of
90,000 tonnes of SRFO from Ruwais on a monthly basis but in 2018
it sold the cargoes through long-term supply agreements from
January through to December.
    - India's MRPL has sold an unusual 40,000-tonne low sulphur
fuel oil cargo with a maximum 1 percent sulphur content loading
from New Mangalore over Jan. 18-20 to Vitol at an unknown
premium to Singapore 380-cst quotes on an FOB basis. 
    - Taiwan's Formosa has offered a 40,000 tonne cargo of
380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 3.5 percent sulphur content
loading on Jan. 9-11 from Mailiao in a tender closing on Dec. 27
with same day validity. 
    - This comes as Formosa sold a similar 380-cst fuel oil
cargo to P66 for Dec. 28-30 loading at a discount of about $10
per tonne to Singapore 180-cst quotes on an FOB basis. 
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fuel oil inventories at the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone
(FOIZ) fell 4.4 percent, or 283,000 barrels (about 42,000
tonnes), to a three-week low of 6.191 million barrels (924,000
tonnes) in the week ended Dec. 24, data from S&P Global Platts
showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - Fujairah fuel oil inventories are now 40 percent lower
from the same time last year.
    - Fujairah's fuel oil stocks averaged 7.93 million barrels
(1.184 million tonnes) in 2018 compared with 9.974 million
barrels (1.489 million tonnes) in the year before, Reuters
calculations showed.
        
    RUSSIA EXPORTS 
    - Russian fuel oil exports <FO-RU-EXP> in November totalled
2.659 million tonnes, up by 23 percent from the previous month
but were 16 percent lower from year-ago levels, according to the
latest data from the Energy Ministry. [nL8N1YT1PB]
    - Russian fuel oil exports were last higher in July when
2.865 million tonnes were exported, the data showed. 
    - This came as Russian fuel oil output <FO-RU-OUT> in
November surged to a 10-month high of 4.283 million tonnes. 
    
    CHINA IMPORTS
    - China has set its 2019 fuel oil import quota for non-state
companies at 16.2 million tonnes, unchanged from 2018 and 2017,
the country's Ministry of Commerce said on its website on
Tuesday. [nB9N1YN013]
    - Companies who have ownership or right of berth, or use
special rail lines to deliver at least 10,000 tonnes of refined
oil products, and store more than 50,000 cubic meters of refined
oil products, will be able to apply for the quota.

northwest Europe recovered slightly on Wednesday, but traders
predicted renewed pressures from a large quantity of imports
heading into a market that is already saturated.
    There were around 500,000 tonnes of diesel on vessels
floating around Europe as storage is at close to capacity and
about 1.5 to 2 million tonnes of product already set to arrive

gasoil for heating.

LONDON, Jan 28 (Reuters) - Distillate margins held their
ground versus crude oil on Thursday despite swelling stocks in
Europe and warm weather that was impinging on consumption. 
    Crude futures spiked by more than 3 percent during the day's
trading on possible cooperation between Russia and OPEC to cut
oil production. But if the higher oil prices proved sustainable,
they could put more pressure on refined product margins. [O/R]
    There were few fundamental reasons for strength in the
distillates pool. Exports from Russia's port of Primorsk edged
lower for February, to 1.268 million tonnes, compared with 1.39
million tonnes in January. [ID:nL8N15C4A1]
    The drop in U.S. stockpiles of diesel and heating oil, which
according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration fell by
4.1 million barrels last week, also provided support. [EIA/S].
    But stocks overall in Europe are full to the brim, with ARA
tanks showing little space and industry consultants PJK
International citing full tanks inland along the Rhine as well.
[PJK/]
    With already half a million tonnes of diesel parked off
Europe's ports, and another 1.5 to 2 million tonnes en route
from the United States and the east, the margins are expected to
come under intense pressure later in the month, barring
larger-than-expected refinery maintenance or a significant and
sustained drop in temperatures. [ID:nL3N15B33C]

LONDON, Jan 28 (Reuters) - Forties crude oil differentials
fell on Thursday despite a new supertanker fixture, for loading
next month, appearing on the shipping lists.
    There was only one Forties deal reported in the daily
trading window, which was done at the steepest discount to dated
Brent in two weeks.
    Shell was the lone trader to submit offers and both were
made below the previous day's spot price, traders said.
    Meanwhile Shell has chartered the VLCC Hakata to load at
Hound Point in mid-February for South Korea.
    This is the first fixture for a cargo loading in February,
according to Reuters data, which ordinarily would offer a degree
of support to differentials.
    So far in January, Forties diffs have fallen by $1.65 a
barrel from the end of December, marking their steepest
one-month drop since 2000, based on Reuters data.
    This is largely a function of differentials having been
inflated in December because of temporary constraints on supply
along the Forties Pipeline System.
    Looking further out, Hound Point will not load any Forties
on supertankers in early March because of maintenance work on
Jetty 1, operator BP <BP.L> said on Tuesday. [nL8N15A46J]

discount of 75 cents to dated Brent.

cargoes of Forties, one loading Feb 10-12 at a discount of 65
cents to dated Brent, and a second for loading Feb 16-18 at a
discount of 50 cents.
    * The average of the three prices is below the average of a
discount of 45 cents seen on Wednesday. No other deals, bids or
offers were reported for any of the BFOE grades.

LONDON, Jan 28 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe rose on Thursday to above $13 a barrel,
supported by a rally in U.S. gasoline futures and continued
overseas demand. 
    Exports from the region continued to support the market,
with several tankers booked in recent days to ship mixed
aromatics to China, according to shipping data. 
    Exports to West Africa have nevertheless weakened, leading
to higher availability of supplies in the region.
    U.S. rbob futures gained more than 4 percent after Motiva
Enterprises shut the naphtha process complex at the company's
603,000 barrel per day (bpd) Port Arthur, Texas, refinery on
Wednesday after a hydrotreater malfunction, sources familiar
with plant operations said on Thursday. [nL2N15C1D9]
    ARA gasoline stocks jumped by 21 percent this week to a near
two-year high, Dutch consultants PJK International said. The
stocks rose to more than 1 million tonnes, their highest level
since March 2014, as traders looked to take advantage of strong
export demand and contango in the market. [ARA/]
    Refineries have been trying to maximize gasoline and naphtha
output in recent weeks in order to benefit from strong cracks
while trying to limit diesel and jet fuel output as the middle
distillates market suffers from a huge oversupply.

SINGAPORE, Jan 28 (Reuters) - Asian fuel oil remained relatively stable on Thursday trading,
following two days of weakening swap and spot differentials amid increasing onshore inventories of
Singapore fuel oil. 
    Spot differentials of fuel oil remained steady with the discount on 180cst fuel oil narrowing by
39 cents to $1.32 per tonne to Singapore quotes, while the discount on 380cst widened slightly by 15
cents to $1.08 per tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    Trading activity in front-month time spreads of 380cst fuel oil was particularly active, traders
said, but prices remained unchanged from yesterday's close at a discount of $2.25 per tonne to
Singapore quotes.
    In contrast, front-month time spreads of 180cst fuel oil widened further by 50 cents to a discount
of $3.50 per tonne to Singapore quotes.
    Until this week, the Singapore fuel oil market was supported by healthy bunker demand and
generally tight supplies in December and January.
    This week's weaker market was expected as supplies were replenished, traders said.
    Weekly onshore stocks of Singapore fuel oil inventories rose 7 percent for the week to Jan. 27 to
a total of 22.295 million barrels, according to data from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore
released on Thursday. [nL3N15C31W]
    This is the first recorded rise of Singapore fuel oil stocks in 7 weeks, demonstrating the
accumulation of delayed arrivals of Western arbitrage cargos due to adverse weather conditions in the
Caribbean and the Black Sea throughout December.

its widest discount since July 2016 on Thursday, as suppliers in the Singapore trading window lured
buyers with lower price levels.

discount of $1.20 per tonne in the previous session. <FO380-SIN-DIF>

landed inventories, also weighed on ex-wharf and delivered differentials trade sources said. 
    380-cst delivered fuel oil deals were heard to have concluded at $372.50 and $374 per tonne,
trade sources said.

tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil, the highest volume since March 13.

    - Hin Leong supplied three of the cargoes, each at $369 per tonne, and Glencore sold one at $370
per tonne.

Thursday turned into a seller of the fuel for the first time since Nov. 10.

traders expect demand to pick up due to the upcoming Lunar New Year in February.

SINGAPORE, Nov 15 (Reuters) - Asian refining margins for 10ppm gasoil rose to a fresh
four-year peak on Thursday, boosted by the current weakness in crude prices, while middle
distillate inventories in Singapore declined  for the first time in three weeks.
    Refining margins for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10SGCKMc1> rose to $18.90 a barrel
over Dubai crude during Asian trading hours, their strongest since November 2014. The margins
were at $18.66 a barrel on Tuesday.
    The current weakness in crude oil prices is helping gasoil margins at the moment, when
overall demand also seems to be quite steady, a Singapore-based trader said.
    India, which is one of the key players in the region, posted diesel sales of 6.99 million
tonnes in October, a rise of 6.7 percent compared to the same period last year, and about 16
percent higher than in September, government data showed on Tuesday. [nL4N1XO48W]
    Domestic consumption patterns in India typically impact its monthly export volumes, which in
turn affects the overall supply in the region.
    Cash premiums for 10ppm gasoil <GO10-SIN-DIF>, however, fell to 10 cents a barrel to
Singapore quotes, hurt by weaker buying interests in the physical market on Thursday. The
premiums were at 19 cents a barrel on Wednesday.
    Meanwhile, jet fuel refining margins <JETSGCKMc1> climbed to $19.40 a barrel over Dubai
crude on Thursday, their highest levels in about four years. Jet cracks were at $19.04 per
barrel on Wednesday.
    Cash differentials for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> remained at a premium for the third straight
session on Thursday, but fell to 18 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes from 24 cents a barrel a
day earlier.
    
    
    SINGAPORE INVENTORIES
    - Singapore onshore middle-distillate stocks dipped 3.4 percent to 9.8 million barrels in
the week to Nov. 14, International Enterprise (IE) data showed. [O/SING1]
    - Overall, onshore middle-distillate inventories were about 19 percent lower than a year
ago.
    - Inventories for light distillates surged over 1 million barrels to a ten-week high of 
12.96 million barrels in week to Wednesday, while fuel oil stocks eased 255,000 barrels to 15.8
million barrels.

    
    API INVENTORY DATA
    - U.S. crude stockpiles rose sharply last week, while gasoline inventories increased and
distillate stocks drew, industry group the American Petroleum Institute said on Wednesday.
[nZXN04FV00]

barrels, compared with expectations for a 1.7 million-barrel drop, the API data showed. [API/S]

    - Singapore trader Hin Leong sold 150,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil to BP for Dec. 1-5 loading
at parity to Singapore quotes.
    - Hin Leong sold another 150,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil to BP for Dec. 8-12 loading at
parity to Singapore quotes.

ahead of U.S. sanctions against Iran that came into effect on Nov.5, customs office data showed
on Thursday. [nL4N1XP22L]
    -  The U.S. oil market is scrambling to adjust to a deep selloff over the last several

SINGAPORE, Nov 15 (Reuters) - Market sentiment eased on Thursday amid signs of rising fuel
oil arbitrage flows into the Singapore hub over the past week, weighing on fuel oil cash
premiums, cracks and time spreads. 
    The December 380-cst barge fuel oil crack to Brent crude was trading at about minus $5.45 a
barrel on Thursday, compared with a discount of $5.20 a barrel in the previous session, broker
sources said.
    The 380-cst Dec/Jan time spread also slipped to about $10.25 a tonne on Thursday, down from
about $10.50 a tonne on Wednesday, the broker sources said. 
    Similarly, lower deal values in the Singapore trading window sent 380-cst cash premiums to a
three-week low of $7.94 per tonne to Singapore quotes on Thursday, down from $8.72 per tonne in
the previous session. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    On Thursday, official data showed Singapore fuel oil net imports in the week to Nov. 14
surged 466 percent to an 11-week high. [nL4N1XQ3AK]
    However, the higher net imports still failed to lift overall inventories of the fuel which
slipped 1.6 percent to a two-week low in the week ended Nov. 14.
    
    INVENTORIES
    - The higher net imports were in line with market expectations of increased arbitrage flows
into Singapore in November, compared with the previous month, with more arrivals being
concentrated in the second half of the month, trade sources said.
    - Onshore fuel oil inventories slipped 255,000 barrels (about 38,000 tonnes) to 15.821
million barrels, or 2.361 million tonnes, data from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore
showed. [O/SING1]
    - Net fuel oil imports came in at 1.359 million tonnes, compared with a near four-month low
of 240,000 tonnes in the week before. Weekly figures like this are volatile, however.
[nL4N1XJ3KH]
    - Singapore fuel oil net imports have averaged at 784,000 tonnes per week in 2018.
    - This week's onshore fuel oil inventories were 33 percent lower than a year earlier.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Bangladesh topped the week ended Nov. 14 at 112,000
tonnes, followed by China at 87,000 tonnes, Hong Kong at 48,000 tonnes and Qatar at 45,000
tonnes.
    - The fuel oil shipment to Qatar in the week to Wednesday was the first time Singapore
exported fuel to the gas-rich Gulf state since at least December 2015, or as far as records go
back, data compiled by Reuters showed.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Malaysia at 267,000 tonnes,
followed by India at 234,000 tonnes, the United Arab Emirates at 197,000 tonnes, Iraq at 186,000
tonnes and Russia at 175,000 tonnes.
    - Singapore's fuel oil imports from Venezuela were at a five-month high of 103,000 tonnes,

LONDON, Aug 29 (Reuters) - Nigerian diffs remained firm on
Wednesday, thanks to demand for October-loading cargoes of Qua
Iboe, while the initial flurry to buy Angolan grades subsided
somewhat, traders said.
    
    NIGERIA
    * Qua Iboe was heard to be changing hands between $1.30 and
$1.50 above dated Brent for September loading and although
offers were heard as high as $1.70-1.90, traders said any
sellers would be unlikely to achieve prices at these levels.
    * Bonny Light was said to be unchanged around $1.30 above
dated Brent. 
    * A handful of cargoes were said to be unsold from the
August and September programmes, down from closer to 30 last
week.

    * Between 15 and 20 cargoes were believed to be left from
Angola's 49-strong October loading programme, although two
traders said the pace had slackened off somewhat in the last few
days.
    * Offers for Dalia held steady at a discount of 60 cents to
dated Brent, while October-loading Nemba was offered at a
premium of 40 cents and Cabinda was indicated at close to 50
cents above dated Brent.

    * India's IOC is seeking light, sweet crude for delivery in
late October via tender. The results were due Thursday or
Friday, traders said.

    DUBAI, April 18 (Reuters) - Asia's refining margin for
180-cst fuel oil against Dubai crude rose to a 5-week high on
Tuesday, after crude oil prices slipped on expectations of
rising U.S. shale oil output in May.
    
    REFINING MARGINS
    - Singapore's May 180-cst fuel oil discount to Dubai crude
<FO180SGCKMc1> narrowed for a second consecutive session on
Tuesday, narrowing 22 cents a barrel from the previous session
to minus $3.72 a barrel.
    - Oil prices hit their lowest in 11 days on Tuesday on news
that U.S. shale oil output in May is expected to post the
biggest monthly rise in more than two years, fuelling concerns
that U.S. production growth is undermining efforts to cut
oversupply. [nL3N1HQ1D9]
    
    ARBITRAGE ASSESSMENTS
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for April are expected
to close unexpectedly higher at 6.5 million to 7.0 million
tonnes, lifted by unusually strong arrivals from the Middle East
and Asia, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed.
[nPGEP834Ja]
    - This comes despite below average Western inflows at under
4 million tonnes, just under the first-quarter average of 7.1
million to 7.2 million tonnes. 
    - Despite expectations of elevated arbitrage arrivals, the
May East-West (EW) arbitrage spread <FOSGEWMc1> - the price
difference between FOB Singapore 180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil
and FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil with maximum 3.5 percent
sulphur - widened to a 5-week high of $23 a tonne. 
    
    SPREADS
    - Liquidity in the ICE traded 380-cst time spreads returned
after remaining depressed over the previous two sessions by 1730
Singapore time (0930 GMT) on Tuesday.
    - Trading more than 200,000 tonnes in contracts, the front
month 380-cst May/June spread contract narrowed its discount by
20 cents per tonne from the previous session, to a 30 cents a
tonne contango.  
    - By contrast, the July/Aug and Aug/Sept 380-cst time spread
contracts slipped on Tuesday. 
              
    WINDOW TRADES
    - 11 cargo trades were reported in the Platts window on
Tuesday totalling 220,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.   
    - PetroChina was again the top buyer of 380-cst fuel oil,
lifting 7 of Tuesday's traded cargoes. Mercuria followed with
another three cargoes and Hin Leong with one. 
    - A total of 2.54 million tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil have

SINGAPORE, April 18 (Reuters) - Refinery maintenance in Asia and the Middle East supported
gasoil and jet fuel margins but supply of the fuels was adequate, traders said. 
    
    - HIGH SULPHUR: Demand for 500ppm sulphur gasoil remained firm in the region while demand
for 10ppm sulphur diesel weakened due to lower demand from Australia, one trader said. 
    - BAHRAIN DIESEL: Bahrain Petroleum Co (Bapco) likely sold 40,000 to 60,000 tonnes of 10ppm
sulphur diesel for May 1 to 4 loading at a premium of about $1.05 to $1.20 a barrel above Middle
East quotes, traders said, though this could not be confirmed.
      The buyer could be Shell, one of them said. 
    - MIDEAST REFINERY MAINTENANCE: Refinery maintenance in the Middle East, both planned and
unplanned, has tightened oil products supply but a closed arbitrage to ship the products west
has muted the impact of the shutdown, traders said.
    - INDIA TO ASIA: India is shipping diesel mainly to Asia instead of Africa or the west as
that is currently the most profitable route, traders said.
      Arbitrage to ship cargoes west has largely not been profitable this year, they said.
    - PHILIPPINES REFINERY: Shell resumed operations at its Tabangao refinery in the Philippines
on Monday following an unplanned shutdown earlier this month, a company spokeswoman said on
Tuesday. [nL3N1HQ3M4]
      Four strong earthquakes which hit the province of Batangas on April 8 caused a power
outage at the refinery, the spokeswoman said.

SINGAPORE, Feb 22 (Reuters) - The Asian jet fuel cash
differential slipped on Wednesday after India made a rare offer
of a spot cargo, traders said.
    Indian Oil Corp offered the jet fuel cargo for export from
Paradip in March. Indian Oil usually sells the jet fuel it
produces from its refineries within India, traders said.
[nL4N1G73GS]
    Cargo flows of distillates from Asia to Europe are expected
even though the arbitrage economics are unprofitable, shipping
fixtures showed. 
    India's Reliance has provisionally booked the Ashley Lady to
ship 100,000 tonnes of ultra-low sulphur diesel from Sikka to
Europe on March 1, the shipping data showed, though the fixture
could not immediately be confirmed.
    BP and Aramco Trading Company have also booked vessels to
ship jet fuel from India and the Gulf to the west, shipbrokers
said.
    Japan's kerosene inventory fell to a nine-month low of 9.16
million barrels in the week to Feb. 18, latest data from
Petroleum Association of Japan showed. <O/JAPAN1> 
    Domestic sales of the heating fuel and jet fuel fell,
however, while sales of diesel picked up slightly, the data
showed. 
    Peak winter demand for kerosene may have passed and refiners
may be maximising diesel production, traders said. 
    In market news, U.S.-based Freepoint Commodities said on
Tuesday it has expanded its presence in Asia, hiring 25 traders
and support staff in the last several months with an eye on
opportunities in metals, oil and agricultural markets to meet
demand in China. [nL4N1G71TR]
    The expansion puts Freepoint in direct competition with
major Swiss commodity traders Glencore and Trafigura, who are
also expanding their businesses in Asia.
    The company has already started trading oil derivatives in
Singapore, an industry source who has seen the trades said.
    Freepoint also plans to join the Platts Market-on-Close
assessment process for physical gasoil, jet fuel and gasoline in
Asia, S&P Global Platts said on Feb. 14 on their website,
referring to its product pricing platform.

SINGAPORE, Feb 23 (Reuters) - The Singapore onshore gasoil
and jet fuel inventory fell in the past week but supply of the
fuels remained ample with spot cargoes appearing from India,
traders said.         
    The city-state's middle distillates stocks fell 8 percent on
the week to a five-week low of 12.587 million barrels in the
week to Feb. 22, latest data from International Enterprise
showed. <O/SING1>
    There were no diesel imports from India, while Chinese
shipments of the fuel also fell, contributing to the drawdown in
stocks, the data showed. 
    Diesel shipments to Australia increased to about 85,000
tonnes from 73,000 tonnes the previous week, though less volumes
were shipped to Indonesia, Vietnam, Myanmar and Malaysia.
    Spot demand for jet fuel appeared from Vietnam with
Petrolimex Aviation seeking 60,000 tonnes of the fuel for
delivery over March to June, traders said. 
    Diesel supply was ample with China and India stepping up
exports of the fuel.
    India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) has
offered a 50ppm sulphur diesel cargo for March in a rare move, a
tender document showed.
    The cargo was offered ahead of a nationwide switch to 50ppm
from April, traders said. MRPL was a regular exporter of 500ppm
sulphur diesel previously. 
    India's Essar Oil also entered the spot market offering a
third cargo for March. 
    China's January exports of diesel fuel rose 32.5 percent
from a year earlier to 960,000 tonnes, data from the Chinese
General Administration of Customs showed. [nB9N1FY02A]
    The figure was still well below a record amount of 1.78
million tonnes shipped out in December but this was likely due
to the lull during the Lunar New Year in late January.     
    
    TENDERS: 
    - Petrolimex Aviation is seeking two cargoes of 10,000
tonnes each of jet fuel for delivery in March and May and four
cargoes of 10,000 tonnes each of the fuel for delivery over
March to June. The tender closes on Feb. 24 and is valid until
Feb. 27. 
    - Essar Oil has offered up to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm
sulphur gasoil for loading from Vadinar over March 15 to 21. The
tender closes on Feb. 24, with same-day validity.
    - MRPL has offered 65,000 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur diesel for
loading from New Mangalore over March 19 to 21. The tender
closes on Feb. 28 and is valid until March 1.

SINGAPORE, Sept 27 (Reuters) - The barge 380-cst fuel oil crack discount to Brent crude held
steady on Thursday despite sharp gains in crude oil prices this week on the back of tight
near-term supply outlook. 
    The crack discount was trading at about minus $11.20 a barrel to Brent crude on Thursday,
broker sources said.
    The discount was at minus $11.15 a barrel in the previous session, the narrowest for this
week. <HFOFARAACMc1> 
    Oil prices rose nearly 1 percent on Thursday, driven by the prospect of a shortfall in
global supply once U.S. sanctions against major crude exporter Iran come into force in just five
weeks' time. [O/R]
    Meanwhile, Singapore fuel oil inventories jumped 15 percent to a 10-week high in the week to
Sept. 26, boosted by thin export volumes, official data showed on Thursday. [nL4N1WD3BZ]    
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Singapore's onshore fuel oil inventories surged 2.328 million barrels, or about 347,000
tonnes, to 17.616 million barrels, or 2.629 million tonnes, data from International Enterprise
(IE) Singapore showed. [O/SING1]
    - Singapore fuel oil exports totalled just 55,000 tonnes in the week to Sept. 26, the lowest
since June 2011. <O-SGEXP-FO>
    - Low export volumes helped lift net fuel oil imports into Singapore to a two-week high of
966,000 tonnes, up 67 percent from the week before, the data showed.
    - Singapore fuel oil net imports have averaged 774,000 tonnes per week in 2018.
    - This week's onshore fuel oil inventories were 24 percent lower than a year ago.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Bangladesh topped the week ended Sept. 26 at 23,000
tonnes, followed by Indonesia at 7,500 tonnes and Myanmar at 10 tonnes.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Russia at 274,000 tonnes, followed
by Malaysia at 191,000 tonnes, Belgium at 101,000 tonnes and Saudi Arabia at 90,000 tonnes.
    - In the United States, fuel oil inventories <RFO-STK-T-EIA> rose 4 percent to their highest
in almost three months, at 29.646 million barrels in the week to Sept. 21, the latest data from
the Energy Information Administration showed. [EIA/D]
        
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Five cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, totalling 100,000 tonnes
of 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO).
    - Gunvor sold all five cargoes to Hin Leong, with two cargoes for Oct. 12-16 loading at a
$5.90 a tonne premium to the average of October Singapore quotes and three cargoes for Oct.
17-21 loading at a $5 per tonne premium to the average of October Singapore quotes.  
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Saudi's Samref has offered 80,000 tonnes of 650-cst to 700-cst HSFO with a maximum 4
percent sulphur content loading from Yanbu on Oct. 7-9.
    - Sri Lanka's Ceypetco is seeking up to 30,000 tonnes of low-sulphur fuel oil with a maximum
175-cst viscosity and maximum 1.8 percent sulphur content for delivery into Colombo over Oct.
30-31, in a tender closing on Oct. 3 with three-day validity.
    - Thailand's PTT Global Chemical sold a 380-cst fuel oil cargo totalling 35,000 tonnes of
fuel oil with a maximum 3.5 percent sulphur content for Oct. 11-13 loading to an unknown buyer
at a premium of $4-$5 per tonne to Singapore quotes on an FOB basis.
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].

LONDON, April 6 (Reuters) - Diesel refining margins in
northwest Europe gained slightly on Thursday, supported by
strong regional demand and a draw in ARA stocks.
    
    * Demand in Germany, Switzerland, Britain and France has
been strong in recent days, drawing cargoes and products from
regional refineries, traders said.
    * Limited imports from the United States were also giving
margins a floor.
    * Gasoil stocks in independently held storage in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp hub edged lower in the week to
Thursday as a contango in the market weakened, making storage
economics less attractive to traders, data from Dutch
consultancy PJK International showed. [ARA/]
    * Stocks also fell due to higher-than-average inland demand
and slower imports from the Baltic.
    * Fuel oil stocks  fell by over a quarter as shipments of
the fuel went to Singapore.
    * Stocks were down 25.3 percent at 1.15 million tonnes,
after hitting an all-time high last week, as two very large
crude carriers and a Suezmax carrying the fuel left the hub for
Singapore in the past week, PJK's Patrick Kulsen said.

discounts of $11 a tonne to ICE April Low-Sulphur Gasoil
futures, stronger by $1 a tonne from trading levels on
Wednesday.

fob ARA to April gasoil futures. 
    * April ICE Low Sulphur Gasoil futures were up $3 at $484 a
tonne at 1545 GMT.
    * Benchmark diesel refining margins <LGO-LCO1=R> were at

    * The April contract traded at a $1.50 a tonne discount to
the May contract, 25 cents a tonne wider.

Qatar was disrupted, industry sources said. But supply is still ample in the region, keeping
regrade prices negative, they added.

disrupted after Qatargas unexpectedly shut its 146,000 barrel-per-day condensate splitter at the

not viable, traders said.
    - But they are trying to sell the cargoes anyway instead of keeping the fuel in tanks as the
market is backwardated, one of them said. 
    - SINGAPORE REFINING COMPANY: Singapore Refining Company is conducting planned maintenance
at a catalyst reformer at its 290,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) refinery, industry sources familiar
with the matter said.
    - The maintenance started in mid-March and is expected to be completed in mid-to-late April,
one of the sources said. [nL3N1HC1B7]
    - PETRON MALAYSIA SEEKS: Petron Malaysia is seeking 299,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil
and 80,000 barrels of jet fuel for delivery in May. 
    -  The tender closes on April 5 and is valid until April 7
    - SINGAPORE CASH DEALS: Two gasoil deals and no jet fuel deals.
    - Hin Leong bought 250,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for April 19-23 loading from

    - Hin Leong bought 150,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for April 30 to May 4 loading
from Freepoint at a premium of 10 cents a barrel to the average of April 24-28 Singapore quotes.

    DUBAI, April 5 (Reuters) - Cash differentials of Asia's 380-cst fuel oil rose for a sixth
consecutive session on Wednesday boosted by continued buying interest in the physical market and
improving sentiment. 
    However, bloated inventories across key storage hubs had traders questioning the extent of
near-term upside potential. 
        
    FUJAIRAH INVENTORIES
    - In the United Arab Emirates, the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil inventories
were down 7 percent, or 876,000 barrels, from the previous week to a total of 11.45 million
barrels (about 1.71 million tonnes) in the week to April 3, data via S&P Global Platts showed.
[nL3N1HD28G]
    - This marks the first weekly decline in FOIZ fuel oil inventories in four weeks, slipping
away from a three-month high in the previous week.
    - Lower utility demand from Pakistan in April was said to have contributed to rising fuel
oil inventories in Fujairah over the past weeks.

    - Ten 380-cst fuel oil cargoes traded in the Platts window totalling 200,000 tonnes. 
    - A total of 860,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil have already traded in the window since the

    - Traders said the upside potential of this latest bullish trading strategy might be weighed
down by ample supplies of the industrial fuel in Singapore, Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp storage
hub, and Fujairah. [ARA/] [O/SING1]

sell-off in time spreads early in the month. [nL4N1G02DI] [nL5N1GF3K3]

    - Improved market sentiment was also evident in the paper markets after 380-cst time spreads
on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) rose higher across most of the 2017 curve. 
    - The ICE-traded 380-cst April/May time spread was trading at a backwardation of 30 cents a
tonne by 1630 Singapore time (0830 GMT), up 30 cents a tonne from parity in the previous
session.
    - The 380-cst May/June time spread was trading at a 10 cents a tonne backwardation, also up
from parity in the previous session.

    - The UAE's ADNOC is offering up to 135,000 tonnes of medium-sulphur fuel oil through three

LONDON, April 4 (Reuters) - Benchmark diesel refining
margins in northwest Europe rose slightly on Tuesday, supported
by firm demand and limited arbitrage into the region.
    
    * Afternoon barge trading liquidity was high for a second
session straight, with nineteen barges changing hands. 
    * Sales of new cars in Germany saw the biggest jump in
almost a year in March, helped by two more selling days than in
the same month last year and echoing signs of strong growth in
other major European auto markets. [nL5N1HC1J3]
    * While around 1 million tonnes of diesel are expected to
arrive in Europe in April from the U.S. Gulf Coast, as that
country's refineries return from maintenance, elevated freight
rates are making it tougher for new bookings.
    * At least one jet fuel cargo meant for export from Qatar
has been disrupted after Qatargas unexpectedly shut its 146,000
barrel-per-day condensate splitter at the Ras Laffan refinery
over the weekend, industry sources said.[nL3N1HC1ZV]
    * Analysts JBC said that U.S. jet fuel demand grew by a
reported 145,000 bpd year-on-year in January, the highest rate
since 2005. That growth more than offset the downward revision
to gasoil demand, which it said was down 35,000 bpd year-on-year

the stage for a bullish trading strategy in April after stalled attempts in March.

    - Seventeen 380-cst fuel oil cargoes traded in the Platts window totalling 380,000 tonnes,
the most window trades since March 1 when 22 deals were reported. [nL3N1GD41A]
    - A total of 660,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil have already traded in the window since the
start of April.
    - An anticipated trading play in March stalled amid abundant physical supplies and a sharp
sell-off in time spreads early in the month. [nL4N1G02DI] [nL5N1GF3K3]
    - Expectations of fewer fuel oil supplies into Asia in April and May make a bullish trading
strategy in April more feasible, traders said. 
    - Cash premiums for the 380-cst fuel <FO380-SIN-DIF> were 15 cents a tonne higher from the
previous session at 34 cents a tonne above Singapore quotes, the highest level since March 1. 
    - Please click on <O/AS> for more details. 

    TIME SPREADS 
    - Reflecting market sentiment, the 380-cst fuel oil market structure on the Intercontinental
Exchange (ICE) traded higher across most of the 2017 curve. 
    - The ICE-traded 380-cst April/May time spread flipped into backwardation of 5 cents a
tonne, by 1830 Singapore time (1030 GMT), up 35 cents a tonne from the previous session.
    - The 380-cst May/June time spread was trading at parity, up from minus 5 cents a tonne in

    DUBAI, April 6 (Reuters) - Falling Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories supported
sentiment on Thursday, lifting buying interest and cash premiums of 380-cst fuel oil to
five-week highs. 
        
    SINGAPORE INVENTORIES
    - Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories fell for a second consecutive week, dropping 7
percent, or 276,000 tonnes, from the previous week to a total of 3.52 million tonnes in the
week to April 5, the latest official data showed. [O/SING1]
    - This came despite a 146 percent jump in net imports over the past week to a four-week
high of 1.2 million tonnes, as import growth outpaced export growth. [nL3N1HE2WJ]
    - Traders said movement of cargoes into floating storage contributed to inventory
draws.
    - Singapore net exports of fuel oil to China soared to their highest since at least
December 2015 at 599,000 tonnes in the week to April 5. 

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - In a signal of growing buying interest, the ratio of standing window bids to offers
continued to rise on Thursday at 24 to 18, respectively. This compared with 20 bids to 18
offers on Wednesday and 14 to 34 at the start of a botched March play. 
    - Twelve 380-cst fuel oil cargoes traded in the Platts window on Thursday totalling
200,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel along with an additional 80,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil. 
    - A total of 1.06 million tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil have already traded in the window
since the start of April.    
    - Please click on <O/AS> for more details. 

    TIME SPREADS 
    - Buying interest in 380-cst time spreads on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) was
less pervasive by 1800 Singapore time (1000 GMT) on Thursday with the market structure
remaining largely unchanged from the previous session.   
    - The ICE-traded 380-cst April/May time spread posted the largest intra-day gains
trading at a backwardation of 60 cents a tonne, up 30 cents a tonne from the previous
session.
    - Further dated 380-cst spreads were either unchanged from Wednesday, or down by a
maximum of 5 cents a tonne during the same time. 
            
    TENDERS
    - Pakistan's PSO is set to import up to 520,000 tonnes of 180-cst HSFO and 110,000
tonnes of 170-cst LSFO in May from multiple suppliers after it received their offers for
delivery in May. 
    - The most competitive offers for the eight 180-cst cargoes were submitted by Vitol,
Gulf Petrochem, Swiss Singapore, Bakri and PetroChina at premiums between $15 to $16.65 per
tonne to MOPAG 180-cst quotes on CFR basis. 
    - Vitol and PetroChina were front runners in the offers for two 170-cst LSFO cargoes
seeking premiums between $43.10 and $51.51 per tonne, respectively, to MOPAG 180-cst
quotes. 
    
    RELATED NEWS
    - Traders in North Asia are rushing to cancel loadings of a range of oil products for
sale to China, ahead of a planned Chinese consumption tax that will make the trade
uneconomic. [nL3N1HE1OI]

LONDON, Feb 9 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins egded
lower on Tuesday as crude futures fell sharply and traders
continued to show interest in storing summer-grade product. 
    Traders have been taking advantage of a wide contango in
forward prices to place summer-grade gasoline into storage tanks
in Europe, but those tanks are filling up fast. 
    As a result, large volumes of winter-grade gasoline are
being placed on tankers offshore from European ports to make
room for summer-grade product, traders indicated.
    Arbitrage bookings out of Europe ebbed on Tuesday, with a
few bookings emerging for journeys to West Africa and the Middle
East, after several transatlantic bookings emerged on Monday.
    Transatlantic shipments were summer-grade gasoline heading
to storage tanks in New York Harbour, market participants
indicated. 
    While the arbitrage to West Africa is workable at the
moment, a combination of the Lunar New Year holiday in several
Asian markets and dwindling demand kept the arbitrage to China
shut.
    China's appetite for high-octane blending components boosted
European gasoline margins in recent months, though rising stored
product weighed heavily on Asian cracks in recent weeks.
    There has been interest, however, in moving the motor fuel
to Asia, loading in late February to early March, traders said.

LONDON, Feb 9 (Reuters) - Benchmark diesel margins in
northwest Europe slid on Tuesday as the supply excess weighed on
prices more heavily than the decline in crude oil.
    There is ample diesel supply in northwest Europe and the
Mediterranean, though traders said the more limited arbitrage
from the U.S. Gulf could help to balance the market over the
coming weeks. Additionally, the onset of refinery maintenance in
Europe, Asia and the United States is exepcted to curtail fresh
deliveries.

northwest Europe edged higher on Monday in very limited trade as
sliding crude oil prices supported the refining complex.

to high storage levels but heating oil buying was stronger due
to cold weather, traders said.

storage near maximum level and large vessels heading to the

data and traders.

refining margins in the region.

LONDON, Feb 8 (Reuters) - North Sea Forties crude oil
differentials were steady on Monday, as thin liquidity due to an
annual oil industry gathering in London eclipsed a supply
shortfall.    
    No deals appeared in the Platts window for a third day.
Volume could remain low this week as many traders will be away
from their desks for the annual IP Week event in London. 
    Forties diffs are holding close to their lowest in a month. 
     
    Crude oil along the Forties Pipeline System in the North Sea
has been running at a reduced rate since an outage along the
system late last week, but is due to return to normal levels
later on Monday or early Tuesday, operator BP said on Monday.
[nL8N15N335]
    Industry monitor Genscape said Forties crude oil was flowing
through the pipeline at a rate of around 400,000 barrels per
day, down from its estimated average of 488,000 bpd.    
    Oil pricing agency Platts said on Monday it planned to offer
an assessment for dated Brent on a cif Rotterdam basis from
March 14, as it strives to protect the benchmark from being
undermined by falling North Sea output. [nL8N15N1O2]    
    Reuters shipping data shows at least four vessels are due to
leave Europe with North Sea crude on board in the coming couple
of weeks.
    The VLCC Hakata has been fixed to load at Hound Point in
late February and is currently in the Mediterranean, heading
west, according to Reuters shipping data.
    Vitol has chartered the VLCC Nave Electron to load this week
at Hound Point to carry Forties to Asia, while BP has fixed the
suezmax Minerva Symphony to load Oseberg at Sture, bound for the
east coast of Canada.  
    P66 has also fixed the aframax Tofteviken, which loaded at
Teesport over the weekend, to take a cargo of Ekofisk to the
U.S. Gulf Coast, while BP has chartered the Shenlong Spirit to
take a North Sea crude to the U.S. market.
    However, trading sources have said this fixture is unlikely
to go ahead now that Brent is commanding its largest premium
over WTI crude in two and a half months. [nL8N15I4O4]
    The tanker is currently in the Irish Sea, having sailed from
Sture and then around the west Scottish coast from Scapa Flow.

Feb 26-28 at a discount of 60 cents to dated Brent, which it
later withdrew. 
    * The last Forties deals were on Tuesday at discounts of 65
cents and 80 cents to dated Brent, making an average of dated
minus 73 cents. Monday's withdrawn offer was above this level,
which leaves Forties unchanged.
    * No other bids, offers or trades were reported for any
grades in the daily window, traders said.

margins steadied on Wednesday as Brent crude futures recouped

placing winter-specification grade into floating storage to make
room for the summer grade.

Administration (EIA) showed on Wednesday. [nL2N15P1EJ]

than 1 million barrels, the EIA said. [nZXN0SNV00]

(bpd), below the same week last year, as maintenance looms.

Wednesday on news from Genscape that a gasoline-making unit at
the 300,000 bpd Irving refinery in Canada was shut down.

tankers have been booked recently to load gasoline in Europe

differentials edged above this week's one-month lows on
Wednesday, as BP bought and bid for a flurry of cargoes loading
in early March, when parts of the Hound Point terminal will be
closed for maintenance.

    LONDON, April 6 (Reuters) - West Africa's crude oil loadings
for Asia are set to fall to a five-month low in April, dragged
down by a backlog of cargoes outside China and strong Brent
prices that hindered new bookings, a Reuters survey of shipping
fixtures and traders showed on Friday.
    Loadings for China, the key consumer of Angolan oil, were
set to hit a 9-month low on a barrel-per-day basis, the survey
showed, while India's bookings were at their lowest in nearly a
year. 
    The shaky figures reflect the overhang of oil currently in
Asia and looking for outlets after a tax change and
anti-pollution drive in China slowed the consumption of its
independent refineries. Seasonal maintenance work limited oil
intake at others. [nL8N1RB5LT]
    The strength of Brent crude benchmark prices also impinged
sales. The contract rose steadily in March, peaking above $70
per barrel, which also pushed its premium to Dubai crude to a
more than two-year high. [nL3N1RB2QZ]
    A wide gap between Brent and other benchmarks makes West
African oil - and all physicaly cargoes prices against dated
Brent - less attractive to buyers with access to crude from
other regions. 
    Indian buyers are particularly aggressive in choosing crude
based on the optimal price, and have in the past year issued
tenders simultaneously for West Africa and U.S. grades.
