SINGAPORE, April 6 (Reuters) - Asia's 380-cst fuel oil cash differential flipped to a premium on
Friday following strong buying interest for cargoes of the fuel for a second straight session. 
    The 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums were at 27 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes on Friday, up
from minus 39 cents a tonne in the previous session and minus 82 cents a tonne on Monday.
<FO380-SIN-DIF>
    Trade sources pointed to falling Singapore fuel oil inventories as well as renewed buying
interest from Pakistan's state-oil company this week as bullish factors, but some were still puzzled
by the abrupt shift in sentiment this week.
    The 380-cst fuel oil market had recently been weighed down by ample supplies of high-viscosity
fuel oil in the Singapore area, trade sources said. 
    On Tuesday, when 380-cst fuel oil cargoes first traded in the Singapore window this week, Hin
Leong had lifted one cargo of the fuel at the equivalent of about $1.25 a tonne below Singapore
quotes.
    Hin Leong on Friday was the sole buyer of all three 380-cst cargoes traded in the window, paying
differentials between around minus 11 cents per tonne to plus $1 tonne to Singapore quotes for the
different cargoes. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fuel oil stocks in the ARA oil hub fell 21 percent, or 222,000 tonnes, from the previous week
to a three-week low of 839,000 tonnes in the week ended April 5, data from Dutch consultancy PJK
International showed. [ARA/]
    - Fuel oil stocks dropped due to exports to Singapore and West Africa, said PJK's Lars van
Wageningen. [nL5N1RI4E1]
    - Still, ARA fuel oil inventories were 27 percent lower than year-ago levels and below the
five-year average of 956,000 tonnes for this time of the year. <STK-FO-ARA>
    - Incoming fuel oil cargoes into the ARA hub originated from France, Poland, Russia and the
United States, the data showed.
    - On Thursday, fewer net imports dragged on Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories to a
12-week low of about 2.94 million tonnes in the week ended April 4, down 9 percent from the week
before, official data showed. [nL4N1RI2ZW]
    - Similarly, fuel oil stocks in the Fujairah storage hub also posted a weekly decline after
slipping 1.4 percent to a four-week low of about 1.05 million tonnes in the week to April 2, data
via S&P Global Platts showed. [nL4N1RH48Q]
    
    PAKISTAN RESUMES IMPORTS
    - Pakistan State Oil (PSO) this week issued its first fuel oil import tender for the year after
suspending purchases at the end of 2017 ahead of an expected pickup in demand during summer.
    - Technical issues at some of Pakistan's newest gas-fired power plants could also be feeding the
country's renewed appetite for fuel oil, sources said. [nL4N1PI2IQ] [nL4N1OS131]    
    - PSO in December halted imports of fuel oil amid an abrupt drop in domestic demand as the South
Asian country turned to liquefied natural gas (LNG) to fuel its power sector. [nL3N1O63E4]
    - The state-owned oil company issued a tender notice inviting bids for the supply of an
unspecified amount of high-sulphur and low-sulphur fuel oil for delivery over May 25-June 10 and
June 11-June 30. Traders said the tender document was released this week.
    - The resumption in PSO's fuel oil imports is expected to strengthen the regional market and
restrict exports of the fuel from the Middle East, where most of Pakistan's fuel oil is supplied
from, three trading sources said.

SINGAPORE, Nov 1 (Reuters) - Asian jet fuel refining margins rose on Thursday to their
highest in more than 3-1/2 years, boosted by aviation demand and weaker crude prices.
    The refining margins, also known as cracks, for jet fuel <JETSGCKMc1> rose to $18.19 a
barrel over Dubai crude during Asian trade, up from $17.54 on Wednesday.
    The region's aviation sector, boosted by new airports, cheaper options for air travel and
increased connectivity, has been one of the primary drivers for Singapore jet fuel margins that
are at their strongest since 2012 for this time of year.
    Passenger numbers at Singapore's Changi airport, the region's biggest air travel hub, for
the first nine months of the year are up by 2.6 million from the same period last year, official
data shows.
    Refinery turnarounds in the region are also keeping fuel supplies in check.
    The winter months in the northern hemisphere typically brings the strongest demand for
kerosene, which is widely used in heating and belongs to the same grade of oil products as
aviation fuel. Jet fuel margins determine the profitability of both.
    Cash differentials for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> remained unchanged on Thursday at a discount
of 1 cent per barrel to Singapore quotes.  
    Meanwhile, cash premiums for 10ppm gasoil fell for a fourth straight session on Thursday,
cooling from multi-year highs touched last week. 
    Cash premiums for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10-SIN-DIF> slipped to 66 cents a
barrel to Singapore quotes, the weakest since Oct. 10. Premiums were at 70 cents on Wednesday.
    Cracks for 10ppm gasoil <GO10SGCKMc1> were little changed on Thursday at around $17.78 a
barrel over Dubai crude.

in the week to Oct. 31, International Enterprise (IE) data showed. [O/SING1]

million barrels a week, compared with a weekly average of about 12 million barrels in 2017,
Reuters calculations show.
    - Overall, onshore middle-distillate inventories were about 21 percent lower than a year
ago.
    
    
    EIA INVENTORIES
    U.S. crude oil inventories climbed for a sixth straight week but grew less than forecast
last week as net imports dropped and government sold barrels from its reserve. There was also a
drawdown in gasoline and distillate stocks. [nL2N1XB0ZX]
    - U.S. crude inventories <USOILC=ECI>, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, rose 3.2
million barrels in the week to Oct. 26, less than analyst forecasts for a build of 4.1 million
barrels.

million barrels, against expectations for a 1.4 million-barrel drop, the EIA data showed.

not only its nuclear ambitions, but this time, its ballistic missile program and its influence

* Tankers diverted in mid-Atlantic to Med
    * In rare arbitrage, cargoes from Europe into Med

    By Ron Bousso
    LONDON, Jan 11 (Reuters) - At least one tanker carrying
diesel en route to New York has been diverted in the
mid-Atlantic to the Mediterranean, where freezing weather from
North Africa to the Balkans has boosted demand for heating oil
and sharply lifted prices.
    At the same time, two 30,000-tonne tankers - the Torm Gyda
and Nord Bell - have been booked by Glencore to go from
northwest Europe to the Mediterranean, according to shipping
data and traders. The vessels were carrying either diesel or
higher-sulphur-content gasoil, traders said.
    Maersk Progress, chartered by BP to carry a 110,000-tonne
cargo of diesel from the Reliance refinery in Jamnagar in west
India to New York, was diverted on Tuesday to the Mediterranean,
according to Reuters ship tracking and traders.
    A second tanker, the 120,000-tonne SKS Dee chartered by
Trafigura, was also expected to turn in the mid-Atlantic towards
Europe, traders said.
    The unusual movements come after prices in the Mediterranean
rose sharply in recent days due to a lack of available supplies
from regional refineries and imports, coupled with cold weather.
    Severe weather in the Black Sea has also led to delays in
tanker loadings, further tightening supplies in the
Mediterranean.
    Prices of gasoil and diesel, used in many countries for
heating, have risen in the Mediterranean to their highest in
months. They surpassed rates in northern Europe, opening a rare
arbitrage. <DL-CIFD-MED>
    The cold spell has also pushed Italy's wholesale day-ahead
gas prices up 50 percent in recent days, prompting suppliers to
step up gas withdrawals from storage.[nL5N1F04SL]

SINGAPORE, Jan 12 (Reuters) - The Singapore gasoil and jet fuel margins jumped to a more
than one-week high on Thursday as inventories fell and as demand from Europe is expected to
increase, trade sources said.

million barrels in the week to Jan. 11, latest data from International Enterprise showed.
    Spot demand from Indonesia for gasoil also supported margins as state-owned Pertamina sought
a cargo for late January, traders said.
    Refinery outages in the Middle East and Russia also boosted sentiment, they added.
    Abu Dhabi's state-owned national oil company ADNOC said on Wednesday it had contained a fire
at the Takreer Ruwais refinery. The fire broke out at the refinery's western processing unit.
[nL5N1F14M6]

processing CDU-12 unit after a pump was damaged by a fire on Wednesday, the energy ministry
said. [nR4N1EP00S]

    SINGAPORE, Jan 11 (Reuters) - Asia's refining margin for 180-cst fuel oil against Dubai
crude sagged to a one-week low on Wednesday weighed down by rising crude oil prices following
news of Saudi supply cuts to Asia. 
    Singapore's February 180-cst fuel oil discount to Dubai crude <FO180SGCKMc1> grew wider for
a second consecutive session on Wednesday, slipping 50 cents a barrel from the previous session
to minus 1.88 cents a barrel.
    On Monday, the front-month refining margin was at its narrowest since the start of the new
year at minus 66 cents a barrel. 
    Meanwhile, cash differentials of the 380-cst fuel oil were steady after three deals were
reported in the Platts window at similar price levels to Tuesday, industry sources said.
    BP bought three cargoes of the 380-cst fuel totalling 60,000 tonnes from Glencore at $1.25
above Singapore quotes each, sources said. 
    Since the start of the year, BP has bought a total of 460,000 tonnes of the 380-cst fuel in
the window through 23 parcels, data compiled by Reuters showed. 
    In other news, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) expects 2016 sales of
bunker fuel for ships to rise to a record for a second consecutive year, with early estimates
showing volumes increased 7.7 percent to 48.6 million tonnes, it said on Wednesday. [nL4N1F1396]

products including gasoline, kerosene, gas oil, bunker A and low sulphur bunker A (LSA) for
delivery by maritime shipment or at a refinery, the first such contracts on a Japanese exchange.
[nL4N1F11MG]

North Sea and Azerbaijan to Asia this month, seeking to plug any supply gap left by OPEC
production cuts. [nL4N1F03FR]
    - Saudi Arabia cut February term crude supplies to refiners in India and Southeast Asia,
seeking to comply with an OPEC deal, but held most of its exports to the rest of Asia steady for

country's imports of diesel and ramp up exports of the fuel, in turn weighing on margins,
traders said on Tuesday. 
    
    - INDIAN MONSOON: Crop-nourishing monsoon rains lashed the Kerala coast in India's southwest
on Tuesday, the India Meteorological Department said, the earliest start to the rains since 2011
which could dent diesel demand. [nL3N1IW0T9]
    Monsoon rains typically reduce the need for diesel used in irrigation pumps. This could
reduce imports of the fuel into the country and ramp up exports, traders said.
    India has been importing diesel in recent weeks due to refinery maintenance as the country
upgraded to euro IV fuel specifications in April, they added.
    - INDIA DIESEL DEMAND OUTLOOK: India's diesel demand is expected to rise to record levels
again this year as a slew of infrastructure projects boosts use of the transport and industrial
fuel, although a government-induced cash shortage will hold growth to its slowest in three
years. 
    Increased fuel efficiency, a fall in commercial vehicle sales, and the use of other fuels
for power generation are also expected to dent demand growth for diesel, analysts and traders
told Reuters.  [nL3N1IW0R6]
    - ADNOC TERM: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company has sealed its July 2017 to June 2018 jet fuel
term contract with at least one buyer at a lower premium than a previous contract, traders said.
[nL3N1IW1CV]
    It set the premium at 75 cents a barrel above benchmark Middle East quotes, down from the $1
a barrel premium for its January to December 2017 jet fuel term contract, they said.
    ADNOC is still negotiating its July 2017 to June 2018 term contract for diesel, they added.

refinery in northern Japan from June 12 to mid-July for scheduled maintenance. [nL4N1HZ077]

SINGAPORE, May 25 (Reuters) - Trading activity in Asia's fuel oil paper markets was
muted on Thursday as industry participants remained on the sidelines as ministers from OPEC
and non-OPEC countries meet in Vienna.
        
    PAPER MARKET
    - Trade volumes on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) were minimal compared to recent
days, industry sources said.
    - The ICE-traded 380-cst June/July time spreads was trading 10 cents lower from its
previous settlement, widening its discount minus $1.10 a tonne. 
    - Open Interest volumes in the 380-cst contract scaled back to 10.7 million tonnes in
contracts, down from a 2017 high of 11.2 million tonnes in the previous session.
[nL4N1IQ41Y] 
    - The 380-cst fuel oil refining margin to Brent crude on ICE narrowed its discount by
about 30 cents a barrel from the previous session to minus $7.30 a barrel, extending
Wednesday's gains.

earlier on Tuesday following three consecutive sessions of sharp losses. [nL4N1IQ41Y]
    - The ICE-traded June 380-cst EW arbitrage spread was unchanged from Wednesday's
settlement at $13.25 cents a tonne higher to $11.75 a tonne by 5:00 p.m. Singapore time
(0900 GMT) on Thursday.
    
    SINGAPORE INVENTORIES
    - Singapore onshore fuel oil inventories fell 12 percent, or 369,000 tonnes, to a total
of 2.85 million tonnes in the week to May 24, their lowest since early January, official
data showed. [O/SING1]
    - Net fuel oil imports fell to 765,000 tonnes, down 53 percent from the previous week.
[nL4N1IR2Z4]

previous week, was nearly double that of its exports which were 25 percent lower.

of May, against 3.821 million tonnes in April.

    SINGAPORE, May 30 (Reuters) - Fuel oil refining margins have been high across all major
regions this year and the extension of the OPEC cuts as well as ongoing investment into
upgrading capacity are likely to continue to support them, JBC Energy Research said in a
note on Tuesday.
    Meanwhile, cash premiums of 180-cst fuel oil slipped to a near two-week low amid weaker
deal values and more aggressive supplier offers on Tuesday, while discounts of 380-cst fuel
oil held steady near Monday's two-month low. 

    REFINING MARGINS 
    - While Russian fuel oil production fell by almost 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) since
the start of the year, shrinking domestic demand helped exports increase by 90,000 bpd,
said JBC. 
    - In June however, the research consultancy expects supply-side pressures to ease as
crude runs in Russia increase following the end of peak refinery maintenance. 
    - In the United States, EIA data showed fuel oil production over the last four weeks
declined by 55,000 bpd despite a 1 million bpd increase in crude runs there. JBC, however,
attributed a change in refiners' crude slate to lighter shale oil, which yields lower
quantities of fuel oil, as a result of increased U.S. shale oil production. 
    - The June 380-cst refining margin on FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil to Brent crude on
the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) was largely unchanged from the previous session,
trading at about minus $7.40 a barrel by 5 pm Singapore time (0900 GMT) on Tuesday, trade
sources said.
    - By comparison, the ICE June refining margin was trading at about minus $7.50 a barrel
during the same time in the previous week. [nL4N1IJ3PL]
    - Fuel oil refining margins have mostly traded well above the above five-year average
since the start of 2017 when OPEC first began implementing its production cut agreement,
which limited supplies of heavy crudes that tend to yield larger quantities of fuel oil
when compared to light crudes.

    WINDOW TRADES

oil.
    - Mercuria and Gunvor each bought 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel from Lukoil and
Trafigura, respectively. Mercuria sold one 40,000 tonne cargo of 380-cst fuel oil to BP. 
    - A total of 1.94 million tonnes of fuel oil have traded in the window since the start
of May, against 3.821 million tonnes in April.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS

    - Sri Lanka's Ceypetco bought 35,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil with a maximum 1.8

SINGAPORE, May 28 (Reuters) - The front-month fuel oil crack and East-West (EW) arbitrage
spread firmed on Monday, boosted by a tight near-term supply outlook and limited availability of
finished grade bunker fuels, trade sources said. 
    Arbitrage flows into Singapore are so far expected to total some 4-5 million tonnes in June,
with 3-4 of these coming arriving from west of the Suez canal and the remaining 1 million tonnes
from the Middle East. 
    This compares to Singapore fuel oil imports of about 6-7 million tonnes in May. 
    The June EW spread was trading at about $16 per tonne on Monday, up from about $15.50 in the
previous week, broker sources said. 
    Supported by weaker crude prices, the June 380-cst fuel oil crack to Brent crude narrowed
its discount to about $10.60 a barrel on Monday. On Friday the fuel oil crack was trading at
about minus $11.45 a barrel, broker sources said. 
    Oil prices fell on Monday, extending even steeper declines from Friday, as Saudi Arabia and
Russia said they may increase supplies and as U.S. production gains show no signs of abating.
[O/R]
    Brent and WTI crude prices have fallen by 6 percent and 8.3 percent respectively from peaks
touched earlier in May.
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Four cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, totalling 60,000 tonnes
of 380-cst fuel oil and 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil.
    - Gunvor bought all three 380-cst fuel oil cargoes from Trafigura on Monday at a $3 per
tonne premium to the average of June 380-cst quotes. 
    - Gunvor also sold to Vitol the 180-cst fuel oil cargo at a $3 per tonne premium to
Singapore 180-cst quotes. 
    - The strong buying interest for fuel oil cargoes on Monday helped firm cash premiums of
both fuel oil grades. <FO180-SIN-DIF>, <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Pakistan's PSO has received offers for three 65,000-tonne cargoes for June 11-20 delivery
into Port Qasim. 
    - Two of the lowest offers came from Gunvor, one for a premium $18.69 per tonne to Middle
East quotes on an FOB basis, and another for a $19.88 per tonne premium. Gunvor's cargo offers
were for loading from Malaysia. 
    - The third lowest offer came from Bakri at a premium of $23.38 per tonne loading from
Fujairah. 
    - India's Reliance is offering up to 45,000 tonnes of carbon black feedstock (CBFS) with a
maximum 90-cst viscosity and a maximum 1.3 percent sulphur content loading from Sikka on June
17-18.
    - Saudi's Samref is offering up to 90,000 tonnes of 650-cst to 700-cst high-sulphur fuel oil
loading from Yanbu on June 5-7.
    - Sri Lanka's Ceypetco is seeking 30,000 tonnes of fuel oil cargoes with a maximum 175-cst
viscosity and a maximum 1.8 percent sulphur content for July 8-9 delivery into Colombo in a
tender closing on June 5 with three-day validity, the tender documents showed.
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
        
    REFINERY OUTAGES

    - The fire was extinguished immediately and there were no injuries.

26. [nIGB41C3ED]

of October, a trader said.

were offered from Russia and Asia despite lower regional
production due to maintenance.

from Asia and the Middle East on offer, traders said.
    * Warm weather and very high storage levels continued to cap
demand.
    * However, refinery turnarounds, which peak in Europe in
March, were helping remove some of the heavy oversupply seen in
recent months. 
    * U.S. refiners have slashed maintenance plans for April by
more than a third, according data from IIR Energy, a shift
likely to support to market confidence that oil's longest,
deepest rout in a generation is finally over.[nL5N16L129]

East and Asia, according to shipping data and traders. This
compared with close to 2.5 million in February.

freight rates fell in recent days, traders said.

February, a trade source said on Monday. The amount is six
percentage points above the five-year average of 52 percent for
early March. [nL5N16M1N3]

LONDON, March 16 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe rose on Tuesday to around $4.5 per barrel,
supported by continued demand from West Africa.
    
    * The market remained under downward pressure from high
supply levels as more summer-grade product was stored in
expectation of higher prices during the peak summer demand
season.
    * U.S. gasoline stocks <USOILG=ECI> fell last week by
747,000 barrels, compared with analysts' expectations in a
Reuters poll for a 2.3 million-barrel drop.[EIA/S]    
    * More than 500,000 tonnes of gasoline have been booked to
ship from Europe to West Africa in March, according to Reuters
shipping data, following renewed buying interest in Nigeria. 
    * Several cargoes were also booked in recent days to the
U.S. East Coast and the Middle East ahead of summer demand. 
    * New bookings of reformate and high-octane blending
components to China for May delivery has sharply dropped in
recent days. April volumes are expected to remain above 500,000
tonnes.
    * Barge discharge and loading waiting times in the ARA hub
are expected to rise in the coming days due to high volumes of
gasoline deliveries, traders and brokers said.

margins in northwest Europe firmed on Wednesday as maintenance
and weeks of limited arbitrage helped erode an overhang of
unwanted product.

from the Middle East and Asia, with more than 1 million tonnes
of diesel already booked. This was still well below the near-2.5
million in February.

Information Administration data. [nL2N16O117]

and a drop in refinery maintenance is expected to pump more
distillates into the Atlantic Basin.

at its Convent refinery in Louisiana for maintenance in October.

Singapore quotes from Monday's $2 settlement as traded volumes shrank, industry sources said.

    * Likely sold cargo to TonenGeneral for May arrival

    By Liz Hampton and Osamu Tsukimori
    HOUSTON/TOKYO, March 16 (Reuters) - Japan will receive a
U.S. crude cargo in May, its second such purchase from the
United States since Washington lifted a four-decade ban on crude
exports, industry sources said on Wednesday.
    This will follow the arrival in April of Japan's first crude
cargo from the United States, bought by Cosmo Oil Co earlier
this year, indicating a growing willingness among Asian refiners
to experiment with new grades as they seek to diversify their
feedstock sources away from the Middle East. [nL3N1531B8]
    The May shipment will be from Phillips 66 <PSX.N>, said the
sources, who did not want to be named as they were not
authorised to speak to media. Phillips 66 has sold a
Panamax-sized cargo likely to Japan's TonenGeneral <5012.T>,
they added. 
    The U.S. firm could not be reached for a comment, while a
spokesman for the Japanese refiner declined to comment.
    Japan usually gets more than 80 percent of its crude from
the Middle East. But Cosmo and TonenGeneral, which have bought
U.S. condensate previously, are among the more adventurous Asian
buyers who are willing to experiment with new grades. [O/JAPAN1]
    Chinese refiner Sinopec Corp <0386.HK> has also bought U.S.
crude, to be loaded from a Gulf Coast port in March.[nL2N14Z05K]
    
    ACTIVE SELLER
    To meet this rising demand, Phillips 66 has been actively
marketing U.S. crude to Asian buyers since Washington lifted the
export ban, joining a string of trading houses who are taking
advantage of the relatively new arbitrage.
    However, the U.S. crude's economics or whether it is more
competitively priced than oil from the Middle East can only be
determined after it is processed at refineries, one source said.
    Phillips 66 has likely shipped out its first U.S. crude
cargo, which is set to arrive into Singapore next month,
shipping data on Thomson Reuters Eikon showed. [nL2N16N1CY]
    Phillips 66 has also been planning to co-load U.S. crude
with Colombian grade Castilla for Asia, although it is unclear
if it has found any buyers for such a cargo, a Singapore-based
trader said.
    In addition to U.S. crude, Phillips 66 has been marketing
Black Hawk condensate and it also regularly sells heavy naphtha
from the United States to Asia, traders said.

BEIJING, June 11 (Reuters) - China National Petroleum Corp
(CNPC) shipped a 60,000-tonne cargo of diesel in late May
destined for Brazil, the Chinese major's first move of the
refined fuel in a shipment of this size to the Americas, an
inhouse newspaper reported on Monday.

one million tonnes of diesel to Latin America since 2015, but
mostly with medium-ranged tankers able to carry about 40,000
tonnes, the report said.

Bayuquan port in Liaoning province in northeast China, according

that larger shipments would help cut the logistics cost.

Sinopec Corp <0386.HK>, shipped several very large crude
carriers of diesel to Europe and West Africa, a sign of surplus
refining capacity in China.  [nL4N1RG44F]

SINGAPORE, July 16 (Reuters) - Strong buying interest on Monday lifted Asia's 380-cst fuel oil
cash premium to a more-than-three-year high just as expectations of ongoing supply constraints
continued to feed bullish sentiment, trade sources said. 
    A lack of fuel oil arbitrage shipments into Asia since the start of the summer months have led
to narrower availability of finished grade bunker fuels in Singapore and are expected to last
through August, the sources said. 
    The 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums were 28 cents a tonne higher from the previous session at
$5.56 a tonne to Singapore quotes on Monday, the widest premium since June 2015. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    The shortage of finished grade bunker fuels in Singapore, coupled with steady demand for bunker
fuels, have also helped boost ex-wharf premiums of the mainstay 380-cst fuel oil to $6-$8 per tonne
to Singapore quotes over the past week, up from $2-$3 per tonne at the start of June, trade sources
said. [nL3N1T73YK]
    
    BUNKER LICENCE REVOKED
    - Marine fuel services provider Pegasus Maritime (Singapore) Pte Ltd has lost its licence to
operate bunker craft in the port of Singapore effective July 16, the Maritime And Port Authority
(MPA) of Singapore said on Monday. [nL4N1UC20H]
    - The MPA has revoked Pegasus Maritime's craft operator licence after investigations earlier
this year revealed the company had allowed an unlicenced craft operator to use its bunker craft to
make bunker deliveries, it said in a statement.
    - Pegasus Maritime is the first company to be stripped of an MPA-issued licence this year after
a clampdown in 2017 on short deliveries to bunker fuel customers saw three of Singapore's top 10
bunker fuel suppliers losing their licences. [nL5N1NC3HJ]

SINGAPORE, Feb 27 (Reuters) - Gasoil and jet fuel cash
differentials fell on Monday as spot supply from India flooded
the market, traders said.     
    India's Essar Oil offered its fourth gasoil cargo for
loading in March, in a sign that gasoil demand in India may have
slowed, traders said.
    Indian Oil Corp also offered a high sulphur gasoil cargo for
March, they added.
    Indian state-owned refiners have also been upgrading their
units to produce cleaner diesel, which may have reduced their
requirements from Essar Oil which supplies diesel to them, which
in turn has increased the latter's diesel exports, one of them
said.
    India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) had
earlier offered 50ppm sulphur diesel, a change from the usual
500ppm sulphur gasoil that it usually exports, traders said. 
    India will move towards 50ppm sulphur diesel nationwide by
April, this year.
    Malaysia's Prime Minister Najib Razak announced on Monday
that Saudi Arabia's state oil company will invest $7 billion
into an oil refinery to be set up by Malaysian oil company
Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas).
    Najib said the decision was made before noon on Monday after
discussions between top executives from Petronas and Saudi
Aramco to build the plant, part of Malaysia's Refinery and
Petrochemical Integrated Development (RAPID) project in
Pengerang in the southern state of Johor. 
    This follows an announcement in Vietnam that the country's
new $7.5 billion Nghi Son oil refinery expects to take delivery
of its first crude oil in May and to have its first products by
the third quarter of the year. [nL4N1G844C]
    This is expected to increase exports of diesel and jet fuel
in the region, which could dent margins, as supply of the fuels
is ample with China stepping up exports of diesel, traders said.
    Still, in the short term, supply is expected to tighten as
refineries in Asia undergo heavy maintenance.
    Sinopec Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd, a unit of state
refiner Sinopec Corp, plans to shut a key crude oil unit and an
ethylene facility for four to five weeks of maintenance starting
in April, a company press official told Reuters. [nB9N15A05N]

    DUBAI, Feb 27 (Reuters) - A recovery in buying interest lent support to Asian fuel oil
markets on Monday, with both cash differentials and prompt month time spreads edging higher,
traders said. 
    Premiums of the 380-cst fuel oil March/April time spread <FO380SGSDMc1> rose to a near
two-week high of $2.75 a tonne, up 50 cents from the previous session. The last time premiums of
the front-month spread were as high was on Feb. 16 after soaring trading volumes of the contract
sparked expectations of a bullish trading play. [nL4N1G02DI]
    While the backwardated market structure over the near term is at odds with current supply
levels, traders said market sentiment continues to draw support from the anticipated trading
play, as well as expectations of an inventory drawdown in March and April stemming from fewer
arbitrage supplies. 
    Since the start of February, Singapore inventories have climbed 2.8 million barrels to a
seven-month high totalling 26.65 million barrels.
    In a market characterised by excess supply, inventories will be rising, and the market will
typically tend to move from backwardation into contango, or if it is already in contango into a
deeper one.
    In the physical markets, cash discounts of the actively traded 380-cst fuel were also at
their narrowest since Feb. 16 on stronger buying interest, industry sources said. 
    Discounts of the 380-cst fuel <FO380-SIN-DIF> were assessed at 4 cents a tonne below
Singapore quotes, up from minus 68 cents a tonne on Friday.

session, with no standing bids or offers in the Platts window in Monday.

SINGAPORE, June 1 (Reuters) - The 380-cSt and benchmark 180-cSt Asia fuel oil cash
discounts widened to fresh 3-month lows as buying interest in a well supplied market
wanes and eager suppliers trade at weaker prices, traders said.
    Only two deals totalling 40,000 tonnes were reported on Wednesday in the Platts
window, split evenly in volume between the 380-cSt and 180-cSt grades, industry sources
said.
    The 380-cSt cargo was traded at $3.50 a tonne below Singapore spot quotes, while the
180-cSt cargo was sold at a discount of $4 a tonne.
    Bids for both fuel oil grades were lower with leading bids for the 380-cSt fuel
ranging between minus $5 and minus $6.25 a tonne to Singapore quotes and bids for the
180-cSt grade between minus $4 and minus $5.25 a tonne, industry sources said. Compared
to yesterday, these bids are approximately $2 to $3 a tonne lower for both fuel grades,
sources said.
    The 380-cSt discount widened by $1.30 a tonne to $3.74 a tonne below Singapore
quotes. This is the first time since Feb 29 that the discount falls below the $4 level.
<FO380-SIN-DIF>
    Similarly, discounts for the 180-cSt fuel fell 98 cents to $3.56 a tonne below
Singapore quotes, its lowest since March 1. <FO180-SIN-DIF>
    In the swaps market, the prompt June visco contract, the price differences between
180-cSt and 380cSt fuel oil, were sold on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) falling
from $5.50 in the previous session, to $4.75 a tonne on Wednesday, said a Singapore-based
derivatives trader. <FOVISSGDFMc1>

to a trade source with direct knowledge of the matter, at a time when the state-owned
National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) is trying to establish market share in the wake of the
sanctions. [nL3N17E2KX]
    - OPEC's oil output fell in May from near a record high, a Reuters survey found on
Tuesday, as attacks on Nigeria's oil industry and other outages outweighed increases in
Iran and Gulf members. [nL8N18S1TL]
    - China is planning changes to the way it handles oil reserves by allowing private
companies to build and operate some of its strategic stockpiles, while also requiring
companies to maintain compulsory inventories, potentially boosting its future imports.

distributors continue to use hundreds of trucks to transport

France that have cut into the world's excess of diesel, jet fuel
and gasoline.[nL8N18V279]

SINGAPORE, Aug 22 (Reuters) - Brent crude's premium to Dubai
rose on Tuesday to $2.13 per barrel for October, the widest
spread between the two crude oil benchmarks since Dec. 21,
according to two trade sources.

Middle East crude and slow the flow of low-sulphur crude from

tonnes of diesel in August. Around 1 million tonnes of it is

weekend, according to industry monitor Genscape. A small fire on
Monday was quickly extinguished, and had no apparent impact on
the restart. [REF/OUT]

Europe and also across the Mediterranean.

bpd Ashdod refinery was not having a large impact on the broader
market, traders said.

recent weeks, but are now being resolved.

Deer Park, Texas, refinery to normal operations by midweek,
sources familiar with plant operations said. [nL2N1L70H1]

SINGAPORE, Aug 24 (Reuters) - The September visco spread fell to a more than one-week
low on Thursday as demand for cutter stocks pushed supplies of low-viscosity fuels used in
blending higher, industry sources said.
    
    VISCO SPREAD
    - The front-month visco spread <FOVISSGDFMc1>, the price differential between the
front-month 180-cst and 380-cst fuel oil grades, fell to $4 a tonne on Friday, its lowest
since Aug. 16.  
    - Industry sources said most recent fuel oil arrivals were of the finished grade that
do not require blending with cutter stocks into on-specification material. 
    - Buying finished fuel oil grades is more economical now than blending unfinished
grades, industry sources said. 
    - The front-month has steadily trended lower over the past few months; averaging $4.50
a tonne in August, $5.70 in July and $6.90 in June. 
    - On May 4, the front-month visco spread rose to a near two-year high of $9.50 a tonne.

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - One 380-cst fuel oil cargo trade was reported in the Platts window.
    - Mercuria bought 20,000 tonnes of the fuel for delivery on Sept. 8-12 from Glencore
for $304 a tonne, or a discount of about 5 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    - Mercuria has been the top buyer of fuel oil cargoes in the window this month having
accumulated a total of 380,000 tonnes of the fuel, up from 40,000 tonnes it bought in July,
data compiled by Reuters showed.
    - Glencore has been the top seller of fuel oil cargoes in August having sold 240,000
tonnes of the fuel, versus no sales in July. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Pakistan's PSO is seeking up to 455,000 tonnes of 180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil
(HSFO) through seven 65,000 tonne cargoes for delivery into Port Qasim in October on an FOB
basis, along with an additional 55,000 tonnes of 170-cst low-sulphur fuel oil (LSFO) for
October delivery into Karachi on a CFR basis. [nL4N1LA3C8]
    - The tender has closed but remains valid until Aug. 28. 
    - This comes after PSO finalised on Aug. 7 the import of five 65,000 HSFO cargoes as
well as one 55,000 tonne LSFO cargo for delivery in September. [nL4N1LA3C8]
    - Bakri supplied three of the HSFO cargoes while PetroChina provided the remaining two
HSFO cargoes and the LSFO cargo.
    - PSO initially sought to import 10 65,000 tonne HSFO cargoes in September but opted
for five for unknown reasons. 
    - Separately, Indonesia's Pertamina has offered up to 200,000 barrels of V-1250
low-sulphur waxy residue for Sept. 25-27 loading from Balikpapan in a tender closing on

LONDON, April 12 (Reuters) -    * Most North Sea
differentials held unchanged on Tuesday, while Forties eased a
touch, having achieved some stability over the previous two
days.
    * Stiff competition from a hefty Urals programme, coupled
with an unfavourable arbitrage to Asia <DUB-EFS-1M> and tepid
demand has kept the North Sea market under pressure this month.
    * Flows of Forties to Asia have slowed to nothing in April,
based on Reuters data. Shipping lists show no tankers have
loaded and departed the North Sea this month bound for either
China or South Korea, after an initial flurry of fixtures fell
through.
    * The VLCC Samail, which loaded in the second half of March,
is still anchored off Hound Point, together with three Aframaxes
-- the Zaliv Baikal, the Alfa Italia and the Ligovsky Prospect,
all of which loaded at Hound Point last week and have no current
orders -- and a fourth Afra, the Monterey, currently for orders
off Southwold, according to Reuters data.
    * A suezmax, the SKS Spey, had been due to load Ekofisk at
Teesport later this month, set for China, but brokers said that
fixture had failed and Shell has now booked the vessel.
    * Traders and shipping sources said there were storage
options that had been booked for the Maran Thetis, currently
anchored off Antifer and controlled by Total.
    
    WINDOW SUMMARY    
    * Petroineos sold a cargo of Forties to Vitol for loading
May 3-5 at a discount of 40 cents to dated Brent. Forties was
last valued on Monday at a discount of 30 cents.
    * Trafigura bid for a cargo of Forties for loading May 6-12
at a discount of 25 cents to dated Brent.

SINGAPORE, April 8 (Reuters) - The Asian 380cst fuel oil
prompt-month and cash differentials moved back into discounts on
Friday amid muted trading activity and weaker buying interest,
traders said. 
    For a second time this week, the 380cst April and May
contracts in the Platts window flipped into a narrow contango of
25 cents a tonne below Singapore quotes, compared with a premium
of 5 cents a tonne the day before, industry sources said.
    In cash deals, one trade was reported with BP selling 20,000
tonnes of 380cst to Vitol at a discount of 50 cents a tonne to
Singapore quotes for April 28 to May 2 delivery, sources said.
    On Thursday, two 380cst fuel oil cash deals were closed at a
zero discount to Singapore quotes with one for delivery between
April 26 and 30, while the other was due between May 3 and 7,
sources said.
    380cst cash differentials ended the week near flat at a
discount of 2 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes, from Thursday's
premium of 21 cents a tonne but stronger than last week's
discount of 86 cents a tonne. 
    
    ARA WEEKLY STOCKS:
    Total product stocks held in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp
(ARA) hub [STK-FO-ARA] rose to a fresh all-time high, led by a
large build in fuel oil stocks, Dutch consultancy PJK
International said on Thursday. [nL5N17A4DM]
    Fuel oil inventories in the hub rose to 1.376 million tonnes
in the week to April 7, up 292,000 tonnes from the previous
week, PJK data showed. 
    One VLCC was expected to arrive at the ARA hub on April 8
and head to Singapore on April 11 with an outbound cargo of fuel
oil, PJK said.  
       
    MARKET NEWS:
    Saudi Arabia's Samref oil refinery has unexpectedly shut
down its 155,000 barrel per day (bpd) vacuum distillation unit,
a source with knowledge of the matter said, triggering a tender
issuance to export residual fuels from the port of Yanbu.
[nL3N17B2IG]
    Crude sellers have ample supplies to offer into spot crude
markets in Asia, with demand cooling due to heavy refinery
maintenance and as a strengthening in prompt prices has deterred
traders from holding oil for sale at later dates. [nL3N17B2BH]
    Freight rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) may
drift lower next week on weaker sentiment among owners and
reduced chartering demand ahead of the release of May's Middle
East loading programme, brokers said on Friday. [nL3N1780JP]
    Rates plunged this week from a two-week high hit on April 1
on slower chartering activity that is expected to extend into
next week.

* North Sea crude oil differentials stabilised on Wednesday,
with Forties edging a whisker higher, while the crude futures
market briefly flipped into backwardation.

second-position contract <LCOc2> for the first time since
January, having held at a discount of around 80 cents just two
weeks ago.

hefty supply of Urals, a close competitor for Forties, put
differentials under pressure earlier this month.
    * While March proved to be a fairly decent month in terms of
flows, the same is not the case in April.
    * No VLCCs have loaded Forties and departed for Asia so far
this month and according to fixtures lists, none are scheduled
to at the moment. But the picture is less gloomy than it might
appear at first glance.
    * Reuters trade flows data shows some 6.3 million barrels of
Forties have loaded so far this month, compared with around 3.6
million at the same point in April last year.
    * The VLCC Samail, which loaded in the second half of March,
is still anchored off Hound Point, together with three Aframaxes
-- the Zaliv Baikal, the Alfa Italia and the Ligovsky Prospect,
all of which loaded at Hound Point last week and have no current
orders -- and a fourth Afra, the Monterey, currently for orders
off Southwold, according to Reuters data.
    * On the demand front, supply of diesel is set to rise even
further this month, adding to an existing surplus of refined
products. [PRO/E]

with no buyers.

bids or offers were reported for any other grades.

SINGAPORE, April 11 (Reuters) - Cash discounts of Asian 380cst fuel oil slipped at the start of
the week despite steady activity in the physical market, traders said. 
    The 380cst fuel oil cash discounts widened to minus 28 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes on
Monday, down 26 cents from Friday's close at 2 cents below Singapore quotes.
    Four cash deals were reported, totalling 100,000 tonnes of 380cst fuel oil for delivery across
Monday's pricing window between April 26 and May 11, with prices ranging between a discount of minus
50 cents and flat to Singapore quotes, industry sources said.
    In swaps, while the April-May spreads contracts for 380cst fuel oil narrowed to a contango of
only 5 cents a tonne to Singapore quotes from Friday's 25 cents a tonne, trading activity in the
contracts was lower as April contracts approach their rollover date in the middle of the month and
open interest dwindled, traders said.
    By contrast, the contango structure in May-June contracts widened in late afternoon on the
Intercontinental Exchange to about minus $2 a tonne to Singapore quotes, industry sources said. 
    Although the East-West arbitrage window remains firmly shut, industry sources said they did not
yet see signs of tightening market supplies after heavy inflows throughout the past two months.

summer peak-demand season, raising the prospect of a worsening diesel glut further down the road.

Sachs <GS.N> said in a report on Monday. [nL3N17E20D]

expected, according to data from the Energy Information

SINGAPORE, April 20 (Reuters) - Asia's cash premiums for 10ppm gasoil rose for the fifth
consecutive session on Friday amid firmer demand, while inventories in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) storage hub dropped to 2018 lows.
    Cash premiums for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10-SIN-DIF> rose to 50 cents a barrel
to Singapore quotes, up from 47 cents on Thursday.
    Middle distillate inventories have fallen across regions with stocks in the Fujairah Oil
Industry Zone dropping 26 percent in the week to April 16, while Singapore onshore stocks
declined about 15 percent in the week ended April 18. [FUJAIRAH/] [O/SING1]
    In the United States, distillate stockpiles fell 3.1 million barrels in the week to April 13
to levels not seen seasonally since 2014. [EIA/S]

traders said.
    Meanwhile, crude oil prices hit their highest in more than three years this week, but market
watchers said prices will not likely crimp demand for middle distillates due to steady economic
growth in the region.
    Sustained high crude prices, however, may impact Asian jet fuel and diesel demand in the
last quarter of 2018 and next year, said Sukrit Vijayakar, director of energy consultancy
Trifecta.
    Cash differentials for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> fell to 90 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes
from 94 cents on Thursday.
    The physical jet fuel market as per the Singapore window remained muted with no trades or
offers on Friday.

supplies of finished grade fuel oil in Singapore helped boost

inventories have dropped at the same time that some supplies in
the region do not meet the standards for use as shipping fuel,
further reducing availability, five trade sources said.
[nL3N1S22HA]
    - The sources said the supply tightness stems from too much
of the supply of bunker fuel being so-called off-specification,
meaning it does not meet standards for use on ships. Singapore
is the world's biggest bunker fuel market.
    - One source said the quality problems might originate from
blending fuel onboard ships, where the blending process cannot
be done as well as at large and specialised onshore facilities.

10-month low of 17.941 million barrels in the week to April 18,
the latest official data showed. <STKRS-SIN>

window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.

Singapore quotes.

* China's U.S. scrap copper imports down 80 y/y pct in Sept
    * Shipments from Japan increase to fill void
    * Surging alumina exports head to Iceland, India

    By Tom Daly
    BEIJING, Nov 1 (Reuters) - Chinese imports of scrap metal
from the United States fell in September, according to customs
data on Thursday, spelling out the impact of tariffs imposed by
Beijing, while India and Iceland benefited from a boom in
Chinese alumina exports. 
    China's General Administration of Customs said in a
statement posted on its website on Thursday that it was making
available to the public monthly data on the import and export of
commodities, including the country of origin for imports and
destination for exports. 
    Customs had previously provided such data for a fee but
suspended this service in April. [nL4N1TN1KS]
    A search of the data showed China imported 9,641,673
kilograms, or just 9,642 tonnes, of scrap copper from the United
States in September, the most recent month available. That was
down 80.1 percent from 50,243 tonnes of imports reported by
customs a year earlier.
    From January to September, scrap copper shipments from the
United States fell 13.8 percent, according to Reuters
calculations, to 335,636 tonnes. 
    China has been cutting imports of scrap and waste for
environmental reasons, and in August imposed a 25 percent tariff
on scrap material from the United States, one of its biggest
suppliers, as part of a tit-for-tat trade row between the
world's top two economies. [nL4N1V04E7]
    Partially replacing the U.S. volumes, scrap copper imports
from Japan in September more than doubled to 46,446 tonnes from
19,198 tonnes a year earlier. 
    Imports of U.S. scrap aluminium, which were also hit with a
25 percent tariff in August on top of an earlier 25 percent
retaliatory tariff in April, fell in September by 39 percent
from a year earlier to 33,880 tonnes. 
    In the January to September, shipments were down a more
modest 5.5 percent to 433,373 tonnes.
    Meanwhile, the data also revealed that countries as far
apart as Iceland, India and Cameroon have been buying Chinese
alumina this year as China has been making rare exports of the
aluminium raw material to cash in on a favourable arbitrage to
international markets. 
    China's alumina exports surged more than fivefold from
August to more than 165,000 tonnes in September. [nL3N1X339M]
    The newly available data showed Iceland imported 39,524
tonnes in September, while India took 36,721 tonnes, Malaysia
29,199 tonnes, Russia 28,133 tonnes and Cameroon 16,400 tonnes.

SINGAPORE, April 20 (Reuters) - The front-month arbitrage spread firmed on Friday after data
this week showed fuel oil inventories in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) oil hub climbed to
their highest level since Dec. 21, while Singapore inventories of the fuel fell to their lowest
since early June. 
    The May East-West arbitrage spread rose to about $13.50 a tonne on Friday, up from about $13 in
the previous session, broker sources said.
    The tighter supplies in Singapore also helped boost the May 380-cst fuel oil time spread to
about $1.10 a tonne on Friday, from about 75 cents a tonne in the previous session, the sources
said. 
    Meanwhile, cash premiums of 380-cst fuel oil cargoes rose to a near three-month high of $1.40 a
tonne on Friday amid firm demand for cargoes of the fuel. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Weekly fuel oil stocks in the ARA oil and storage hub rose by 152,000 tonnes to a 17-week high
of 1.135 million tonnes in the week ended April 19, data from Dutch consultancy PJK International
showed. [ARA/]
    - Fuel oil stocks rose by over 15 percent in the absence of any exports onboard a very large
crude carrier (VLCC), which typically carry 270,000 tonne cargoes, PJK's Lars van Wageningen said.
[nL8N1RW5R8]
    - Compared with last year, ARA fuel oil inventories were 4 percent higher and were above the
five-year average of 960,000 tonnes for this time of the year. <STK-FO-ARA> 
    - Incoming fuel oil cargoes into the ARA hub originated from Estonia, Norway, Poland, Russia and
the United States, the data showed.
    - Fuel oil stocks in the Fujairah storage hub this week were also higher, rising 2 percent to a
three-month high of about 1.288 million tonnes in the week to April 16, data via S&P Global Platts
showed. [nL3N1RV40X]
    - By contrast, Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories fell 9 percent to a more than
10-month low of about 2.678 million tonnes in the week ended April 18, despite lower net imports,
official data showed. [nL3N1RW3GU]
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Five cargo trades totalling 100,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil were reported in the Singapore
trading window, the highest daily volume since March 12.
    - Hin Leong bought all five cargoes at premiums of about $1.40 to $1.50 a tonne to Singapore
quotes, lifting three from Trafigura and two from Glencore. 
    - By comparison, 380-cst fuel oil cargoes on Thursday traded at a premium of $1 a tonne. 
    - A total of 203,000 tonnes of fuel oil cargoes exchanged in the Singapore window this week, up
from 180,000 tonnes in the previous week.

SINGAPORE, Sept 10 (Reuters) - Asia's front-month time spread edged slightly higher on
Monday in a sign of stabilising market sentiment after steady losses over the past month. 
    The 380-cst Oct/Nov time spread was trading at about $4 a tonne, up from about $3.70 a tonne
on Friday, broker sources said. 
    Higher arbitrage supplies into Asia have weighed on market sentiment since around
mid-August, but steady demand and lower regional output due to refinery maintenance is expected
to limit further losses, trade sources said.

SINGAPORE, Sept 10 (Reuters) - Asian refining margins for jet fuel slipped on Monday after
registering their biggest percentage gain in two months last week, but traders remained
optimistic about stronger demand over the next few months.
    Jet cracks <JETSGCKMc1>, which rose 5 percent last week, were at $15.92 a barrel over Dubai
crude during Asian trading hours, against $16.03 on Friday.
    Cash differentials for the aviation fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> narrowed discounts to 30 cents a
barrel to Singapore quotes on Monday, compared with a 31 cent discount on Friday.
    The jet fuel market is a little slow at the moment, but overall sentiment is on the bullish
side because fourth-quarter demand is around the corner and supply is relatively tight, trade
sources said.
    During winter months in the northern hemisphere, typically from around the fourth quarter,
demand in the region picks up for kerosene used in heating. Kerosene and jet fuel belong to the
same grade of oil products, with jet fuel margins determining the profitability of both.
    Meanwhile, cash premiums for 10ppm gasoil <GO10-SIN-DIF> edged lower on Monday to 57 cents a
barrel to Singapore quotes, partly hurt by weaker bids and offers in the physical market.
    The prompt-month time spread, however, widened its backwardated structure and prevented a
wider slip in cash differentials.
    On Friday gasoil premiums were at 59 cents a barrel, the highest since S&P Global Platts
switched the benchmarks in gasoil grades in January to maximum sulphur content of 10 ppm
sulphur, from 500 ppm sulphur previously. 
    Inventories for middle distillates in Singapore have climbed in the past two weeks but are
still much lower than a year ago, which is providing price support, market watchers said.
    Singapore onshore middle distillate stocks rose by about 10 percent in the week to Sept. 5
to 11.4 million barrels, which is about 15 percent lower than a year ago, International
Enterprise (IE) data showed last week. [O/SING1]
    The crack for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10SGCKMc1>, which has gained about 4
percent in the past month, dipped to $16.33 a barrel over Dubai crude on Monday, from $16.44 on
Friday.

discount of $2.65 a barrel to the balance of September Singapore quotes.

loan, sources told LPC, a fixed-income news service. [nL5N1VW0PZ]
    - China's crude oil imports rose 6.5 percent in August from a month earlier to their highest
since May, boosted by a rebound in demand from smaller, independent refiners, customs data
showed on Saturday. [nL3N1VU04X]
    - Oil prices rose on Monday as U.S. drilling stalled and investors anticipated lower supply

    NEW YORK, Sept 5 (Reuters) - U.S. crude oil exports eased
slightly to 2.1 million barrels per day (bpd) in July from a
record 2.2 million bpd in June, foreign trade data from the U.S.
Census Bureau showed on Wednesday.
    The United States lifted a 40-year ban on crude oil exports
in late 2015 and since then tankers filled with U.S. oil have
landed in more than 30 countries. 
    In July, 18 countries purchased U.S. crude, the data showed.
    The United States exported crude to Peru and Dominican
Republic for the first time in over a year in July, the data
showed. 
    Shipments to Peru were about 26,000 bpd while Dominican
Republic purchased about 16,000 bpd of U.S. crude. Both
countries received crude from the U.S. for the first time since
May last year. 
    Meanwhile, China, the biggest buyer in June, dropped to
second place in July, behind Canada. 
    Crude exports to Canada were 420,000 bpd while shipments to
China fell to about 384,000 bpd in July from a record 510,000
bpd in June. 
    Still, other top buyers were from Asia, including Taiwan,
which imported a record at about 143,000 bpd, and Japan which
bought a record 89,000 bpd.
    India and Thailand purchased 102,000 bpd and 78,000 bpd
respectively. 
    Top European buyers were Britain, which bought 142,000 bpd
and the Netherlands, which imported 75,000 bpd.
    Exports to United Arab Emirates were 84,000 bpd and exports
to France were 51,000, while Spain purchased 49,000 bpd of U.S.
crude.

SINGAPORE, Aug 8 (Reuters) - Time spreads and refining margins of 380-cst fuel oil firmed on
Wednesday, despite limited trade activity, clawing back losses in the previous session.
    This came as Singapore's weekly onshore fuel oil inventories fell for a third straight week
to a more than nine-year low of 14.348 million barrels, or about 2.141 million tonnes, in the
week ended Aug. 7, data from International Enterprise Singapore showed on Wednesday.
[nL4N1UZ3HN]
    Time spreads of 380-cst fuel oil for Sept/Oct bounced back to a premium of about $5.50 a
tonne on Wednesday after slipping to a near three-week low of $5 a tonne on Tuesday, broker
sources said. <FO380SGSDMc2>
    The Sept 380-cst barge crack to Brent crude was also slightly higher at about minus $8.45 a
barrel, from minus $8.60 a barrel on Tuesday, the sources said.
    Prospects of fresh arbitrage supplies into Singapore this week weighed on market as traders
anticipated supply shortages in the city state may soon begin to ease.
            
    INVENTORIES
    - Singapore residual fuel stocks are now at their lowest since July 2009 after falling 3
percent, or 451,000 barrels, or 67,000 tonnes, in the week to Aug. 7. <STKRS-SIN>
    - This came despite higher weekly fuel oil net imports into Singapore in the week to Aug. 7
which rose 91 percent from the week before to 467,000 tonnes.
    - On average, however, Singapore fuel oil net imports stood at 751,000 tonnes per week in
2018.
    - Demand for marine fuel oil in Singapore may have contributed to the latest decline in
weekly stocks, two trade sources said.
    - Singapore fuel oil inventories have been hammered by months of below-average arbitrage
flows into Singapore as cargoes were diverted to the Middle East to meet strong seasonal demand
there for power generation.
    - But as Middle East demand starts winding down around the start of next month, and fresh
supplies began to emerge this week from regional suppliers there, the downward pressure on
Singapore supplies may soon end.
    - This week's onshore fuel oil inventories were 39 percent lower than a year ago.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to China topped the week ended Aug. 7 at 61,000
tonnes, followed by Bangladesh at 46,000 tonnes and New Caledonia at 40,000 tonnes.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Italy at 154,000 tonnes, followed
by the UAE at 129,000 tonnes, Iraq at 102,000 tonnes and Russia at 83,000 tonnes.
    - Fuel oil imports into Singapore from the UAE were at a nine-week high in the week to Aug.
7.

LONDON, March 18 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe edged up on Friday, buoyed largely by strong
export demand to West Africa.
    
    * Nigeria is set to ramp up the amount of crude oil it swaps
for vital gasoline imports by more than a third as it grapples
with the worst economic crisis in years. [nL5N16P4FW]
    * State oil company NNPC agreed deals with seven refining
companies - ENI, Essar, Litasco, Total, Cepsa, Societe Ivorienne
de Raffinage (SIR) and Vitol refining arm Varo, with local
partners - to take oil in exchange for gasoline imports,
according to traders and other sources close to the
negotiations. 
    * Firming demand for exporting low-octane gasoline to West
Africa is boosting demand for naphtha, used as a blending
component in the motor fuel.
    * New bookings of reformate and high-octane blending
components to China for May delivery have sharply dropped in
recent days. April-arrival volumes are expected to remain above
500,000 tonnes.
    * India's gasoline consumption is surging and has become one
of the fastest-growing components of global oil demand.
[nL5N16Q3EX]
    * Exxon Mobil reported unplanned flaring due to a breakdown
at its 149,500-barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery in Torrance,
California, according to a filing with state pollution
regulators. [nENN2ZL3CM]
    * The gasoline-producing unit at Shell's joint-venture
316,600 bpd Deer Park, Texas, refinery has been out of
production since Wednesday night when a leak was discovered in a
pipe on the unit, according to sources familiar with plant
operations. [nL2N16Q01I]

window. Bids emerged at $381 a tonne fob ARA.

Thursday. Gunvor sold to BP, Shell, Rolympus and others.

with $82-$90 discounts on Thursday.

SINGAPORE, March 21 (Reuters) - Asia fuel oil markets started the week on a high note on Monday
with 380cst spot premiums reaching their highest levels in almost nine months on the back of sustained
buying interest, traders said. 
    380cst spot premiums rose 48 cents to $3.27 a tonne above Singapore quotes, the highest since June
23. 
    Strong buying interest also contributed to the strengthening of 380cst front month time spreads
with total transacted volumes reaching more than 1 million tonnes in the swaps markets, more than 60
percent of which were for the April-May time spread contracts, traders said. 
    Time spreads for the April-May contracts strengthened from their Friday discount of approximately
$1.50 a tonne to less than $1 a tonne below Singapore quotes on Monday. 
    Seven deals were reported on Monday totalling 140,000 tonnes of fuel oil. 
    The buyers of today's cargoes, however, were slightly more varied, traders said. 
    Glencore, Petrochina and Vitol each purchased two cargoes of 380cst fuel oil, while Gunvor bought
a seventh cargo of 180cst fuel oil. 
    Since the start of the March trading play, 4.28 million tonnes of fuel oil cargoes have exchanged
hands in the Singapore Market on Close price assessment process by Platts, industry sources said.
[nL3N16P041]
    
    CHINA IMPORT DATA:
    Imports of fuel oil into China, the world's largest consumer of fuel oil, fell 19 percent to 2.3
million tonnes during the first two months of the year, official customs data provided by China's
General Administration of Customs showed. [nEAP222934] [nEAP222935]
    In February, total fuel oil imports were down 36 percent compared with last year, while exports
fell 17 percent, the data showed. 
    Demand for fuel oil in China has been on a steady decline since last year when Beijing allowed
independent 'teapot' refiners to import crude for the first time to encourage competition and boost
private investment. [nL3N1031SX]
    Despite the decrease in overall imports, the customs data showed imports of Singapore fuel oil to
China were up 92 percent during February and 57 percent in the first two months of the year to 292,000
tonnes and 741,000 tonnes, respectively.
    Singapore was the lead exporter of fuel oil to China in February, followed by Malaysia with
206,000 tonnes and Saudi Arabia with 130,000 tonnes. 
        
    TENDERS AND AWARDS:
    Korea Western Power Co Ltd has bought 45,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil from Daewoo
International Corp as well as 45,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil from Hanwha Corp. [nL3N16T1S9]
    Both cargoes are slotted for arrival in April.
    
    RELATED NEWS:
    Saudi Aramco Chief Executive Amin Nasser said his company will continue to invest in upstream and
downstream sectors, expecting an upwards adjustment in oil prices to begin by the end of 2016.
    Nasser said the Saudi oil giant is looking to expand its downstream investments in China,
Malaysia, India, Vietnam and Indonesia. He was speaking at the China Development Forum in Beijing on
Monday. [nB9N16N00V]

SINGAPORE, May 18 (Reuters) - Low sulphur diesel cash differentials jumped on
Thursday on the back of firm demand from India, though a build-up in inventory of
diesel and jet fuel in Singapore capped gains, trade sources said. 
    
    - VIETNAM AND INDIAN PURCHASES: Vietnam's top fuel importer Petrolimex bought
three cargoes totalling 105,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for loading from
Singapore or Malaysia at a premium of 70 to 75 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes,
traders said. 
    Indian Oil Corp bought three cargoes of 40ppm sulphur diesel for delivery in
June from Vitol and Totsa at a premium of about $3.20 a barrel on a delivered basis,
traders said. This could not be confirmed immediately with the relevant companies. 
    - SINGAPORE STOCKS: Singapore onshore middle distillates stocks jumped by 14
percent to a two-month high of 13.157 million barrels in the week to May 17, latest
data from International Enterprise showed. <O/SING1>
    Diesel shipments from Singapore and Malaysia fell compared with a week ago while
imports of the fuel rose from India, South Korea and Iran, contributing to the build
up in stocks, the data showed. 
    Vietnam also shipped about 38,000 tonnes of diesel to Singapore in an unusual
move, the data showed. 
    - LIGHT CYCLE OIL SHIPMENTS RESUME TO CHINA: China has resumed imports of light
cycle oil (LCO) after buyers cancelled shipments in April, as a planned Chinese
consumption tax has not been announced, four industry sources said this week. 
[nL4N1IK310]
    Less than 1 million tonnes of LCO are being shipped from South Korea to China in
May and June, compared with a peak of 2 million to 3 million tonnes, said two of the
sources, both from South Korean refiners. The lower volumes reflects cautious
buyers, they said.
    Premiums have also dropped to below $1 a barrel on a free-on-board (FOB) Korea
basis for the cargoes, compared with a peak of about $6 a barrel earlier this year,
and $2 to $3 a barrel in April, the sources added.
    - WEST AFRICA'S MOVE TO CLEANER FUELS: West Africa's move towards cleaner fuel
from July could open up opportunities for Asian traders and mop up excess supply of
low sulphur diesel in the region, traders and refining sources said. [nL4N1IK26N]

    - SINGAPORE CASH DEALS: Two gasoil deals, no jet fuel trades. 
    - Gunvor sold two cargoes of 150,000 barrels each of 10ppm sulphur diesel for
loading between June 2 and June 6 to Vitol at a premium of $1 a barrel to the
average of June 1-June 7 Singapore quotes.

LONDON, May 16 (Reuters) - Gasoline benchmark refining
margins in northwest Europe declined on Tuesday for a second
session, weighed by slowing exports to the U.S. East Coast.
    * The arbitrage from Europe to the U.S. East Coast was
marginally open but tanker bookings were limited as traders were
wary of slowing demand in the key hub.
    * Motorists logged 272 billion miles on U.S. roads and
highways in March, a 0.8 percent increase from last year,
according to data released Tuesday by the U.S. Department of
Transportation.[nL2N1II0ZM]
    * Around 400,000 tonnes of gasoline and blending component
are expected to head from northwest Europe to China in May, a
marked increase from the previous months, traders said. 
    * The global oil market is rebalancing and the pace at which
supply and demand are falling into line is picking up, even if
inventories still fail to reflect the impact of OPEC supply
cuts, the International Energy Agency said on Tuesday. 
[nL8N1II210]
    * Saudi Arabia's state-run oil company Saudi Aramco said on
Tuesday it had signed a joint development agreement with Chinese
defence conglomerate China North Industries Group Corp (Norinco)
for a refining, petrochemical and retail project.[nL8N1II4PN]

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, May 17 (Reuters) - Singapore fuel oil refining margins against Brent and
Dubai crude trended higher on Wednesday to near multi-month highs, lifted by falling crude
prices, seemingly narrower regional supplies and firm demand for cargoes and bunker fuels. 

    REFINING MARGINS
    - While some industry participants attributed shrinking onshore Singapore inventories
as one factor contributing to improved refining margins, others said this was not
necessarily indicative of narrowing supplies because there were ample volumes stored on
vessels off Singapore. 
    - Reuters data showed that the June 180-cst fuel oil crack narrowed its discount to
Dubai crude <FO180SGCKMc1>, to minus $2.90 from minus $3.09 on Tuesday and compared with a
four-month low of minus $2.83 on Friday. 
    - Similarly, the June 180-cst refining margin's discount to Brent crude <FO180BRTCKMc1>
was minus $4.02 a barrel, close to Friday's four-month low of minus $3.99.   
    - In Europe, refining margins on FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil to Brent crude for June
on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) were at about minus $7.20 a barrel by 5pm Singapore
time (0900 GMT) on Wednesday, compared with about minus $7.50 in the previous session,
trade sources said.
    - European fuel oil refining margins are at the highest level at this time of the year
for five years, one trader said.
     
    ARBITRAGE FLOWS 
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia are expected to close at about 6.5 million tonnes
in May, compared with the previous month's revised total of about 6.65 million tonnes,
buoyed by strong arrivals from the Middle East for a third consecutive month and despite
below-average Western arrivals, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed.
[nPGEj7p9Wa]    
    
    TENDERS
    - Bangladesh Petroleum Corp (BPC) has received offers from 11 companies for fuel
supplies in the second half of the year, with Unipec and Vitol looking set to win the
tender with the lowest offers on middle distillates and fuel oil, a BPC official said.
[nL4N1IJ274]
    - Thailand's Bangchak Petroleum is offering two 40,000 tonne cargoes of vacuum
low-sulphur waxy residue (VLSWR) for loading May 23-25 and June 2-6 at Sriracha.
[nL4N1IJ1EI]
    - Saudi's Samref refinery awarded Shell an 80,000 tonne cargo of 650-cst HSFO for
delivery at Yanbu May 23-25 at a discount of $17 a tonne to 380-cst Singapore quotes FOB.
[nL4N1IJ31J]
            
    OTHER NEWS
    - More than 20 tankers carrying crude and fuel oil are anchored off the ports of
China's eastern Shandong province because onshore storage tanks are full, according to
trade sources and shipping data on Thomson Reuters Eikon. [nL4N1IJ292]

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, May 22 (Reuters) - Sentiment in Asia's fuel oil market continued to decline
on Monday, depressing the 380-cst June East-West (EW) arbitrage spread on the
Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) which slipped to its lowest this year after seven
consecutive sessions of losses.
    While recent onshore fuel oil inventories in Singapore have fallen below average levels
since the start of the year, traders said sentiment was weighed down by concerns that
supplies could quickly bounce if inventories stored recently aboard vessels around the
city-state are reintroduced.

    ARBITRAGE SPREAD 
    - The ICE-traded June EW spread was trading at about $12 a tonne on Monday after
reaching an intra-day low of $11.50 a tonne. 
    - By comparison, the June arbitrage spread was trading at about $15 a tonne at the
start of Monday in the previous week. 
    - Other factors contributing to the sharp decline in arbitrage spreads include weaker
Singapore 380-cst fuel oil prices and lower tanker freight rates over the past week. 
    - On Friday, Reuters reported that freight rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs)
were set to slide further this week, falling below tanker break even costs on routes from
the Middle East, as too many ships chase too few cargoes. [nL4N1IL3B6]
    - Reuters data showed the front-month EW spread <FOSGEWMc1> between FOB Singapore
180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil and FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil with maximum 3.5 percent
sulphur slipped to its lowest since September 2016 at $20.25 a tonne, down 75 cents from
the previous session.
    - On May 4, the June EW spread was at its highest since mid-January at $29.25 a tonne,
before beginning its nearly uninterrupted decline to Monday's 7-month low. 

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Two cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of
180-cst fuel oil. No deals for 380-cst fuel oil were reported.
    - Mercuria bought both cargoes, taking one from Total and another Shell. 
    - Mercuria has now bought 1 million tonnes of fuel oil in the window since the start of
May. 
    - A total of 1.52 million tonnes of fuel oil have traded in the window since the start
of May, against 3.821 million tonnes in April.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Indonesia's Pertamina is offering up to 80,000 barrels of vacuum residue with a 0.35
percent maximum sulphur content for loading on June 5-6. [nL4N1IO2LK]
    The tender closes on May 23 and is valid until May 26. 
    - Bahrain's Bapco is offering 60,000 to 80,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a
maximum sulphur content of 4 percent loading on June 23-27 form Sitra in a tender closing
on May 23. [nL4N1IO2MZ]

its Natref refinery, which is a joint-venture with Total. Total was not immediately
reachable for comment.

the issue, traders said. India is a typical supplier of diesel to South Africa from
Asia.

to 40,000 tonnes each of 40ppm sulphur diesel for delivery in JNPT, Kandla, Chennai

maintenance, they added, though this could not be confirmed. <MDIS/TENDA>

for loading in June to BP at a premium of between 60 cents and 65 cents a barrel to
Middle East quotes, down from the premium of about 65 cents a barrel it sold to
Vitol earlier, traders said.

jet fuel for delivery in June 16 to June 17 from Saudi Aramco at a premium of $1.20

confirmed.

0.25 percent sulphur gasoil for delivery into Dumai between June 11 and June 15 at
a discount of 30 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes, traders said, though this
could not immediately be confirmed.

    SINGAPORE, May 23 (Reuters) - The arbitrage spread and front-month time spread for 380-cst
fuel oil recovered some losses made in the previous session but sentiment remained little
changed amid concerns that fuel oil stored in vessels around Singapore could quickly flood the
market. 

    ARBITRAGE SPREADS
    - The ICE-traded June 380-cst EW arbitrage spreads edged 25 cents a tonne higher to $11.75 a
tonne by 5:30 p.m. Singapore time (0930 GMT) on Monday. 
    - On Monday, the June arbitrage spread sank to $11.50 a tonne in the previous session, its
lowest this year, after seven consecutive sessions of losses. [nL4N1IO3KG]
    - Industry sources expected June arrivals into Singapore to total between 4 to 4.5 million
tonne in June, down from May's estimate of about 5 million tonnes. 
    - The ICE-traded 380-cst June/July time spreads also recovered some of their losses,
narrowing its discount by 30 cents a tonne from the previous session to minus $1.50 a tonne.
    - Open Interest volumes in the 380-cst contract held steady near the 2017 high for any
380-cst fuel oil futures contract at just under 11 million tonnes. 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Two cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst
fuel oil along with another 20,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Gunvor sold the 180-cst fuel cargo to Mercuria and Glencore sold the 380-cst cargo to
Coastal. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    BREAK-BULK BUNKERS MARKET
    - Tighter availabilities of 380-cst fuel oil after nearly three months of elevated trade
activity in cargoes of the fuel has lifted spot premiums of the break-bulk ex-wharf parcels
industry sources said. 
    - Industry sources said prompt offers for ex-wharf parcels were mostly made by 'smaller'
suppliers in recent days as larger ones focused more on servicing their contracted volumes of
bunker fuels.
    - Over the past two weeks, ex-wharf premiums have averaged above $4 a tonne to Singapore
quotes compared with an average of about $2.50 to $3 a tonne to Singapore quotes in the
preceding two weeks. 
        
    TENDERS
    - BP bought 35,000 tonnes of 380-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) from India's IOC for
delivery on June 7-9 at a discount of about $5 a tonne to the average of Platts MOPS and Argus
quotes for 380-cst fuel oil, FOB basis. [nL4N1IP35U]
    - Taiwan's Formosa sold 10,000 tonnes of pyrolysis fuel oil to Simosa at a premium of about
$34 a tonne to Singapore 180-cst fuel oil quotes, FOB basis, for loading on June 4-6.
[nL4N1IP2V3]
    - Indonesia's Pertamina is offering several term cargoes of vacuum residue and 180-cst fuel
oil for delivery over July to September. [nL4N1IP2DR]

with one to two 200,000 barrel cargoes of 180-cst HSFO.
