SINGAPORE, May 16 (Reuters) - Jet fuel cargoes are likely to remain
predominantly in the east instead of being shipped to the United States as the
trade route is not profitable at present, traders said on Tuesday. 
    
    - ARBITRAGE FOR JET FUEL: Arbitrage to ship jet fuel from South Korea to the
United States is not profitable for June, traders said.
    It was slightly profitable for May but now is no longer profitable, one of
them said.
    This could build up the region's jet fuel supply, the source added.     
    - ADNOC TERM TALKS: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) is negotiating
with companies to sell diesel and jet fuel through term contracts for loading
between July 2017 and June 2018, traders said. [nL4N1II1K8]
    It is seeking a premium of about $1.30 a barrel to Middle East quotes for
diesel and a premium of about 90 cents to $1 a barrel for jet fuel, one of them
said.
    Buyers want a premium of about 70 cents a barrel for the jet fuel cargoes,
the trader added. 
    - CHANGE IN BENCHMARK: Commodity pricing agency Argus plans to lower the
sulphur content of its benchmark gasoil assessments in Singapore and the Middle
East from January 2018 onwards, a senior company official told Reuters on
Tuesday. [nL4N1II30K]
    Argus is proposing that its free-on-board Singapore and Middle East 10
parts-per-million (ppm) sulphur gasoil price assessments will become the basis
against which it prices other gasoil grades.
    - NEW OIL TERMINAL IN MYANMAR: Puma Energy Asia Sun, a joint venture between
Puma Energy and local firm Asia Sun Energy, is looking to move beyond storage
services in Myanmar and include oil products' distribution in the country, said a
top executive. [nL4N0V120K]
    The company opened the country's newest and largest oil products' terminal on
May 6 with a storage capacity of 91,000 cubic metres in Thilawa.
    The terminal, which cost $92 million, is designed to hold mostly middle
distillates, with 29,000 cubic metres of space for gasoil and 21,000 cubic metres
for jet fuel.    
        
    - SINGAPORE CASH DEALS: Two gasoil deals, no jet fuel trades. 
    - Winson Oil sold 250,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil to Total at a
premium of 20 cents a barrel to the average of May 31 to June 6 Singapore quotes.
    - Total bought 150,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for June 2-June 8
loading from Freepoint at a premium of 30 cents a barrel to the average of June 1
to June 7 Singapore quotes.

differentials in the Mediterranean region fell on Monday while

driving market sentiment to an extent, analysts said.

tonnes, while India's domestic demand for the transportation fuel usually remains weaker during

week. [nB9N1RY01N]

    * Price formula based on Argus WTI, Brent swaps, DFL

 (Adds quotes, details)
    By Florence Tan and Jessica Jaganathan
    SINGAPORE, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Taiwanese state oil refiner
CPC Corp has signed its first long-term deal to buy U.S. crude,
a company official said on Monday, one of only a few such deals
by Asian buyers who normally purchase U.S. oil on the spot
market.
    The deal for delivery in 2019 will ensure that Taiwan,     
which became a regular importer of U.S. oil at the end of 2017,
will get a steady supply of U.S. crude for five months from
early next year.
    CPC has awarded a tender to an unnamed U.S. trading company
and it will receive 2 million barrels of U.S. West Texas
Intermediate (WTI) Midland crude every month between February
and June, the official said.
    Taiwan is Asia's third-largest buyer of U.S. oil, with
monthly imports averaging 3.6 million barrels between January
and November, according to Refinitiv Eikon data. The imports -
to replace African supplies snapped up by China - are mostly
offloaded at Kaohsiung, CPC's import terminal, the data showed.
    Separately, CPC has also bought 6 million barrels of spot
WTI Midland crude to be delivered to Taiwan in January priced at
a premium to dated Brent, the official said.
    The term deal is also significant as the counterparties may
have found a way to bridge a gap in pricing U.S. oil to Asia.
    U.S. oil purchases in Asia have so far been opportunistic,
based on arbitrage opportunities. Most buyers still prefer
Middle East and Russian oil priced on cheaper Dubai benchmark or
Atlantic Basin cargoes priced on Brent, rather than U.S. oil
priced off WTI.
    The cargoes will be priced at a differential to a formula
comprising the Argus WTI Houston crude price assessment, Brent
swaps and dated to front-line swaps (DFL), the CPC official
said.
    This allows CPC to convert WTI prices to dated Brent, which
is one of two price markers used in Taiwan's domestic oil
pricing, he added.
    The Argus WTI Houston price assessment is a U.S. Gulf coast
benchmark price assessment determined by trades done at a
differential to the CME Group's Nymex Cushing futures price,
according to price agency Argus Media.
    The DFL is a monthly cash settled swap based on the
difference between the Platts daily assessment price for Dated
Brent and the daily settlement price for the Brent front-month,
or first line, futures contract, according to the
Intercontinental Exchange Inc <ICE.N>.
    Global oil exchanges and CME Group Inc <CME.O> have also
recently launched new WTI futures contracts for oil deliverable
in Houston, Texas. [nL2N1WZ1VR]

    SINGAPORE, Dec 9 (Reuters) - Asia's fuel oil refining margin for the benchmark
180-centistoke narrowed its discount to Dubai crude on Friday, lifted by bullish
sentiment, as industry participants expected supplies to remain tight into the new year
amid firm demand.    
    Singapore's Jan. 180-cst fuel oil discount to Dubai crude <FO180SGCKMc1> narrowed by
81 cents a barrel on Friday to minus $1.49 cents a barrel.
    Traders said market fundamentals were bullish given tightening structural supplies of
on-specification fuel oil as well firm demand for use in marine fuels and power
generation.
    Since the start of the week, the January refining margin recouped some of the losses
made in the week before following the OPEC-Russia deal to cut production by a combined 1.2
million barrels per day which sparked a rally in crude prices. [nL8N1DV1UH]
    The front month refining margins were up $1.26 a barrel over the past week from minus
$2.75 a tonne on Monday. 
    Following the OPEC-Russia deal in the previous week, the refining margin fell from a
near five-year high of minus 6 cents a tonne on Nov. 30 to minus $3.27 a tonne in the
following two days as crude prices rallied. [nL4N1DX3F9]

    ARA INVENTORIES:
    Fuel oil stocks independently held in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub soared
17 percent, or 108,000 tonnes, to a total of 733,000 tonnes in the week to Dec. 8, data
from Dutch consultancy PJK International showed. [ARA/]
    Despite rising to a two-week high in the week to Dec. 8, fuel oil inventories in the
ARA were 38 percent lower from the same time last year. 
    Traders also expected fuel oil inventories in the ARA to remain depressed as an open
arbitrage window meant cargoes would be shipped to Singapore. 
    One very large crude carrier (VLCC) left the ARA hub on Dec. 4 to Singapore with a
cargo of fuel oil, while another VLCC was expected to load and depart on Dec. 9, PJK data
showed.

    SINGAPORE, Dec 13 (Reuters) - Values of near-dated 380-cst fuel oil flat price swaps
traded on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) were higher on Tuesday amid hedging activity
by buyers of the fuel who were looking to take advantage of the dip in prices in the
previous session caused by declines in crude oil prices, fuel oil brokers and traders
said. 
    Flat price swaps for the 380-cst fuel for the first three months of the new year were
40 cents to 50 cents higher by 1730 Singapore time (0930 GMT) amid active trading on ICE,
the sources said. 
    Meanwhile, traders said premiums of the Dec/Jan time spreads for the 380-cst fuel
eased due to a lack of buying interest for the contracts which expire in two days.
    In the physical markets, cash premiums held steady despite muted trading activity in
the Platts window on Tuesday.
    Two cash deals were reported in the window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel
oil and another 20,000-tonne cargo of  380-cst grade. 
    
    RELATED NEWS:
    - China's Guangdong Zhenrong Energy Co will submit a plan by April to revamp a
century-old oil refinery in Curacao, as it seeks to secure a $5.5 billion project that
will give China a foothold in the Caribbean's second-largest oil refinery. [nL4N1E32X1]
    - U.S. shale oil production is set to end a five-month decline in January, the U.S.
government said on Monday, a move that comes just days after OPEC and rival producers
agreed to reduce their crude oil output in an effort to boost prices. [nL1N1E71G3]

SINGAPORE, Dec 9 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil differentials were
steady on Friday, edging slightly higher after a slowdown in
physical gasoil cargo trades, traders said.
    There were no deals traded after 27 cargoes changed hands on
Thursday, they added. 
    Winson Oil has sold more than 9 million barrels of 500ppm
sulphur gasoil since Dec. 1. The Hong Kong-based company earlier
bought about 14.5 million barrels of the fuel from mid-September
to end-November, Reuters calculation of trade data showed. 
    Hin Leong has sold more than 4 million barrels of the fuel
since Dec. 1, compared with nearly 7 million barrels bought
since mid-September.       
    Operations at the 65,000 barrels per day (bpd) CCR2
hydrocracker at Royal Dutch Shell's 404,000 bpd Pernis refinery
will be reduced from Friday as part of industrial action, FNV
union spokesman Egbert Schellenberg said. [nL5N1E3521]
    Capacity at the hydrocracker was expected to be cut by
around 20 percent, he said. The lower production would also
impact other units, including the associated crude distillation
unit.
    This could encourage more diesel cargoes to be shipped from
Asia to Europe, traders said. 
    The east-west spread, firm for most of the year and keeping
barrels in Asia, started weakening recently, they added. 
    Shipping fixtures showed BP had provisionally chartered the
Zaliv Vostok to ship 90,000 tonnes of ultra low sulphur diesel
from Singapore to Europe.
    Valero also provisionally chartered the Polar Cod to ship
60,000 tonnes of jet fuel from South Korea to the U.S. West
Coast, shipping fixtures showed. 
    In the Middle East, Tasweeq has offered gas-to-liquid (GTL)
jet fuel for January loading, traders said.
    Tasweeq's exports of jet fuel are expected to rise once
production from its new Ras Laffan 2 condensate splitter
stabilises, they added.     
    
    TENDERS: 
    -  Tasweeq has offered about 40,000 tonnes of GTL jet fuel
for Jan. 22 to 27 loading. The tender closes on Jan. 13 and is
valid until Jan. 14.

SINGAPORE, Dec 15 (Reuters) - A drop in inventory drove up differentials for gasoil on
Thursday, while demand for jet fuel remains robust, industry sources said. 
    Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks fell 12 percent on the week to a more than
five-month low of 11.955 million barrels in the week to Dec. 14, latest data from International
Enterprise Singapore showed.
    Diesel shipments to Bangladesh, Malaysia and Brunei increased from the week before, while
imports of the fuel from South Korea and Saudi Arabia ceased, contributing to the drawdown of
inventory, the data showed.
    Workable arbitrage economics to ship diesel from east to west was likely drawing South
Korean cargoes, an industry source said. 
    Jet fuel demand is expected to be robust from North Asia due to a cold winter boosting
demand for heating fuel kerosene, while global air travel is also likely to be higher end of the
year, traders said. 
    Japan's kerosene demand is likely to rise nearly 10 pct in December from a year ago due to a
rebound after warm winters last year, president of the Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ)
Yasushi Kimura said on Thursday.  [nL4N1EA2Y6]
    The country's kerosene demand in November was about 30 percent higher than last year due to
a slew of cold waves, said Kimura, who also serves as chairman of Japan's top oil refiner JX
Holdings. 
    The spike in kerosene demand is also boosting medium-range tanker rates, a shipbroker said.
Japan typically imports kerosene from South Korea where companies lease storage. 
    Caltex Australia expects its 2016 jet fuel volumes to grow by about 5 percent, which is
expected to boost jet fuel demand. [nL4N1EA1EG]
    The company also said it was increasing sales volumes of its differentiated diesel to mining
and transport customers, although the volumes are small.     
    Global jet fuel consumption is expected to increase 11.6 percent to 7.168 million
barrel-per-day by 2025, boosted by strong outlook in passenger transport and air freight in the
U.S. and China aviation sectors, oil analyst BMI Research said. [nL4N1EA1UD] 
    But globalisation hitting a plateau and faltering growth in Middle Eastern hub are expected
to weigh on jet fuel demand, BMI said. 
    China's November diesel output gained 0.6 percent on year to 15.27 million tonnes, data from
the National Bureau of Statistics showed on Thursday. [nB9N1DX02G]
    Chinese refiners typically ramp up exports of oil products in December as they try to
utilise their leftover quotas, but diesel demand is expected to be higher ahead of the Chinese
New Year period, traders said.

SINGAPORE, Dec 13 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differentials slipped on
Tuesday on ample supply of the fuel though exports from India and China have
slowed this month compared with previous months, traders said. 
    The cash differential for the benchmark 500ppm sulphur gasoil fell by 13 cents
to minus 28 cents a barrel on Tuesday, the lowest since Dec. 7, Reuters data
showed.           
    India's Essar Oil likely sold up to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for
Jan. 6 to 10 loading to Litasco at a premium of 70 cents a barrel to Middle East
quotes, an industry source said. But this could not immediately be confirmed with
the relevant companies.
    India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) likely sold a jet
fuel cargo for Feb. 3 to 5 loading to Shell at a discount of $1.10 a barrel to
Singapore quotes, the source added, but this could also not be confirmed. 
    India's fuel demand rose 12.1 percent in November compared with the same month
last year, with diesel sales going up 10.5 percent year-on-year, according to
latest data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) of the oil
ministry. [nENNGC70SB]
    Some spot demand appeared from Sri Lanka with Ceylon Petroleum Corp seeking a
jet fuel cargo for December delivery, traders said.
    Refineries in the Middle East are expected to ramp up exports of diesel and
jet fuel once they return from maintenance, traders said.
    Most of the diesel cargoes are likely to remain in the Middle East, however,
as they do not meet more stringent European specifications for colder weather,
they added.
    Jet fuel cargoes could head to Europe as the arbitrage economics looks more
viable, one of them said.
    Thailand's PTT has yet to finalise a term deal to sell 9 cargoes of 500ppm
sulphur gasoil for 2017, an industry source said. 
    It is not clear why the company has delayed awarding the tender which closed
in late November.     
    
    TENDERS:

over Dec. 20 to 21. The tender closes on Dec. 15 and is valid for 48 hours. 

    CASH DEALS: One gasoil deal, no jet fuel trades.
    - Glencore bought 170,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for Jan. 2 to 6
loading from Hin Leong at $63.70 a barrel.

LONDON, Sept 11 (Reuters) - Nigerian crude prices rose on
Tuesday after refiner BP bought more October-loading cargoes in
the daily trading window and bid for a number of different
grades.
    
    NIGERIA
     * BP bought two more cargoes of October-loading crude from
Vitol. The company bought one cargo of mid-October loading Bonny
Light at $1,55 a barrel above dated Brent and a late
October/early November-loading cargo of Qua Iboe at $1.75 above
the dated price, three traders said.
    * BP was also said to have bid for the four largest grades,
Bonny Light, Qua Iboe, Forcados and Bonga, as high as $1.75 a
barrel, from closer to $1.65 on Monday. 
    * BP built up a fairly sizeable position in October-loading
cargoes of the four grades, which are linked to the swaps
market, in the last week or so. 
    * Traders at two refiners said this had tightened
availability to the point where sellers were loath to cut their
prices, even though half the October loading programme is still
up for sale, with just days to go before the release of the
November schedules. 
    
    ANGOLA
    * Fewer than a dozen cargoes of October loading crude are
still unsold. ENI and Unipec were still said to be offering
Olombendo, with the latter also said to be offering cargoes for
delivery in China. 
    * Among the crude still available are one or two cargoes of
Gindungo held by Total.
    
    TENDERS
    * Indian Oil Corp is running a tender to buy West African or
U.S. crude for loading on Nov. 5-15. The tender closes on
Tuesday and the result is likely to emerge on Wednesday.
    * Indonesia's Pertamina recently bought two 950,000-barrel
cargoes of Bonny Light from Shell and Chevron for October
arrival.

for physical cargoes of the fuel. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories slipped 2 percent, or 499,000 barrels (74,000
tonnes), to a two-week low of 22.031 million barrels (about 3.29 million tonnes) in the week ended
March 7, data from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed on Thursday. [O/SING1]
    
    SINGAPORE INVENTORIES 
    - The lower Singapore fuel oil stocks came amid a 76 percent drop in net imports of the fuel
into the city-state from the week before to a seven-week low of 279,000 tonnes, the data showed.
    - Over the past week, Singapore fuel oil imports were at a two-week low of 1.08 million tonnes,
while exports were at a 12-week high of 798,000 tonnes, the data showed.
    - Compared with year-ago levels, onshore fuel oil inventories were 21 percent lower.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to Hong Kong topped the week at 174,000 tonnes, followed
by China with 172,000 tonnes and Japan with 119,000 tonnes, the data showed.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Russia at 457,000 tonnes, followed by
Iraq at 216,000 tonnes, Thailand at 61,000 tonnes and Greece at 50,000 tonnes, according to the
data. 
    - Fuel oil imports into Singapore from Russia were at a four-week high, while imports from the
Netherlands were absent for a second consecutive week, according to the data. 
    - Fuel oil inventories in Singapore have averaged 21.982 million barrels (3.28 million tonnes) a
week since the start of 2018.

LONDON, Jan 17 (Reuters) - Diesel barge differentials in
Northwest Europe weakened on Tuesday to their lowest level in
four months amid weak demand and rising imports.
    
    * Demand in the region remained limited. Very low water
levels along the Rhine river severely limited barge loading
capacity into Germany and Switzerland, traders and brokers said.
    * Strong demand for heating oil in the Mediterranean opened
an arbitrage from the Baltic Sea, with Glencore booking two
cargoes of high sulphur gasoil, according to traders.

recent days from refinery outages in the regions as well as in
the Middle East and Russia.[nL4N1F63DR]

refinery within 48 hours, with the impact from the fire limited
to propylene production.[nL4N1F63KW]
    * Traders nevertheless expected the refinery's diesel and
jet production to be impacted due to the usually lengthy
start-up of units.
    * The Ruwais outage has already resulted in the deferral of
the delivery of at least two cargoes in January.
    * BP is shipping a 250,000 tonne cargo of diesel onboard the
VLCC Eco Seas into Rotterdam, according to Reuters ship tracking
and traders. [nL5N1F63KQ]

of $14 a tonne fob ARA to the February Low Sulphur Gasoil

Singapore on Tuesday evening has been extinguished, the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) said on
Wednesday.
    - The cause of the fire is not yet known and is under investigation, an SCDF spokesman told
Reuters on Wednesday.
    - The fire-struck storage tank was said to have contained fuel oil, according to a Tankstore
employee.
    - The terminal resumed normal operations around 5 am Singapore time (2100 GMT) on Wednesday with
only the fire-damaged fuel oil tank taken offline, another Tankstore employee said. 
    - The fire is not expected to have any material impact on fuel oil trading and supply in
Singapore, two Singapore-based fuel oil traders said.
    - Singapore-based Tankstore operates the terminal on Pulau Busing, an island off Singapore's
southwest coast. It has a total capacity of 2 million cubic metres, or 112 tanks, to store petroleum
and petrochemical products, according to the company's website.

drop in U.S. inventories, while ARA trading activity remained
strong.

million
barrels, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll
for a 2.0 million-barrel drop, EIA data said. [EIA/S]

onshore

    * A number of tankers were booked to ship gasoline from
Europe to
the U.S. East Coast after a period of little activity, according
to shipping data.
    * Still, barge trading activity in the ARA hub remained
strong,

in the Argus platform at 468,000 tonnes so far, according to
traders.

this month, according to shipping data.

gasoline each in northwest Europe or the Mediterranean along the
route.

weeks

the oil-rich country closer to its goal of fuel
self-sufficiency.

naphtha. [nL8N1R230S]

SINGAPORE, Dec 14 (Reuters) - Asia's cash differentials for
10 ppm gasoil strengthened on Friday, helped by firmer buying
interest in the physical market and potential arbitrage
opportunities.
    Cash discounts for 10ppm gasoil <GO10-SIN-DIF> narrowed to
58 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes as the December/January
spread narrowed by 6 cents to 71 cents per barrel. The cash
differentials were at a discount of 78 cents a barrel on
Thursday.
    The East-West arbitrage, especially from the Gulf or India
to Europe, was open and should prompt more gasoil shipments to
the West, which is low on inventories and uses gasoil for winter
heating, trade sources said.
    But steep clean freight rates might keep the arbitrage flows
in check, they added.
    There could still be a surge in East-West distillate flows
if the European heating oil market gets bullish as rising water
levels on the Rhine river started to re-open inland German
markets for shipping, Vienna-based consultancy JBC Energy said .
    Gasoil stocks independently held in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) refining and storage hub fell
for the ninth straight week in the week to Thursday, data from
Dutch consultancy PJK International showed. [nIGN4551EC]
    The exchange of futures for swaps (EFS), which determines
the gasoil price spread between Singapore and Northwest Europe
<LGOAEFSMc1>, was around minus $19 per tonne on Friday,
according to Refinitiv Eikon data. 
    The arbitrage is usually profitable when the EFS trades at
about minus $18 a tonne or below, traders said.
    Refining margins for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content
<GO10SGCKMc1> rose to $14.01 a barrel over Dubai crude, from
$13.90 per barrel on Thursday. 
    Meanwhile, refining margins for jet fuel <JETSGCKMc1>,
climbed to $15.56 a barrel over Dubai crude during Asian trading
hours. They were at $15.48 per barrel a day earlier. 
    Cash discounts for the aviation fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> widened
on Friday, hurt by weaker deals in the physical market. They
were at a discount of $1.07 a barrel to Singapore quotes,
compared with a discount of 77 cents a barrel on Thursday.
    
    
    ARA STOCKS
    - Gasoil stocks in ARA refining and storage hub <STK-GO-ARA>
fell to 1.9 million tonnes in the week to Dec. 13, versus 2
million tonnes in the preceding week, according to data from
Dutch consultancy PJK International. [ARA/]
    - Gasoil inventories fell 5 percent as demand increased
along the river Rhine, where water levels recovered after some
rainfall, allowing barge shipping to return to normal levels.
    - Low gasoil imports and exports to West Africa also
contributed to the decrease, PJK said.
    - Jet fuel inventories <STK-JET-ARA> dipped 1.7 percent to
621,000 tonnes, PJK data showed.
    - Compared with year-ago levels, jet fuel stocks were down
about 8 percent, while gasoil inventories were about 1 percent
lower.
    
     
    SINGAPORE CASH DEALS
    - One gasoil deal, two jet fuel trades.
    - Vitol bought 150,000 barrels of 500ppm gasoil from Shell
for Dec. 29-Jan. 2 loading at a discount of $1.50 a barrel to
the first half of January Singapore quotes.
    - Shell sold 100,000 barrels of jet fuel to Hin Leong for
Dec. 29-Jan. 2 loading at a discount of $1.30 a barrel to
Singapore quotes.
    - Hin Leong bought 100,000 barrels of jet fuel from Unipec
for Jan. 3-7 loading at a discount of $1.10 a barrel to
Singapore quotes.
    - For more information, please click [O/AS]       
    
    
    OTHER NEWS
    - Oil prices slipped on Friday after China reported slower
economic growth, pointing to lower fuel demand in the world's
biggest oil importer, although market sentiment was supported by
supply cuts agreed last week by major crude producers. [O/R]
    - China's November refinery production eased off highs
touched in the previous two months, official data showed on
Friday, as plants scaled back runs amid swelling oil product
inventories and slowing sales. 
    Refineries processed 50.46 million tonnes of crude oil last
month, or 12.28 million barrels per day, up 2.9 percent from the
same month last year, but down from a record of 12.49 million
bpd in September, data from the National Bureau of Statistics
showed. [nL3N1YI1Q6]

refining margins fell slightly on Friday but held near a
one-year high, supported by tight supplies in the Atlantic
basin.

Mediterranean continued to ramp up as refineries return to
normal operations, with more than 600,000 tonnes now expected to
arrive on the route in October, according to traders.

and the Middle East to Europe remain high, with several cargoes
booked over the past day, according to shipping data.

remain low in October due to refinery maintenance in the
country, keeping supplies in the region tight, traders said.

to seasonal refinery maintenance.

the product seen weak, according to data from Dutch consultancy
PJK International. <ARA/>

the first half of this year, the first time since 2009, the
European Automobile Manufacturers Association said this week.

gasoline car sales rising by nearly 10 percent from the first
half of 2016, making up for a roughly 4 percent loss in diesel
car sales in the same period, the group said.[nL8N1MA39D]

SINGAPORE, Sept 26 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differentials edged higher on
Tuesday as traders expected demand for the fuel to pick up in the fourth quarter,
industry sources said. 
    
    - RISING DIESEL DEMAND: A massive surge in demand for diesel fuel this year has been
the main driver for higher crude oil consumption in 2017 along with buying to fill up
strategic petroleum reserves, an executive from oil major Royal Dutch Shell said on
Tuesday.
    Diesel demand for 2017 is making up about 50 percent of the year-on-year demand
growth in oil products after only making up 27 percent of the increase in last year's
consumption, said Mike Muller, Shell's vice president, crude trading and supply, at an
industry conference in Singapore. In 2016, gasoline and other oil products pushed the
demand higher, he said.
    The recent hurricane that shut down refiners along the Gulf Coast of the United
States also contributed to higher demand for diesel and other middle distillates, he
said. Hurricane Harvey dumped record amounts of rain on the Texas and Louisiana coasts
and caused about 4.4 million barrels per day of refining capacity to close, or about 24
percent of the U.S. total.
    To make up for the shortfall in oil products, output buyers have turned to European
refiners while European buyers have raised imports from processors in Asia.
    - INDIA OFFERS JET FUEL: India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) has
offered 40,000 tonnes of jet fuel for early November loading, traders said. 
    - CHINA'S SHIPMENTS TO NORTH KOREA: China's fuel exports to North Korea fell in
August, along with iron ore imports from the isolated nation, as trade slowed after the
United Nations' latest sanctions, but coal shipments resumed after a five-month hiatus,
customs data showed on Tuesday. [nL4N1M72QL]
    China's gasoline shipments to North Korea were kept at a trickle at 180 tonnes, up
slightly from July's 120 tonnes but down from almost 5,000 tonnes a year earlier. Diesel
were just 170 tonnes, compared with zero tonnes a year ago.
    At the end of June, Reuters reported China National Petroleum Corp <CNPET.UL> (CNPC)
suspended sales of gasoline and diesel to North Korea over concerns CNPC would not get
paid for its goods. The measures are still in place, sources familiar with the matter
say.
    Fuel prices in the country have surged in recent months, people familiar with the
matter say.

SINGAPORE, Sept 27 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil cash
differentials remained steady on Wednesday as China allocated a
fourth round of quotas to export oil products including diesel
and jet fuel.
    
    - CHINA QUOTA: China has allocated 1.644 million tonnes of
refined product export quotas to two state-owned companies,
China National Petroleum Corp and Sinopec, a source familiar
with the plan said on Wednesday. [nL4N1M83EL] 
      That would bring total export quotas to about 37.4 million
tonnes for 2017.
    - CHINA'S DIESEL DEMAND: China's refined oil products stocks
fell 1 percent in August from end-July to the lowest level since
December while crude oil inventories also dropped in August, the
official Xinhua OGP industry newsletter said on Wednesday.
[nL4N1M83BS]
      Diesel led the drop among refined oil products with a 1.7
percent fall to 7.33 million tonnes, the lowest since December
2016, reflecting eased glut in domestic market.
      Diesel demand from industrial, mining and infrastructure
projects improved in August, Xinhua said.
     INDIA REFINING CAPACITY: India needs to double its refining
capacity by 2040 to meet rising fuel demand as an expanding
middle class buys more passenger vehicles and its economy grows,
a top refinery official said on Wednesday. [nL4N1M8357]
     India's refining capacity must increase to 465 million
tonnes by 2040, from about 230 million tonnes currently, and
investments are already being made, said Shrikant Madhav Vaidya,
Indian Oil Corp's <IOC.NS> executive director of operations.
     The major drivers for India's fuel demand growth will be 
continued strong sales of passenger vehicles, substitution of
liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) as a cooking fuel, growing
urbanization and the country's demand for infrastructure and
consumer goods, he told the S&P Global Platts APPEC conference
in Singapore.
    Apart from demand for gasoline in passenger cars, India's
appetite for jet fuel is also expected to grow as the country 
modernises and expands its airport capacity, with plans to build
about 200 new airports in the next 10 years, B. Anand, chief
executive officer of private Indian refiner Essar Oil Ltd said.

SINGAPORE, Sept 25 (Reuters) - Backwardation in the front-month time spread of Asia's 380-cst fuel oil rose to
its widest May 5 on Monday, boosted by bullish market momentum due to expectations of fewer arbitrage arrivals in
October and November, industry sources said. 
    The 380-cst Oct/Nov time spread <FO380SGSDMc1> rose to $3 a tonne, up from $2.75 a tonne in the previous session.
    While the near-term supply and demand market fundamentals appear supportive, some traders said that the market
may have become overbought given ample inventories in key storage hubs and no significant shortage of supplies
following the end of peak summer demand. 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Two cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - PetroChina sold two 20,000 tonne cargoes of 380-cst high-sulphur fuel (HSFO) to Hin Leong at a premium of about
$1.75 to $1.90 a tonne to Singapore quotes, sources said. 
    - The weaker deal values on Monday dragged on 380-cst fuel oil cash differentials <FO380-SIN-DIF>, which were at
$1.89 a tonne above Singapore quotes, down from a near three-month high of $2.14 in the previous session. 
    - On Friday, strong buying interest saw three 380-cst fuel oil cargoes change hands at premiums as high as $2.35
a tonne to Singapore quotes, boosting cash premiums of the fuel to their highest since June 29. 
    - A total of 2.082 million tonnes of fuel oil has traded in the window since the start of the month, against
1.402 million tonnes in August.

percent sulphur content to UAE's Enoc, industry sources said. [nL4N1M62UY]
    - The cargo is due for loading on Oct. 9-11 loading from Chennai and was sold at a $5 to $9 per tonne discount to

northwest Europe firmed on Tuesday as export demand remained
supported by refinery maintenance and other issues.

with flows to the U.S. East Coast at roughly 1 million to 1.5
million barrels, the same level as before Hurricane Harvey,
traders said.

autumn.

Middle East.

the region. [nL2N1M61SR]

stockpiles faster than expected, putting the global market
firmly on track to rebalance, senior oil executives said on

of peak winter demand for kerosene when refiners maximise the yield of kerosene in favour of jet
fuel, trade sources said.
    
    - JET FUEL: China Aviation Oil is seeking 105,000 tonnes of jet fuel for delivery in
November, much higher than the 25,000 tonnes it typically seeks every month, traders said.
    - OIL STOCKS: Singapore middle distillates stocks fell by 6 percent to a three-month low of
10.485 million barrels in the week to Sept. 27, data from International Enterprise showed.
<O/SING1>
    - CHINA QUOTA: China has allocated 1.644 million tonnes of oil product export quotas for the
fourth quarter to two state-owned oil majors, China National Petroleum Corp and Sinopec, a
document reviewed by Reuters showed. [nL4N1M91B2]
      The quota awards, shown in a Ministry of Commerce document, mean China's total oil product
exports for 2017 will fall to about 37.4 million tonnes, some 19 percent lower than last year. 
      The volume was well below industry expectations, and Beijing had also excluded other
refiners CNOOC and Sinochem Corp in this round of quotas.

recover from weeks of disruptions due to Hurricane Harvey, offering respite to buyers in Latin
America and Europe. [nL8N1M867Z]
      The gradual resumption of operations in the region that has become a major oil export hub
has prompted a drop on both sides of the Atlantic in benchmark gasoline and diesel refining
margins, which measure profit from converting crude into fuels.
    - SWISS SINGAPORE TO EXPAND: Commodity trader Swiss Singapore Overseas aims to double its
revenue over the next few years by expanding its oil and coal portfolio, and is ramping up
hiring, a senior company official told Reuters. [nL4N1M926F]
      The firm, part of the Indian multinational conglomerate Aditya Birla Group, posted a
turnover of $4.6 billion in its last financial year and is set to achieve $5 billion this year,

sidelines of the S&P Global Platts APPEC conference in Singapore.

SINGAPORE, Dec 27 (Reuters) - The front-month 380-cst barge fuel oil crack moved on Thursday
to its narrowest discount to Brent crude for three weeks, despite a spike in crude oil prices
since Wednesday.
    The narrower crack reflected expectations of tighter fuel oil arbitrage volumes in January,
compared with December, trade sources said. 
    The crack discount was at minus $6.27 a barrel to Brent crude, up from minus $7 a barrel in
the previous session; and the narrowest discount since Dec. 5, Refinitiv data showed.
<HFOFARAACMc1>
    Meanwhile, Singapore fuel oil inventories slipped 3 percent to a two-week low in the week
ended Dec. 26, even though net import volumes increased and held above the 2018 weekly average,
official data showed. [nL3N1YW1O0]
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Onshore fuel oil stocks declined 613,000 barrels (about 91,000 tonnes) to 20.2 million
barrels, or 3.015 million tonnes, in the week to Dec. 26, data from Enterprise Singapore showed.
[O/SING1]
    - Higher bunker fuel demand in Singapore amid falling outright fuel oil prices may have led
to lower stock levels, trade sources said.
    - In the week to Dec. 19, Singapore fuel oil stocks hit a near seven-month high 20.813
million barrels, or 3.106 million tonnes. [nL3N1YP3GD]
    - Net fuel oil imports in the week to Wednesday came in at 975,000 tonnes, up 3 percent from
the week before, and were well above the 2018 weekly average of 802,000 tonnes.
    - However, this week's onshore fuel oil inventories were 20 percent lower than a year
earlier.
    - Net exports of fuel oil to Hong Kong topped the week ended Dec. 26 at 137,000 tonnes,
followed by the Philippines at 87,000 tonnes and Bangladesh at 60,000 tonnes.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Russia at 313,000 tonnes, followed
by Venezuela at 258,000 tonnes, Mexico at 156,000 tonnes and Cyprus at 134,000 tonnes.
    - Singapore's fuel oil imports from Venezuela in the week to Dec. 26 were at their highest
since the week to Feb. 13 when 285,000 tonnes were imported, the data showed.
        
    TENDERS
    - South Korea's EWP bought 30,000 tonnes of 540-centistoke (cst) LSFO with a maximum 0.3
percent sulphur content for delivery into Ulsan over Jan. 8-12 from Hanwha at a discount of
about $7 per tonne to the monthly average of Singapore 180-cst HSFO quotes for December on a CFR
basis.
    - The discount for EWP's latest LSFO requirement is somewhat unusual as LSFO typically
trades at a premium to HSFO since it is a cleaner burning fuel.
    - However, the monthly average of physical spot fuel oil prices published in December are
higher than the daily price as oil product markets have dropped in line with a plunge in crude
oil prices this month and that accounts for the discounted price differential, said a
Singapore-based fuel oil trader.
    - The utility last purchased LSFO cargoes in August, taking in two 40,000-tonne cargoes at
premiums of about $65 to $75 per tonne to Singapore quotes on a CFR basis.
    - Taiwanese refiner CPC has offered two catalyst fractionator bottom (CFB) cargoes totalling
up to 30,000 tonnes for export over Jan. 10-20, in a tender closed on Dec. 27 with next day

SINGAPORE, Dec 27 (Reuters) - Asia's cash differentials for 10ppm gasoil firmed on Thursday,
but stayed within sight of the widest discounts for this year as abundant supplies and subdued
buying interest continued to dampen market fundamentals.
    Cash discounts for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10-SIN-DIF> were at 93 cents a
barrel to Singapore quotes on Thursday, compared with a discount of 98 cents a barrel on
Wednesday -- the widest levels since Singapore's benchmark was shifted to 10ppm gasoil in
January this year from 500ppm gasoil previously. 
    Battered by inflated stock levels in the region, cash differentials for the benchmark gasoil
grade have steadily declined since hitting this year's peak of $1.86 a barrel on Oct. 24, when
demand was stronger. 
    Middle distillate inventories in Singapore climbed 414,000 barrels to a nearly nine-month
high of 11.5 million barrels in the week to Wednesday, data from Enterprise Singapore showed on
Thursday.
    Refining margins for 10ppm gasoil <GO10SGCKMc1> dipped to $13.35 a barrel over Dubai crude
during Asian trade, from $13.92 a barrel on Wednesday.
    Diesel exports from China, which is pivotal for the overall supplies in the region, would be
higher in December compared with November, trade sources said. China exported 1.23 million
tonnes of diesel in November, down 37.5 percent year-on-year. [nB9N1YH02N]
    In order to consume the additional export quotas and for better margins amid weaker domestic
prices, China's December export volumes for diesel would be much bigger, a middle distillate
trader said.
    Last month, China released 2 million tonnes of additional fuel export quotas for this year,
taking total 2018 quotas to about 48 million tonnes. [nL4N1Y23EL]
    Cash discounts for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> widened to $1.21 a barrel to Singapore quotes on
Thursday, as against a discount of $1.19 a barrel on Wednesday.
    Jet fuel refining margins <JETSGCKMc1> fell to $14.79 a barrel over Dubai crude on Thursday,
from $15.45 a barrel on Wednesday. 

     
    SINGAPORE INVENTORIES
    - Singapore onshore middle-distillate stocks rose 3.7 percent to 11.5 million barrels in the
week to Dec. 26, according to data from Enterprise Singapore released on Thursday. [O/SING1]
    - Since the start of the year Singapore middle-distillate inventories have averaged 9.6
million barrels a week, compared with a weekly average of about 12 million barrels in 2017,
Reuters calculations showed.
    - Overall, onshore middle-distillate inventories were about 46 percent higher than a year
ago.

SINGAPORE, March 12 (Reuters) - Asia's jet fuel cash premiums extended losses on Monday, falling
to a near five-week low as slowing seasonal demand weighed on bullish sentiment that boosted the jet
fuel market to multi-year highs since the start of the year, trade sources said. <JET-SIN-DIF> 
    Japanese demand for the middle distillate fuel for the remainder of March still prevalent in the
market but its imports of the fuel in April was so far seen as limited due to ample supplies and
receding winter demand, trade sources said. 
    Meanwhile, sustained buying interest for physical cargoes of 10ppm gasoil helped firm cash
differentials of the fuel to its widest premium in a month at 20 cents a barrel on Monday, up from
an 18 cents a barrel premium on Friday and a 2018 low of minus 6 cents a barrel in the previous
week. <GO10-SIN-DIF> 
    
    TENDERS 
    - India's Essar Oil sold up to 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel loading from Vadinar over April 21-25
to Unipec at a premium of about $1.50-$1.60 a barrel to Middle East quotes on an FOB basis, sources
said.
    - Essar Oil is also offering up to 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel loading from Vadinar for June 16-30
delivery in a tender closing on March 9 with same day validity, sources said.
    - For more information, please see [MDIS/TENDA].
    
    CPC OUTAGE 
    - Taiwan's government has ordered state-run refiner CPC Corp to partially suspend operations at
a refinery in the southern city of Kaohsiung, a government official told Reuters on Monday, after a
fire injured three workers. [nL3N1QU1EW]
    - CPC's Talin refinery in Kaohsiung was hit by an explosion on Saturday and part of its
production will be suspended until further review, said Chung Mon Pi, chief secretary of the city's
Labour Affairs Bureau.

oil trader Winson Oil went on a buying spree, trade sources said.

those from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) under a different free trade

route from South Korea to southern Vietnam is likely to incur higher freight charges making
their cargoes more expensive, traders said.

gained in the week to Nov. 11, latest data from the Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ) showed.

week and was up 3 percent from a year ago, the data showed, indicating rising demand.

supported by spot demand from Sri Lanka and Vietnam, trade sources said.

for 2018, multiple trade sources said. [nL3N1NR2B0]

SINGAPORE, Nov 15 (Reuters) - Despite the slide in crude oil prices, the front-month fuel oil
crack edged lower on Wednesday, likely as a result of selling pressure from refinery hedging, industry
sources said. 
    Premiums of the front-month time spread for the mainstay 380-cst fuel oil were also slightly
narrower as trade activity remained lacklustre, a broker source said.
    This came as fuel oil inventories in the Fujairah oil hub slipped for a second straight week to a
near nine-month low in the week ended Nov. 13, official data showed. 
             
    INVENTORIES
    - Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil inventories fell 3.7 percent, or 321,000 barrels
(about 48,000 tonnes), from a week ago to 3.320 million barrels (1.24 million tonnes) in the week
ended Nov. 13, data via S&P Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - Fuel oil inventories in Fujairah were last lower in the week to Feb. 20 when they stood at 8.053
million barrels  (1.2 million tonnes).
    - Weekly Fujairah fuel oil inventories averaged 10.36 million barrels (or 1.55 million tonnes)
since records began at the start of the year.
    
    ARBITRAGE
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for November are poised to close at nine-month high of
around 7 million tonnes, boosted by recovering Western arrivals, near record-high inflows from the
Middle East and 11-month high intra-Asia volumes, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed
on Tuesday. [nPGE2x6Gga]
    - Western arrivals rebounded to a three-month high of 3.7-3.8 million tonnes, boosted by unusually
high volumes from the United States amid an open U.S.-Asia arbitrage that has also extended into
arrivals for December, with just under 3 million tonnes notionally assessed for the month so far, the
assessments showed. 
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Two cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel
oil.
    - Petco supplied all of Wednesday's cargoes, selling one 20,000-tonne cargo of the fuel to Hin
Leong and another 40,000-tonne cargo to BP. 
    - The volume of fuel oil cargoes Petco sold on Wednesday is the largest in daily volume trade it
has made in the physical window in 2017, and the company's first cargo sale since June 21. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - India's IOC is seeking up to 15,000 tonnes of high-sulphur fuel oil for import into New
Mangalore on Dec. 15-19 in a tender closing on Nov. 20, industry sources said. 
    - Indonesia's Pertamina offered in a term tender to export four to six 80,000 barrel cargoes per
month of vacuum residue with a maximum 0.35 percent sulphur content from Plaju over either the first
quarter, or first half, of 2018, sources said. 
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA]

SINGAPORE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The second-month East-West (EW) arbitrage spread of 380-cst fuel
oil narrowed to a near two-month low on Monday as arrivals into Singapore through December are
expected to improve, industry sources said. <FOSGEWMc2>
    Recently, weaker fuel oil prices in northwest Europe due to rising Russian fuel oil exports
after the conclusion of the refinery maintenance season there, as well as relatively weaker tanker
charter rates, have encouraged some suppliers to lock in fresh supplies into Singapore, sources
said. 
    
    ARBITRAGE FLOWS
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for November were poised to close at nine-month high of
around 7 million tonnes, boosted by recovering Western arrivals, near record-high inflows from the
Middle East and 11-month high intra-Asia volumes, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research
released on Nov. 14 showed. [nPGE2x6Gga]
    - Western fuel oil arrivals into Singapore are estimated at about 3.8-4.3 million tonnes for
November and about 3-4 million tonnes in December, industry sources said.
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Four cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 80,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel
oil.
    - Hin Leong bought three 20,000-tonne cargoes of the fuel from Glencore, while BP bought a
fourth similar cargo from Shell. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Saudi's Samref refinery is offering up to 90,000 tonnes of 650-cst to 700-cst high-sulphur
fuel oil loading from Yanbu between Nov. 29 and Dec. 3 in a tender closing on Nov. 20, industry
sources said. 
    - Taiwan's Formosa is offering up to 13,000 tonnes of pyrolysis fuel oil with a  maximum 0.2
percent sulphur content loading on Dec. 1-3 from Mailiao in a tender closing on Nov. 21 with same
day validity, sources said.
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
        
    DOWNSTREAM SAUDI 
    - Saudi Aramco has shut down its 80,000 barrel per day crude oil refinery in Jeddah
indefinitely, converting the complex into a hub for oil products distribution, it said on Sunday.
[nL8N1NP095]
    - The shutdown is not expected to cause a shortage of oil products in Saudi Arabia as Aramco
will meet demand from other refineries, industry sources said earlier on Sunday.
    - Until the Jizan refinery is up and running in 2018, oil products will be supplied to Mecca
from Aramco's facilities in Yanbu and Rabigh.

    ROSNEFT, CEFC DEAL
    - Rosneft had signed an oil supply deal with CEFC China Energy Company Ltd, Russia's largest oil
producer said in a regulatory filing on Monday, confirming a Reuters report last week. [nL8N1NQ0Z0]
    - Apart from extending Russia's lead over Saudi Arabia as China's top oil supplier, the deal
will make CEFC, a hitherto little-known fuel trader, a top-10 global oil merchant.
    - Rosneft said it would supply up to 60.8 million tonnes of oil over the five years starting
from January 1, 2018.

SINGAPORE, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil margin rose to the highest in
November boosted by spot demand from Vietnam and a supply outage in Australia, trade
sources said on Friday. 
    
    - VIETNAM DIESEL: Vietnam's top fuel importer, Petrolimex, is seeking its first
ultra low-sulphur diesel cargo, a tender document showed.
      From January next year, diesel automobiles produced, assembled or imported into
Vietnam are expected to meet Euro 4 fuel standards, which requires a sulphur content of
50ppm, prompting fuel importers to seek low sulphur diesel. 
      Petrolimex is seeking 35,000 tonnes of 10ppm sulphur diesel for loading between
Dec. 6 and Dec. 10. It is also seeking two cargoes each of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for
loading over Dec. 4 to 8, and Dec. 16 to 20. The tender closes on Nov. 20 and is valid
until Nov. 22.
    - AUSTRALIA REFINERY OUTAGE: Exxon Mobil said on Friday that there was no danger to
the community or environment after heavy gas flaring at an oil refinery near Melbourne
in Australia following an interruption to power.
      The oil giant said in a statement emailed to Reuters that it was working to
restore its Altona refinery to normal operations as quickly as possible.
      A spokeswoman for the Metropolitan Fire Brigade said the refinery was flaring
because of a power outage in the area, adding that this was normal practice.
      The refinery churns out up to 14 million litres of refined products per day, with
petrol making up about 60 percent of production, diesel 30 percent and jet fuel around
10 percent, according to the company's website.
    - INDIA OFFERS GASOIL:  Indian Oil Corp has offered seven cargoes of 27,000 to
29,000 tonnes each of 0.2 percent sulphur gasoil on a free-on-board basis for loading
over December to March. The tender closes on Nov. 17. 
      India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) has offered 80,000
tonnes of 50ppm sulphur gasoil for loading in December in a tender that closes on Nov.
21.

    Selling pressure has weighed on fuel oil cracks since the start of the week amid concerns of rising
Russian fuel oil exports following the end of major refinery maintenance work there, as well as improving
arbitrage flows into Singapore, industry sources said. 
    
    ARBITRAGE FLOWS 
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for November are on track to close at nine-month high levels of
above 7 million tonnes for the month, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research (TROR) showed on
Tuesday. [nPGE80slPa]
   - The flows are boosted by rebounding Western arrivals, near record-high inflows from the Middle East
and 11-month high intra-Asia volumes, the assessments showed. 
    - The Plata Sunrise, a Trafigura chartered VLCC tanker, has loaded up to 270,000 tonnes of fuel oil
from the Euro Tank terminal in Rotterdam and is due for arrival in Singapore on Dec. 31, shipping data in
Reuters Eikon showed.
    - Koch has placed on subjects the New Medal tanker vessel to load up to 270,000 tonnes of fuel oil
from Rotterdam around Dec. 21 for discharge into Singapore by end-January for a $3.6 million fee,
shipping data showed.
    
    WINDOW TRADES
    - Three cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Higher deal values on Wednesday, compared to the previous session, pushed cash premiums of the
380-cst fuel oil to a more than two-week high. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    - Meanwhile, aggressive offers for 180-cst cargoes in the window from Reliance weighed on cash
premiums of the fuel to a near two-week low. <FO180-SIN-DIF>
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details.

    - Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil inventories rose 16 percent, or 1.321 million barrels
(about 197,000 tonnes), from a week ago to an eight-week high of 9.641 million barrels (1.44 million
tonnes) in the week ended Nov. 20, data via S&P Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - Fuel oil supplies from Saudi, the UAE and Iran contributed to inventory build over the past week,
assessments by TROR showed. 
    - Weekly Fujairah fuel oil inventories averaged 10.34 million barrels (or 1.54 million tonnes) since
records began at the start of the year.
    
    TENDERS

Mailiao on Dec. 1-3 for discharge into an unspecified destination.

SINGAPORE, Nov 21 (Reuters) - Tighter spot availability of bunker grade 380-cst high-sulphur
fuel oil in Singapore boosted ex-wharf premiums of the fuel to their highest in about six weeks,
industry sources said.
    Singapore 380-cst fuel oil ex-wharf premiums have traded at a premium of around $3-$5 a tonne to
Singapore quotes over the past two weeks, up from about $1-$3 a tonne through most of October,
sources said.

oil and 20,000 tonnes of the 180-cst grade; the highest overall daily volume since Nov. 6.
    - Glencore sold 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil to BP and another 40,000 tonnes of the same
fuel to Vitol, charging both buyers a premium of $1 a tonne to Singapore quotes for the cargoes. 
    - Hin Leong bought the 20,000-tonne 180-cst fuel oil cargo from Gunvor at parity to Singapore
180-cst quotes.

maximum sulphur content of 2.59 percent into Pyong Taek on Dec. 9-16, in a tender closing on Nov.
27. 
    - The last time the power utility issued a tender to import a similar cargo of fuel oil was in
July for delivery over Aug. 7-11. 
    - India's Reliance is offering up to 40,000 tonnes of carbon black feedstock (CBFS) with a
maximum 1.2 percent sulphur content for Dec. 7-8 loading from Sikka, sources said. 
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].

at its 790,000 barrels-per-day refinery in Yeosu for planned maintenance in February, two industry
sources said on Tuesday. [nL3N1NR1XW]
    - The refiner will shut its No. 1, 125,000 bpd crude oil unit and a 53,000 bpd fluid catalytic
cracker (FCC) for about a month from early February, one of the sources familiar with the matter
said.

in August next year for a month's maintenance work, two trade sources said on Tuesday. [nL3N1NR2VS]

distillation unit, which has a capacity of 110,000 barrels per day, a hydrocracker and a 36,500-bpd
delayed coker, the sources said.

SINGAPORE, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Cash premiums of Asia's high-sulphur fuel oil edged higher on
Thursday amid improved deal values in the Singapore trading window, sources said.
    Meanwhile, despite sharply lower net imports of fuel oil into Singapore, onshore stocks of the
industrial fuel were virtually unchanged over the past week, official data from IE Singapore showed.
[O/SING1]
        
    INVENTORIES
    - Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories slipped just 0.3 percent, or 10,000 tonnes, to a
six-week low of 3.52 million tonnes in the week ended Nov. 15, the data showed.
    - This came as weekly net imports into Singapore fell to a three-month low of 0.43 million tonnes,
down 40 percent from a week ago.
    - Weekly Singapore fuel oil imports were at 684,000 tonnes, the lowest since February 2016 while
exports sank to an eight-month low of 256,000 tonnes, the data showed. 
    - Fuel oil inventories fell below their year-on-year levels for the first time in five-weeks,
standing at 2.4 percent below their year-ago levels.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to China topped the weekly list (168,000 tonnes); followed by
Papua New Guinea (2,000 tonnes) and India (200 tonnes).
    - Largest Singapore net imports originated from Russia (178,000 tonnes), followed by Venezuela
(140,000 tonnes), the U.S. (75,000 tonnes), and Malaysia (72,000 tonnes).
    
    ARBITRAGE FLOWS
    - Western fuel oil arrivals into Singapore are estimated at about 3.8-4.3 million tonnes for
November and about 3-4 million tonnes in December, industry sources said. 
    - The Gener8 Andriotis, a Socar chartered VLCC tanker, on Monday loaded up to 275,000 tonnes of
fuel oil from the Vopak's Europort terminal in Rotterdam and is due to discharge her cargo in Singapore
around Dec. 24, ship broker reports and ship tracking data in Reuters Eikon showed. 
    - Socar chartered the tanker vessel for a $3.6 million fee, the data showed. 

    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Four cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil
and another 60,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Cash differentials of both fuel oil grades edged higher on the back of higher deals values on
Thursday, sources said. 
    - Vitol sold to Gunvor one 40,000-tonne cargo of 180-cst fuel oil. 
    - Hin Leong bought two 20,000-tonnes cargoes of 380-cst fuel, one from Shell and another from
Trafigura. BP bought the remaining 20,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil from Shell. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - South Korean refiner GS Caltex is offering up to 80,000 tonnes of fuel oil with a maximum 4.5
percent sulphur content loading from Yeosu over Dec. 8-12 in an offer closed on Nov. 14, sources said. 
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].

    CHINA DATA 
    - China's fuel oil output in October rose 4.6 percent from last year to 2.38 million tonnes, data
from the statistics bureau showed on Thursday, as refiners pumped up oil products at faster pace in the
fourth quarter. [nB9N1NJ00F]

SINGAPORE, Nov 14 (Reuters) - The front-month fuel oil crack and time spread for the mainstay
380-cst fuel oil slipped on Tuesday despite weaker crude oil prices amid limited trade activity,
broker sources said. 
    Meanwhile, the front-month 180-cst time spread flipped back into backwardation on Tuesday. The
180-cst time spread flipped into contango on Monday, for the first time since Sept. 12, as ample
supplies of the fuel weighed, industry sources said.. <FO180SGSDMc1>

    CRACKS 
    - Fuel oil refining margins in Singapore in October closed 30 percent higher than the same time
a year ago, despite rising crude prices and may remain elevated as OPEC is expected to continue
propping up the oil price by withholding supplies of fuel oil rich grades. [nL3N1NG2ZS]
    - The higher margins provides an incentive for so-called simple oil refineries, which lack the
ability to upgrade fuel oil to gasoline and diesel, to maximise their output, preventing a drawdown
of high inventories.
    - Weekly fuel oil stocks in Singapore are 13 percent higher from the same time last year, while
inventories in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp hub are up 122 percent from a year ago, official data
shows. <STKRS-SIN>, <STK-FO-ARA>
       
    VENEZUELA WOES
    - Oil-dependent Venezuela's crude output dipped last month below 2 million barrels per day, its
lowest level in nearly three decades, global producer group OPEC said on Monday.
    - Venezuela's annual oil output was 2.373 million bpd in 2016 and 2.654 million in 2015,
according to the data it gives OPEC.
    - Venezuela is a key supplier of fuel oil, but its exports of the industrial fuel have declined
significantly, dogged by refinery outages as well as quality issues with the fuel oil it exports.
[nL1N1IC0W1] [nL3N1HL2CT]
    - Since the start of the year, Singapore imported a total of 3.29 million tonnes of fuel oil
from Venezuela, down 30 percent from the 4.69 million tonnes imported over the same period last
year, official data compiled by Reuters showed. 
        
    TENDERS
    - Oil traders Unipec and Vitol placed the lowest offers in a tender by Bangladesh Petroleum Corp
to buy up to 1.27 million tonnes of oil products for import in the first half of 2018, three
industry sources said on Tuesday. [nL3N1NK2GO]
    - Vitol made the lowest offer for fuel oil cargoes out of four other companies.
    - The Swiss oil trader placed an offer of $31.29 a tonne above benchmark fuel oil quotes for
120,000 to 160,000 tonnes of 180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil on a CFR basis.  
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - One cargo trade was reported in the Platts window after Vitol sold 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst
fuel oil to Gunvor, sources said.

as oil price agency switches its underlying gasoil grade in its benchmark prices to 10ppm

quotes, they said.

      Unipec, the trading arm of China's state-owned Sinopec, placed the lowest offer for the
gasoil and jet fuel cargoes beating six other companies, two of the sources said. 
      It placed an offer of $2.76 a barrel above benchmark gasoil quotes and $3.34 a barrel
above benchmark jet fuel quotes for 390,000 to 490,000 tonnes of 500 ppm sulphur gasoil and
50,000 tonnes of jet fuel, according to those two sources.
      The trader also placed an offer of $2.42 a barrel above benchmark gasoil quotes and $3.34
a barrel above benchmark jet fuel quotes for similar volumes of gasoil and jet fuel, they added.

LONDON, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Nigerian crude was offered a
touch lower on Thursday, under pressure from the persistent
overhang of unsold cargoes, although this surplus could soon
clear, given demand from Turkish and Asian refiners.

    NIGERIA AND ANGOLA
    * Vitol offered a cargo of Qua Iboe delivered into Rotterdam
in early December at a premium of $3.55 a barrel to dated Brent
on a CFR basis, which traders said equated to around $1.50 a
barrel FOB, a few cents lower than recent indications for this
grade.
    * Now that oil pricing agency Platts says it is considering
including other crudes in its dated Brent assessment, traders
said offers for WAF cargoes delivered in northwest Europe would
likely become more frequent.
    * India imported 336,500 bpd of Nigerian crude in September,
20.7 percent more than in August, according to data from
industry and shipping sources. But, highlighting the challenge
to light, sweet West African crudes from U.S. oil, imports in
September this year were nearly 40 percent lower than those in
September last year.
    * At the last count, there were around 25 cargoes left for
sale from the October and November programmes, marking very
little change over the last week. 
    
    RELATED NEWS
    * U.S. crude oil stockpiles rose last week for the third
consecutive weekly build as refineries continued to reduce
output for seasonal maintenance, while gasoline inventories grew
unexpectedly, the Energy Information Administration said on
Thursday. Crude inventories <USOILC=ECI> rose 6 million barrels
in the week to Oct. 5, compared with analysts' expectations for
an increase of 2.6 million barrels. [EIA/S]
    * OPEC sees the oil market as well supplied and is wary of
creating a glut next year, the group's secretary-general said on
Thursday, suggesting producers are in no rush to expand a June
agreement that raises output. [OPEC/M]
    * Africa's GDP growth is rising but it must do more to
solidify a fragile recovery and prepare for major disruptions in
the global economy, the International Monetary Fund's top
official for Africa said. [nL8N1WR2V2]
    
    
    TENDERS
    * Turkish refiner Tupras awarded a tender later for delivery
of 1 million barrels of light sweet crude to Total for a
shipment of Forcados delivering Nov 17-18, traders said.
    * Chevron won a tender from Indonesia's Pertamina for a
delivery of Escravos crude oil between Dec 3-5.  
    * Indian refiner HPCL was said to have issued a three-month
term tender for crude delivering between December this year and
March next year.    
    * IOC has issued a tender for light sweet crude for December
delivery that will be awarded on Thursday, traders said.

SINGAPORE, Aug 17 (Reuters) - The front-month East-West spread for 380-cst fuel oil fell for
a fourth straight session on Friday and hit its lowest in nearly two weeks, as industry
participants anticipated higher arbitrage flows into Singapore, trade sources said.
    While the improved supply outlook helped dampen bullish market sentiment in the past week,
concerns of contaminated bunker fuels in Singapore that emerged in July and a lack of finished
grade fuel oil may still lend support in the near term, the sources said. 
    The front-month 380-cst fuel oil arbitrage spread was at $21.25 a tonne on Friday, down from
$22 a tonne in the previous session and from $24.50 a tonne on Monday. <FO380SGEWMc1>
            
    INVENTORIES
    - Weekly fuel oil stocks in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) oil and storage hub edged
up 0.6 percent, or 6,000 tonnes, to a two-week high of 1.058 million tonnes in the week ended
Aug. 16, data from Dutch consultancy PJK International showed. [ARA/]
    - ARA inventories were largely steady this week despite the loading of a very large crude
carrier (VLCC) this week with fuel oil heading to Singapore, while another unspecified cargo
size departed for the Mideast Gulf, the data showed. [nL5N1V74T9]
    - ARA fuel oil imports in the week to Aug. 16 originated from the Baltics, France, and
Russia, the data showed.
    - Compared with last year, ARA fuel oil inventories were 25 percent higher and well above
the five-year average of 850,000 tonnes for this time of the year. <STK-FO-ARA>
    - This came as Singapore's onshore fuel oil inventories climbed to a three-week high of
2.279 million tonnes in the week to Aug. 15, snapping three weeks of declines and edging away
from a nine-year low in the previous week. [nL4N1V7386]
    - By contrast, weekly fuel oil inventories in the Fujairah hub fell from an eight-month high
to 1.387 million tonnes in the week ended Aug. 13. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - In the United States, inventories of the fuel rose 1 percent to a two-week high of 4.277
million tonnes in the week to Aug. 10. [EIA/D]

0.95 percent sulphur content for Sept. 16-30 delivery into Karachi.

180-cst quotes on a CFR basis.
    - PSO has largely ceased importing fuel oil since late June due to lower power generation

further details of the meeting.

of the issue.

Kazakh CPC Blend differentials eased against dated Brent in

their plans. They then tried to sell the cargoes in the market,
putting additional pressure on Urals prices.

    * There were no bids or offers for Urals loading from
Novorossiisk
port in October in the Platts window on Thursday, traders said.

    * Austria's OMV tried to sell 90,000 tonnes of CPC Blend
loading
from Yuzhnaya Ozereyevka on Oct. 27-31 at dated Brent minus
$1.10 a barrel, but failed to find a buyer though the offer was
15 cents a barrel lower than recent estimations, traders said.

    * Stranded cargoes on sale at big discounts - traders

    By Hallie Gu and Dominique Patton
    BEIJING, April 24 (Reuters) - Some of China's sorghum
importers have asked the government to waive the anti-dumping
deposits on U.S. exports for cargoes that are already on their
way to the nation, two sources familiar with the matter told
Reuters.
    The Ministry of Commerce last week slapped imports of
sorghum from the United States with a 178.6 percent deposit
starting from April 18 as a trade spat between the world's two
biggest economies escalates. Sorghum is a grain used in animal
feed and to manufacture liquor [nL3N1RU37T] 
    One of the sources said his company was pushing for Beijing
to impose the new tariffs only on cargoes that were loaded at
U.S. ports after April 18, to protect almost a dozen vessels
carrying U.S. sorghum that have already started sailing.    
    The other source said a group of companies that includes at
least one state-owned firm met with the Commerce Ministry in
recent days to discuss concessions around the new tariff, but
did not disclose further details of the meeting.
    The sources declined to be identified due to the sensitivity
of the issue.
    The Ministry of Commerce did not respond to a request for
comment.
    The scramble to get government concessions underscores
concerns among Chinese companies that the growing trade dispute
between the U.S. and China will inflict financial pain at home
as well as on China's top trading partner.
    It also threatens to disrupt supplies of critical
ingredients for China's vast agriculture sector.
    News of the levy, which is high enough to bring trade to a
halt, has prompted some vessels carrying U.S. sorghum to change
course and forced many importers to find new buyers outside of
China for their grain. [nL1N1RX03B]
    Multiple grain traders based in Asia said the stranded
shipments are on offer at big discounts. 
    The Chinese importers will likely have to pay the deposit
and face the biggest risk from the levy. With the deposit, an
average cargo of 60,000 tonnes of sorghum is now worth about $27
million, almost double the value before the scheme.

SINGAPORE, Jan 17 (Reuters) - The discount in Asia's front-month 380-cst fuel oil time spread
was trading at its widest since early-August on Wednesday as concerns of limited spot demand and
ample prompt supplies of the fuel continued to weigh on market sentiment, trade sources said.
<FO380SGSDMc1>
    The Singapore 380-cst Feb-March time spread was trading at a discount of 70 cents a tonne
around 5pm Singapore time (0900 GMT) on Wednesday in the Intercontinental Exchange, down from its
minus 50 cents a tonne settlement in the previous session, trade sources said. 
                  
    FLOWS
    - With just over 6 million tonnes notionally assessed so far, total fuel oil flows into East
Asia for January are expected to close lower than December's 10-month high of about 6.7 million
tonnes, amid lower than the usual Western and intra-Asia arrivals, assessments by Thomson Reuters
Oil Research showed on Tuesday. 
    - Middle Eastern inflows, however, are expected to be as high as they have been in three of
the past four months, with already over 2 million tonnes notionally assessed amid the ongoing
lack of demand from Pakistan and above-average exports from Abu Dhabi, Iraq and Iran, the
assessments showed. 
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) fuel oil inventories dropped 6 percent, or 545,000
barrels (about 81,000 tonnes), to a three-week low of 8.529 million barrels (1.273 million
tonnes) in the week ended Jan. 15, data via S&P Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - On average, Fujairah fuel oil inventories totalled 10.301 million barrels (or 1.537 million
tonnes) per week since records began in January 2017.
    
    TENDERS
    - India's BPCL is offering 25,000 tonnes vacuum gasoil (VGO) with a 2.7 percent sulphur
content loading from Kochi between Jan. 26 and Jan. 31 in a tender closing on Jan. 18, sources
said. 
    - BPCL earlier cancelled for unknown reasons its offer to export 25,000-40,000 tonnes of VGO
with a 2.5 percent sulphur content loading from Kochi on Jan. 15-16, sources said. [nL4N1P73J9]
    - Taiwan's Formosa sold up to 40,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil with a maximum 4 percent
sulphur content loading from Mailiao on Jan. 24-26 to Vitol at a discount of about $15 a tonne to
Singapore 180-cst quotes on an FOB basis, traders said.
    - Saudi's Satrop refinery, a joint venture between Aramco and Total, has in a rare move
offered to sell up 80,000 tonnes of VGO loading from Jubail over Feb. 6-8 in an offer closing on
Jan. 17 with next-day validity, trade sources said.
    - Several sources told Reuters in December that the Satorp refinery would undergo planned
maintenance in the first quarter of 2018. [nL3N1O61KI]
    - The 400,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) refinery will likely shut a few secondary units, one of
the traders said.

MOSCOW, Oct 3 (Reuters) - Urals differentials held stable in
quiet trade on Wednesday, while light Caspian CPC Blend
differentials softened due to lower demand for October cargoes.
    * Urals differentials remained under pressure in northwest
Europe
due to weak demand and low refining margins, traders said.

    * Buyers awaited bigger discounts, while sellers didn't want
to
place cargoes at cheaper levels, so trade was sluggish, traders
said.

    * In the Mediterranean, nearly all the Urals volumes for
loading
in October were already placed with most of the 140,000-tonne
cargoes fixed to journeys to Asia, market sources said.

    * High demand for Urals in the south and ample supply of
volumes
in the north resulted in arbitrage of the Russian grade from the
Baltic to the Mediterranean, traders said.

    * At least three Urals cargoes loading from Baltic ports in
October were fixed to be shipped to the Mediterranean region,
traders said. Trafigura, Eni and Glencore were said to be
sellers of those cargoes, but the details on the buyers and the
destinations were not clear.

    * CPC Blend differentials weakened due to low demand for
remaining
cargoes from the October loading plan.

    * In the Platts window, Austria's OMV offered 85,000 tonnes
of CPC
Blend for loading on Oct. 22-26 at dated Brent minus $0.55 a
barrel, but failed to find a buyer even though the offer was 10
cents a barrel lower than the recent estimations.

to
raise oil output to cool rising prices and informed the United
States before a meeting in Algiers with other producers, four
sources familiar with the plan said. [nL8N1WJ289]

    * Saudi Arabia plans to raise oil production in November
from an
October output level of 10.7 million barrels per day to meet
rising crude demand, the energy minister of the world's top
exporter said on Wednesday. [nL8N1WJ2Y4]

two-week low. <FO180BRTCKMc1>

demand and rising inventories of the fuel across key storage hubs. [nL8N1O714F] [nL3N1O83L9]

    - Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories fell 4.1 percent, or 983,000 barrels (about
147,000 tonnes), to a two-week low of 23.214 million barrels (3.46 million tonnes) in the week ended
Dec. 13, data from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed on Thursday. [O/SING1]
    - This came as net imports into Singapore fell 10 percent from the previous week to a two-week
low of 934,000 tonnes, Reuters calculations showed.

    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to China topped the weekly list at 305,000 tonnes,
followed by South Korea with 76,000 tonnes and Hong Kong with 75,000 tonnes, the data showed.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Malaysia at 316,000 tonnes, followed by
Russia with 315,000 tonnes, Venezuela with 238,000 tonnes, and the United States with 154,000 tonnes
- data.
    - In the United Arab Emirates, stocks of the fuel in the Fujairah storage hub fell 13.4 percent
to a three-week low of 10.664 million barrels (1.59 million tonnes) in the week to Dec. 11, data via

    - Fuel oil inventories in Fujairah fell over the past week following an increase in export

    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].

million ($8.9 million) to boost liquefied natural gas (LNG) bunkering in the port of Singapore.
[nL4N1OE1DX]

LNG-fuelled vessels it launched in September 2015.

support the building of LNG-fuelled vessels, it added.

    SEOUL/SINGAPORE, Dec 18 (Reuters) - South Korean refiner GS
Caltex Corp has bought a rare cargo of Cold Lake crude, the
company's first purchase in more than two decades of this
Canadian oil grade, a company spokesman said on Monday.
    The second-largest refiner in South Korea bought 300,000
barrels of the heavy sour crude for delivery in the second half
of February, he said.
    The refiner is trying out a small volume of the oil, which
has a quality similar to that of Iraq's Basra Heavy crude, a
person familiar with the matter said, speaking on condition of
anonymity because he wasn't authorised speak to media. 
    About 300,000 barrels of Cold Lake were loaded onto Panamax
Selecao on Dec. 13 at Vancouver for delivery to an unspecified
destination, trade flows data on Thomson Reuters Eikon showed.

briefly opened when the discount between U.S. West Texas
Intermediate crude and Brent futures <CL-LCO1=R> stretched as
wide as $7 a barrel last week on a disruption in Forties crude
supply. [nL3N1OB15B]
    Heavy crude produced in Canada is trading close to its
deepest discount in four years as pipeline constraints pushed
western Canadian crude inventories to record highs. [nL1N1OF019]
    GS Caltex operates a 790,000 barrels per day refinery in
Yeosu. The refiner is equally owned by GS Energy Corp, a unit of
GS Holdings <078930.KS>, and U.S. oil major Chevron Corp
<CVX.N>.

expressed interest in purchasing Canadian crude. [nL4N1M82EW]

an over 7-month high on Tuesday on the back of firm demand from Indonesia, trade
sources said.

sulphur gasoil for delivery into Cat Lai over Jan. 15 to 19 or on a
free-on-board basis, in a tender that closes on Dec. 15, according to a tender
document.
    The company has asked for two loading options for the cargo, either from

South Korea kicks in next year where taxes on gasoil imports from the latter
will be removed, similar to imports from Southeast Asia.

fuels from January.

62-day maintenance starting Nov. 18, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
