162,000 barrel of crude oil per day. 
    
    * INDONESIA'S JET FUEL DEMAND: Indonesian state-owned Pertamina's jet fuel
imports are expected to climb to around 1 million barrels per month in 2018 from
around 800,000 barrels per month this year due to firm demand from the aviation
sector, the head of the state-owned company's procurement unit said on Tuesday.
[nL3N1OC22J] 
      The company hopes to supply around 90 percent of its import needs through
term contracts, with the rest through spot market deals, Toto Nugroho, Senior
Vice President of the firm's Integrated Supply Chain unit, told reporters.

site at Bukom Island in Singapore over the weekend could have affected a thermal

SINGAPORE, Dec 18 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil market was supported by spot demand from
Vietnam, Pakistan and East Africa, ahead of a benchmark change by pricing agency Platts in
Singapore and the Middle East, trade sources said.    
    * PLATTS CHANGES GASOIL BENCHMARK: Platts' change in pricing methodology to reflect the
underlying
grade for its benchmark gasoil assessment to 10ppm from the current 500ppm kicked in on Monday
as physical deals reflected January loading cargoes, traders said. 
But there was only one trade on Monday using December pricing, they added. 

    * VIETNAM BUYS: Vietnam's Saigon Petro bought 10,000 tonnes of 50ppm sulphur diesel for
loading in
January from a trading house at a premium of 30 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes, an industry
source said.
It bought the cargo on a free-on-board basis. 

    * PAKISTAN BUYS: Pakistan State Oil likely bought 55,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil
from
Renish Petroleum for delivery into Karachi over Dec. 21 to 23 at a premium of $4.23 a barrel to
Singapore quotes, traders said, though the deal could not immediately be confirmed. 

    * SRI LANKA CANCELS TENDER: Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp cancelled a tender seeking
120,000
barrels of jet fuel for delivery over Jan. 4 to 5, traders said.
BB Energy had placed the sole bid of $5.16 a barrel to Singapore quotes, but the tender was not
awarded, they added. 
It was no clear if Ceypetco is planning to re-issue the tender. 

    * INDIA SELLS GASOIL: India's Essar Oil has sold up to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for
loading from Vadinar over Jan. 14 to 18 at a premium of 20 cents a barrel to Middle East quotes,
traders said, though this could not immediately be confirmed. 

    * MALAYSIA REFINERY MAINTENANCE: Malaysia's Petronas will likely have a refinery maintenance
in
the first quarter of next year, industry sources said.
The plans have not been finalised but will likely involve a secondary unit, one of the sources
said. 
    * KENYA OIL IMPORTS: Kenya's oil importers are seeking nearly 600,000 tonnes of oil products
for
delivery in January and February, including 164,602 tonnes of jet fuel and 218,388 tonnes of
50ppm sulphur gasoil, a tender document showed. [nL4N1OI2PR] 
The tender closes on Dec. 21 and is valid until Dec. 22.
Kenya's oil imports could grow after it commissions a new pipeline connecting Mombasa to Nairobi
by end of December, which will ease waiting time in Mombasa, a source close to the matter said.

SINGAPORE, Dec 15 (Reuters) - Muted trade activity left Asia's fuel oil market little changed on Friday but
falling inventories in key storage hubs and expectations of narrower arbitrage arrivals in January supported
sentiment and narrowed the discount in fuel oil refining margins this week, sources said. 
    The discount of Asia's January 180-cst fuel oil crack to Brent crude narrowed 4 cents a barrel from the previous
session to minus $5.83 a barrel on Friday, up from a 10-month low of minus $6.49 a barrel a week ago. <FO180BRTCKMc1>
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fuel oil stocks in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) oil hub slipped 1 percent, or 12,000 tonnes, from the
previous week to a total of 1.17 million tonnes in the week ended Dec. 14, data from Dutch consultancy PJK
International showed. [ARA/]
    - Compared with the same time last year, ARA fuel oil inventories are 50 percent higher and are above the
five-year average of 842,000 tonnes for this time of the year. <STK-FO-ARA>
    - Outgoing fuel oil cargoes from the ARA hub over the past week included one Singapore-bound VLCC tanker and a
panamax tanker heading to the U.S., PJK data showed. [nL8N1OE61I]
    - In Singapore, official data showed fuel oil inventories fell 4.1 percent, or 147,000 tonnes, to a two-week low
of 3.46 million tonnes in the week to Dec. 13 as net imports dropped 10 percent from a week earlier, official data
showed. [nL4N1OE3FC]
    - Similarly, in the United Arab Emirates, stocks of the fuel in the Fujairah storage hub fell 13.4 percent to a
three-week low of 1.59 million tonnes in the week to Dec. 11 amid increased shipments of the fuel to Singapore, data
via S&P Global Platts showed. [nL3N1OD3BW]
    
    ARBITRAGE FLOWS
    - Total fuel oil flows into East Asia for December is expected to close at 10-month high of about 6.5 million
tonnes, above November's inflows that were revised lower to about 6.3 million tonnes following the delay of some
cargo arrivals from November into December, assessments by Thomson Reuters Oil Research showed on Tuesday.
[O/FUELARB]
    - Western volumes for December are assessed at 4.0-4.1 million tonnes, up from the previous week's assessments of
3.6-3.7 million tonnes and above November's revised total of 3.1-3.2 million tonnes, according to the assessments. 
    - However, January arrivals are expected to be substantially lower, with just 1.4-1.5 million tonnes notionally
assessed so far and less than three weeks of the West-to-East tanker-fixing window left open, the assessments showed.

SINGAPORE, Dec 19 (Reuters) - Elevated deal values for physical cargoes of 380-cst high-sulphur
fuel oil (HSFO) lifted cash premiums of the mainstay residual fuel to a more than one-month high on
Tuesday. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    By contrast, cash premiums of the lower viscosity 180-cst HSFO fell from their near three-month
high in the previous session as suppliers accepted lower premiums for cargoes of the fuel, trade
sources said. <FO180-SIN-DIF>, [nL4N1OI3Q8]
    
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Six cargo trades were reported in the Platts window, totalling 40,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel
oil and another 100,000 tonnes of 380-cst fuel oil.
    - Mercuria bought both 20,000-tonne 180-cst HSFO cargoes from Trafigura. 
    - Mercuria also bought one 20,000-tonne 380-cst HSFO cargo from Shell and later sold a
40,000-tonne cargo of 380-cst HSFO to Gunvor. 
    - Hin Leong bought two 20,000-tonne 380-cst HSFO cargoes, one from Shell and another from Vitol.
    - A total of 1.08 million tonnes of fuel oil have traded in the window in December so far,
against 1.32 million tonnes in November.
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - UAE's ADNOC is offering up to six 90,000-tonne cargoes of 70-80-cst straight-run fuel oil with
a maximum 1.2 percent sulphur content loading in Ruwais over January 1-3, 5-7, 11-13, 16-18, 22-24
and 27-29 in a tender closed on Dec. 12 and valid until Dec. 14, sources said.
    - Adnoc has also offered two 45,000-tonne cargoes of cracked medium-sulphur 380-cst fuel oil
loading from Ruwais over Jan. 12-14 and Jan. 24-26 in an offer that is already closed for bids,
industry sources said. 
    - Saudi's Aramco is offering up to 80,000 tonnes of A991-spec 180-cst fuel oil from its refinery
in Ras Tanura for delivery on Jan. 1-3 in a tender closing on Dec. 19, sources said. 
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
        
    LNG BUNKERS
    - Singapore-based Pavilion Gas Pte Ltd said on Tuesday it has been awarded a Liquefied Natural
Gas (LNG) bunker supply contract by PSA Marine Pte Ltd for the supply of LNG bunker fuel from 2019.
[nL4N1OJ1JG]
    - LNG bunker fuel to be supplied to two harbour tugs that can run on both LNG and standard
marine fuel and that are due to be delivered to PSA Marine in 2019.

LONDON, Dec 13 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe dropped on Wednesday following a large build in
U.S. inventories as a major Scottish refinery started shutting
down following a pipeline outage.
    * U.S. gasoline stocks <USOILG=ECI> rose by 5.7 million
barrels
last week, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters
poll for a 2.5 million-barrel gain, the EIA said. [EIA/S]
    * Ineos may bring forward maintenance work at its 200,000
bpd
Grangemouth refinery in Scotland due to the unplanned outage at
its Forties North Sea crude pipeline, which threatens to choke
the plant's feedstock, industry sources said.[nL8N1OD3TC]
    * The refinery's 65,000 bpd crude distillation was being
shut on
Wednesday and the second 110,000 bpd CDU was planned to shut
down next week, trading sources told
Reuters.[REF/OUT][nL8N1OD5IS]
    * On Wednesday, Ineos' 240,000 bpd Lavera oil refinery in
the
south of France was fully shut down due to a power outage on
Monday, trading sources told Reuters. [nL8N1OC4EL]
    * The refinery is a major gasoline exporter. 
    * The 60,000 tonne tanker Amalia has been booked to deliver
gasoline from the ARA hub to Australia, a rare arbitrage that
follows the drop in prices last week, traders said.
    * The STI Hammersmith and the STI Milwaukee each loaded
gasoline
cargoes in Spain last month to go to Amsterdam but had to wait
by up to six days outside the port.
    * The STI Fontvieille loaded a 35,000 tonne gasoline cargo
for BP
at the Turkish port of Tutunciftlik on November 24, but was
diverted away from Amsterdam and is now calling on Durban,
according to ship tracking.

   GASOLINE
    * No barges of eurobob gasoline traded during the afternoon
session. Bids were seen at $583-$584 a tonne fob ARA.
    * Some 12,000 tonnes traded elsewhere during the day at
$585.50-$598 a tonne fob Amsterdam-Rotterdam, compared with
$604.50-$608.50 a tonne on Tuesday. Total, BP and Litasco sold
to Gunvor, Shell and Trafigura.  
    * Shell and Gunvor sold to Total barges of premium unleaded
gasoline at $597 and $596 a tonne fob ARA, compared with $613 a
tonne. 
    * BP sold a cargo to Gunvor at $583 a tonne cif Rijeka.
    * The January swap stood at $581.50 a tonne at the close,
down
from $599 a tonne.
    * The benchmark EBOB gasoline refining margin dropped to
$6.15 a
barrel from $7.54 a barrel at the previous close.
    * Brent crude futures <LCOc1> fell by 79 cents to $62.56 a
barrel
by 1656 GMT.
    * U.S. front-month RBOB gasoline futures <RBc1> were down
2.34
percent at $1.6590 a gallon. 
    * The RBOB crack versus U.S. crude <RBc1-CLc1> was down 8.5
percent at $12.95 a barrel.

compared

    LONDON, March 3 (Reuters) -  
    * Forties bid up at highest since early January after five
supertankers booked to take this grade to Asia in late March.
    * Ekofisk diffs sold off heavily for mid-March, but rising
for loadings later in the month.
    * Five VLCCs fixed so far to carry North Sea crude to Asia
in March, which, if all result in an actual voyage, will make
this month the largest in terms of flows in at least three
years, according to Reuters data. 
        
    FIXTURES - REUTERS SHIPPING DATA
    * Vitol fixes VLCC Samail to load at Hound Point on March
25, bound for South Korea.
    * Koch fixes VLCC Olympic Lion to load unspecified North Sea
crude on March 25 to go to Singapore.
    * Vitol fixes VLCC Gener8 Hercules to load at Hound Point on
March 28, bound for South Korea.
    * Earlier this week, Unipec fixed VLCC Shanghai to load at
Hound Point on March 28, bound for China.
    * Unipec also fixed VLCC Sandra to load an unspecified North
Sea crude on March 16, bound for South Korea. 
        
    WINDOW SUMMARY
    * Glencore sold a cargo of Ekofisk to BP for loading March
23-25 at a premium of 65 cents to dated Brent.
    * Statoil sold Total a cargo of Ekofisk for loading March
17-19 at 25 cents above the dated Brent price.
    * The quality premium for Ekofisk for March is 57 cents,
meaning the average of the trades makes Ekofisk the
lowest-priced crude and therefore it sets the dated price.
    * Unipec bid for a cargo of Forties for loading March 25-28
at a premium of 20 cents to dated Brent. This compares with a
bid at 15 cents above the dated benchmark.
    * Trading sources said Unipec submitted a further bid for
Forties at 25 cents above dated Brent, for a cargo loading March
25-28.

    LONDON, March 8 (Reuters) - Benchmark diesel refining
margins in northwest Europe firmed again on Tuesday as
maintenance work cleared cargoes from storage and crude oil
futures dipped lower. 

    * Refinery turnarounds in Europe, the U.S. Gulf Coast and
Middle East are limiting the amount of diesel available, traders
said. 
    * This has helped to alleviate the excess that had dogged
the market for months, and had cleared out the bulk of the
vessels that had been floating with distillates.
    * Exports from Russia were higher than expected, with
refineries set to ship around 3.2 million tonnes of diesel from
the Baltic and Black Sea in March.
    * Exports from the United States had climbed over the week,
with more than 1 million tonnes of diesel expected to land in
Europe in March.
    * Refinery maintenance work has helped balance the market,
clearing some distillates from storage. On Tuesday, ExxonMobil
said multiple units at its Rotterdam refinery were currently
closed, while Spain's La Coruna and Bilbao refineries were also
undergoing works. [REF/OUT]
    * Egypt's EGPC issued a tender to sell a 25,000 tonne cargo
of jet fuel from the port of Alexandria from April 5-7. 
    * Hellenic Petroleum issued a tender to sell one 30,000
tonne cargo of gasoil with a sulphur content of 0.1 percent for
loading from March 18-23, traders said.

steady at a two-week low and Ekofisk weakened, as ample supplies

SINGAPORE, March 7 (Reuters) - The 380cst premium strengthened on Monday for the fifth
straight session to hit a five-week high, lifted by sustained strong bidding for cargoes,
traders said.
    The rise in 380cst cash differentials is a sharp reversal from discounts that reached a more
than four-month low on Feb. 23 of minus $5.35 per tonne to Singapore quotes.
    Cash differentials for 380cst rose 24 cents from Friday's close, strengthening the premium
to 70 cents per tonne above Singapore quotes from a premium of 46 cents per tonne.
    The buying pressure also helped raise the March-April time spread differentials from $0 per
tonne on Friday, to a premium of 25 cents per tonne to Singapore quotes on Monday. 
    By contrast, differentials for the April-May and May-June time spread swaps weakened into
slightly deeper discounts, traders said without pointing to any specific reason. 
    While Monday's 18 reported trades in Platts' Market on Close (MoC) pricing process matched
that of Friday's, the volume of fuel oil traded was 20,000 tonnes lower at 420,000 tonnes of
380cst fuel oil.
    Since the start of March, the total volume of high sulphur fuel oil traded in Platts' MoC
pricing process in Singapore rose to 1.74 million tonnes, well above the combined total of 1.65
million tonnes for January and February.
    
    INTERNATIONAL MARKETS:
    January Russian refinery runs fell by 0.2 million barrels per day (mbpd) from last year to
54 mbpd, according to Energy Aspects' data review released on Wednesday last week. 
    Russian fuel oil output fell year-on-year by 0.33 mbpd as did fuel oil yields which fell
further to 20.7 percent, Energy Aspects said.
    
    TENDERS:
    Korea Western Power Co Ltd bought 45,000 tonnes of low-sulphur fuel oil and 45,000 tonnes of
high-sulphur fuel oil for arrival in March via two tenders closed on Friday, a source from the
utility said on Monday. [nL4N16F22X]
    Hanwha Corp supplied 45,000 tonnes of low-sulphur fuel oil for delivery between March 20 and
24, while Hyundai Corp supplied the other 45,000 tonne cargo of high-sulphur fuel oil for March
27 to 31 delivery.

SINGAPORE, Aug 8 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil cash differentials could firm as Saudi
Aramco's trading company seeks large volumes of gasoil in the spot market, trade sources said on
Tuesday. 
    
    - ARAMCO SEEKS GASOIL: Aramco Trading Company is seeking 1.4 million barrels of 500 parts
per million (ppm) sulphur gasoil for delivery over August to September, likely to meet a spike
in domestic demand during the summer or due to a supply shortfall, traders said. 
    - EMARAT SEEKS JET FUEL: Emirates General Petroleum Corp (Emarat) is seeking 55,000 tonnes
of jet fuel for delivery in September in a tender that closes on Aug. 14 and is valid until Aug.
16.
    - JAPAN REFINERIES HALT SHIPMENTS: Two Japanese oil refiners said on Tuesday they had halted
berth product shipments at their refineries in eastern Japan as a weakening Typhoon Noru moves
north. [nL4N1KU14Y]
    JXTG Nippon Oil & Energy Corp has suspended shipments at its refineries in Sendai and
Negishi, a company spokesman said, while Cosmo Energy said it had suspended shipments at its
Chiba refinery. 
    But this is expected to have minimal impact on oil product exports, a source with a Japanese
refiner said. It may affect barges for domestic shipments but not medium-range or larger tankers
typically used for exports, the source added. 
    - CHINA CRUDE IMPORTS FALL: China's crude oil imports in July fell to the lowest since
January calculated on a daily basis as refiners drew from high stockpiles after bumper purchases
earlier in the year and as refineries scaled back production. [nL4N1KT315]
    The General Administration of Chinese Customs said on Tuesday China bought 34.74 million
tonnes of crude oil in July, or about 8.18 million barrels per day (bpd), though this is still
about 12 percent higher than the July 2016 level.
    But traders and analysts widely expect China's crude imports to pick up again in the fourth
quarter as new refineries start up, which could drive up oil product exports.
    - QATAR IMPORTS JET FUEL: The Silver Millie has been provisionally booked to ship 310,000
barrels of jet fuel to load from Singapore on Aug. 16 headed to Mesaieed in Qatar, shipping
fixtures showed. This is unusual as Qatar is typically an exporter of the fuel. It is unclear if
Qatar Petroleum has scheduled a refinery turnaround which is prompting the imports of the fuel.

SINGAPORE, Oct 5 (Reuters) - Cash discounts for jet fuel in Asia were at their lowest in
over a week on Friday, buoyed by expectations for stronger winter demand despite a weekly build
in Singapore stocks from higher net imports.
    In the week to Oct. 3, Singapore was a net importer of about 46,000 tonnes of aviation
turbine fuel, International Enterprise (IE) data showed on Thursday. That compares with net
imports of about 3,000 tonnes in the preceding week.
    Cash differentials for jet fuel <JET-SIN-DIF> narrowed to a discount of 42 cents a barrel to
Singapore quotes, compared with a discount of 62 cents a barrel on Thursday.
    Jet fuel/kerosene markets are expected to strengthen over the next couple of weeks as stocks
of fuel build for winter heating use, trade sources said. 
    Kerosene, which is used for winter heating, and jet fuel are closely related and belong to
the same grade of refined products, with jet fuel margins determining the profitability of both.
    The cracks, or refining margins, for jet fuel <JETSGCKMc1> climbed to $16.03 a barrel over
Dubai crude during Asian trading hours on Friday, from $15.75 a barrel on Thursday.
    Meanwhile, cracks for gasoil with 10ppm sulphur content <GO10SGCKMc1> edged lower to $16.03 
a barrel over Dubai crude, from Thursday's $16.20 a barrel.
    Cash premiums for 10ppm gasoil <GO10-SIN-DIF> fell to 45 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes
on Friday, compared with a premium of 54 cents a barrel a day earlier. 


    ARA STOCKS
    - Gasoil stocks independently held in the ARA refining and storage hub rose 0.8 percent in
the week to Thursday, data from Dutch consultancy PJK International showed. [ARA/]
    - Gasoil inventories <STK-GO-ARA> for the week to Oct. 4 were at about 2.93 million tonnes,
the highest since March this year.
    - Stocks of gasoil, which is currently very expensive, were up slightly as more imports came
into the ARA region and demand up the Rhine slowed compared with last week, despite some exports
to Britain and the Mediterranean, PJK's Lars van Wageningen said.
    - Jet fuel inventories <STK-JET-ARA> fell 1.6 percent to 672,000 tonnes, PJK data showed.
    - Compared with year-ago levels jet fuel stocks were unchanged, while gasoil inventories
were about 15 percent higher.

    - Four gasoil deals, no jet fuel trades.
    - BP bought 150,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil from Shell for Oct. 20-24 loading at a premium
of 30 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes.
    - BP bought another 150,000 barrels of 10ppm gasoil from Shell for Oct. 20-24 loading at a
premium of 20 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes.

each to BP for Oct. 29-Nov. 2 loading at $99.30 per barrel.

SINGAPORE, Oct 5 (Reuters) - Undeterred by rising crude prices, the November 380-cst barge
fuel oil crack on Friday extended gains for a fourth straight session as concerns of tightening
supplies from looming U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil exports from next month continued to boost
sentiment.
    The November 380-cst barge crack was trading at about minus $10.75 a barrel to Brent crude
during Asia trade, up from Thursday's close at minus $10.86 a barrel, Refinitiv data showed.
<HFOFARAACMc2>
    The last time the front-month crack discount was narrower was on Aug. 23 when Brent crude
traded at around $74 a barrel. [LCOc1]

market due to U.S. sanctions on Iran's crude exports. [O/R]
    Meanwhile, fuel oil inventories in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) fell this week
following increased shipments of the fuel to Singapore, where weekly fuel oil inventories held
steady, the latest data showed.

tonnes, to a total of 1.247 million tonnes in the week ended Oct. 4, data from Dutch consultancy

unable to balance the exports. [nL8N1WK4O2]

    - Singapore fuel oil exports totalled 231,000 tonnes, up from a more than seven-year low of

[nL4N1WD3BZ]

SINGAPORE, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The front-month 380-cst barge fuel oil crack on Wednesday
widened its discount to Brent crude away from a near 1-1/2 year high in the previous session as
crude oil prices clawed back some losses. 
    The December 380-cst barge fuel oil crack to Brent crude was trading at about minus $4.70 a
barrel on Wednesday, compared with a discount of $4.30 a barrel in the previous session, broker
sources said.
    On Tuesday, the front-month crack discount was at its narrowest discount to Brent crude
since June 2017, according to Refinitiv data in Eikon. <HFOFARAACMc1>
    Oil bounced by more than 1 percent on Wednesday to claw back some of the previous day's
6-percent plunge, lifted by a report of an unexpected decline in U.S. commercial crude
inventories and record Indian crude imports. [O/R]
                
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - Four cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, totalling 80,000 tonnes
of 180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO).
    - Hin Leong bought three 20,000 tonne cargoes of the fuel, lifting two cargoes from Gunvor
and one from Mercuria.
    - P66 bought the fourth cargo from Gunvor. 
    - The 80,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil traded on Wednesday was the highest daily volume of
180-cst fuel oil traded in the window since June 5 when a similar quantity of the fuel exchanged
hands. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details.

percent sulphur content loading from Mumbai over Dec. 6-8 in a tender closing on Nov. 22. 
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Fuel oil inventories at the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) jumped 15 percent, or
999,000 barrels (about 149,000 tonnes), to a four-week high of 7.775 million barrels (1.16
million tonnes) in the week ended Nov. 19, data from S&P Global Platts showed. [FUJAIRAH/]
    - Fujairah fuel oil inventories rose amid increased fuel oil imports from the Black Sea as
well as residual fuel imports from the U.S. Gulf, one trade source said. 
    - The inventory build was in contrast to widespread expectations of growing pressures on
fuel oil inventories in the Fujairah oil hub from early-November when U.S. sanctions on Iranian
oil exports took effect.
    - Iran is a major fuel oil producer with exports of the fuel totalling about 17 million
tonnes in 2017, of which an estimated 500,000-600,000 tonnes per month was shipped into
Fujairah, industry sources said. 
    - Fujairah fuel oil inventories are now 19 percent lower from the same time last year.
    - In 2018, Fujairah's fuel oil stocks averaged 8.107 million barrels (1.21 million tonnes)
compared with 9.974 million barrels (1.489 million tonnes) in the year before, Reuters
calculations showed.
        
    INDIA DATA
    - India's crude oil imports in October rose to their highest level in at least more than
seven years, data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) of the oil ministry
showed on Tuesday. [nL4N1XV4Q8]
    - Crude imports in October climbed 10.5 percent from a year earlier to 21.02 million tonnes,
the highest monthly import figure in PPAC data going back to April 2011.
    - Imports rose as many refiners resumed purchases after maintenance of units.
    - India's fuel oil exports totalled 0.31 million tonnes in October, down from 0.32 million
tonnes in September, but up from the 0.27 million tonnes exported in the same period last year,
the preliminary trade data showed. 
    - Fuel oil imports totalled just 50,000 tonnes in October, down from 70,000 tonnes in the
previous month and sharply lower from the 120,000 tonnes imported in October last year, the data
showed.

SINGAPORE, May 31 (Reuters) - The front-month 380-cst fuel oil crack discount to
Brent crude was only slightly wider on Thursday, despite sharp gains in overnight crude
oil prices, reflecting the bullish market fundamentals of the residual fuel.
    In another illustration of bullish market sentiment, 380-cst cash premiums climbed
to their highest since March 2016 amid limited availability of finished-grade spot
cargoes of the fuel, trade sources said. <FO380-SIN-DIF>
    Since around the start of April, global fuel oil markets have been supported by
rising seasonal demand for cooling in the summer as well as tighter supplies stemming
from refinery maintenance, outages and upgrades in key producing regions, trade sources
said.
    The June 380-cst fuel oil crack to Brent crude was trading at a discount of about
$10.60 a barrel on Thursday, slightly down from the $10.50 a barrel discount in the
previous session, broker-sources said.
    Oil prices eased slightly on Thursday following a rally in the previous session, as
investors eyed a surprise increase in U.S. crude oil inventories and looked to a
possible rise in output when OPEC and other producers meet in June. [O/R]
    Meanwhile, Singapore fuel oil inventories jumped to a two-month high in the week to
May 30 after climbing 15 percent from the week before, official data showed on Thursday.
    
    INVENTORIES
    - Singapore weekly onshore fuel oil inventories jumped 2.711 million barrels (about
405,000 tonnes) to a total of 21.052 million barrels (3.142 million tonnes) in the week
ended May 30, data from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore showed. [O/SING1]
    - This came as weekly net imports of the fuel oil into Singapore jumped 22 percent
from a week earlier to a two-week high of 935,000 tonnes.
    - The increase in outright fuel oil stocks is the largest weekly volume increase
since the week to June 14 when stocks soared 4.674 million barrels (698,000 tonnes).
    - Compared with year-ago levels, the latest onshore fuel oil inventories were 11
percent higher, the widest year-on-year surplus since the week ended Jan. 3.
    - Singapore's net exports of fuel oil to China topped the week ended May 30 at
211,000 tonnes, followed by Malaysia at 193,000 tonnes and South Korea at 90,000 tonnes.
    - The largest net imports into Singapore originated from Russia at 264,000 tonnes,
followed by the Netherlands at 195,000 tonnes, Iraq at 188,000 tonnes and Venezuela at
154,000 tonnes.
    - Fuel oil imports into Singapore from Venezuela returned in the week ended May 30
after a five-week absence and were at a near four-month high.
            
    WINDOW TRADES    
    - One cargo trades were reported in the Singapore trading window, totalling 20,000
tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil.
    - Shell sold the 180-cst fuel oil cargo to Hin Leong at $456 per tonne. 
    - Please click on [O/AS] for more details. 
    
    TENDERS
    - Thailand's PTT Global Chemical (PTTGC) sold a 35,000 tonne cargo of 380-cst fuel
oil with a maximum 3.5 percent sulphur content to an unknown buyer loading over June
11-13 from Map Ta Phut at a narrow premium to Singapore 380-cst quotes, sources said.
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
    
    OW CASE
    - A Danish court on Wednesday sentenced the former manager of OW Bunker's Singapore
subsidiary to 18 months in prison after he was found guilty of granting credit outside
his mandate, contributing to the bankruptcy of the marine fuel oil supplier.
[nL5N1T13FB]
    - The city court of Aalborg said it found Lars Moller, head of Dynamic Oil Trading
in Singapore, guilty of giving a trading partner an unrecoverable credit worth $90.2
million without having the authority to do so from the management in Denmark and without
recording it in the company's accounting system.
    
    RELIANCE & IRAN 
    - India's Reliance Industries Ltd, owner of the world's biggest refining complex,
plans to halt oil imports from Iran, two sources familiar with the matter said, in a
sign that new U.S. sanctions are forcing buyers to shun oil purchases from Tehran.
[nL3N1T21DA]

margins in northwest Europe were little changed on Tuesday but

month.

weighed down by persistent strength in European fuel oil markets as well as elevated Singapore

SINGAPORE, July 18 (Reuters) - Asia's 380-cst fuel oil cash premiums fell to a near

aggressive supplier offers.

cents a tonne. [O/AS]  
    - By comparison, Monday's two 380-cst deals were traded at a 70-90 cent premium to
Singapore quotes. 
    - The lowest supplier offers for 380-cst fuel oil on Tuesday were at premiums ranging
from 30 cents to 85 cents a tonne, compared with a range of about plus $1.50 to $1.60 a
tonne in the previous session. 
    - 180-cst cash premiums <FO180-SIN-DIF> to Singapore quotes fell to 40 cents a tonne,
their lowest since June 12.

SINGAPORE, Dec 28 (Reuters) - Asian gasoil differentials were steady on Wednesday as supply
of the fuel remained ample, trade sources said.
    Eight gasoil cargoes exchanged hands in Singapore, continuing the high volume of gasoil
trading since mid-September, they added. 
    About 14 long-range sized vessels are temporarily storing gasoil offshore, up from 8 earlier
this month, likely to store the traded volumes, industry sources said.
    A Suezmax and a very large crude carrier (VLCC) could also be storing gasoil offshore, he
added, though this could not immediately be confirmed. 
    Japan's kerosene stocks rose 53,000 kilolitres to 2.16 million kilolitres in the week to
Dec. 24 despite a slightly lower refinery operating rate, latest data from the Petroleum
Association of Japan showed. 
    Exports of the fuel fell 30 percent from the previous week while jet fuel exports rose 40
percent, the data showed.
    Japan is expected to see average to warmer weather from January to March, which could dampen
demand for kerosene. [nL4N1EG20K]
    This is in contrast with November, when domestic sales of kerosene rose due to colder
weather stoking demand. [nL4N1DI3HM]
    Japan's total oil sales rose in November from a year ago, marking the first rise in 14
months, trade ministry data showed. [nL4N1EN1WX]    
    Heavy refinery maintenance in the first quarter is expected to boost gasoil differentials in
the first quarter of next year, trade sources said. 
    Maintenance is expected to be heavier than in 2016 and about the same as 2015, one of them
said. 
    Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) likely sold 40,000 tonnes of jet fuel for Jan. 24 to 25 loading
at a premium of about 50 cents a barrel to Middle East quotes, an industry source said. The deal
could not be confirmed with KPC.

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, Dec 21 (Reuters) - Cash premiums of 380-cst fuel oil sagged to a near two-week
low after aggressive selling by BP <BP.L> in the Platts window, industry sources said. 
    Premiums of 380-cst fuel oil <FO380-SIN-DIF> were assessed 10 cents lower from the previous
session at $2.20 a tonne to Singapore quotes, its lowest premium since Dec. 9.
    Five 380-cst fuel oil cargoes were traded in the window on Wednesday totalling 100,000
tonnes, all of which were offered by BP. Hin Leong lifted three of the cargoes while PetroChina
picked up the remaining two. 
    BP's sold its five cargoes at a premium of $2 a tonne above Singapore quotes at the front of
the trading window and a $2.25 a tonne premium at the middle and back end of the window. 
    These premiums were at least 75 cents a tonne lower than the next most competitive offer in
Wednesday's window, sources said. 
    On Tuesday, the company was asking for a premium of $2.50 a tonne above Singapore quotes for
similar cargoes across the trading window but failed to find a buyer.
    Traders said the narrowing cash premiums were suggestive of an improving supply outlook
after weeks of shortages.
    Other signs of improving supply-demand balances included the narrowing of prompt month time
spreads <FO380SGSDMc1>, shrinking East-West (EW) arbitrage spreads and visco spreads
<FOVISSGDFMc1>, as well as lower refining margins <FO180SGCKMc1> for the industrial fuel. 
    For instance, while the January EW spreads were up 50 cents from the previous session on
Wednesday, the arbitrage spread has contracted $5.50 a tonne from an 11-month high of $34.25 a
tonne reached on Dec. 2. 
                        
    RELATED NEWS:
    * Malaysia's state oil firm Petroliam Nasional Bhd will trim crude output by up to 20,000
barrels per day (bpd) in 2017, down about 3 percent from this year's estimated production,
honouring the country's commitment to reduce supply as part of a deal agreed this month between
OPEC and other global producers. [nL4N1EG1K3]

SINGAPORE, Dec 27 (Reuters) - The Asian diesel margin climbed to a nearly one-week high on
Tuesday as stocks of the fuel were depleted in China, the world's second largest oil consumer,
trade sources said. 
    China's diesel inventories slid to a record low at end-November, sliding 3.9 percent from a
year earlier to 5.95 million tonnes, according to data from the official Xinhua news agency.
[nL4N1EL1WU]
    Xinhua said in its report that diesel supply had become tight as refineries across China
tempered production while they upgraded facilities to produce higher-quality fuels in order to
meet stricter emissions limits on gasoline and diesel that China is introducing from Jan. 1. 
    China will apply mandatory National V standards for diesel and gasoline starting Jan. 1, the
state planner said.
    The standards are equivalent to Euro V specifications that allow a maximum sulphur content
of 10 parts per million (ppm). 
    While this is expected to change the quality of diesel exports in the future, no change in
exports is expected in January, an industry source said. 
    Eventually, there will likely be more 10ppm sulphur diesel for export as the refineries
upgrade their facilities, the source added.   
    Accordingly, the cash premium for 10ppm sulphur diesel in Singapore also rose, also likely
in anticipation of demand from Europe when colder temperature starts drawing diesel cargoes for
heating, traders said.   
    Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) is seeking up to 178,000 tonnes of gasoil for
delivery in January, also helping to boost gasoil margins, traders said.

Ain Sukhna over Jan. 23 to 25. The tender closes on Dec. 29 and is valid until Jan. 3.

By Roslan Khasawneh
    SINGAPORE, Dec 22 (Reuters) - The front-month arbitrage window for North West European (NWE)
fuel oil cargoes into East Asia shrank to a near six-week low on Thursday following a surge in
Singapore fuel oil inventories, industry sources said.
    The January East-West (EW) spread <FOSGEWMc1> - the price differential between FOB Singapore
180-cst high-sulphur fuel oil and FOB Rotterdam barge fuel oil with maximum 3.5 percent sulphur
- fell $1 a tonne from the previous session to $27.75 a tonne, its lowest since Nov. 11.
    This came as onshore inventories of Singapore fuel oil climbed by 2.53 million barrels
(about 351,000 tonnes) in the week to Dec. 21 to 23.01 million barrels (3.4 million tonnes),
snapping four consecutive weeks of decline. [/SING1]
    Some traders anticipated a rise in inventories at the tail end of December and in early
January due to a delay in arbitrage arrivals from various locations including the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub and the Black Sea. 
    The rise in inventories to a one-month high in the week to Dec. 21 was boosted by a 633
percent surge in fuel oil net imports from the previous week to 1.07 million tonnes.
[nL4N1EH2ME]
    The top four net exporters of the fuel into Singapore were Russia (418,000 tonnes),
Venezuela (202,000 tonnes), Malta (150,000 tonnes) and Thailand (140,000 tonnes).

oil refinery in Central Java in 2021, one year earlier than its previous target, its chief

    SINGAPORE, Dec 19 (Reuters) - Asia's fuel oil refining margin for the benchmark
180-centistoke fuel oil to Dubai crude on Monday retreated from a near three-week high seen on
Friday as rising crude oil prices weighed on markets, traders said. 
    Despite muted trading activity ahead of the holiday season, Singapore's January 180-cst fuel
oil discount to Dubai crude <FO180SGCKMc1> pulled away from a December high recorded in the
previous session, slipping 46 cents a barrel to minus 95 cents a barrel.
    On Nov. 30, discounts of the front-month refining margin were at minus 6 cents a barrel,
their narrowest in nearly five years, on the back of firm seasonal demand and limited supplies.
[nL4N1DU3HD]
    But a sharp rally in crude oil prices following the OPEC/Russia deal to curb production saw
the refining margin collapse by $3.21 a barrel over the subsequent two trading sessions. 
    In physical markets, cash differentials for the 180-cst and the more actively traded 380-cst
were mixed amid varying buying interest in the Platts window, industry sources said. 
    Lower outright bids and offers for the 380-cst fuel saw its cash differentials
<FO380-SIN-DIF> slip 57 cents a tonne to a premium of $2.53 a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    By contrast, stronger buying interest and elevated offers for the lower viscosity 180-cst
fuel boosted its premiums to $4.37 a tonne, up 85 cents a tonne from the previous session. 
    A total of 40,000 tonnes of the 180-cst fuel were traded in the window on Monday, in
addition to 20,000 tonnes of the 380-cst fuel oil.

with the matter say, digging a deeper foothold in the global supply market just before
production cuts agreed with OPEC and other producers are scheduled to kick in. [nL4N1EB2GZ]
    * Beijing will not issue fuel export quotas for independent refineries next year, dealing a
blow to the upstart group of companies and scrapping a key component of a scheme that has
transformed China's oil markets, three sources said. [nL4N1EB30D]

SINGAPORE, Dec 30 (Reuters) - Annual average margin on Asian
gasoil fell to its lowest in seven years as supply of the fuel
remained ample while demand failed to catch up.
    The average margin for 2016 fell by $3 from a year-ago level
to about $10 a barrel, the lowest since 2009, Reuters data
showed. 
    China's largest state refiner Sinopec Corp on Friday began
supplying the Chinese capital with a new, lower-emission grade
of petrol and diesel in line with efforts to combat smog that
has plagued the country just a month into the winter.
[nL4N1EP1NZ]
    Spot demand from Egypt supported gasoil margins in Asia.
State-owned Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) is seeking up
to 1.012 million tonnes of high sulphur gasoil for delivery into
Suez, Ain Sukhna and Alexandria ports in February and March.
[nL4N1EP15P]
    Egypt's government has approved a deal to hand over two Red
Sea islands to Saudi Arabia and sent it to parliament for
ratification, despite a legal dispute over the plan, according
to state television. [nL5N1EO2MK]
    The deal, announced in April, caused public uproar and rare
protests by Egyptians who said the uninhabited islands of Tiran
and Sanafir belonged to their country.
    The controversy has become a source of tension with Saudi
Arabia, which has provided billions of dollars of aid to Egypt
but recently halted fuel shipments amid deteriorating relations.
    A drawdown in stocks in both the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp
hub and the Singapore regions are expected to boost gasoil
margins.
    Gasoil stocks in independently held storage in the
Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp hub rose by 1.6 percent in the week
to Thursday as inland demand slowed, data from Dutch consultancy
PJK International showed. [nL5N1EO2O7]
    Low water levels on the Rhine River are hindering demand for
middle distillates as barges can only operate at around 30
percent of their capacity, PJK's Patrick Kulsen said.
    At least 14 long-range 2 sized vessels are temporarily
storing gasoil off Singapore waters and could set sail to Europe
should demand improve, traders said.

SINGAPORE, Dec 27 (Reuters) - Spot demand from South Korea and Indonesia is expected to
boost high sulphur fuel oil cash differentials though ample supply pressured cash premiums
downwards on Tuesday, trade sources said.
    Indonesia's state-owned Pertamina entered the spot market seeking 160,000 barrels of marine
fuel oil for January and South Korea's utilities East West Power and Western Power sought
cargoes for January, they said.
    Potentially lower imports from Russia could also boost fuel oil differentials in 2017, an
industry source said. 
    Russia's output of oil products is expected to fall by about 2.5 percent in 2017 due to
further work on a massive refinery modernisation programme aimed at boosting fuel quality, a
deputy energy minister said. 
    Production of fuel oil could decline by more than two million tonnes due to an increase in
export duty from Jan. 1, 2017. [nL5N1EJ04C]
    Taiwan's Formosa Petrochemical Corp offered a high sulphur cargo for January, helping to
meet some of the spot demand, traders said.     
    Indonesia's Pertamina also offered a low sulphur fuel oil cargo for January, traders added.

overseas demand pushed northwest European gasoline cracks to
their lowest in more than seven weeks on Friday.  
    
    * U.S. gasoline consumption was significantly lower in April
than reported at the time, according to new data published by
the the U.S. Energy Information Administration. [nL8N19N2QE]

analysts to reassess the strength of gasoline demand in the
world's largest consumer of gasoline in automobiles.

were more than 20 percent higher in the week to June 30 as
exports from the region slowed. [ARA/]      
    * U.S. gasoline stocks <USOILG=ECI> also posted an

said.

LONDON, July 5 (Reuters) - Diesel refining margins in
northwest Europe declined on Tuesday amid a sharp slump in
global oil prices and a steady rise in supplies.

contango did encourage some buying, traders said. Still, limited
storage capacity put a cap on the buying.

diesel and heating oil at large discounts as output remained
high.

diesel cracks increased expectations for European refineries to
reduce operating rates.

stronger demand for fuel oil and the lower costs of crude oil,
traders said.
    * Signs of growing stress were also showing on the U.S. East

percent at its 185,000 barrel-per-day refinery outside of
Philadelphia.[nL1N19R0PF]

SINGAPORE, July 5 (Reuters) - The front month July-August time spread for 380-cst
fuel oil narrowed its contango on Tuesday in renewed buying interest, traders said. 
    The 380-cst July-August time spreads <FO380SGSDMc1> discount was 50 cents narrower at
minus $1.25 a tonne to Singapore quotes, Thomson Reuters data showed. 
    The front month viscosity spread <FOVISSGDFMc1>, the price difference between 180-cst
and 380-cst swaps, continued to come off its recent high and settled at $5 a tonne on
Tuesday. On Friday, the spread was at $7 a tonne, its highest since Oct. 15. 
    In the physical market, two cash deals were fixed in the Platts window totalling
40,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil. Tuesday's deals were done at a wider discount of minus
$2 to minus $2.50 a tonne to Singapore quotes, compared to the last time the 180-cst fuel
traded at minus $1 a tonne on Friday. 
    Traders said that Mercuria was active in both seeking and offering 380-cst in the
window. Mercuria's offers for 380-cst fuel were most aggressive at minus $2 a tonne,
compared to offers from Glencore, Repsol and Gunvor that ranged between a discount of 75
cents a tonne to parity to Singapore quotes, sources said. 
    Mercuria was also most aggressive in seeking 380-cst fuel oil after having placed
bids at a discount of $5 a tonne to Singapore quotes across the assessment window,
compared to others that bid in the range of about minus $2.25 to minus $4.30 a tonne to
Singapore quotes, trade sources said. 
    Cash discounts for benchmark 180-cst fuel oil <FO180-SIN-DIF> were 42 cents lower to
minus $2.14 a tonne to Singapore quotes while 380-cst cash discounts <FO380-SIN-DIF>
edged 5 cents lower to minus $2 a tonne to Singapore quotes. 
    
    RELATED NEWS:
    - Crisis-struck Venezuela is sending two supertankers filled with fuel oil across the
oceans to Singapore, in what traders described as a surprise move that could help ease a
tight market. [nL4N19R2BH]
    - Oil fell below $50 a barrel on Tuesday as concern about a potential slowdown in
economic growth that would sap demand trumped supply outages in Nigeria and other
exporting nations. [nL8N19R17I]
    - Shipping Corporation of India <SCI.NS> (SCI) will resume sailing to Iran this month
after a four-year gap, transporting an oil cargo for a state-run refiner, the chairman of
India's biggest shipping company said on Tuesday.

SINGAPORE, Aug 10 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil margin rebounded to a one-week high on
Thursday after a fire shut a secondary unit at South Korea's second-largest oil refinery and as
spot demand appeared from Sri Lanka, trade sources said. 
    
    - GS CALTEX FIRE: GS Caltex said it has shut a heavy oil upgrading unit after a fire on
Thursday. [nL4N1KW26S]
      The blaze, which is now under control, broke out in the 66,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) heavy
oil upgrading unit or Vacuum Residue Hydrocracker (VRHCR), at GS Caltex's Yeosu refinery,
located in southwest of Seoul. 
      This could reduce diesel exports from South Korea, which could in turn boost margins for
the fuel, traders said. 
    - SRI LANKA SEEKS GASOIL, JET FUEL: Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp is seeking a
combination cargo of diesel and gasoline for delivery in mid-September and another cargo of
gasoil and jet fuel for delivery in early October through two separate tenders. <MDIS/TENDA>
    - VIETNAM BUYS:  Vietnam's Saigon Petro bought 10,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for
Sept. 9 to 13 delivery into Cat Lai at a premium of $1.30 a barrel to Singapore quotes. 
    - INDIA SELLS GASOIL: India's Essar Oil likely sold up to 70,000 tonnes of 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for Sept. 8 to 12 loading at a premium of about 30 to 40 cents a barrel to Middle East
quotes, lower than a previous cargo sold, traders said.
    - SINGAPORE STOCKS: Singapore onshore gasoil and jet fuel stocks fell 9 percent to a
three-week low of 11.806 million barrels in the week to Aug. 9, the latest data from
International Enterprise (IE) showed. <O/SING1> 
      There were fewer cargoes arriving into Singapore compared with the previous week, likely
due to firm demand from Europe. 
    - GREECE REFINERY MAINTENANCE: Greece's Hellenic Petroleum said it had moved forward planned
maintenance work at its 100,000 barrel per day (bpd) Elefsina refinery, which would remain fully
shut down until September as a result. [nL5N1KW33D]

SINGAPORE, Aug 11 (Reuters) - The Asian gasoil margin edged higher on Friday, supported by
spot demand from Vietnam and as refinery outages in South Korea curtailed supply causing the
time-spread to flip back into backwardation, traders said. 
    
    - PETROLIMEX BUYS GASOIL: Petrolimex, Vietnam's top fuel importer, bought two cargoes of
35,000 tonnes each of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for loading from Singapore, Thailand or Malaysia at
a premium of 20 cents a barrel to Singapore quotes, on a free-on-board basis, traders said. 
    - EMARAT SEEKS: Emirates General Petroleum Corp is seeking up 16,000 tonnes of 10ppm sulphur
diesel for delivery into Jebel Ali over Sept. 4 to 5 in a tender that closes on Aug. 15 and is
valid until Aug. 17.     
    - INDIA REFINERS: India's state oil refiners - long focused on churning out transport and
cooking fuels - are planning a $35 billion push into petrochemicals to meet an expected surge in
demand for goods ranging from plastics to paints and adhesives. [nL4N1KT3SI]
    The drive comes as the government seeks to promote durable, cheaper materials in industries
such as farming and food packaging, while refiners eye long-term threats to their business from
renewable energy and a shift to electric vehicles.
    - WORLD OIL DEMAND: World oil demand will grow more than expected this year, helping to ease
a global glut despite rising production from North America and weak OPEC compliance with output
cuts, the International Energy Agency said on Friday. [nL5N1KX1NO]
      The agency raised its 2017 demand growth forecast to 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd)
from 1.4 million bpd in its previous monthly report and said it expected demand to expand by a
further 1.4 million bpd next year.

LONDON, Aug 14 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwest Europe held their ground on Monday, but demand
concerns began to emerge for bookings to the United States and
West Africa.
    * At least one additional cargo of gasoline was booked to
sail from Europe to the Middle East, according to shipping
fixtures. 
    * Saudi Aramco plans to shut its condensate splitter at the
Ras Tanura refinery in October for planned maintenance, industry
sources told Reuters. [nL8N1L00LF]
    * One of the sources said the 225,000 barrel per day (bpd)
splitter, which processes light oils, would be down for 30 days.
The 550,000 bpd Ras Tanura is Saudi Arabia's largest refinery. 
    * A string of vessels carrying gasoline have been booked to
sail from Europe to the United States but traders said these
voyages were booked weeks ago and demand was relatively soft on
the route for new bookings. [nL4N1KV4D7] [nL5N1KC3AK]
    * West Africa was well supplied with fuel after a month of
strong bookings to Nigeria. Traders said the bulk of the cargoes
were part of the country's crude-for-products oil swap and
Nigeria was oversupplied with gasoline as a result. 
    * A fire hit the 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) Ashdod,
Israel oil refinery, owner Paz Group said in a statement.
[nL8N1L01B8]
    * U.S. investors increased their bets on rising gasoline by
2 million barrels to 47 million barrels in the week to Aug. 8.
Fund managers are now more bullish on gasoline prices than at
any time since the middle of February. [nL1N1KX1N2]
    * Chinese oil refineries operated in July at their lowest
daily rates since September 2016, official data showed on
Monday, to ease brimming inventories as state-owned oil giants
faced off independents in a retail petrol price war.
[nL4N1L019S]

the afternoon session at $539 a tonne fob ARA. That compared

Amsterdam-Rotterdam, compared with Friday's trades at $538-$543

LONDON, July 29 (Reuters) - Northwest European gasoline
margins fell on Friday, pressured by weak overseas demand and
heavy Atlantic basin supplies.
  
     * Simple European refiners are cutting runs by up to 5
percent, enabling them to hold onto some profits by taking out
marginal barrels and units that produce lower-quality fuels,
according to a Mediterranean trade source. [nL8N1AF3PC]
    * Results this week from majors including Royal Dutch Shell
<RDSa.L>, Total <TOTF.PA>, BP <BP.L> and ENI <ENI.MI> show
refinery margins crashing by as much as half from last year.
    * Chevron Corp <CVX.N> posted its worst quarterly loss since
2001 on Friday and Exxon Mobil Corp <XOM.N> reported a 59
percent slide in quarterly profit, both victims of a prolonged
rout in crude prices CLc1LCOc1 and sinking income from refining,
a sign of the broad malaise across the energy sector.
[nL1N1AF0NC]
    * Exxon processed 4 percent less crude in the quarter than a
year ago and produced less gasoline, an unusual step as low oil
prices typically encourage refiners to produce more.
    * PBF Energy Inc <PBF.N> has cut production by up to 7
percent across its refinery network to deal with slumping
margins caused by soaring inventories of gasoline and diesel,
PBF Chief Executive Officer Tom Nimbley said on an earnings call
on Friday. [nL1N1AF0US]
    * Philadelphia Energy Solutions Inc <PESC.N> was in the
market for gasoline after the company shut a gasoline-making
unit at the Girard Point section of its Philadelphia refinery
complex, according to traders. [nL1N1AE0W5]
    * Spain's 220,000 barrels-per-day Bilbao oil refinery

SINGAPORE, Feb 14 (Reuters) - Asian regrade prices remained
negative on Tuesday as jet fuel demand starts to wane at the end
of peak winter season, traders said.    
    Regrade prices refer to the price difference between gasoil
and jet fuel/kerosene, which is used as a heating oil. A
negative regrade indicates lower jet fuel prices against gasoil
prices. 
    Jet fuel supply was plentiful with India's Essar Oil and
Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) offering up to
100,000 tonnes of the fuel for loading in March, traders said.
    Diesel supply from India, however, was tight with many
refineries preparing to shift production towards lower sulphur
diesel ahead of a country-wide shift in April, they said.
    Indian Oil offered a high sulphur gasoil cargo for loading
in Kandla in March, likely due to a refinery maintenance,
traders said, though this could not immediately be confirmed. 
    Spot demand for diesel also appeared from South Africa with
Engen Petroleum seeking a cargo for March, which could help to
absorb some of the excess ultra low sulphur diesel supply,
traders said.     
    China's state planner will raise diesel retail prices by 50
yuan ($7.28) per tonne from Wednesday, the National Development
and Reform Commission (NDRC) said in a statement on its website
on Tuesday. [nB9N1FG01U]
    The price increase is the second upward adjustment since
January this year.
    Oil refiner TonenGeneral Sekiyu will reduce crude refining
capacity at its four domestic refineries in Japan by 71,500
barrels per day (bpd) by March 31 to meet a government order on
boosting efficiency, its top executive said. [nL4N1FZ1SI]
    The cuts would be made at multiple crude distillation units
(CDUs) at all of its four refineries in its home market though
the details have not been decided yet, TonenGeneral President
Jun Mutoh said on the sidelines of its 2016 earnings.

29 loading from New Mangalore. The tender closes on Feb. 21 and
is valid until Feb. 22. 
    - Indian Oil Corp has offered 26,000 to 28,000 tonnes of 0.2
percent sulphur gasoil for March 6 to 8 loading from Kandla. The
tender closes on Feb. 16 and is valid until Feb. 17.

LONDON, Feb 14 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins
slightly declined on Tuesday but held near three-month highs due
to strong demand in Asia and the Middle East and refinery
outages in the region.

recent days from robust demand in Asia and the Middle East,
where refinery outages have limited production.
    * Several cargoes of gasoline and reformate have been booked
in recent days from northwest Europe and the Mediterranean to
the Middle East and Singapore, according to shipping data.

cargoes leaving the area to West Africa.

    By Devika  Krishna Kumar
    NEW YORK, Jan 6 (Reuters) - U.S. gasoline prices recently
soared to multiyear seasonal highs over European prices, setting
the stage for more imports from across the Atlantic, but high
freight costs mean not everyone will be able to take advantage
of the arbitrage opportunity.
    The difference between benchmark RBOB U.S. gasoline <RBc1>
and benchmark Eurobob gasoline <EUROBOB-ARA> prices hit their
widest for this time of year in at least six years late in
December. 
    After about a year of oversupply on the U.S. East Coast,
inventories are falling in line with historic averages. In
addition, a spate of refinery outages and stronger crude prices
has helped boost gasoline prices, traders said. [REF/OUT]
[nL5N1E505D]
    However, European prices have not rallied at a similar pace,
opening up an arbitrage opportunity for European refiners. Exxon
Mobil Corp <XOM.N> and Cepsa SA <CPF.GQ> have successfully
booked cargoes in recent days, traders said.    
    One New York Harbor cash trader said the arb is at its
strongest in the last 12 months, excluding periods when the key
Colonial Pipeline that supplies product to the East Coast was
shut.
    Benchmark U.S. gasoline's premium over European gasoline
widened to as much as $7.49 per barrel by Dec. 27, the biggest
seasonal gulf since at least 2010. 
    The U.S. East Coast accounts for nearly a third of the
country's total gasoline demand. Because European refiners
produce more gasoline than required on that continent, they have
long profited by exporting to the busy East Coast.
    The widening in the U.S. gasoline premium over Europe has
not yet led to a surge in imports. Due to high freight rates,
few cargoes have been able to go through and the window to make
this trade profitable has narrowed in recent days. 
    Imports of total motor gasoline into PADD 1, or the East
Coast, sank to the lowest in a year in the week to Dec. 23 at
374,000 barrels per day. Last week, imports rebounded to a
one-month high of 690,000 bpd in the week to Dec. 30, according
to U.S. government data. [EIA/]
    Spot tanker freight rates from Rotterdam to Philadelphia
<TC-RDM1-PHL> have climbed through December to the highest
levels in more than a year. 
    Several tankers were tentatively booked out of Europe on the
transatlantic route in recent days, traders said, but few
cargoes went through. 
    In the last week of December, about seven cargoes were
booked on the transatlantic route and so far in January, there
have been around 11 cargoes locked in.
    However, two fixtures slated for mid-January loadings, the
Navig8 Constellation and the STI Battery, failed, according to a
source familiar with the matter. Several other tankers that have
been fixed will likely also not sail, traders and ship brokers
said, due to soaring freight rates.
    Slow winter month demand also can limit imports. The U.S.
East Coast gets one or two big snowstorms that crush demand in
January or February, making it harder to find buyers.

SINGAPORE, Jan 9 (Reuters) - Colder weather in Europe is expected to increase
gasoil shipments from Asia, which could boost margins for the fuel, traders said on
Monday.
    A cold snap is sweeping across Europe, boosting demand for power, and is
expected to increase demand for gasoil, which is used as heating fuel. [nL5N1EV16V]
    Taiwan's Formosa Petrochemical Corp <6505.TW> sold 300,000 barrels of jet fuel
for Feb. 6 to 10 loading from Mailiao to Winson Oil at a discount of 10 cents a
barrel to Singapore quotes, traders said.
    This is a big jump from the discount of $1 a barrel Formosa achieved for
November-loading cargo from Vitol earlier, reflecting the uptick in demand for the
fuel, they added.
    Heating demand for kerosene has likely reduced the supply of jet fuel as
refiners adjust yield to meet peak winter demand, in turn boosting prices for the
aviation fuel, they said.
    In the Gulf, Emirates General Petroleum Corp (Emarat) is seeking 60,000 tonnes
of jet fuel for early February delivery, which is expected to support jet fuel
differentials in the short term, traders said.
    Still, supply of jet fuel and diesel are expected to increase in the first
quarter of this year from the previous quarter as refineries return from
maintenance, which could reduce the differentials, they added.

SINGAPORE, Jan 5 (Reuters) - The Asian high sulphur gasoil
differential spiked to a more than one-month high on Thursday,
supported by spot demand from Indonesia, traders said.
    The cash differential for the 2,500 ppm sulphur gasoil
gained 18 cents to minus 31 cents a barrel on Thursday, the
highest level since Nov. 15 when it was minus 30 cents a barrel,
Reuters data showed.
    Indonesia's Pertamina is seeking half a million barrels of
the grade for imports in January, supporting demand for the
fuel, traders said.
    The Southeast Asian country reduced the sulphur in its
diesel to 2,500 ppm from the current 3,500 ppm from this
January. [nL4N1EV2NB]
    But most of the demand for the high sulphur fuel is expected
to be met by production from domestic refineries, a source
familiar with the matter said.
    Pertamina is expected to import mainly diesel with a sulphur
content of 350 ppm and 500 ppm this year, Deputy Chairman Ahmad
Bambang said. 
    Demand for high-quality diesel and gasoline is going up due
to the narrow price difference between lower quality and higher
quality fuels, a Pertamina official said, declining to be named
as he was not authorised to speak to the media.
    Pertamina was also seeking 440,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur
gasoil for loading over February to May, traders said. 
    Demand for gasoil from Myanmar is also growing, they added.
    Myanmar's monthly imports of gasoil is expected to hit up to
200,000 tonnes from about 70,000 to 80,000 tonnes a month
previously, traders said. [nL5N1EV058]
    
    TENDERS: 
    - Pertamina is seeking 500,000 to 535,000 barrels of 0.25
percent sulphur gasoil for delivery into Balongan over Jan. 16
to 18. The tender closes on Jan. 9 and is valid until Jan. 11.
    - Pertamina is also seeking four cargoes of 110,000 barrels
each of 500ppm sulphur gasoil for loading over Feb. 8 to 10,
March 3 to 5, April 18 to 20 and May 22 to 24. The tender closes
on Jan. 10 and is valid until Jan. 13.
    - India's Essar Oil has offered up to 70,000 tonnes of
500ppm sulphur gasoil for loading from Vadinar over Feb. 4 to 8.
The tender closes on Jan. 9, with same-day validity.
    - India's Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL)
has offered 40,000 tonnes of jet fuel for Feb. 25 to 27 loading
from New Mangalore. The tender closes on Jan. 10 and is valid
until Jan. 11.
    - Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has offered 6,000 tonnes of light
diesel oil for loading from Budge-Budge over Jan. 29 to 31. The
tender closes on Jan. 6 and is valid until Jan. 9.
    
    CASH DEALS: One gasoil deal, one jet fuel trade.
    - Hin Leong bought 150,000 barrels of 500ppm sulphur gasoil
for Jan. 23 to 27 loading from Total at a discount of 10 cents a
barrel to the average of Jan. 23 to 27 Singapore quotes.
    - Hin Leong bought 100,000 barrels of jet fuel for Jan. 25
to 29 loading from Total at a discount of 50 cents a barrel to
the average of Jan. 25 to Feb. 1 Singapore quotes.

By Devika  Krishna Kumar
    NEW YORK, Jan 6 (Reuters) - U.S. gasoline prices recently
soared to multiyear seasonal highs over European prices, setting
the stage for more imports from across the Atlantic, but high
freight costs mean not everyone will be able to take advantage
of the arbitrage opportunity.
    The difference between benchmark RBOB U.S. gasoline <RBc1>
and benchmark Eurobob gasoline <EUROBOB-ARA> prices hit their
widest for this time of year in at least six years late in
December. 
    After about a year of oversupply on the U.S. East Coast,
inventories are falling in line with historic averages. In
addition, a spate of refinery outages and stronger crude prices
has helped boost gasoline prices, traders said. [REF/OUT]
[nL5N1E505D]
    However, European prices have not rallied at a similar pace,
opening up an arbitrage opportunity for European refiners. Exxon
Mobil Corp <XOM.N> and Cepsa SA <CPF.GQ> have successfully
booked cargoes in recent days, traders said.    
    One New York Harbor cash trader said the arb is at its
strongest in the last 12 months, excluding periods when the key
Colonial Pipeline that supplies product to the East Coast was
shut.
    Benchmark U.S. gasoline's premium over European gasoline
widened to as much as $7.49 per barrel by Dec. 27, the biggest
seasonal gulf since at least 2010. 
    The U.S. East Coast accounts for nearly a third of the
country's total gasoline demand. Because European refiners
produce more gasoline than required on that continent, they have
long profited by exporting to the busy East Coast.
    The widening in the U.S. gasoline premium over Europe has
not yet led to a surge in imports. Due to high freight rates,
few cargoes have been able to go through and the window to make
this trade profitable has narrowed in recent days. 
    Imports of total motor gasoline into PADD 1, or the East
Coast, sank to the lowest in a year in the week to Dec. 23 at
374,000 barrels per day. Last week, imports rebounded to a
one-month high of 690,000 bpd in the week to Dec. 30, according
to U.S. government data. [EIA/]
    Spot tanker freight rates from Rotterdam to Philadelphia
<TC-RDM1-PHL> have climbed through December to the highest
levels in more than a year. 
    Several tankers were tentatively booked out of Europe on the
transatlantic route in recent days, traders said, but few
cargoes went through. 
    In the last week of December, about seven cargoes were
booked on the transatlantic route and so far in January, there
have been around 11 cargoes locked in.
    However, two fixtures slated for mid-January loadings, the
Navig8 Constellation and the STI Battery, failed, according to a
source familiar with the matter. Several other tankers that have
been fixed will likely also not sail, traders and ship brokers
said, due to soaring freight rates.
    Slow winter month demand also can limit imports. The U.S.
East Coast gets one or two big snowstorms that crush demand in
January or February, making it harder to find buyers.

SAO PAULO, Aug 23 (Reuters) - The Brazilian government is
considering the creation of a private-sector fund to help
subsidize insurance for farmers, potentially cushioning them
from possible budget cuts in agricultural aid, newspaper Valor
Econômico reported on Tuesday.
    According to Valor, the proposed fund would bear part of the
cost of farming insurance policies, adding that the idea is
under discussion between Agriculture Minister Blairo Maggi's
team, insurers and farming groups. 
     Efforts to contact the ministry's press staff in Brasilia
for comment before working hours were unsuccessful.
    The government currently subsidizes up to 55 percent of the
cost of farming insurance policies depending on the region or
the type of crop, Valor reported. 
    Maggi, who is also a major soybean farmer, says a greater
share of the insurance costs should be borne by private
investors, the paper said.
    His remarks underscore efforts by interim President Michel
Temer's administration to scale back heavy government
intervention that led to a record budget deficit and Brazil
losing investment-grade credit ratings.
    The proposed farming insurance fund resembles one created in
Spain, according to Valor. Talks on the project are preliminary
and may not yield an accord, Valor said.
    Brazil is the world's largest exporter of beef, poultry,
soybeans, coffee, eucalyptus pulp, concentrated orange juice and
tobacco.

SINGAPORE, Sept 21 (Reuters) - Time spreads and cracks of 380-cst high sulphur fuel oil
extended gains on Friday and ended the week higher as a tighter supply outlook provided support.
    The 380-cst fuel crack for October narrowed its discount to Brent crude to about minus
$10.90 a barrel on Friday, up from about minus $11.20 a barrel in the previous session, broker
sources said.
    The front-month crack on Monday was at a discount of $11.43 a barrel. <HFOFARAACMc1>
    The firmer crack came despite higher crude prices on Friday which rose ahead of a meeting of
OPEC and other large crude exporters that will focus on production increases as U.S. sanctions
restrict Iranian exports. [O/R]
    The Oct/Nov 380-cst time spread also firmed to about $4.75 a tonne on Friday, the brokers
said. 
    The front-month time spread was at $4.50 a tonne in the previous session and $4 a tonne at
the start of the week. <FO380SGSDMc1>
    Firm fuel oil demand and shrinking output amid refinery maintenance and upgrades is expected
to limit arbitrage flows into Asia from October. 
    Renewed U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil products are also contributing to lower fuel oil
supplies.

    INVENTORIES
    - Weekly fuel oil stocks in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) oil and storage hub fell
11 percent, or 143,000 tonnes, to a total of 1.138 million tonnes in the week ended Sept. 20,
data from Dutch consultancy PJK International showed. [ARA/]
    - ARA fuel oil stocks were at a seven-week high in the week before. 
    - Exports of fuel oil from the ARA region in the week to Sept. 20 were headed to the Arabian
Gulf and the Mediterranean, the data showed. [nL8N1W65CS]
    - ARA fuel oil imports in the week ended Sept. 20 originated from France, Poland, Russia,
the UAE and the UK.
    - ARA fuel oil inventories were 3 percent higher from year-ago levels and well above the
five-year average of 923,000 tonnes for this time of the year. <STK-FO-ARA>
    - Meanwhile, onshore Singapore inventories of fuel oil dipped to a two-week low of 15.288
million barrels, or about 2.281 million tonnes, in the week ended Sept. 19 as fuel oil net
imports fell 55 percent from the week before to 578,000 tonnes, official data showed on
Thursday. [nL3N1W637Z]

* Storage of jet fuel unusual in current market - traders
    * ENOC uses Iranian condensate to make oil products
including jet
    * ENOC cuts Iranian condensate buys ahead of U.S. sanctions 
    * Other grades produce lower volumes of jet fuel, more
expensive

    By Seng Li Peng and Jessica Jaganathan
    SINGAPORE, Sept 21 (Reuters) - Emirates National Oil Company
(ENOC) has chartered at least one vessel to store jet fuel to
ensure supply to airlines in Dubai as pending U.S. sanctions on
Iran have cut off its access to feedstocks for producing the
aviation fuel, said several industry sources. 
    ENOC has chartered the Suezmax-sized tankers Portman Square
and NS Africa for 30 to 60 days with an option to store oil
products, according to two shipbrokers. 
    The company will store jet fuel onboard at least one of the
vessels, which can store about 100,000 tonnes of jet fuel, two
industry sources said. 
    The price difference between current and forward month jet
fuel swaps is in a narrow contango, a market structure where the
price of a later-dated commodity is higher than the prompt
price. That contango is not enough to cover the cost of storing
the fuel on ships, making ENOC's move unusual, said three trade
sources. 
    Jet fuel differentials in the Middle East have been trading
at low levels due to high refining run rates and weak demand
from Europe, one of the sources said. So, ENOC's demand for fuel
to fill the ships could boost the differentials, he added. 
    While the ship-borne storage will help ENOC ensure an
immediate supply of jet fuel for Dubai International Airport,
the stockpiling also highlights ENOC's lack of access to Iranian
condensate, an ultra-light crude oil, used to produce jet fuel.
    The United Arab Emirates (UAE) government asked ENOC to
replace its Iranian condensate purchases with other grades such
as Eagle Ford from the United States after the announcement of
the U.S. sanctions against Iran, said three industry sources who
track oil and gas cargoes closely.
    The United States has already enacted sanctions limiting
Iranian participation in the global banking system and new
edicts against the country's petroleum sector go into effect on
Nov. 4. 
    ENOC processes Iranian condensate at its 140,000
barrels-per-day condensate splitter at the UAE port of Jebel
Ali, which typically yields about 20 percent jet fuel. 
    However, ENOC's alternative condensate supply yields less
jet fuel than the Iranian grade, said one of the three sources,
which is reducing the overall jet fuel volumes.
    The last Iranian condensate delivered into Jebel Ali was in
August, according to Thomson Reuters shiptracking data. The
company has also bought U.S. and Saudi condensate since June,
the data showed. 
    ENOC did not immediately reply to a Reuters request seeking
comment by email outside of business hours.    
    Qatar also produces condensates but the UAE, Saudi Arabia,
Egypt and Bahrain are in the midst of a diplomatic dispute with
the country.

LONDON, Feb 5 (Reuters) - Gasoline refining margins in
northwestern Europe declined on Friday to around $9.5 a barrel
as exports to Asia ground to a halt ahead of the Chinese New
Year.
    Chinese purchases of high octane blending components
supported gasoline cracks around the world in recent months,
pushing them to their highest seasonal levels in years.
    But the arbitrage to Asia was closed on Friday, according to
traders, and was expected to remain so as Asian activity was set
to slow down due to holidays in the region next week, traders
said.
    European gasoline prices tracked Asia, where gasoline
margins marked their biggest weekly fall in more than two years
on Friday on ample supplies. [nL3N15K35I]
    Still, exports from Europe to the Middle East offered some
support, with at least one cargo booked over the past day from
the Mediterranean, according to shipping data.

LONDON, Feb 2 (Reuters) - Forties differentials edged higher
on Tuesday after coming close to their lowest level in nearly a
month in the previous session.    
    Vitol bought two cargoes for loading in the middle of the
month, but no new fixtures for Asia are lined up as yet and the
March loading programme for Forties is set to be one of the
largest in five years. [O/LOAD] 
    So far there is just one supertanker of Forties booked to
sail to Asia in February, compared with the three that sailed in
January, based on Reuters shipping data. 
    The VLCC Hakata has been tentatively scheduled to load at
Hound Point in late February, though Reuters shipping data shows
that this fixture has not yet been set in stone.
    In terms of arbitrage, the window of opportunitity to ship
North Sea crude to the United States appears to have closed,
with Brent futures having risen to their highest premium to WTI
futures since early December.
    The premium of Brent crude to Dubai has fallen to its lowest
since late November, meaning that oil priced off the North Sea
benchmark can compete more effectively for Asian buyers than it
has done in the past couple of months. <DUB-EFS-1>
    Traders said that activity in the Forties market had slowed
in the past week, partly because of maintenance work at Hound
Point in early March, which will stop all supertanker crude
loadings.
    Only a quarter of all vessels reported to have loaded at
Hound Point in the past three months have been VLCCs, Reuters
data showed.
    
    BRENT/FORTIES
    * Shell sold a cargo to Vitol for loading Feb. 16-18 at a
discount of 65 cents to dated Brent.
    * BP sold a separate cargo to Vitol at a discount of 80
cents to dated Brent for loading Feb. 14-16.
    * The average of the two trades was above the average
reported on Monday.
    * No other bids, offers or trades for other grades were
reported.

LONDON, Feb 4 (Reuters) - North Sea crude oil differentials
held steady on Thursday after no bids, offers or deals were
concluded in the daily window, traders said.
    Differentials for Forties and Ekofisk have fallen in the
last two weeks to around their lowest in nearly a month, as a
dearth of new shipping fixtures, particularly to Asia, has
sapped some strength from the market.
    Furthermore, the premium of Brent over U.S. crude futures
yawning to its widest since early December has acted as a
deterrent to shipments west.
    Earlier in the week, traders cited at least two West African
cargoes and one North Sea cargo that had originally been fixed
to sail to the U.S. Gulf, but with the arbitrage window now
firmly shut, those deals looked unlikely to go ahead.
    So far, there is just one supertanker of Forties that has
been booked to sail to Asia this month, compared with three that
sailed in January, according to shipping data and industry
sources. 
    The VLCC Hakata has been tentatively booked to load at Hound
Point in late February, but according to shipping data, the
fixture is still tentative.
    A second supertanker, the Ellinis, loaded at Hound Point in
January, originally chartered by Shell and bound for Asia, but
has since discharged in Rotterdam and returned to Hound Point.
    
    FORTIES/EKOFISK
    * No bids, offers or trades were reported for any grades in
the daily window, traders said.
    * On Tuesday, a Feb. 16-18 cargo traded at a discount of 65
cents to dated Brent and a cargo loading Feb. 14-16 traded at an
80-cent discount to the benchmark, while Ekofisk was offered on
Wednesday at a premium of 25 cents to the dated price.
