LONDON, Feb 1 (Reuters) - Forties crude oil differentials
were offered at their lowest in nearly a month on Monday as a
dearth of new fixtures for supertankers bound for Asia and a
larger loading programme for March weighed on the market.    
    No deals were reported in the daily trading window. Forties
was offered at its lowest since early January, although this
offer met with no buyers and was then withdrawn, traders said. 
    The four crude streams that make up the dated Brent
benchmark - Brent itself, Ekofisk, Oseberg and Forties - will
load at an average 968,000 barrels per day (bpd) in March,
compared with a final average of 1.014 million bpd reported in
February. [O/LOAD]
    The Forties stream will include 24 cargoes, which will load
at an average rate of 465,000 bpd next month, up from February's
average daily rate of 455,000 bpd.
    This will be the second-largest monthly loading programme in
the last five years, after January's 523,000-bpd schedule.  
    There is less scope for some of this greater supply to be
absorbed in March, when repair work at Hound Point, where
Forties loads, will halt all loadings of crude oil onto Very
Large Crude Carriers for two weeks.
    So far, there is just one supertanker of Forties booked to
sail to Asia in February, compared with the three that sailed in
January, based on Reuters shipping data.

a discount of 75 cents to dated Brent.
    * BP offered a cargo of Forties for loading Feb. 14-16 at a
discount of 85 cents to dated Brent.
    * Both offers were subsequently withdrawn and compare with
an average discount of about 61 cents for Forties last Thursday.

the New York Harbour area last week, traders said.

the low side, PJK's Lars van Wageningen said. <STK-GO-ARA>

week to May 24, up from 593,000 tonnes in the previous week, the data showed. <STK-JET-ARA>

SINGAPORE, Jan 9 (Reuters) - Advanced demand for delivered bunker fuels has so far been limited
as China-based shippers have yet to stock up ahead of the Chinese New Year celebrations in
mid-February, three bunker fuel traders said.
    In a sign of slow demand and ample supplies, 380-cst ex-wharf premiums this week have traded at
$2.00-$2.50 a tonne to Singapore quotes, down from around $3.00 a tonne in the previous week, trade
sources said.
    Traders, however, expect bunker demand to pick up by mid-January as buyers fill their
requirements. 
    
    ARBITRAGE
    - UML, Socar's shipping arm, has chartered a very large crude carrier, Happiness I, to load up
to 270,000 tonnes of fuel oil from Rotterdam around Jan. 15 for discharge into Singapore by
end-February for a $3 million fee, according to ship broker sources and ship tracking data in
Reuters Eikon.
    
    TENDERS
    - The UAE's ADNOC has offered a variety of fuel oil grades for export in February from its
Ruwais refinery in an offer closed to bidders on Jan. 8, trade sources said. 
    - ADNOC is offering two 45,000-tonne cargoes of cracked medium-sulphur fuel oil from Ruwais
loading over Feb. 6-8 and Feb. 18-20. 
    - It is also offering two 90,000-tonne cargoes of straight-run fuel oil with a maximum 1.2
percent sulphur content loading on Feb. 8-10 and Feb. 24-26. 
    - The state-run company is offering 40,000 tonnes of 93-cst low-viscosity fuel oil with a 3.93
percent sulphur content loading on Feb. 11-13. 
    - Since January last year, ADNOC has typically exported four to five 90,000-tonne cargoes of
straight-run fuel oil each month after a fire broke out at its 800,000-barrel-per-day Ruwais
refinery. [nL5N1FA3XW]
    - It is unclear why ADNOC's fuel oil exports for February are this varied in quality, but two
trade sources said this may be due to increased refining capacity at one of its secondary units. 
    - South Korea's GS Engineering & Construction said in June it won an order worth $865 million to
restore a fire-hit refinery unit which it expected to complete by early 2019.[nL3N1JR14F]
    - For more information, please see [FUEL/TENDA].
        
    SHELL HEIST 
    - Eleven men were charged in a Singapore court on Tuesday in connection with a large-scale oil
theft at Shell's biggest refinery, while police said they were investigating six other men arrested
in a weekend raid. [nL4N1P41JH]
    - Police said on Tuesday they had detained 17 men, whose ages ranged from 30 to 63, and seized
millions of dollars in cash and a small tanker during their investigations into theft at the Pulau
Bukom industrial site, which sits just south of Singapore's main island.
    - Nine Singaporeans were immediately charged in the theft, of which eight were employees of the
Singapore subsidiary of Royal Dutch Shell Plc <RDSa.L>, court documents showed. Two Vietnamese
nationals were charged with receiving stolen goods on a small tanker named Prime South, the
documents showed.
    - The court documents seen so far allege three incidents of gasoil theft: on Nov. 21, 2017, of
more than 2,322 tonnes valued at S$1.277 million; and on Jan. 5 and 7 this year of a combined 2,062
tonnes of gasoil valued at S$1.126 million.

outages in Europe, including at the region's largest refinery.

week to July 28, compared with analysts' expectations in a

barrels, the highest on record.

which is most reliant on imports from Europe, rose, casting
doubt on its demand for imports.
    * The European barge crack slipped to $12.94 per barrel from
more than $13 on Tuesday. 
    * Gunvor was restarting units at its 110,000 barrel per day
(bpd) Ingolstadt, Germany, oil refinery after a leakage on a
cooling water line on July 27 led to a partial unplanned
shutdown, the refinery said in an emailed statement. [REF/OUT]

not restart until the second half of August at the earliest,
also underpinned prices. [nL5N1KN4UD]

cargoes were also booked on the route in recent days.

to traders, and were expected to remain strong in August.

the afternoon session at $546 a barrel fob ARA, down from $547 a
tonne a day earlier.

    By Devika  Krishna Kumar
    NEW YORK, Aug 1 (Reuters) - Enterprise Products Partners LP
<EPD.N> said on Wednesday it would expand its Seaway crude
pipeline system capacity to about 950,000 barrels per day (bpd)
from 850,000 bpd.
    The company said it expects to add drag reducing agents
(DRAs) to boost capacity on the Seaway 2 line by about 100,000
bpd by September. The Seaway system hauls crude from Cushing,
Oklahoma, the delivery point for U.S. oil futures, to Gulf Coast
refineries.
    Enterprise said it was also evaluating more expansions of
the Seaway system and was mulling converting natural gas liquids
(NGL) pipelines to crude oil in order to help alleviate pipeline
takeaway constraints in the Permian basin.
    The production surge in the Permian basin, the biggest
oilpatch in the United States, has outpaced pipeline takeaway
capacity, causing bottlenecks and depressing prices in the
region. 
    Enterprise said total crude oil pipeline transportation
volumes were a record 2.1 million bpd for the second quarter of
2018 compared to 1.5 million bpd for the second quarter of 2017.
    The Midland-to-Sealy crude oil pipeline averaged 545,000 bpd
of gross transportation volumes from the Permian basin. That
pipeline was recently expanded to 575,000 bpd and is fully
subscribed under long term contracts, the company said during
its earnings call. 
    In its Houston terminal alone, the company has over 2
million bpd of crude export capacity along with about 1 million
bpd at its Texas City facility with Enbridge. 
    U.S. crude exports have surged since Washington lifted a ban
in late 2015 and have helped support oil prices <CLc1> as
production has climbed to a weekly record of about 11 million
bpd.
    In July, Enterprise said it was planning to develop an
offshore crude oil export terminal off the Texas Gulf Coast
capable of fully loading Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs),
which have capacities of about 2 million barrels. [nBw7rtqK1a]
    The project has seen demand from international customers as
well as U.S. producers, the company said.
